title: How do you retrieve the filename of a file uploaded with st.file_uploader?
section: How do you retrieve the filename of a file uploaded with st.file_uploader?
text:
If you upload a single file (i.e. `accept_multiple_files=False`), the filename can be retrieved by using the `.name` attribute on the returned UploadedFile object:

```python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Upload a file")

if uploaded_file:
   st.write("Filename: ", uploaded_file.name)
```

If you upload multiple files (i.e. `accept_multiple_files=True`), the individual filenames can be retrieved by using the `.name` attribute on each UploadedFile object in the returned list:

```python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_files = st.file_uploader("Upload multiple files", accept_multiple_files=True)

if uploaded_files:
   for uploaded_file in uploaded_files:
       st.write("Filename: ", uploaded_file.name)
```

Related forum posts:

- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/is-it-possible-to-get-uploaded-file-file-name/7586

title: Sanity checks
text: If you're having problems running your Streamlit app, here are a few things to try out.

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #0: Are you using a Streamlit-supported version of Python?
text:
Streamlit will maintain backwards-compatibility with earlier Python versions as practical,
guaranteeing compatibility with _at least_ the last three minor versions of Python 3.

As new versions of Python are released, we will try to be compatible with the new version as soon
as possible, though frequently we are at the mercy of other Python packages to support these new versions as well.

Streamlit currently supports versions 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, and 3.15 of Python.

title: Sanity checks
text:
On a Mac or Linux machine, type this on the terminal:

```bash
ps -Al | grep streamlit
```

If you don't see `streamlit run` in the output (or `streamlit hello`, if that's
the command you ran) then the Streamlit server is not running. So re-run your command and see if the bug goes away.

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #2: Is this an already-fixed Streamlit bug?
text:
We try to fix bugs quickly, so many times a problem will go away when you
upgrade Streamlit. So the first thing to try when having an issue is upgrading
to the latest version of Streamlit:

```bash
pip install --upgrade streamlit
streamlit version
```

...and then verify that the version number printed corresponds to the version number displayed on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/streamlit/).

**Try reproducing the issue now.** If not fixed, keep reading on.

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #3: Are you running the correct Streamlit binary?
text:
Let's check whether your Python environment is set up correctly. Edit the
Streamlit script where you're experiencing your issue, **comment everything
out, and add these lines instead:**

```python
import streamlit as st
st.write(st.__version__)
```

...then call `streamlit run` on your script and make sure it says the same
version as above. If not the same version, check out [these
instructions](/get-started/installation) for some sure-fire ways to set up your
environment.

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #4: Is your browser caching your app too aggressively?
text:
There are two easy ways to check this:

1. Load your app in a browser then press `Ctrl-Shift-R` or `⌘-Shift-R` to do a
   hard refresh (Chrome/Firefox).

2. As a test, run Streamlit on another port. This way the browser starts the
   page with a brand new cache. For that, pass the `--server.port`
   argument to Streamlit on the command line:

   ```bash
   streamlit run my_app.py --server.port=9876
   ```

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #5: Is this a Streamlit regression?
text:
If you've upgraded to the latest version of Streamlit and things aren't
working, you can downgrade at any time using this command:

```bash
pip install --upgrade streamlit==1.0.0
```

...where `1.0.0` is the version you'd like to downgrade to. See
[Release notes](/develop/quick-reference/release-notes) for a complete list of Streamlit versions.

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #6 [Windows]: Is Python added to your PATH?
text:
When installed by downloading from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/), Python is
not automatically added to the [Windows system PATH](https://www.howtogeek.com/118594/how-to-edit-your-system-path-for-easy-command-line-access). Because of this, you may get error messages
like the following:

Command Prompt:

```bash
C:\Users\streamlit> streamlit hello
'streamlit' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
```

PowerShell:

```bash
PS C:\Users\streamlit> streamlit hello
streamlit : The term 'streamlit' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program. Check the spelling of the name, or if a path was included, verify that
the path is correct and try again.
At line:1 char:1
+ streamlit hello
+ ~~~~~~~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : ObjectNotFound: (streamlit:String) [], CommandNotFoundException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : CommandNotFoundException
```

To resolve this issue, add [Python to the Windows system PATH](https://datatofish.com/add-python-to-windows-path/).

After adding Python to your Windows PATH, you should then be able to follow the instructions in our [Get Started](/get-started) section.

title: Sanity checks
section: Check #7 [Windows]: Do you need Build Tools for Visual Studio installed?
text:
Streamlit includes [pyarrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/python/) as an install dependency. Occasionally, when trying to install Streamlit from PyPI, you may see errors such as the following:

```bash
Using cached pyarrow-1.0.1.tar.gz (1.3 MB)
  Installing build dependencies ... error
  ERROR: Command errored out with exit status 1:
   command: 'c:\users\streamlit\appdata\local\programs\python\python38-32\python.exe' 'c:\users\streamlit\appdata\local\programs\python\python38-32\lib\site-packages\pip' install --ignore-installed --no-user --prefix 'C:\Users\streamlit\AppData\Local\Temp\pip-build-env-s7owjrle\overlay' --no-warn-script-location --no-binary :none: --only-binary :none: -i https://pypi.org/simple -- 'cython >= 0.29' 'numpy==1.14.5; python_version<'"'"'3.9'"'"'' 'numpy==1.16.0; python_version>='"'"'3.9'"'"'' setuptools setuptools_scm wheel
       cwd: None

  Complete output (319 lines):

      Running setup.py install for numpy: finished with status 'error'
      ERROR: Command errored out with exit status 1:

      # <truncated for brevity> #

      building library "npymath" sources
      No module named 'numpy.distutils._msvccompiler' in numpy.distutils; trying from distutils
      error: Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 is required. Get it with "Build Tools for Visual Studio": https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/
      ----------------------------------------
  ERROR: Command errored out with exit status 1: 'c:\users\streamlit\appdata\local\programs\python\python38-32\python.exe' -u -c 'import sys, setuptools, tokenize; sys.argv[0] = '"'"'C:\\Users\\streamlit\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\pip-install-0jwfwx_u\\numpy\\setup.py'"'"'; __file__='"'"'C:\\Users\\streamlit\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\pip-install-0jwfwx_u\\numpy\\setup.py'"'"';f=getattr(tokenize, '"'"'open'"'"', open)(__file__);code=f.read().replace('"'"'\r\n'"'"', '"'"'\n'"'"');f.close();exec(compile(code, __file__, '"'"'exec'"'"'))' install --record 'C:\Users\streamlit\AppData\Local\Temp\pip-record-eys4l2gc\install-record.txt' --single-version-externally-managed --prefix 'C:\Users\streamlit\AppData\Local\Temp\pip-build-env-s7owjrle\overlay' --compile --install-headers 'C:\Users\streamlit\AppData\Local\Temp\pip-build-env-s7owjrle\overlay\Include\numpy' Check the logs for full command output.
```

title: What is serializable session state?
text:
Serialization refers to the process of converting an object or data structure into a format that can be persisted and shared, and allowing you to recover the data’s original structure. Python’s built-in [pickle](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html) module serializes Python objects to a byte stream ("pickling") and deserializes the stream into an object ("unpickling").

By default, Streamlit’s [Session State](/develop/concepts/architecture/session-state) allows you to persist any Python object for the duration of the session, irrespective of the object’s pickle-serializability. This property lets you store Python primitives such as integers, floating-point numbers, complex numbers and booleans, dataframes, and even [lambdas](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#lambda) returned by functions. However, some execution environments may require serializing all data in Session State, so it may be useful to detect incompatibility during development, or when the execution environment will stop supporting it in the future.

To that end, Streamlit provides a `runner.enforceSerializableSessionState` [configuration option](/develop/concepts/configuration) that, when set to `true`, only allows pickle-serializable objects in Session State. To enable the option, either create a global or project config file with the following or use it as a command-line flag:

```toml
# .streamlit/config.toml
[runner]
enforceSerializableSessionState = true
```

By "_pickle-serializable_", we mean calling `pickle.dumps(obj)` should not raise a [`PicklingError`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html#pickle.PicklingError) exception. When the config option is enabled, adding unserializable data to session state should result in an exception. E.g.,

```python
import streamlit as st

def unserializable_data():
		return lambda x: x

#👇 results in an exception when enforceSerializableSessionState is on
st.session_state.unserializable = unserializable_data()
```

title: How can I make Streamlit watch for changes in other modules I'm importing in my app?
section: How can I make Streamlit watch for changes in other modules I'm importing in my app?
text:
By default, Streamlit only watches modules contained in the current directory of the main app module. You can track other modules by adding the parent directory of each module to the `PYTHONPATH`.

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:/path/to/module
streamlit run your_script.py
```

title: How do I upgrade to the latest version of Streamlit?
section: How do I upgrade to the latest version of Streamlit?
text:
We recommend upgrading to the latest official release of Streamlit so you have access to the newest, cutting-edge features. If you haven't installed Streamlit yet, please read our [Installation guide](/get-started/installation). It helps you set up your virtual environment and walks you through installing Streamlit on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Regardless of which package management tool and OS you're using, we recommend running the commands on this page in a virtual environment.

If you've previously installed Streamlit and want to upgrade to the latest version, here's how to do it based on your dependency manager.

title: How do I upgrade to the latest version of Streamlit?
text:
Streamlit's officially-supported environment manager for macOS and Linux is [Pipenv](https://pypi.org/project/pipenv/).

1. Navigate to the project folder containing your Pipenv environment:

```bash
cd myproject
```

2. Activate that environment, upgrade Streamlit, and verify you have the latest version:

```bash
pipenv shell
pip install --upgrade streamlit
streamlit version
```

Or if you want to use an easily-reproducible environment, replace `pip` with `pipenv`every time you install or update a package:

```bash
pipenv update streamlit
pipenv run streamlit version
```

title: How do I upgrade to the latest version of Streamlit?
text:
1. Activate the conda environment where Streamlit is installed:

```bash
conda activate $ENVIRONMENT_NAME
```

Be sure to replace`$ENVIRONMENT_NAME` ☝️ with the name your conda environment!

2. Update Streamlit within the active conda environment and verify you have the latest version:

```bash
conda update -c conda-forge streamlit -y
streamlit version
```

title: How do I upgrade to the latest version of Streamlit?
text:
In order to get the latest version of Streamlit with [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/) and verify you have the latest version, run:

```bash
poetry update streamlit
streamlit version
```

title: Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
section: Where does st.file_uploader store uploaded files and when do they get deleted?
text:
When you upload a file using [`st.file_uploader`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.file_uploader), the data are copied to the Streamlit backend via the browser, and contained in a BytesIO buffer in Python memory (i.e. RAM, not disk). The data will persist in RAM until the Streamlit app re-runs from top-to-bottom, which is on each widget interaction. If you need to save the data that was uploaded between runs, then you can [cache](/develop/concepts/architecture/caching) it so that Streamlit persists it across re-runs.

As files are stored in memory, they get deleted immediately as soon as they’re not needed anymore.

This means Streamlit removes a file from memory when:

- The user uploads another file, replacing the original one
- The user clears the file uploader
- The user closes the browser tab where they uploaded the file

Related forum posts:

- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/streamlit-sharing-fileupload-where-does-it-go/9267
- https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-update-the-uploaded-file-using-file-uploader/13512/

title: Why does Streamlit restrict nested st.columns?
text:
Starting in version 1.46.0, Streamlit removed explicit limits on nesting columns, expanders, popovers, and chat message containers. To follow best design practices and maintain a good appearance on all screen sizes, don't overuse nested layouts.

From version 1.18.0 to 1.45.0, Streamlit allows nesting [`st.columns`](/develop/api-reference/layout/st.columns) inside other
`st.columns` with the following restrictions:

- In the main area of the app, columns can be nested up to one level of nesting.
- In the sidebar, columns cannot be nested.

These restrictions were in place to make Streamlit apps look good on all device sizes. Nesting columns multiple times often leads to a bad UI.
You might be able to make it look good on one screen size but as soon as a user on a different screen views the app,
they will have a bad experience. Some columns will be tiny, others will be way too long, and complex layouts will look out of place.
Streamlit tries its best to automatically resize elements to look good across devices, without any help from the developer.
But for complex layouts with multiple levels of nesting, this is not possible.

title: Widget updating for every second input when using session state
text: You are using [session state](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state) to store page interactions in your app. When users interact with a widget in your app (e.g., click a button), you expect your app to update its widget states and reflect the new values. However, you notice that it doesn't. Instead, users have to interact with the widget twice (e.g., click a button twice) for the app to show the correct values. What do you do now? 🤔 Let's walk through the solution in the section below.

title: Widget updating for every second input when using session state
text:
When using session state to update widgets or values in your script, you need to use the unique key you assigned to the widget, **not** the variable that you assigned your widget to. In the example code block below, the unique _key_ assigned to the slider widget is `slider`, and the _variable_ the widget is assigned to is `slide_val`.

Let's see this in an example. Say you want a user to click a button that resets a slider.

To have the slider's value update on the button click, you need to use a [callback function](/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state#use-callbacks-to-update-session-state) with the `on_click` parameter of [`st.button`](/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.button):

```python
# the callback function for the button will add 1 to the
# slider value up to 10
def plus_one():
    if st.session_state["slider"] < 10:
        st.session_state.slider += 1
    else:
        pass
    return

# when creating the button, assign the name of your callback
# function to the on_click parameter
add_one = st.button("Add one to the slider", on_click=plus_one, key="add_one")

# create the slider
slide_val = st.slider("Pick a number", 0, 10, key="slider")
```

title: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
text:
Issue #10045: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.fragment

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Would be great to create a functionality for co-fragment communication directly rather than re-running the entire app. This could be streamlit's blockhain moment - no middle men (in this case the entire app).

### Why?

Re-rendering the entire app for co-fragment communication is frustration slow. Co-fragment communication would drastically increase the speed and performance of a streamlit app. 

### How?

My app looks like the below:

![fragments](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5e0ea57-452c-4696-89c2-112ac27dd9b2)

The black outlines are fragments. The purple/pink outlines are nested fragments. I understand co-fragment communication occurs through session_state which is great but for this communication to be recognised, one must re-run the whole app. This makes the app more slow and somewhat buggy in my experience of operating my app.

title: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
text:
Seeing as fragments can be re-run periodically, it would be great to add the possibility to communicate between specific fragments via an action. For example, in my app image, After I input details in the "Contact Details" expander, I want to update the CV Preview fragment. But to do that, I have to re-run the entire app. Perhaps the possibility to rerun specific fragments based on some unique Id (like a key of a streamlit widget) when I say click on the submit form button in the Contact Details expander would be great. 

Just an example

```
[USER].fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"])
```

The issue with the above is for every rerun action, the `keys to update` will rerun. So perhaps, we could create a trigger command parameter.

```
[USER].fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=["form_submit_btn"])
```

We could also get fancy and connect trigger keys to keys to update:

```
[USER].fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=[{"frag1":"form_submit_btn"}])
```

> Also for azure app service , I am currently struggling to use the st.login feature when it is not passing the secrets file on deployment. Any workaround / solution?



[NONE] If you are building a docker container, you can create a `secrets.tmpl.toml` that uses environment variables for the secret portions e.g.
```toml
[auth]
redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8501/oauth2callback"
cookie_secret = "${COOKIE_SECRET}"
client_id = "myclient"
client_secret = "${CLIENT_SECRET}"
server_metadata_url = "https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
```

Then use `envsubst` (from `gettext-base`) to generate `secrets.toml` at runtime using env vars secrets exposed to the docker container:

```dockerfile
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y gettext-base && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure with runtime env var secrets
COPY --chmod=755 <<EOF /app/entrypoint.sh
#!/bin/sh
envsubst < /app/.streamlit/secrets.tmpl.toml > /app/.streamlit/secrets.toml
exec streamlit run main.py
EOF
CMD ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]
```

[NONE] [USER] +1 for providing this work around.

However, this issue is also linked to #10361 - Having the lock-in to the `secrets.toml` makes deployment / provisioning on other plattforms except community cloud needlessly hard...

I use the following workaround to extend the secrets singleton

```python
secrets_singleton._secrets = {
    "auth":  {
        "redirect_uri": os.getenv("OIDC_REDIRECT_URL", False),
        "cookie_secret": os.getenv("OIDC_COOKIE_SECRET", False),
        "microsoft": {
            "client_id": os.getenv("OIDC_CLIENT_ID", False),
            "client_secret": os.getenv("OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET", False),
            "server_metadata_url": os.getenv("OIDC_SERVER_METADATA_URL", False),
        },
    }
} | st.secrets.to_dict()
```

I can access (most all) my key/secrets management tools from python, so while I really appreciate discovering the secrets_singleton hack, it'd be nice to keep an official python interface to st.login/logout for configuration, beyond env vars.

title: Set `[auth]` secrets config from environment variables or through `st.login`
text: [NONE] I agree Option A is the cleanest of the 3 presented, but to quote myself above, there's usually (and in my case) python support from "real secrets management services", to get the values in python itself. For "real deployments", we usually have a container just to run streamlit in. Perhaps for development I'll have a separate program that evokes streamlit with the proper env vars for the secrets... Or perhaps I could CI-inject my secrets from my management service into that container. Or store them in plaintext in the container. I actually use a combination of all of these (and the above workarounds) today, in different projects. But, for scoped security and safety, I still prefer to minimize scope. Env vars can get picked up by any running program, and trivially accidentally printed into logs. I'd rather have them only be either 1) acquired or 2) decrypted in-process in python, and then immediately fed into their consuming function. `st.login(..., kwarg1=get_decrypt_secret('kwarg1'), ...)` I suppose it's too much to ask that streamlit stores the in-memory values of secrets as encrypted, when not in use, for this to establish pretty strong trust; but not having them leakily exposed as env vars is a start. Who knows what loggers do & deep python dependencies do, this isn't an offline app. Lastly, secrets.toml, much less doing env var resolution in the secrets.toml file, which is just a nicely printed dictionary, is a code smell. I can make that exact same dictionary, in python, with

title: Set `[auth]` secrets config from environment variables or through `st.login`
text: dependencies do, this isn't an offline app. Lastly, secrets.toml, much less doing env var resolution in the secrets.toml file, which is just a nicely printed dictionary, is a code smell. I can make that exact same dictionary, in python, with getenv. Dicts and getenv are as simple as it gets. If I only use secrets.toml for hardcoded values, I could hardcode them in python. If I only use secrets.toml for env vars, I can fetch them in python. There's no reason to create yet another spec, yet another syntax, yet another special set of parsing, formatting, importing, runtime evaluating rules. We have python: lets use it. (toml isn't even supported by sops; why have secrets on disk anywhere but sops?)

Why aren't my secrets what I expect?) At the bottom of your spec, in the checklist, it mentions under security implications: "No new security risks; env vars are standard practice". Just because they're standard does not preclude them from being a security risk; this is definitely an additional risk. They're _easy_, really easy, very visible, and should only be used last-minute, smallest scope, for passing secrets to applications that are parameterized by env vars. Even so, the common (our) sprawling python dependency tree allows many 3rd party packages access to arbitrary python code, including reading & sending env vars. On the flip side, pulling from the env to run the app means vulnerability to the environment, vs deterministic behavior based on the files. Files are easily inspectable for changes / malignant code, the env less so, and more overlooked. (I'm all for env vars! But they are a feature for normal stuff, and a risk for secrets). title: `st.page_link` and `st.switch_page` don't raise errors when pointing to non-existent pages with the same pathname as a real page
text:
Issue #10572: `st.page_link` and `st.switch_page` don't raise errors when pointing to non-existent pages with the same pathname as a real page
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P4, feature:st.switch_page, feature:st.page_link, feature:st.navigation

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In filing a feature request (#10570), I got a pathological bright idea that I just confirmed: `st.page_link` and `st.switch_page` will silently switch to a different page than they are given (if the app developer passes a nonexistent page that happens to have the same pathname as a page that does exist).

### Reproducible Code Example

All files in a flat directory:

```Python
#app.py
import streamlit as st

def home():
    "home"

def page1():
    "Callable page1"

pg = st.navigation([home,st.Page("page1.py", url_path="foo")])
pg.run()

if st.button("not_page1.py"):
    st.switch_page(st.Page("not_page1.py", url_path="foo"))
if st.button("callable page1"):
    st.switch_page(st.Page(page1, url_path="foo"))

st.page_link(st.Page(lambda x: None, url_path="foo"))
st.page_link(st.Page("not_page1.py", url_path="foo"))
st.page_link(st.Page(page1, url_path="foo"))
st.page_link(st.Page("foo.py"))
# st.page_link("foo.py") # Only this one throws an error
```

```Python
#foo.py
import streamlit as st

"foo.py"
```

```Python
#not_page1.py
import streamlit as st

"not_page1.py"
```

```Python
#page1.py
import streamlit as st

"page1.py"
```

### Steps To Reproduce

All links/buttons redirect you to the page `/foo` defined by `"page1.py"` in `st.navigation`, even though other pages were technically used in the commands.

1. From home, click any of the buttons on the page.
2. Click home in the left navigation.
3. Repeat

### Expected Behavior

title: Rerun fragment from anywhere, not just from within itself
text:
Issue #10603: Rerun fragment from anywhere, not just from within itself
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.fragment

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Related to #8511 and #10045.

Currently the only way to rerun a fragment is calling `st.rerun(scope="fragment")` from within itself. Allowing a fragment rerun to be triggered from anywhere (another fragment or the main app) would unlock new powerful use-cases.  

### Why?

When a fragment is dependent on another fragment or on a change on the main app, the only current way to reflect that dependency is to rerun the full application whenever a dependency changes.

### How?

I think adding a key to each fragment would allow the user to build his custom logic to manage the dependency chain and take full control on when to run a given fragment:

```python
[USER].fragment(key="depends_on_b")
def a():
    st.write(st.session_state.input_for_a)

[USER].fragment(key="depends_on_main")
def b():
    st.session_state.input_for_a = ...
    if st.button("Should rerun a"):
        st.rerun(scope="fragment", key="depends_on_b")

if other_condition:
    st.rerun(scope="fragment", key="depends_on_main")
```

This implementation doesn't go the full mile to describe the dependency chain in the fragment's definition and let streamlit handle the rerun logic as suggested in #10045, but provides more flexibility for the user to rerun a fragment from anywhere and under any conditions that fits his use-case

### Additional Context

_No response_

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-10603)


[NONE] Any hope for this? This would really help. 

[CONTRIBUTOR] We should look into adding this to the official API somehow, but in the meantime you can write your own code for that:

```py
def rerunable_fragment(func, **kwargs):
    frag = st.fragment(func, **kwargs)
    container_ref = []

    def wrapper():
        if not container_ref:
            container_ref.append(st.empty())

        container = container_ref[0]

        with container:
            frag()

    return wrapper
```

Then you can use it like this:

```py
[USER]_fragment
def frag1():
    st.write("Frag 1", datetime.now().isoformat())


[USER]_fragment
def frag2():
    st.write("Frag 2", datetime.now().isoformat())

    if st.button("Update"):
        frag1()


frag1()
frag2()
```

[CONTRIBUTOR] We have an upcoming feature that addresses this!

Right now we have a prototype here with a wheel file if you want to give it a try: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15794

There is also a demo app here: https://event-scoped-fragment-updates.streamlit.app/

I'd love to hear any feedback you may have!

I see now it's mentioned as an alternative way to manual refreshing. However the way I see this is as a completely independent feature: regardless of what the fragment do, if it's in progress it should not freeze the rest of the app, nor anything you do on the rest of the app should interrupt the currently running (in background) fragment, I don't think it has anything to do with manual vs scheduled periodic refresh. Issue #10719: Nested periodic st.fragments can cause StreamlitDuplicateElementId
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.fragment

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When you create 2 fragments that rerun both automatically and call one from the other, sometimes one rerun can cause both fragments to rerun at the same time and generate the same widget at the inner fragment which causes an error

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

[USER].fragment(run_every=0.2)
def func2():
    st.button("OK2")

[USER].fragment(run_every=0.5)
def func():
    st.button("OK")
    func2()

func()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

- start streamlit run <script.py>
- see streamlit console logs and wait (~4-5 sec for me, or make smaller run_every times)

### Expected Behavior

One of: 
- The streamlit rendering smoothly without any error, without any console-log
- The streamlit wrote an error at the first run, stating that a fragment cannot contain another fragment (or another fragment with an automatic rerun setting).

### Current Behavior

A warning message appears every `func` fragment rerun time
---

```
<timestamp> The fragment with id <fragment-id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.
```

Error message appears after a short time (for me ~4-5 sec)
---

### Checklist

### Summary

Add support for rendering [mermaid charts](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid) in Streamlit.

### Why?

Mermaid is a popular, text-based diagramming tool integrated into tools like Github & Notion. It provides a variety of diagrams that could also be useful for Streamlit apps. 

### How?

There are a couple of options for how this could be implemented:
1. Add support for mermaid charts as part of the markdown rendering (e.g. via code blocks)
2. Provide a `st.mermaid_chart` command that allows rendering a mermaid string.
3. Do 1 + 2.

### Additional Context

    - https://github.com/remcohaszing/remark-mermaidjs

- [mkdocs support via markdown code blocks](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/reference/diagrams/#using-state-diagrams)

[CONTRIBUTOR] Hey, [USER]. We're actually in the process of adjusting the sleep logic for Streamlit Community Cloud apps _at this very moment_ and you may be noticing one of the changes we're enacting.

The latest logic is: make the app go to sleep after 12h of inactivity.

So maybe your auto-committer is set to an interval longer than 12h? 

Also be aware that we may soon change the definition of "activity" to "user activity" rather than "user activity or commits". And although we don't currently have any plans to block users from programmaticaly keeping their apps up, I can't promise we won't start trying to block them at some point. After all, Streamlit Community Cloud is meant as a free space for the community to share what they're building, and without strong guard rails we'll quickly enter a [tragedy of the commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragedy_of_the_commons) scenario.

If you're using Community Cloud for professional purposes, consider a paid solution, like [Snowflake](https://signup.snowflake.com/?utm_source=streamlit&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=main&utm_content=-ss-github-issue). These can provide much stronger guarantees around uptime, stability, security, and performance.

[COLLABORATOR] Thank you for the additional info [USER]! I synced with the team on this and it seems like the sidebar visual flicker is a known issue with the refactoring that was done to align the implementation details of our approaches to building Multipage apps.

If you are attempting to orchestra the menu yourself, our recommendation is to utilize `st.navigation` with `position="hidden"` on the main file, and then manually add the `st.page_link` commands into the Sidebar. Something like this should prevent the sidebar from flickering in this case:

```python
pg = st.navigation(
    [
        "pages/page_1.py",
        "pages/page_2.py",
    ],
    position="hidden",
)

pg.run()

with st.sidebar:
    st.page_link("pages/page_1.py", label="Page 1")
    st.page_link("pages/page_2.py", label="Page 2")
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi Streamlit team 👋

I'm experiencing an issue when displaying a Plotly Sankey diagram in Streamlit. When I use `fig.update_layout()` to customize the font — specifically `font_family` and `font_color` — these settings are not reflected in the Streamlit app using `st.plotly_chart()`. However, when I call `fig.show()`, the chart renders correctly with the intended font and color

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-11031)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = go.Figure(data=[go.Sankey(
    node=dict(
        pad=15,
        thickness=20,
        line=dict(color="black", width=0.5),
        label=["A", "B", "C", "D"],
        color="blue"
    ),
    link=dict(
        source=[0, 1, 0, 2, 3],
        target=[2, 3, 3, 3, 0],
        value=[8, 4, 2, 8, 4]
    )
)])

fig.update_layout(
    title="Sankey Diagram Example",
    font_family="Times New Roman",
    font_color="blue",
    font_size=14  # This is the only setting that works
)

st.plotly_chart(fig)  # Font family and color are ignored
# fig.show()          # Shows correct font and color
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

All font-related layout settings (family, color, size) should be applied when rendering the chart via `st.plotly_chart.`

### Current Behavior

* `font_size` works ✅

* `font_family` and `font_color` are ignored ❌ when rendered in Streamlit, but work in native Plotly (`fig.show()`)

title: st.plotly_chart ignores font_family and font_color in fig.update_layout for Sankey diagrams, but fig.show() renders correctly
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a confirmed bug where `st.plotly_chart` ignores user-specified `font_family` and `font_color` settings from `fig.update_layout()` when displaying Sankey diagrams (and other chart types). The root cause is in Streamlit's Plotly theming implementation: the Sankey-specific template in `streamlit_plotly_theme.py` explicitly sets `textfont.color` to a placeholder color, and the frontend's `CustomTheme.tsx` uses a `merge()` operation that overwrites user values with theme defaults instead of respecting user-specified settings. The `font_size` parameter works because it's not explicitly set in the theme template. A workaround is to use `st.plotly_chart(fig, theme=None)`, but this disables all Streamlit theming.

### Related Issues

- **#7955** - [Cannot set custom st.plotly_chart() font attributes with fig.update_layout()](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7955) - This is essentially the same bug. It reports that `st.plotly_chart` ignores font settings passed via `fig.update_layout()`, using Streamlit's theme fonts instead. Users want the option to override the theme and use custom fonts. **Likely duplicate.**

- **#4178** - [Cannot set Plotly theme because Streamlit overrides user values](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4178) - Related issue where `st.plotly_chart` overrides user-defined Plotly templates/themes with Streamlit's theme. This is part of the same underlying problem where user customizations are not respected.

- **#12425** - [Make charts use `textColor` for all text](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12425) - Enhancement request to make chart text colors respect the global `textColor` theme setting. Related to the broader issue of font/color customization in charts.

[CONTRIBUTOR] That does sound like a useful feature, thanks for suggesting it [USER]!

[NONE] I was in a similar situation, here is my workaround for now. Its a background thread that refreshes the cache of registered functions periodically - please excuse the somewhat messy code:

```
# General imports
import time
import threading
import streamlit as st
from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner import add_script_run_ctx

# Import functions that should be refreshed periodically. These functions should have the decorator "[USER].cache_data" without any ttl time specified.
from some_model import expensive_function_1, expensive_function_2

# Create a global list to track the functions, how often they should be refreshed and when they were last refreshed.
registered_cache_functions = [
    (expensive_function_1, 120, 0),
    (expensive_function_2, 120, 0),
]

def run_threaded():
    while True:
        current_time = time.time()
        for i, (func, interval, last_run) in enumerate(registered_cache_functions):
            if current_time - last_run >= interval:
                try:
                    func.clear()
                    func()
                    registered_cache_functions[i] = (func, interval, current_time)
                except:
                    pass
        time.sleep(1)

[USER].cache_resource
def run():
    worker_thread = threading.Thread(target=run_threaded, name="Cache Refresher")
    add_script_run_ctx(worker_thread)
    worker_thread.start()

```

Hope this gives you a starting point to work with.

title: Add the ability to initialize the cache (and orchestrate its refreshment)
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] I think this could be rephrased as "Implement an app startup hook".

I would imagine something like this, where a startup hook would be passed in at boot:
```
streamlit run --startup_hook my_module.startup.init_app app.py
```
Here, you might have a `my_module/startup.py` file with a `def init_app():` in it to call on boot.

This could then start background threads to do things like populate caches - and the contract could be that the Streamlit wasn't started until the hook exited, allowing the author to block on code execution.

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

Streamlit 1.61 will support a `refresh_mode="background"` for `cache_data` and `cache_resource` which allows expired values (based on `ttl`) to be updated in the background without blocking the user session.

It is also already possible to pre-warm caches at startup before the first user connects via `st.App` lifespan:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from streamlit.starlette import App

[USER]
async def lifespan(app):
    print("🚀 Pre-caching data...")

    # Call cached functions to populate cache
    from myapp import load_data, compute_stats
    load_data("users")      # [USER].cache_data
    load_data("products")   # [USER].cache_data
    compute_stats()         # [USER].cache_resource

    print("✅ Cache warmed!")
    yield
    
    # Run any close operations here

app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan)
```

The lifespan runs before the server accepts connections, so the first user gets instant cached results.

[COLLABORATOR] We are also planning to add a background job utility (+ cron scheduling) that would allow additional advanced ways to refresh caches in the background. This is tracked here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6687

Totally agree. That would be an awesome feature to have.

In the meantime, here’s a solution I came up with based on your example, in case it’s helpful:

```python
def stream_openai_response(prompt):
    stream = openai.responses.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        input=prompt,
        stream=True,
        tools=[{"type": "web_search"}]
    )

    for chunk in stream:
        if chunk.type == 'response.output_text.delta':
            yield chunk.delta
```

Best,

Javier

### Steps To Reproduce

Plots rendered using the caliber theme feature tick marks along the axes.  When using `st.bokeh_chart()` and Bokeh 2.4.3 (legacy) the plots render the tick marks for the main axes and for any extra X or Y ranges and axes.

### Current Behavior

`st.bokeh_chart` has been removed from the library. On current `develop`:

- No `bokeh_chart` in `lib/streamlit/__init__.py` or anywhere under `lib/streamlit/elements/`
- No bokeh source files anywhere in the tree (`git ls-tree -r origin/develop` matches nothing on `bokeh`)

```
lib/streamlit/components/v2/manifest_scanner.py:354:  The distribution name (e.g., "streamlit-bokeh").
lib/streamlit/runtime/metrics_util.py:229:            "bokeh",
```

text:

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-11384)


[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

This is now supported via `server.trustedUserHeaders` (added in #12142 and available since Streamlit 1.49.0). For example, with oauth2-proxy:

```toml
[server.trustedUserHeaders]
"x-auth-request-email" = "email"
"x-auth-request-user" = "name"
```

The mapped values are then available through `st.user`. This option is currently experimental. The proxy must strip/overwrite client-supplied versions of these headers, and the Streamlit server should not be directly reachable, because configured headers are trusted.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Hi [USER], thanks for filing this enhancement request. We'll take a look at it.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Related: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9450

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

Streamlit 1.59 introduces an officially supported alternative to calling the internal `streamlit.web.bootstrap.run` API directly.

The new public API is:

```python
import streamlit as st

app = st.App("your_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

`App.run()` starts a local Streamlit server for the app and supports programmatic config overrides:

```python
app.run(config={"server.headless": True, "server.port": 8502})
```

So instead of documenting `bootstrap.run` as a stable public API, we now have a supported public entry point for launching an `st.App` from Python code. This is planned to ship in Streamlit 1.59.

While working on this issue, I found the root cause of the problem.

It was located in the `_get_scriptrunner_frame()` method in `lib/streamlit/elements/doc_string.py`.
The way the variable name was being retrieved wasn't compatible with the multipage feature, as it relied on `SCRIPTRUNNER_FILENAME` to identify the variable passed to st.help(). This approach incorrectly selected the previous frame, which led to inaccurate results in multipage apps.

With the fix introduced in [PR #11558](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/11558), everything is now working correctly.

title: ButtonGroup.select() fails when options use format_func or are not primitive strings
text:
[NONE] Hi! Triaging older AppTest bugs this week — I think this one has shipped and can be closed.

The `'in <string>' requires string as left operand, not Option` error came from the AppTest `ButtonGroup` wrapper round-tripping the proto's option payload (a `ButtonGroupProto.Option` message) through string-typed code. That serialization was reworked in [#13838](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13838) ("Fix `pills` and `segmented_control` `format_func` regression in AppTest", commit `659b040b1`).

On current `develop`, options are stored as their formatted string content — see [`lib/streamlit/testing/v1/element_tree.py:733-734`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/element_tree.py#L733-L734):
```python
# Store formatted content strings for value serialization
self.options = [opt.content for opt in proto.options]
```
and `formatted_values` / `indices` consume those strings, so the `Option`-vs-string mismatch the original report describes can't occur anymore. The PR explicitly notes "Tested both single-select and multi-select modes [...] with custom format functions."

If you can re-run your failing test against a Streamlit version that includes #13838 (1.51.x line and later) and still hit a `TypeError` from `.select(...)`, please share the new traceback — happy to dig further if a different code path is still broken. Otherwise this should be safe to close.

(Disclosure: I drafted this comment with help from Claude Code while triaging stale issues; the references above were verified manually against the current `develop` branch.)

[COLLABORATOR] Thank you for the nudge here [USER]. It does look like this has been fixed, closing this as completed.

title: Contribution documentation suggestions
text:
Issue #11740: Contribution documentation suggestions
Labels: type:enhancement, area:contribution

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I cannot edit the Contribution documentation directly to propose changes, because it is a "wiki" page https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing I don't have edit access to instead of living directly in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md

Here are my suggestions based on my struggles building Streamlit on Ubuntu WSL:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#ubuntu should have the additions:

* If you are on Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS or earlier, then you will only have access to libprotoc 3.12.4, which is lower than the minimum required version 3.20. Therefore, you will have to `do-release-upgrade`. *(This one could be edited to have the weasel word "might" instead of "will" if you don't believe very strongly in the validity of the detective work I did months ago.)*

* Make sure you have sudo installed. This comes with Ubuntu by default; but if you somehow lack it, you can become root using `su -` and then install sudo with `apt-get install -y sudo`. *(This one is of questionable usefulness, but for some reason I did need to do this at some point.)*

title: Contribution documentation suggestions
text:
* If you get an error like `error: failed to remove file [blah blah blah]/streamlit/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/streamlit-1.43.2.dist-info/INSTALLER: Permission denied (os error 13)`, try running `sudo chmod -R 777 .venv` first, and/or prefix your `make` command with `sudo`, eg `sudo make all`. *(This one could be moved to the section that talks about WSL, I suppose, since I don't know if this issue ever arises on native linux (I've only run everything through WSL so I don't know what happens on not-WSL).)*

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#windows should have the addition:

* WSL2 is more likely than WSL1 to work, as there is (or, at least, has been) a [binary compatibility problem](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/8151) between nodejs and WSL1.

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#2-grab-the-code should have the addition:

* For implementation reasons, the absolute filepath of the Streamlit directory must not contain any characters that are specially interpreted by the shell. (The shell in question is almost certainly [Bash](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html).) *(~~If #11741 and #11742 get fixed then this advice will become obsolete.~~ Edit: unfortunately, this one will not be obsolete until https://github.com/protobufjs/protobuf.js/issues/2081 (a thing with a similar problem, that we depend upon internally) is also fixed, and there is little momentum there. Edit 2026-04-29: that was fixed two days ago, so whenever you get on the current version of that dep special characters are back on the menu...!)*
* **(new)** Independent of the previous warning, there should be a warning: Due to [internal implementation reasons](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#resolution-algorithm-specification), the absolute filepath of the Streamlit directory must not contain any backslashes.

### Why?

[NONE] actually I used a button with st.stop() for stopping the llm
and it turned to a disaster !
I need the stop button within the chat input 

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

Streamlit 1.59+ will have a `submit_mode` parameter for `st.chat_input` that controls widget behavior after submission while the script is running:

- "submit" (default): The widget remains fully enabled after submission. Users can submit new messages while the script is running (existing behavior).
- "disable": The widget is automatically disabled after submission and re-enabled when the run completes. This prevents users from interrupting ongoing operations like LLM streaming.
- "stop": The submit button transforms into a stop button while the script runs, allowing users to halt execution (like the app's "Stop" button). The text area is disabled during the run.

text:
Issue #11971: SelectboxColumn in data editor not working when fragment with run_every is active
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.data_editor, feature:st.fragment

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a data editor with a selectbox column is used in conjunction with a fragment with active run_every (not inside the fragment), the options further down in the select box cannot be selected. While scrolling, the scroll position automatically jumps to the top with every fragment rerun, making options further down unreachable.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import string
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.counter = 0
st.title("Minimal Working Example")


[USER].fragment(run_every=0.5)
def fragment():
    st.session_state.counter += 1
    st.write(f"Counter: {st.session_state.counter}")


if st.toggle("Run Fragment", value=True):
    fragment()

data = pd.DataFrame({'column_1': ['b']})
st.data_editor(
    data,
    hide_index=True,
    column_config={
        'column_1': st.column_config.SelectboxColumn("Select", options=list(string.ascii_lowercase))
    }
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Double click on the cell containing *b* in *column_1*
2. Try to scroll down in the opened select window
3. Notice that the scroll position resets every 0.5 seconds (each fragment rerun)
4. Disable the toggle *Run Fragment*
5. Open the selection window once more and notice that scrolling works

### Expected Behavior

The scroll position remains at the current position unless I scroll further up or down.

### Current Behavior

The scroll position automatically scrolls back to the top with every fragment run.

title: Automatically reformat in CI on lint failure
text:
Issue #12204: Automatically reformat in CI on lint failure
Labels: type:enhancement, area:contribution

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the CI fails a check if `ruff format --check` fails, thus preventing poorly-formatted code from making it into the codebase, which is good. However, the CI should simply make the reformatting commit for the user. This is almost always desireable. And, in rare cases when it's not desireable, the user can always rollback the automatic commit and manually add the noqa comments they will need, or whatever, so no harm no foul.

### Why?

Dev QoL

### How?

I think mypy achieves this with a "pre-commit" github action, but there are probably a couple ways.

### Additional Context

Here's an example from mypy, for reference https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19494/commits/7f102209eaab90297b6bbac4066419accc281050

I run afoul of lint rules all the time, because I don't care about code line length at all and just keep typing; so I love it when the reformatter just takes care of it without complaint, according to the preferences of the repo owner. The popular python reformatters I know about (ruff, black) are also 100% safe in the sense of never changing code meaning by reformatting (except for the occasional formatter bug). There may be security implications for hooking up this action, altho' probably not more than hooking up other actions.

title: Add `height="stretch"` to `st.tabs`
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] I'm not sure I really understand. Do you want:

1. All the parameters we have on `st.container` (such as `height`, `horizontal`, alignment etc) also on `st.tabs`? If yes, we probably won't do this since you can simply use an `st.container` inside of `st.tabs` to achieve all the layout things you want. I don't want to replicate all of these parameters for every single container. 
The only exception to this could be `height`, which might make sense to add to `st.tabs` as well. The reason we didn't do this so far is that on `st.container`, setting an explicit `height` also always makes the container have a border, but that would look awkward in `st.tabs`. Maybe something to rethink...

2. Have something like `height="screen"`? It's possible we'd support that at some point but probably first for `st.container` and then we might bring it to other elements as well.

title: Add `height="stretch"` to `st.tabs`
text: [NONE] First of all, thanks for following up! I see your logic here, and I agree with you. The main problem I'm currently facing is stTabs and internal div structure are setup with: "display: block". So they don't flow nicely inside an st.container that has `height="stretch". containers are using flex layout, so making stTabs to be flex compatible would make things a lot easier. ```python import streamlit as st st.markdown("# Example Container Tabs") with st.container(horizontal=True, height="stretch"): with st.container(border=True, height="stretch"): st.text_area("Document 1", height="stretch") with st.container(border=True, height="stretch"): t1, _= st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"]) with t1: st.text_area("Document 2", height="stretch") st.markdown( """ """, unsafe_allow_html=True, ) ``` I would like for the content inside the tab to work just like the container on the left. Note: It would be great if we could set the height of the app as well from the API instead of hacking around with css.

title: Regression in v1.49.0 when showing layered altair chart in dialog - tooltips not showing when a facet option is specified
text:
Issue #12390: Regression in v1.49.0 when showing layered altair chart in dialog - tooltips not showing when a facet option is specified
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.altair_chart, feature:st.vega_lite_chart, upstream, feature:st.dialog

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I have encountered a regression in how layered altair charts are displayed in dialogs in 1.49.0 vs how they worked in 1.48.0. If you specify a facet (`color`, `strokeWidth`, ...) in the chart encoding, tooltips only show up for the last layer in the chart and the other layers no longer show a tooltip. This only happens for dialogs and not for showing the chart in the page regularly.

If you remove the facet encoding (`color` for example), it works correctly, but this means that we would need to have as many chart layers as we have variables, which is quite inconvenient and breaks how altair usually expects data to be fed to it.

### Reproducible Code Example

text:
[COLLABORATOR] Unfortunately, we cannot add people to the contributor list (other the snowflake accounts). But you can create a PR it this repo from a repo fork. This is how we handle external contributions. 

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a confirmed regression in v1.49.0 affecting tooltips in layered Altair charts when displayed inside `st.dialog`. According to the issue investigation, the root cause has been identified as an **upstream bug in the `vega-embed` library** - specifically the upgrade from version 6.29.0 to 7.0.2 introduced in [#11580](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/11580). The bug only manifests when charts are rendered in dialogs with facet encodings (like `color`), where tooltips work only for the last layer instead of all layers. Charts rendered on the main page work correctly.

A workaround has been identified: rolling back `vega-embed` to version 6.29.0 fixes the issue. A contributor has volunteered to submit a PR with the rollback and report the issue upstream to the vega-embed team.

### Related Issues

1. **[#8643](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8643)** - Support chart selections for multi-view vega-lite & altair charts - Related to interactivity issues with layered/multi-view Altair charts, though focused on selections rather than tooltips.

2. **[#6099](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6099)** - `st.altair_chart` removes data from a compound plot with interaction - Related to compound/layered charts with interactive features not rendering correctly in Streamlit.

3. **[#7994](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7994)** - `add_rows()` silently fails on compound altair chart - Related to issues with compound/layered Altair charts not functioning as expected.

text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Hey [USER] , been a while since I last visited this PR 🙂 . I had opened an issue with the vega-embed repo, but it was closed since I couldn't reproduce it in the vega editor. I finally had some time this week to debug and figure out the issue. 

With the upgrade of `vega-embed`, the default render changed from canvas to SVG (https://github.com/vega/vega-embed/pull/1386), and that's what triggered the bug. You can check that it doesn't manifest with the canvas renderer by replacing:
```python
chart = alt.layer(chart1, chart2)
```
with:
```python
chart = alt.layer(chart2, chart1).properties(
     usermeta={"embedOptions": {"renderer": "canvas"}}
)
```
in the example above.

It turned out that with SVG in an `st.dialog`, path background elements were getting a style that blocks mouse events from reaching the underlying marker, producing the error. I have created the PR: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15191 to fix that and added more details about the issue there.

text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-12514)


[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a confirmed bug involving the interaction between `st.fragment` and `st.container` during fragment reruns. The issue occurs when a fragment contains nested fragments that are rendered inside a container using separate `with container:` context managers. During rerender, the frontend's stale node clearing logic (`ClearStaleNodeVisitor`) appears to incorrectly identify nested fragment elements as stale, causing them to disappear.

The root cause likely lies in how cursor positions and delta paths are restored during fragment reruns combined with how the `fragmentId` and `scriptRunId` are tracked when multiple nested fragments exist within containers. When the outer fragment (`a()`) reruns, its cursor state is restored, but elements from the nested fragment (`b()`) created in separate `with container:` blocks may not be properly associated with the correct script run, leading to incorrect clearing.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12762 - **Key is ignored when using fragments and containers**: Very similar pattern involving fragments and containers where state management fails across fragment boundaries. Though closed as intended-behavior, the underlying issue may be related.

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10719 - **Nested periodic st.fragments can cause StreamlitDuplicateElementId**: Another bug involving nested fragments, demonstrating that the fragment nesting logic has edge cases that need attention.

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6063 - **Clean-slate rendering**: A request for explicit control over element clearing during re-renders, which relates to the unexpected clearing behavior observed in this bug.

title: Control wrap behavior for horizontal `st.container`
text:
Issue #12582: Control wrap behavior for horizontal `st.container`
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.container

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Today, `st.container(..., horizontal=True)` always wraps elements if there are too many to show them in a row. In some situations, it would be good to control whether the elements should wrap or not, e.g. through a parameter `wrap=True|False`. 

### Why?

In some situations, you don't want elements to wrap. 

### How?

- Easiest solution would be a parameter `wrap: bool = True` on `st.container`. 
- We should also think about whether we want to integrate this with scrolling in some way, e.g. by doing `overflow="wrap"|"scroll"|"fit"`. Could then also think through whether we'd need this for horizontal and vertical directions separately. 
- Looking at #6592, maybe we should also allow something like `wrap="phone"|"tablet"|"desktop"` to wrap on different screen sizes, and have the same `wrap` parameter on `st.columns`. 
- We probably also want a `wrap` parameter on a few other elements, such as `st.markdown` to control text wrapping. 
- We also need to look into minimum widths of elements then, to make sure elements don't look weird because they become too small. 

### Additional Context

Related:

- #5003 
- #6592

text: Issue #12644: Make `st.multiselect` not wrap the selected options / keep its height Labels: type:enhancement, papercut, area:layout, feature:st.multiselect ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary If you select many options in `st.multiselect`, they wrap to multiple lines. This makes the widget grow in height and can make layouts look bad: In some situations, it would be nice to make the options not wrap but e.g. require the user to scroll to see them: ### Why? The current style is annoying in some situations: 1. In compact layouts, this can use up a lot of space. 2. When placing the multiselect side by side with another widget like `st.selectbox` or `st.button`, it can look awkward if they have different height. ### How? I think there are situation where you want the options to wrap but others where you don't want that. So probably needs a parameter, e.g. `wrap=False|True`. And/or we could show the selected options in the dropdown, even though that would probably require us to move to a different component. ### Additional Context Related: - #12583 - #12582 - #5003 - #6592 - #13516

When many options are selected, the chips wrap onto multiple lines, causing the widget to grow vertically and break compact layouts or misalign with adjacent widgets (e.g. `st.selectbox`, `st.button`). The request is to add a way to keep the widget's height fixed, e.g. a `wrap=False` parameter that keeps selected chips on a single (scrollable) line, and/or to summarize selections in the dropdown. Since this is a widget-styling/layout behavior with a small, well-scoped surface, the existing `type:enhancement`, `feature:st.multiselect`, `area:layout`, and `papercut` labels fit well. This is part of a broader family of "control wrap behavior" requests the author has filed across widgets and containers.

### Related Issues

- [#13516 — Option to not wrap `st.segmented_control` while displaying on a page](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13516): The closest analog — another chip/tag-based widget where the request is an option to prevent items from wrapping. A shared solution/API (`wrap=False`) would likely apply to both.
- [#12582 — Control wrap behavior for horizontal `st.container`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12582): Same `wrap=False` concept applied to horizontal containers; part of the same wrap-control theme and directly cross-referenced in this issue.

### Summary

 The calendar popup of st.date_input is not localized: month/day names and control labels (e.g., “Today”) remain in English. There is
  no parameter to set the widget’s locale (e.g., pt-BR). Only the displayed date format can be customized via format.

  Steps to Reproduce

  1. Set your browser’s primary language to Portuguese (Brazil).
  2. Run:

  import streamlit as st
  from datetime import date

  st.date_input("Data", value=date.today(), format="DD/MM/YYYY")

  3. Open the date picker popup and observe that month/day names and labels are in English.

  Expected Behavior

  - Calendar UI strings (month/day names and labels like “Today”) should be localized based on the client/browser locale, or
  - A public parameter should allow explicitly setting the widget locale (e.g., st.date_input(..., locale="pt-BR")).

  Actual Behavior

  - Only the date format changes. Calendar UI strings remain in English.
  - No locale parameter exists for st.date_input.

  Environment

  - Streamlit: latest
  - Python: 3.12
  - Browser/OS: Chrome on Windows (also reproducible elsewhere)

  Request
  Please add localization support for the calendar UI in st.date_input, either by automatically respecting the client locale or by
  exposing an explicit locale parameter (e.g., locale="pt-BR").

title: Support for Multiple Named Custom Themes
text:
Issue #12702: Support for Multiple Named Custom Themes
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:theming

### Problem

Currently, Streamlit allows us to define only **one** custom theme in the .streamlit/config.toml file. While this is a great feature, it feels limiting. Much like developers/users who enjoy switching between light and dark modes in their IDEs/browsers, I often want to change the look and feel of my app based on different contexts, events, or even personal mood. 

### Solution

```toml
# .streamlit/config.toml

[theme]
base = "corporate-light" # Default active theme key

# Define the "Corporate Light" theme
[theme.corporate-light]
name = "Corporate Light" # A friendly name, cannot use default theme 'dark' or 'light'
primaryColor = "#1e3a8a"
backgroundColor = "#ffffff"
secondaryBackgroundColor = "#f0f0f0"
textColor = "#31333F"
font = "sans serif"

# Define a "Midnight Dark" theme
[theme.midnight-dark]
name = "Midnight Dark"
primaryColor = "#bfdbfe"
backgroundColor = "#1e293b"
secondaryBackgroundColor = "#334155"
textColor = "#f1f5f9"
font = "sans serif"
```

title: `ValueError: Paths don't have the same drive`
text:
[NONE] Hi! Triaging older bugs this week — I think this one has shipped and can be closed.

The traceback you posted points at `event_based_path_watcher.py` lines 402 and 452, where `os.path.commonpath([path, abs_changed_path]) == path` raised `ValueError: Paths don't have the same drive` on Windows when an event referred to a file on a different drive than a watched directory.

That call site is now wrapped in `try/except ValueError` on `develop` and the different-drive case just continues the loop — see [`lib/streamlit/watcher/event_based_path_watcher.py:454-468`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/watcher/event_based_path_watcher.py#L454-L468). The fix landed in [#12741](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12741) (commit `a8e49a83d`, "Fix file watcher issue with common path check") on 2025-10-15, after this issue was filed.

If you can update past the release containing #12741 (1.50.x line and later) and still see the same `ValueError` traceback, please share the new full traceback (with the post-fix line numbers) — the protection is specifically for the `commonpath` ValueError, so any remaining occurrence would point at a different code path and would be worth tracking separately.

Otherwise this should be safe to close. Thanks!

(Disclosure: I drafted this comment with help from Claude Code while triaging stale issues; the references above were verified manually against the current `develop` branch.)

### Summary

Default st.dataframe() beheviour is only displaying 4 decimals, and then you have to double click on the cell to actual see if it has more decimals to it. 
The pandas dataframe is rounded and might show inaccurate number depending on your desires.
What I've found in my situation is that I want the actual precison as if I viewed the data in a speadsheet.

### Why?

I desired in many cases to have full decimal presion when showing number in a st.dataframe()

### How?

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

def show_dataframe_with_full_decimal_presion(df):
    column_config = {
        col: st.column_config.NumberColumn(col, format="%f")
        for col in df.select_dtypes(include="number").columns
    }
    st.data_editor(df, column_config=column_config)

# Sample DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "item": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
    "value": [123.456, 78.1234567, 45.1, 12.0],
    "otherValue": [1.22323123123, 3.456789, 7.0, 0.0001234],
    "role": ["x", "z", "k", "j"]
})


# show with defaul streamlit behavior

st.header("default dataframe limited to 4 deimals")
st.dataframe(df)

st.header("full presision")
show_dataframe_with_full_decimal_presion(df)
```

### Additional Context

It could be awesome to have a option:
st.dataframe(myDf, full_decimal_precision=true) 

Its the equvilient of displaying a regular pandas dataframe in st.dataframe() and then press the "3 dots" near the column header, choosing "format" and choosing "plain"

title: Prevent updates of disabled inputs in `AppTest`
text:
Issue #12844: Prevent updates of disabled inputs in `AppTest`
Labels: type:enhancement, papercut, feature:app-testing

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It would be great, if `AppTest` would check whether an element is disabled before updating its value. Trying to do so should lead to an error or at least a warning.

### Why?

When running AppTests I sometimes stumble upon cases, where the tests work even when they shouldn't ... just for me to find out, that again I changed values of disabled elements within the tests and `AppTest` happily does that.

Having at least a warning would make it easier to find those quirks in the tests.

### How?

Nothing needs to change in the interface.

For convenience and backward compatibility it would be possible to include a flag in `AppTest` to configure the behavior, e.g. `at = AppTest('test_main.py', default_timeout=30, on_update_disabled_element='warning')`
with the possible values:
- `accept`: take the new value without complaint (default, current behavior)
- `warning`: take the new value and issue a warning
- `error`: raise an error when trying to update a disabled element

### Additional Context

Below you can find a short example to illustrate the problem: currently the test succeeds even though changing the value would not be possible in the app itself.

To run the example
- save the code as `test_main.py`
- run `pytest`

title: Prevent updates of disabled inputs in `AppTest`
text:
To run the example
- save the code as `test_main.py`
- run `pytest`

```python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

st.text_input('Text', value='initial value', disabled=True, key='k_text')


def test_disabled_input():
    at = AppTest('test_main.py', default_timeout=30)
    at.run()

    at.text_input(key='k_text').set_value('new value')
    at.run()

    assert at.text_input(key='k_text').value == 'new value'
```

# Summary
The site randomly shows "0" for images inserted via st.image() and MediaFileManager logs "Missing file".

## More information
I have a couple of jpg images embedded with st.image() and randomly they will not render, instead there will just be a 0 shown instead. Reloading the page or rerunning the code fixes the problem. When I reload the page often enough one ore several of the images will break again and just show a 0.

    MediaFileManager: Missing file d8a7ff62725a8ab1609c9335ba2e85375f491027d91b3badb27a6ccd

# Steps to reproduce
Run this code (ideally with --log_level error):

```python
import streamlit as st
if st.checkbox('checkbox'):
    st.image("foo.jpg")
```

Toggle that checkbox repeatedly (this method is quicker than reloading the page) and look at the console output. Maybe rerun the code once in a while. (Of course you need to put any jpg image named "foo.jpg" in the same folder).

## Actual behaviour
Sooner or later (5-50 clicks) the image will *not* be shown. Instead, in its place a 0 appears. A "MediaFileManager: Missing file" error is shown in the terminal.

## Expected behaviour
Images should always be shown.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Hi [USER] !

It will be really difficult to debug without being able to run the code, so if you are able to share your code (or better, provide a toy example that illustrates the problem simply, that would make life a lot easier.

Here are a couple thoughts that might help us solve the problem.

The MediaFileManager manages all the media in memory. At the end of the script run, all media that was not used in that run, is deleted (to conserve memory). Based on this, we should ensure everything working though I’m curious with race cases (for example, is this an issue with multiple people requesting the website, perhaps that causes a problem)? Does this occur standalone when one user interacts with it?

MatPlotlib is unfortunately not thread safe. So, one should not use st.pyplot with no figure. Even more protection is needed and matplotlib offers a locking mechanism, In another application, I wrote:

```python
import matplotlib
from matplotlib.figure import Figure

matplotlib.use("agg")

_lock = RendererAgg.lock

# ...code...

with _lock:
    fig = Figure()
    ax = fig.subplots()
    # ...perform work on ax
    st.pyplot(fig)
```

You can see it in action here: https://github.com/kmcgrady/book_reco/blob/master/books.py#L16

Hopefully that helps with a solution. If not and you can provide a simple example that causes the problem, please let me know.

title: Images sometimes do not appear
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Hey [USER] Just want to follow up. I spent some time today investigating it. I am reasonably confident on the problem and can reproduce it. In essence: * One specific process is running Streamlit and images (from pyplot in this case) are generated and stored in memory for that process. * Streamlit Share has multiple processes and a system designed to have messages/requests target the same process to grab the correct custom generated image/video/media. * That process fails when making image (and probably other media) requests. It's targeting any process, and if it targets the wrong one, the image will not be found. This is why you see some requests work and some don't (that may seem random). I had trouble by uploading the same code to my personal Streamlit share because there was no problem. That is because my service is only one process. When a process gets too much attention (as in your case when we marketed it for Streamlit Share), we add more resources to it and now we have multiple processes causing the issue. I was able to demonstrate this on my system by upping the number of processes. title: Images sometimes do not appear
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] I see numerous more cases of this issue happening in this thread. To be clear, here's what goes on below the hood:

* images are loaded and stored in memory per script run.
* images are only removed when the latest script run does not use images from the _previous_ script run.

With that in mind, this leads to some important outcomes.
* If you have your streamlit app running with replicas behind a load balancer, _you will see issues_. The image is stored in the memory of the app where the script ran and is connected. If your request for the image is received with a different replica, it will not respond. The best solution is to enable some sort of sticky routing. We have some thoughts on this, but it's going to be a longer time to a solution.
* If you are assuming that images are being received past the script run will be generated, this may present a problem. I imagine this less a use case.

Outside of above, if you have a simple code example/repro steps to demonstrate the issue. It would be very helpful.
