title: Launch by module - redux!
text:
Issue #12972: Launch by module - redux!
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:cli

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Instead of requiring an actual python file to be passed into `streamlit run`, it would be nice to use a python package location instead

### Why?

We use pants, and a launch by module feature would make our lives much better.

I would want to do the following in pants, where I do not have access to the final file path of the built module)

```python
pex_binary(
    name="streamlit_dash",
    entry_point="streamlit",
    dependencies=[
        "3rdparty/python#streamlit",
        "//my/dash:module",
    ],
    include_tools=True,
    # If I knew the final resolved path here I could use that, but I don't!
    # But I do know the module!
    args=["run", "my.dash.module"],
)
```

### How?

If a module was passed in, it could be converted to a file with the following:

```python
import importlib

module_file = importlib.import_module(module_name).__file__
```

In fact, I am currently using the following shim to make this work, but it's a little bit hacky:

```python
"""Shim so we can launch streamlit by module instead of by file.

This plays much better with pants pex binaries.
"""

import importlib
import sys

import streamlit.web.cli

if len(sys.argv) < 2:
    raise ValueError("No module specified to run.")
module_name = sys.argv[1]
module_file = importlib.import_module(module_name).__file__
sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", module_file] + sys.argv[2:]
sys.exit(streamlit.web.cli.main())
```

It could even be behind a flag if that was easier, e.g. `--module=<module>`

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

We added `st.App(...).run()`in Streamlit 1.59. This doesn't add direct support for modules in `streamlit run`, but can be used to enable execution of modules via `python -m myapp`.

This gives Streamlit apps an officially supported Python entry point, so launcher files can be run directly with:

```bash
python app.py
uv run app.py
```

It also works well with PEP 723 inline script dependencies, e.g. a launcher can declare `streamlit` and app-specific dependencies directly in the file and be run with `uv run app.py` without a separate environment setup step.

Example:

```python
import streamlit as st

app = st.App("streamlit_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

title: Support real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script
text:
Issue #12980: Support real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:runtime

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit requires rerunning the entire script to refresh visual elements such as charts or plots.
This feature request suggests adding native support for incremental or real-time updates to chart components, allowing smoother dashboards for live data without script reruns.

### Why?

I often build dashboards with data that changes every few seconds (e.g. IoT sensors, live logs, financial data).
The current rerun mechanism makes the app flicker and consume excessive CPU, as every update forces Streamlit to re-execute all widgets and scripts.
A lighter update mechanism would make Streamlit much more efficient for real-time applications.

### How?

Introduce a new method, for example:

chart = st.line_chart(initial_data)
chart.update(new_data)

or a context manager such as:

with st.chart("my_chart") as chart:
    chart.update(data)

This would allow partial UI updates for selected components instead of full script reruns, leading to faster refresh rates and better performance.

### Additional Context

This feature would be highly valuable for real-time dashboards and data streaming use cases.
Similar functionality exists in libraries like Plotly Dash (dcc.Interval) or Bokeh Server.
Discussion inspiration: Streamlit Community Forum – Real-time dashboard performance

[NONE] https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment

[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] as an update on this, in 1.63 we released a feature allowing targeted runs of fragments from callbacks, so you could now create a refresh button that will update only your charts without re-running the entire script. 

For example, 

```
import streamlit as st
st.title("Live sensor dashboard")
# Expensive setup outside the fragment — not re-executed on refresh.
conn = get_sensor_connection()
[USER].fragment(key="charts")
def charts():
    st.line_chart(conn.read_recent())
charts()
# The button lives outside the fragment; clicking it reruns only "charts".
st.button("Refresh charts", on_click=lambda: st.rerun("charts"))
```

I am wondering also if you have tried `run_every` with fragments to refresh only the charts on an interval?

```
[USER].fragment(run_every="2s")
def live_chart():
    st.line_chart(conn.read_recent())
live_chart()
```

I'm leaving this issue open since this is talking more about automatic updates based on data changes instead of user events. This is something we are also working on supporting -- curious to see how close `run_every` alone would meet your use case and whether there are gaps still.

title: Support real-time chart updates without rerunning the entire script
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] I am doing a gap analysis of your issue, and I believe this pattern is now covered by various shipped features and bug fixes (scroll to top). 

I made a demo app here: https://live-operator-demo.streamlit.app/

It also shows how to implement this pattern with code example for anyone interested in implementing an app like this. 

Polling updates that only re-run the charts:

```
import streamlit as st

# Expensive, one-time setup lives OUTSIDE the fragment, so it runs once and is
# not repeated on every refresh.
[USER].cache_resource
def get_connection():
    return connect_to_feed()

conn = get_connection()

# Anything in the main script body (title, filters, a text input) runs once and
# stays put while the tiles below refresh on their own.
st.text_input("Operator notes")

# Each tile reruns on its OWN timer — only the tile re-executes, not the script.
[USER].fragment(run_every="1s")
def price_tile(symbol):
    df = conn.read_recent(symbol)            # fetch latest for this tile
    st.metric(symbol, f"${df['price'].iloc[-1]:,.2f}")
    st.line_chart(df, x="time", y="price")

for col, sym in zip(st.columns(3), ["BTC-USD", "ETH-USD", "SOL-USD"]):
    with col:
        price_tile(sym)
```

I wanted to build this out to ensure there is no flickering or scrolls and I don't see any -- as mentioned above, I believe we have fixed some bugs that were likely affecting this for you. 

If anyone has any remaining gaps around this pattern, please comment here and tag me or create a new issue. 
I have also opened two new issues about more specific related aspect: a [freshness signal](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17141) and [server-driven updates](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17142).

title: Inconsistent margin above the first checkbox/toggle inside a horizontal container inside a column
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] thanks for reporting this, just want to suggest as a workaround, you could replace the columns with a horizontal + vertical containers. 

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a CSS styling bug related to checkbox/toggle margin handling inside nested layout containers. The issue occurs when checkboxes or toggles are placed inside a horizontal `st.container` that is itself inside an `st.column`. 

**Root Cause Analysis:** The bug originates in `frontend/lib/src/components/core/Block/styled-components.ts` (lines 166-171). When a column uses default vertical alignment (TOP), a CSS rule applies `marginTop: theme.spacing.sm` (0.5rem) to the first checkbox using the selector `& ${StyledElementContainer}:first-of-type > ${StyledCheckbox}`. However, when checkboxes are inside a horizontal container, the `:first-of-type` CSS selector only matches the first `StyledElementContainer` containing a checkbox within that container, causing only the first checkbox to receive the margin while others do not. This results in inconsistent vertical spacing between checkboxes in the same horizontal row.

### Related Issues

- **#10265** - Same author reported a very similar bug where the `:last-of-type` selector caused unexpected margins on the last checkbox. This is essentially the same underlying issue but manifesting differently with horizontal containers.

- **#12434** - Related alignment issue where padding on elements inside horizontal containers causes visual misalignment, showing a pattern of layout issues with horizontal containers.

- **#11207** - Related enhancement request for toggle widget layout control, indicating user needs around toggle/checkbox styling in containers.

---

title: Opening an `st.dialog` with a button shortcut highlights UI elements within the dialog
text: ### Expected Behavior Opening a dialog with a button shortcut should not cause visibly different behavior compared to opening it with a button click ### Current Behavior If the dialog does not contain a widget, or if it does contain a widget but the dialog has not yet been opened in the current session, using a shortcut to open the dialog will give the Close Dialog button the state Focus, drawing a red square around the button: If the dialog contains a widget, subsequent shortcut uses will give the widget the state Focus-visible. In that case, using the shortcut button doesn't introduce the Focus-visible state, although it does not clear it if the Focus-visible state was already introduced. A regular button click does clear it.

title: Opening an `st.dialog` with a button shortcut highlights UI elements within the dialog
Opening an `st.dialog` with a button shortcut highlights UI elements within the dialog
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This bug report describes an issue where opening an `st.dialog` via a button's keyboard shortcut (new `shortcut` parameter) causes UI elements inside the dialog to display unwanted focus states (`:focus-visible` styling). When the dialog is triggered via keyboard, the browser tracks keyboard navigation mode, and when focus is automatically moved inside the dialog (for accessibility), this causes visible focus rings on the close button or the first widget. This behavior differs from clicking the button with a mouse, which does not apply focus-visible styling. The root cause appears to be in how keyboard-initiated actions interact with the dialog's focus management. When a shortcut triggers the dialog, the browser's focus-visible heuristics persist the keyboard navigation state, causing the `:focus-visible` CSS selector to match elements inside the dialog. A potential fix would involve programmatically managing focus state or using techniques like `blur()` to reset focus-visible state when the dialog opens via keyboard shortcut. ### Related Issues - **#9243** - [Popover and dialog first widget is always active](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243): This is the most closely related issue, describing the same underlying behavior where the first widget inside `st.dialog` or `st.popover` appears active/focused by default. The new issue #13263 is a more specific manifestation triggered by keyboard shortcuts rather than general dialog opening. - **#12496** - [Improve focus state of tertiary button](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12496): Related issue about focus state styling on buttons, specifically the tertiary button's red focus border appearing too tight. Labels: type:bug, status:needs-triage

- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.

### Summary

When using the newly introduced option to provide a callable as data argument, the callable runs without ScriptRunContext.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# app.py
import csv
import io

import streamlit as st


def to_csv() -> str:
    foo = st.session_state.get("foo", "nope")
    print(foo)
    buffer = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(buffer)
    writer.writerow([foo])
    buffer.seek(0)
    return buffer.getvalue()


st.download_button(
    label="Download",
    data=to_csv,
    file_name="foo.csv",
    mime="text/csv",
)

st.session_state["foo"] = "bar"
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Click the button

Raises Thread 'asyncio_0': missing ScriptRunContext! This warning can be ignored when running in bare mode.

### Expected Behavior

When called from the download_button, the function `to_csv` should have context, and see the currenct `session_state`.

### Current Behavior

Warning

```
Thread 'asyncio_0': missing ScriptRunContext! This warning can be ignored when running in bare mode.
```

[NONE] Somehow I missed this issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13337
Closing as duplicate

[NONE] Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `[USER].cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. Both just look like they worked.

Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `[USER].cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. We only found the mechanism by tracing the full call graph of the callable, not just inspecting it — a lambda that looks pure can still be unsafe if anything it calls touches cached/session state indirectly.

We ended up moving off lazy `data=` entirely (eager bytes, pre-warmed at save time) because we couldn't make the callable's dependency tree provably free of session/cache reads. For anyone hitting this: if your callable calls anything that isn't a pure function of its arguments, the missing context isn't just a perf/warning issue, it's a correctness one.

text:
Issue #13600: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
Labels: type:enhancement, area:server

Starting with **Streamlit 1.53**, we're introducing experimental support for running Streamlit with [Starlette](https://www.starlette.io/) as the underlying web framework. This is the first step toward our long-term goal of **fully migrating from Tornado to Starlette/ASGI**, and we need your help to identify any issues or gaps before the full transition.

## What's New

> **Note:** To use the experimental Starlette features, you need to install the optional dependencies:
>
> ```bash
> pip install streamlit[starlette]
> ```

### 1. Starlette Server Mode (Experimental)

You can now run Streamlit using Starlette instead of Tornado by setting a config option:

```toml
# .streamlit/config.toml
[server]
useStarlette = true
```

Or via command line:

```bash
streamlit run app.py --server.useStarlette=true
```

### 2. ASGI App Entry Point (Experimental)

For advanced use cases, you can now create an ASGI-compatible Streamlit application using the new `App` class:

```python
from streamlit.starlette import App

app = App("main.py")
```

Run it with `streamlit run` (preferred):

```bash
streamlit run myapp.py
```

Streamlit will automatically detect the `App` instance and run it in Starlette mode. Alternatively, you can use any ASGI server directly:

```bash
uvicorn myapp:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8501
```

The `App` class supports advanced configuration including:

title: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
text:
Streamlit will automatically detect the `App` instance and run it in Starlette mode. Alternatively, you can use any ASGI server directly: ```bash uvicorn myapp:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8501 ``` The `App` class supports advanced configuration including: - **Custom HTTP routes** — Add REST API endpoints alongside your Streamlit app - **Middleware** — Add security headers, authentication, logging, etc. - **Lifespan hooks** — Run code on startup/shutdown (e.g., pre-warm caches, initialize resources) - **Framework integration** — Mount Streamlit inside FastAPI, Django, or other ASGI frameworks > 📖 For more details on the `App` interface and its full capabilities, see the [specification in PR #13449](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/13449).
Example: Adding custom routes ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.routing import Route from starlette.responses import JSONResponse async def health_check(request): return JSONResponse({"status": "healthy", "service": "streamlit-app"}) async def get_data(request): return JSONResponse({"items": ["apple", "banana", "cherry"], "count": 3}) app = App( "main.py", routes=[ Route("/api/health", health_check), Route("/api/data", get_data), ], ) ```
Example: Adding custom middleware ```python from streamlit.starlette import App from starlette.middleware import Middleware from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware): async def dispatch(self, request, call_next): response = await call_next(request) response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff" response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "SAMEORIGIN" return response app = App( "main.py", middleware=[Middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)], ) ```
Example: Mounting FastAPI in Streamlit

title: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
text:
Example: Mounting FastAPI in Streamlit ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from starlette.routing import Mount from streamlit.starlette import App # Create FastAPI sub-application api = FastAPI() [USER].get("/health") async def health(): return {"status": "healthy"} [USER].post("/predict") async def predict(data: dict): return {"prediction": data.get("value", 0) * 2} # Mount FastAPI into Streamlit app # - Streamlit UI at / # - FastAPI endpoints at /api/* # - FastAPI docs at /api/docs app = App( "dashboard.py", routes=[Mount("/api", app=api)], ) ```
Example: Mounting Streamlit in FastAPI ```python from fastapi import FastAPI from streamlit.starlette import App # Create the Streamlit sub-application streamlit_app = App("dashboard.py") # Create FastAPI with Streamlit's lifespan to manage the runtime lifecycle api = FastAPI(lifespan=streamlit_app.lifespan()) [USER].get("/api/data") async def get_data(): return {"data": [1, 2, 3]} # Mount Streamlit under /dashboard api.mount("/dashboard", streamlit_app) # Run with: uvicorn myapp:api ```
Example: Lifespan hooks for startup/shutdown ```python from contextlib import asynccontextmanager from streamlit.starlette import App [USER] async def lifespan(app): # Startup: runs before accepting connections print("🚀 Starting up...") model = load_ml_model() # Pre-warm caches db = init_db_connection() # Yield state accessible via app.state yield {"model": model, "db": db} # Shutdown: cleanup resources print("👋 Shutting down...") db.close() app = App("main.py", lifespan=lifespan) ```
## Why We're Migrating to Starlette/ASGI The migration to Starlette/ASGI will unlock numerous frequently-requested features: ### Custom HTTP Endpoints - #439 - #9673 - #6195 - #9090 - #11333 - #8713 ### Security Headers & Middleware - #6417 - #9160 - #861 - #8823 ### Framework Integration & ASGI Support

This looks a bit more like an issue in our component v2 scanner, not necessary related to Starlette cc [USER] <details> <summary>Claude analysis on this issue</summary> # Summary This is a **bug in the components v2 `manifest_scanner.py`**, not specifically Starlette's fault. ## The Issue Looking at `lib/streamlit/components/v2/manifest_scanner.py:191`: ```python def _is_likely_streamlit_component_package( dist: importlib.metadata.Distribution, ) -> bool: # ... name = dist.name.lower() # <-- BUG: dist.name can be None ``` The dist.name attribute from importlib.metadata.Distribution can be None in edge cases: - Corrupted or malformed package metadata - Certain editable installs - Packages installed in unusual ways When dist.name is None, calling .lower() on it throws: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'lower' Why Starlette Triggers It Starlette itself isn't the problem, but it likely: 1. Has a dependency installed in a way that produces a distribution with None name 2. Or one of its transitive dependencies has malformed metadata The scan iterates over all installed distributions via importlib.metadata.distributions(), so any broken package in the environment can trigger this. The Fix The code should guard against None before calling .lower(). A simple fix would be: ```python def _is_likely_streamlit_component_package( dist: importlib.metadata.Distribution, ) -> bool: # Skip distributions without a name if dist.name is None: return False name = dist.name.lower() # ... ``` There are also other places in the file that use dist.name (lines 238, 510) that should be similarly guarded, though they're

text: [NONE] Hi [USER] This feature looks promising, and I'm excited to see the progress being made! However after upgrading Streamlit to v1.57.0, I encountered an issue with my Streamlit setup under bazel. Bazel replicates the directory structure during the build process by creating a real folder tree but symlinking every individual file to its actual location in the cache to save disk space. This behavior applies to the static frontend files bundled with the Streamlit library. Here is an example of the directory structure generated by Bazel: ```bash # The 'static' folder is real, but files inside are symlinks $ ll ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/ Permissions Size Date Modified Name ... lrwxr-xr-x@ - 21 Apr 15:39 file_util.py -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/file_util.py drwxr-xr-x@ - 21 Apr 15:39 static $ ll ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/ Permissions Size Date Modified Name lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 favicon.png -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/favicon.png lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 index.html -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/index.html lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 manifest.json -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/manifest.json drwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 static ``` ## The Problem The Starlette router used for serving Streamlit’s static files returns a 404 error because the default configuration for Starlette’s `StaticFiles` does not follow symlinks. Since the actual files reside outside the perceived "root" directory in the Bazel sandbox, Starlette blocks access to them for security reasons. ## Proposed Solutions After looking into the codebase, I believe there are two viable options to resolve this. (Details at the bottom.) ### 1. Set `follow_symlink = True` for `_StreamlitStaticFiles` `_StreamlitStaticFiles` inherits from `starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles`.

title: [Request for feedback] Starlette/ASGI Support in Streamlit
text: ## Proposed Solutions After looking into the codebase, I believe there are two viable options to resolve this. (Details at the bottom.) ### 1. Set `follow_symlink = True` for `_StreamlitStaticFiles` `_StreamlitStaticFiles` inherits from `starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles`. We can explicitly set the `follow_symlink` parameter to `True` in the constructor. Location: ```python # Proposed change super().__init__(directory=directory, html=True, follow_symlink=True) ``` This may have security implications as it allows serving files outside of the specified directory if there are symlinks pointing to them. However, since the static files are bundled with the Streamlit library and nothing else, this should not be a concern in this case. ### 2. Resolve the Static Files Path in `get_static_dir()` Streamlit's static directory path is determined by `get_static_dir()` function which is calculated relative to `file_util.py` location. Since `file_util.py` is also a symlink in the Bazel environment, we can resolve the physical path using `os.path.realpath` before passing it to the handler. Location: ```python def get_static_dir() -> str: """Get the folder where static HTML/JS/CSS files live.""" dirname = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)) # `realpath` instead of `normpath` return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dirname, "static")) ``` Note: The result of this function is passed to `create_streamlit_static_handler` as `directory=`. I understand that Bazel support might not be a primary focus for the project, but addressing this would significantly improve compatibility for users in monorepo and containerized environments. ### Summary

A streamlit log handler to allow using Streamlit to show logs.

### Why?

Python's built-in logging framework is extremely versatile. Hooking into that would make debugging easier.

In my own app, I have observations I both want to save to a log system and show to the user. Having a streamlit log handler allows me to do that without duplicating code.

### How?

I have written something that I use in my own project that can be used as a starting place:

title: Streamlit log handler
Streamlit log handler
text:
The "log_containter" in st.session_state allows you to specify where the logs should be shown. The obvious use case is a collapsed expander that can be opened to see what logs there are. It is not the most transparent way of doing it, and it risks them not being shown (if it is set on on page, and the page is then changed).

You can set the object to show by e.g. `logger.error("Example error log message", extra={"object": object_to_log})`

You can set where you want the text to link to by e.g `logger.error("Example error log message.",extra={"link": "#" + self.name})`. This allows you to link in the same page (used as shown) or another page. You could also make the log message into a markdown text with the link, but you typically don't want that in other log systems, so doing that would make the logging less versatile.

This is just a suggestion, it works for my app, but I am sure many improvements can be done. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

[CONTRIBUTOR] I [USER] picking up this issue
[USER] 

[CONTRIBUTOR] This bug occurs when `st.date_input` is the first widget inside an `st.popover` or `st.dialog`. When the popover/dialog opens, it auto-focuses on the first focusable element (the date input field). The BaseWeb Datepicker component used by `st.date_input` is designed to open its calendar dropdown when the input receives focus, which creates the unintended UX of the calendar immediately appearing when the popover opens. This contrasts with `st.selectbox` which only opens on click, not focus.

**Root cause**: The combination of two behaviors: (1) popover/dialog auto-focus on first widget, and (2) BaseWeb Datepicker opening on focus. A fix could either modify the autofocus behavior in popover/dialog, or prevent `st.date_input` from opening on programmatic/initial focus (only on user click).

### Related Issues

- **#9243** - [Don't autofocus first element in `st.popover` and `st.dialog`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243): This is the parent issue that #13633 is directly related to. The current bug is a specific manifestation where the autofocus on `st.date_input` causes its dropdown to automatically open.

- **#8284** - [`st.popover` not closing when opening another PopOver](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8284): Related popover/dropdown interaction bug where dropdown-containing widgets inside popovers cause UI state issues.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a confirmed bug related to the auto-focus behavior in `st.popover` and `st.dialog` containers. When a popover/dialog opens, it auto-focuses the first focusable widget inside it. For `st.date_input`, this focus event triggers the calendar dropdown to open automatically, creating a confusing UX. The root cause is in the BaseWeb Popover component's default `autoFocus` behavior combined with the BaseWeb Datepicker's behavior of opening its calendar when receiving focus. The fix likely involves either disabling auto-focus on the popover/dialog containers or preventing the date picker from opening on focus.

### Related Issues

- **#9243** This is the parent issue that discusses the general auto-focus behavior. The current issue is a specific symptom where the auto-focus causes the date input dropdown to open, which is more problematic than just visual focus.

title: Form "Enter" (or shortcut) does not send updated focused input field
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This bug report describes a regression where pressing Enter to submit a form does not include the updated value from the currently-focused `st.number_input` field. The user must either click the submit button, press Enter twice, or click outside the input before pressing Enter. **Potential Root Cause:** The issue likely stems from a race condition in the form submission timing. When Enter is pressed in `NumberInput.tsx`, the `handleKeyPress` handler calls `commitValue()` (which schedules a React effect to update the widget state manager) and then immediately calls `widgetMgr.submitForm()` synchronously. Since the widget state update happens asynchronously in a `useEffect` (via `useBasicWidgetState` hook), the form submission may copy widget states before the number input's new value has been propagated to the form's pending changes. This timing issue may have been introduced or exacerbated by PR #10018 (commit d25aef32) which changed trigger events to be scheduled at the end of the event loop for batching purposes. ### Related Issues 1. **#9761 - [Allow st.form enter_to_submit to work for non-text elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9761)**: Directly related enhancement request noting that `enter_to_submit` behavior only works for text inputs, not for `st.number_input`, `st.radio`, or `st.dataframe` selections. 2. **#11087 - [st.form, pressing 'Enter' keyboard button should auto focus to next input field](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11087)**: Related to Enter key behavior within forms - requests improved Enter key navigation between form fields. 3. **#10959 - [time_input does not keep the entered value when tabbing out of it](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10959)**: Similar focus/value-commit issue where tabbing out of `st.time_input` resets the value instead of committing it, pointing to

title: Back button doesn't work with elements synced with query params
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Marking as enhancement since this is currently expected. We'll figure out whether we want to change this behavior with the upcoming `bind` parameter, and maybe also for `st.query_params`. 

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a request for browser back/forward to restore widgets that are manually synced with `st.query_params`. Assigning query params uses `pushState` (`handlePageInfoChanged` in `App.tsx`), so the URL and history stack do change, but `onHistoryChange` is built around page navigation. On the same page it either does not produce a useful rerun, or it reruns with `getQueryString()` reading stale React `queryParams` instead of `document.location.search`. Even a correct rerun would not restore the slider here, because the keyed widget value in `st.session_state` is only initialized from the URL once. Maintainers already marked this as expected and want to revisit it with `bind="query-params"` (which currently uses `replaceState`, so it does not create history entries either).

### Related Issues

- [#13963](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13963): Same-page back/forward with `st.navigation` does rerun, but `st.query_params` stays stale. That report explicitly calls out this single-page case and traces the stale values to `getQueryString()` preferring React state over the restored URL.
- [#9279](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9279) (closed): Cross-page back navigation dropped query params on the first rerun. Cited by the reporter; fixed in PR #13129 via `preserveQueryParams`, which did not cover same-page query-param history.
- [#9325](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9325): Original request to bind widget/`session_state` values to query params. Relevant because restoring widgets from history is part of that binding/bookmarkability design, not just a one-off `popstate` fix.

title: `AppTest` fails to resolve imports when using a src layout
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-13909)


[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a bug in how `AppTest` (and the underlying `ScriptRunner`) sets up `sys.path` when executing scripts. The root cause is in `modified_sys_path` (`lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/exec_code.py`), which is intended to prepend the script's **directory** to `sys.path` during execution. However, it receives and inserts the full **file path** (e.g., `/project/src/myapp/app.py`) instead of the parent directory (`/project/src/myapp/`). Since Python expects directories in `sys.path`, this has no effect on import resolution. In a flat layout, this bug is masked because the CWD (already in `sys.path`) typically matches the script's directory. In a src layout, the script lives in a subdirectory (e.g., `src/myapp/`) that is not the CWD, so sibling module imports fail with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

The fix would involve changing `modified_sys_path` to use `os.path.dirname(main_script_path)` instead of the raw file path, or having `AppTest` explicitly add the script's parent directory to `sys.path`.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8154 — `AppTest` doesn't work with relative filenames in `st.sidebar.page_link()`. Related because it also involves path resolution issues within the `AppTest` framework.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8429 — Unable to test a multipage app with custom sidebar using `AppTest`. Related because the test runner cannot resolve page paths correctly, which is another manifestation of path handling issues in `AppTest`.

title: Add anchors=False parameter to st.markdown()
text:
Issue #13913: Add anchors=False parameter to st.markdown()
Labels: type:enhancement, papercut, feature:markdown

### Summary

Add an `anchors=False` parameter to `st.markdown()` to disable automatic anchor links on headers within markdown content. Currently, `st.header()` and `st.subheader()` support `anchor=False`, but there's no way to disable anchors for headers (h1-h6) rendered via `st.markdown()`.

### Why?

When using markdown headers (`###`, `####`, etc.) for styling purposes (e.g., to get larger text) rather than for navigation, the auto-generated anchor links can be confusing for users. The current workarounds are:
- Use raw HTML instead of markdown headers
- Only use `st.header()`/`st.subheader()` which support `anchor=False`, but these don't cover h4-h6

### How?

Introduce a new parameter to `st.markdown()`:

```python
st.markdown("### My heading", anchors=False)
```

This would disable anchor links for all headers in that markdown block.

### Additional Context

This came from an internal discussion. The existing `anchor=False` on `st.header()` and `st.subheader()` is great, but extending this to `st.markdown()` would provide a complete solution for users who want styled text without navigation anchors.

```Python
    st.Page(page, title="Query Params", default=True),
    st.Page(lambda: None, title="Other Page", url_path="other"),
]).run()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: Back button changes URL query params but not `st.query_params` until user leaves page and comes back
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a bug where browser back/forward navigation on the **same page** sends stale query parameters to the server, causing `st.query_params` to reflect the wrong values. The root cause is in the frontend `onHistoryChange` handler in `App.tsx`. When the browser's `popstate` event fires, the browser URL updates correctly, but `App.getQueryString()` reads from `this.state.queryParams` (which still holds the last server-set value) rather than from `document.location.search`. The `onHistoryChange` handler calls `onPageChange` with `preserveQueryParams=true` but does not pass the actual URL query string, so the stale state value is sent to the server in the rerun `BackMsg`. This issue was partially addressed in PR #13129 (which fixed cross-page back navigation for #9279), but the same-page case was not covered. A potential fix would be to have `onHistoryChange` explicitly read and pass `document.location.search` as the `queryString` parameter to `onPageChange`, ensuring the actual browser URL query string is sent to the server instead of the stale React state. ### Related Issues - **#13853** - [Back button doesn't work with elements synced with query params](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13853): Very closely related — reports that browser back button doesn't trigger a rerun for single-page apps using `st.query_params`. title: WebSocket fails behind Istio VirtualService despite websocketUpgrade: true, causing localhost requests to stall even with normal CPU/memory usage
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This issue reports that Streamlit's WebSocket connection (`/_stcore/stream`) fails when deployed behind an Istio VirtualService with `websocketUpgrade: true`, causing the browser to fall back to HTTP polling. Additionally, the user reports that even localhost requests from within the same pod become extremely slow despite normal CPU/memory usage. **Root cause analysis:** Streamlit relies on a WebSocket connection at the `_stcore/stream` endpoint for all client-server communication. When deployed behind a reverse proxy with a path prefix (e.g., `/prefix/path`), the frontend constructs the WebSocket URI based on `window.location` via `getPossibleBaseUris()` (in `frontend/connection/src/utils.ts`). If the proxy's path rewriting doesn't perfectly align with what Streamlit expects, the WebSocket upgrade request may be routed incorrectly or stripped of necessary headers by Istio's Envoy sidecar. This is a known category of issues with Streamlit behind reverse proxies — the `server.baseUrlPath` config, CORS settings (`server.enableCORS`), and XSRF protection (`server.enableXsrfProtection`) all play a role. The localhost stalling behavior is unusual and may stem from Tornado's event loop being blocked by repeated failed WebSocket upgrade attempts or the ping interval settings (default 30s with Tornado >= 6.5), which can interact poorly with proxy timeouts. The user should ensure `server.baseUrlPath` is configured to match their Istio prefix path, and may need to disable CORS/XSRF protection for their deployment. ### Related Issues - **#8188** — [Unnecessary failover on /_stcore/stream](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8188): Very closely related — reports Streamlit failing to establish WebSocket connections (`/_stcore/stream`) when deployed behind a reverse proxy (AWS ALB), with the app hanging at skeleton elements. title: "Missing Submit Button" error displayed while a form is loading
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a valid bug in the `st.form` frontend component. During initial page load on slow connections, the "Missing Submit Button" error briefly flashes because the form renders before all its child elements (including the submit button) have been received from the backend. **Root cause:** The `Form` component in `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/Form/Form.tsx` checks whether to show the "Missing Submit Button" warning based on two conditions: (1) no submit button is registered in `formsData`, and (2) `scriptRunState === ScriptRunState.NOT_RUNNING`. The problem is that `NOT_RUNNING` is the **default initial state** (see `ScriptRunContext.tsx` line 70 and the commented-out `INITIAL` state in `ScriptRunState.ts` lines 18-21). On slow connections, there's a window where the form component renders with `NOT_RUNNING` before the script has actually started running — the frontend cannot distinguish "script hasn't started yet" from "script has finished." This causes the form to incorrectly conclude the script completed without a submit button, flashing the error until the script actually runs and delivers the submit button delta. ### Related Issues - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13002 — Request to disable sidebar rendering until page load is complete. Same class of problem: premature rendering of UI elements/errors before the backend script has finished executing. - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5798 — Request to optimize static file loading and reduce app startup time. Faster loading would reduce the window during which this flash occurs, though it wouldn't fix the root cause. - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11010 — Reports flickering and weird behavior during page load in multipage apps after upgrade. Related to the general theme of visual glitches during

title: Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present on OIDC logout with AWS cognito
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a bug in the OIDC logout flow when using AWS Cognito as the identity provider. The root cause is in `build_logout_url()` in [`lib/streamlit/auth_util.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/auth_util.py#L223-L226), which constructs the logout URL using the standard OIDC RP-Initiated Logout parameter name `post_logout_redirect_uri`. However, AWS Cognito's logout endpoint does **not** follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout specification — it expects the parameter to be named `redirect_uri` (or `logout_uri`) instead. When Streamlit sends `post_logout_redirect_uri`, Cognito rejects it with "Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present". The logout itself still succeeds server-side (cookies are cleared before the redirect), which is why pressing the browser back button shows the user as logged out. A potential fix would be to either detect Cognito-style endpoints and use the appropriate parameter name, or to allow users to configure custom logout parameters for non-standard providers. ### Related Issues - **#12144** ([st.logout() doesn't redirect to correct Cognito ESE](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12144)) — CLOSED. Very similar Cognito logout issue from v1.48.0 where `client_id` was missing from the logout URL. Fixed via revert in 1.48.1, but the underlying Cognito parameter naming incompatibility (`post_logout_redirect_uri` vs `redirect_uri`) was not addressed. - **#12169** ([Breaking Change: Streamlit 1.48 breaks st.logout()](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12169)) — CLOSED. Related regression where `post_logout_redirect_uri` caused errors with Auth0 as well, confirming that multiple providers have non-standard logout parameter expectations. - **#11703** ([Allow advanced customization of OIDC/OAuth2 parameters in st.login()](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11703)) — OPEN. Enhancement request for customizable OIDC parameters that could serve as a workaround for provider-specific logout parameter requirements. --- *This is an automated triage comment using `claude-4.6-opus-high-thinking`. Please verify

text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14601)


[CONTRIBUTOR] ## Reproduction Assessment: **CONFIRMED** (via code analysis)

This bug is confirmed real. I was unable to do a live reproduction (no Cognito user pool available), but the root cause is unambiguous from the source code.

### Root Cause

In [`lib/streamlit/auth_util.py:223-226`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/auth_util.py#L223-L226), `build_logout_url()` hardcodes the OIDC standard parameter name `post_logout_redirect_uri`:

```python
logout_params: dict[str, str] = {
    "client_id": client_id,
    "post_logout_redirect_uri": post_logout_redirect_uri,
}
```

AWS Cognito's logout endpoint does **not** follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout spec. It requires `redirect_uri` (or `logout_uri`), not `post_logout_redirect_uri`. It also ignores `id_token_hint`.

So Streamlit sends: `?client_id=...&post_logout_redirect_uri=...&id_token_hint=...`
But Cognito expects: `?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...`

This matches the exact error reported: *"Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present"*

### Why logout still works

The server-side logout (cookie clearing) happens **before** the redirect to the provider's logout endpoint. So the Streamlit session is invalidated regardless of whether the provider redirect succeeds — which is why pressing back shows the user as logged out.

### Scope

This likely affects any OIDC provider whose `end_session_endpoint` doesn't follow the RP-Initiated Logout spec parameter naming. Related: #12169 showed Auth0 had the same issue.

A potential fix would be to allow users to configure custom logout query parameters, or to detect non-standard providers and adjust the parameter name accordingly.

title: Required String parameter 'redirect_uri' is not present on OIDC logout with AWS cognito
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Hey! The diagnosis here seems right. Cognito's logout endpoint doesn't follow the OIDC RP-Initiated Logout spec and expects `redirect_uri` instead of `post_logout_redirect_uri`.

I put together a draft PR (#14868) that adds an optional `[auth.logout_params]` section to secrets.toml so you can override the default parameter names. For Cognito it'd look like:

```toml
[auth.logout_params]
redirect_uri_name = "redirect_uri"
include_id_token_hint = false
```

Still needs a more thorough review/approval but wanted to get it out there. Would love to know if the config shape makes sense for your use case.

title: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
text:
Issue #14622: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
Labels: type:bug, area:security, feature:cache, status:confirmed, priority:P3, area:backend

## Summary

Two distinct cache-key collision bugs exist in `lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py` that can cause `[USER].cache_data` and `[USER].cache_resource` to return stale or wrong data without any error.

---

## Bug 1 — Deterministic sampling seed enables adversarial hash collisions

**Affected code:** `_to_bytes()` in `hashing.py`, large-object sampling branches for Pandas Series/DataFrame, Polars Series/DataFrame, and NumPy arrays.

**Root cause:** When a data structure exceeds the sampling threshold (`_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE = 50_000` rows or `_NP_SIZE_LARGE = 500_000` elements), the code samples a smaller subset before hashing. The sampling seed is hardcoded:

```python
# Pandas
series_obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0)
df_obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0)

# Polars
obj.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, seed=0)

# NumPy
state = np.random.RandomState(0)
np_obj = state.choice(flat, size=_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE)
```

Because the seed is always `0`, the sampled row indices are globally fixed and known in advance. An adversary who knows which indices will be sampled can craft two structurally different inputs that produce the same hash by only modifying non-sampled positions.

**Minimal reproduction (NumPy):**

title: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
text:
**Minimal reproduction (NumPy):**

```python
import numpy as np, hashlib
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

_NP_SIZE_LARGE  = 500_000
_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE = 100_000

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

total = _NP_SIZE_LARGE + 10_000
arr_a = np.zeros(total, dtype=np.float64)
arr_b = arr_a.copy()

# Compute which indices are NOT sampled (fixed because seed=0)
sampled = np.random.RandomState(0).choice(np.arange(total), size=_NP_SAMPLE_SIZE)
mask = np.ones(total, dtype=bool)
mask[sampled] = False
arr_b[mask] = 255.0  # modify only non-sampled positions

print(get_hash(arr_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(arr_b))  # same hash — COLLISION
```

**Minimal reproduction (Pandas):**

```python
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, hashlib
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

_PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE  = 50_000
_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE = 10_000

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

n = _PANDAS_ROWS_LARGE + 5_000
df_a = pd.DataFrame({"val": np.zeros(n)})
df_b = df_a.copy()

sampled = df_a.sample(n=_PANDAS_SAMPLE_SIZE, random_state=0).index
all_idx = pd.Index(range(n))
non_sampled = all_idx.difference(sampled)
df_b.loc[non_sampled, "val"] = 99.0

print(get_hash(df_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(df_b))  # same hash — COLLISION
```

**Impact:** `[USER].cache_resource` is shared across all user sessions. An adversary who can send a request to the app can pre-compute a colliding payload and silently poison the cache, causing all subsequent users to receive the adversary's data instead of the real result — with no error raised.

---

## Bug 2 — PIL P-mode images: palette bytes omitted from hash

**Affected code:** PIL `Image.Image` branch in `_to_bytes()`.

title: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
text:
---

## Bug 2 — PIL P-mode images: palette bytes omitted from hash

**Affected code:** PIL `Image.Image` branch in `_to_bytes()`.

**Root cause:** For palette-indexed (`mode="P"`) PIL images, `tobytes()` returns only the palette index per pixel, not the actual color table. Two images with identical pixel indices but different color palettes produce identical hashes despite being visually distinct.

```python
# current code
np_array = np.frombuffer(pil_obj.tobytes(), dtype="uint8")
return self.to_bytes(np_array)
```

**Minimal reproduction:**

```python
from PIL import Image
import hashlib, numpy as np
from streamlit.runtime.caching.hashing import update_hash
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType

def get_hash(obj):
    h = hashlib.md5(usedforsecurity=False)
    update_hash(obj, h, CacheType.DATA)
    return h.hexdigest()

img_a = Image.new("P", (100, 100), 0)
img_b = Image.new("P", (100, 100), 0)

palette_a = [0] * 768
palette_b = [0] * 768
palette_a[0:3] = [0, 0, 0]    # index 0 → black
palette_b[0:3] = [255, 0, 0]  # index 0 → red

img_a.putpalette(palette_a)
img_b.putpalette(palette_b)

print(get_hash(img_a))  # same hash
print(get_hash(img_b))  # same hash — COLLISION, despite different colors
```

**Impact:** Two visually different images (e.g., a legitimate chart vs. a manipulated one) share the same cache key. The first cached result is returned for all subsequent inputs regardless of actual image content.

---

## Proposed Fix

A fix has been submitted as PR #14610. The approach:

title: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
text:
---

## Proposed Fix

A fix has been submitted as PR #14610. The approach:

1. **Sampling seed**: Derive the seed from the data (hash of first row / first 64 elements) so that sampled indices are content-dependent. Falls back to `seed=0` for unhashable payloads to preserve the existing pickle fallback path.
2. **PIL P-mode**: Prepend `getpalette()` bytes to `tobytes()` output before hashing.

---

## Environment

- Streamlit version: all versions with large-object sampling (introduced with the sampling optimization)
- Python: 3.10+
- OS: Linux / macOS / Windows (platform-independent)

title: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Both halves of this report are now fixed, so closing. This issue covered two distinct defects, which is why neither PR used a closing keyword — each only partially addressed it: **1. PIL P-mode palette omission** — fixed in #15397 (merged 2026-06-04, `fec0f584da`). `tobytes()` returns only palette indices, not the colour table, so two P-mode images with identical indices and different palettes hashed the same. The palette is now included in the hash. **2. Hash collision via the fixed sampling seed** — fixed in #16284 (merged just now, `a2414ead3f`), which adds the `runner.cacheHashSeed` config option. On the second one, worth being precise about what it does and does not do. Large pandas/polars/numpy objects are still hashed from a sample rather than in full, because hashing them completely is substantially slower — measured at roughly 37–47x for a 10M-element numpy array. So the seed does not eliminate collisions; it **relocates** them. It is an escape hatch for an app that has actually hit a collision, letting you move which positions are sampled so the two colliding objects stop mapping to the same key. If you need hashing to be exact rather than merely differently-sampled, the durable answer remains `hash_funcs`: ```python [USER].cache_data(hash_funcs={pd.DataFrame: lambda df: pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df).sum()}) def my_func(df): ... ``` That bypasses sampling entirely for the given type. The option accepts an integer from 0 to 4294967295. The default is `0`, which is exactly the value that was hard-coded before, so existing cache keys are unchanged by the upgrade. Anything unusable —

title: bug: [USER].cache_data hash collision via fixed sampling seed and PIL P-mode palette omission
text: sampling entirely for the given type. The option accepts an integer from 0 to 4294967295. The default is `0`, which is exactly the value that was hard-coded before, so existing cache keys are unchanged by the upgrade. Anything unusable — out of range, non-numeric, `true`, `inf` — is ignored with a logged warning and falls back to the default rather than raising from the hashing path. Note that changing the seed invalidates every existing cache entry for large objects, so it should be kept stable across restarts and across replicas if you use a shared or persisted cache.

[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14622)


[CONTRIBUTOR] ## Reproduction Results — All Three Bugs Confirmed

I reproduced all three reported hash collisions against the current `develop` branch (`lib/streamlit/runtime/caching/hashing.py`).

### Bug 1a — NumPy sampling collision (seed=0)

Two arrays with 510,000 elements that differ only at non-sampled positions produce identical hashes:

```text
arr_a hash: 68322062a574164a6eba20f0626e5e32
arr_b hash: 68322062a574164a6eba20f0626e5e32
COLLISION: True
```

### Bug 1b — Pandas DataFrame sampling collision (random_state=0)

Two DataFrames with 55,000 rows that differ only at non-sampled rows produce identical hashes:

```text
df_a hash: 30563bf8063974ed7b4a40da2b62f0e3
df_b hash: 30563bf8063974ed7b4a40da2b62f0e3
COLLISION: True
```

### Bug 2 — PIL P-mode palette omission

Two P-mode images with identical pixel indices but different color palettes (black vs red) produce identical hashes:

```text
img_a hash: ae16f3aab7562c60cedc051dd3a40c61
img_b hash: ae16f3aab7562c60cedc051dd3a40c61
```

Labels: type:enhancement, area:widgets

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I have a widget (e.g. `key="input"`) and a button to set an arbitrary value to my widget (e.g. `st.session_state["input"] = "arbitrary value"`). That works fine.

Now, if I add `bind="query-params"` to my widget, my button still updates the widget, but not the query param. If the user reloads the page, the new value is not persisted. 😢 And if my button sets the query param (`st.query_params["input"] = "arbitrary value"`), that raises a
> streamlit.errors.StreamlitAPIException: Cannot directly set query parameter 'input' - it is bound to a widget. Modify the widget value instead.

And the suggestion to "Modify the widget value instead" doesn't work; it doesn't update the widget. Anyway, I wouldn't want to pass `"arbitrary value"` to the widget's `value`/`default` as I would expect this to clear the query param from the URL, and the value would go back to `"default"` if the user reloads the page (the point of the query param is to persist).

Here is a simple example with `st.text_input()`, but this applies to all widgets with `bind="query-params"`.

title: Set state of a widget with `bind="query-params"`
text: Here is a simple example with `st.text_input()`, but this applies to all widgets with `bind="query-params"`. ```py import streamlit as st st.markdown("Edit the text input below, then try the buttons below.") with st.container(horizontal=True): if st.button('1. Set session state to "arbitrary value"'): st.session_state["input"] = "arbitrary value" if st.button('2. Reset session state to "default"'): st.session_state["input"] = "default" with st.container(horizontal=True): if st.button('3. Set query param to "arbitrary value"'): st.query_params["input"] = "arbitrary value" if st.button('4. Reset query param to "default"'): st.query_params["input"] = "default" st.text_input("Input", "default", key="input", bind="query-params") ``` ### Why? I have multiple widget+button pairs like that in my Streamlit app, and I have been syncing the session state and query params manually (which doesn't always work reliably). I was thrilled by the new `bind="query-params"` (THANK YOU!!! ❤️ ), but that is a blocker for me to adopt it. ### How? I imagine two solutions: 1. The widget could update the query param if the session state has changed since the last render. I think that would be ideal. 2. We could allow setting `st.query_params["input"] = "arbitrary value"`. I guess that should then automatically update the session state. ### Additional Context Real-world examples: 1. I have two buttons next to a `st.segmented_control()` to select and deselect all options. 2. I have a dice button next to a selectbox to select a random option.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Interesting discovery! If we force an update of the query params AFTER the `st.text_input()`, the `2. Reset session state to "default"` button works! 😲

Here's how:
```py

```
Or:
```py

```
But this does NOT work:
```py

```

I wouldn't consider this a solution, or even a satisfying workaround, since:
1. It only works to reset the default value, and not any other value, like the `1. Set session state to "arbitrary value"` button.
2. It's really not obvious, especially because we need to run `st.query_params.update()` AFTER the `st.text_input()`, and not when in the button's `on_click`.

But it hints at some code already partially handling this.

title: `st.switch_page` switching to a blank page
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This issue reports `st.switch_page` navigating to a blank page instead of the target page, with the URL not updating. The same author previously reported this in #14709, which was closed as cannot-reproduce. This new issue includes full reproducible code. **Root cause analysis:** The user's entrypoint (`project.py`) uses third-party components (`EncryptedCookieManager` from `streamlit_cookies_manager_ext` and `streamlit_js_eval`) that can call `st.stop()` or trigger `st.rerun()` **before** `st.navigation()` runs. Critically, the code checks `if "cookie_manager" not in st.session_state` but only ever sets `st.session_state["cookies"]` — so the key `"cookie_manager"` is never stored. This means a new `EncryptedCookieManager` is created on every rerun, and `cookies.ready()` likely returns `False` on the first render (since the component requires a browser round-trip), triggering `st.stop()` before `st.navigation()` executes. When `st.switch_page` triggers a rerun, `st.navigation()` never runs, so no navigation message is sent to the frontend, resulting in a blank page. This appears to be a **user code issue** (session state key mismatch) rather than a Streamlit framework bug. However, it does highlight a usability concern: when `st.stop()` is called before `st.navigation()` during a page-switch rerun, the result is a silent blank page with no error feedback. ### Related Issues - [#14709](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14709) — Same author, same problem (`st.switch_page` not working), closed as cannot-reproduce. This issue (#14732) is a re-filing with more detailed code. - [#9009](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9009) — `st.switch_page` does not function within a `try/except` block. Related pattern where execution flow control (`st.switch_page` uses a `RerunException` internally) conflicts with user code patterns. - [#10756](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10756) — Custom components unmount and reload on `switch_page`. Labels: type:bug, feature:st.dataframe, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.column_config, upstream

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A material icon in the `display_text` of a `LinkColumn` fails to render when the `width` is less than 4 times the length of the icon's name (e.g. `OPEN_IN_NEW` or `SIGNAL_CELLULAR_CONNECTED_NO_INTERNET_0_BAR`).

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-14782)

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

data_df = pd.DataFrame([["https://issues.streamlit.app"] * 6])

st.dataframe(
    data_df.style,
    width="content",
    column_config={
        "0": st.column_config.LinkColumn("22px", width=22, display_text="🔗"),
        "1": st.column_config.LinkColumn("44px", width=44, display_text=":material/open_in_new:"),
        "2": st.column_config.LinkColumn("43px", width=43, display_text=":material/open_in_new:"),
        "3": st.column_config.LinkColumn("172px", width=172, display_text=":material/signal_cellular_connected_no_internet_0_bar:"),
        "4": st.column_config.LinkColumn("171px", width=171, display_text=":material/signal_cellular_connected_no_internet_0_bar:"),
        "5": st.column_config.LinkColumn("small", width="small", display_text=":material/signal_cellular_connected_no_internet_0_bar:"),
    },
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Try the code above
2. Notice some columns show part of the name of the icon instead of the expected icon (`OPEN_IN_NEW` and `SIGNAL_CELLULAR_CONNECTED_NO_INTERNET_0_BAR`).

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the material icon to render even if it doesn't fit in the cell, as emojis do (see 🔗 in the first column).

title: `LinkColumn(width=..., display_text=":material/...` fails to render the icon when the width (in pixels) is less than 4 times the length of the icon's name (in characters)
text: ### Expected Behavior I would expect the material icon to render even if it doesn't fit in the cell, as emojis do (see 🔗 in the first column). Alternatively, I wouldn't mind if it raised an exception (with a clear message). I don't really need this to work. It's just that the current behavior wasn't obvious. I fell down the trap when I switched from `"🔗"` to `":material/open_in_new:"` while I had a `width=40`, and it wasn't obvious why that didn't work. ### Current Behavior ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.56.0 - Python version: 3.11.9 - Operating System: macOS - Browser: Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

title: `LinkColumn(width=..., display_text=":material/...` fails to render the icon when the width (in pixels) is less than 4 times the length of the icon's name (in characters)
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a bug in how material icons render in `LinkColumn` when the column width is too narrow. When `display_text=":material/open_in_new:"` is used, Streamlit extracts the icon name (`"open_in_new"`) and renders it using the "Material Symbols Rounded" font via ligatures on the glide-data-grid canvas ([`LinkColumn.ts`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DataFrame/columns/LinkColumn.ts#L73-L117)). The ligature mechanism requires the **full** text (e.g., `"open_in_new"`) to match and render as a single icon glyph. When the column width drops below ~44px, glide-data-grid's canvas text rendering truncates the display text to fit the cell, breaking the ligature match and causing the raw (partial) text to appear instead of the icon. Emojis like 🔗 are single Unicode characters, so they are not affected by text truncation in the same way. A potential fix could involve Streamlit overriding the column's minimum width when a material icon is used as `display_text`, or providing a custom cell renderer that prevents text truncation for icon-font cells. ### Related Issues - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9444 — **Re-calculate dataframe column width when a column is sorted**: Also involves column width interacting poorly with icon rendering (sort arrow overlapping header text). Both highlight that width calculations don't account for icon/symbol content. - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11794 — **Sort LinkColumn by display_text**: Related to `LinkColumn` + `display_text` behavior; while about sorting rather than rendering, it shares the same feature surface area. - https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10365 — **Inline code replaces / with _ sometimes**: Related to material icon shortcode parsing issues; both involve material icon syntax (`:material/...:`) not working as expected in certain contexts. --- *This is an automated triage

text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-14782)


[CONTRIBUTOR] I've been looking at this — material icons in `LinkColumn` break when the column is narrow. The root cause is glide's `truncateString` (`max = w / 4`) slicing the ligature string before `fillText`, which breaks font shaping. For example, `"open_in_new"` (11 chars) gets sliced at any width below 44px.

We can fix this on the Streamlit side by resolving icon names to their Unicode codepoints before passing them to glide (single char, never truncated). This involves creating a map which will increase our bundle size ~15-20kb. But I think this might be worth fixing in glide instead — either relaxing the heuristic for short strings, or adding an opt-in flag to use canvas clipping instead of string truncation. Both would be small patches and would help any glide consumer using icon fonts or ligatures.

What's your read [USER] — worth exploring a glide-side fix, or better to handle it in Streamlit?

[CONTRIBUTOR] Oh wow! Good catch! I didn't expect that to depend on the length of the icon's name. 😲 

I'll update the issue title and description so it's not specific to 44px.

For example, `display_text=":material/signal_cellular_connected_no_internet_0_bar:"` fails with `width=171` or `width="small"`, which should be plenty enough to render the icon. 😬

title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
text:
Issue #14917: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, area:frontend, feature:custom-components, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.dialog

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

### Summary

When a `[USER].dialog` is opened from a Streamlit custom component (e.g. via
`Streamlit.setComponentValue(...)` on user interaction) and then closed, the main content
area's scroll position — `section[data-testid="stMain"]` in the parent DOM — is reset. This
is a regression that was introduced in Streamlit 1.41.0 and was made strictly worse in
1.53.0.

### Bisect (using streamlit-pdf-viewer as the test vehicle)

| streamlit-pdf-viewer | Streamlit | Browser  | scrollTop 200 → | Verdict              |
|----------------------|-----------|----------|-----------------|----------------------|
| 0.0.25               | 1.40.2    | both     | 200             | ok                   |
| 0.0.25               | 1.47.0    | both     | 200             | ok *(reporter's env)*|
| 0.0.25               | **1.52.0**| firefox  | 200             | **ok**               |
| 0.0.25               | **1.53.0**| firefox  | 0               | **regression**       |
| 0.0.25               | 1.53.0    | chromium | 0               | regression           |
| 0.0.25               | 1.56.0    | both     | 0               | broken               |
| 0.0.26+              | 1.40.2    | both     | 200             | ok                   |
| **0.0.26+**          | **1.41.0**| firefox  | 0               | **regression**       |
| 0.0.26+              | 1.41.0    | chromium | ~174            | minor shift          |
| 0.0.26+              | 1.56.0    | firefox  | 0               | broken               |

title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
text:
Two distinct regressions are visible:

1. **1.40.2 → 1.41.0** — Firefox-only reset. Only triggers when the custom component's DOM
   has a `.scrolling-container` wrapper plus an absolutely-positioned sibling (a common shape
   for components with overlay controls). A minimal-DOM component escapes it.
2. **1.52.0 → 1.53.0** — reset on **both** browsers, regardless of DOM shape. Any custom
   component that triggers a rerun via `st.dialog` close hits this.

After 1.53.0, there is no version of the downstream component that avoids the bug.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit_pdf_viewer import pdf_viewer  # pip install streamlit-pdf-viewer==0.0.26


[USER].dialog("popup")
def show_popup():
    st.text("Close me and observe the page scroll reset.")


with open("resources/test.pdf", "rb") as f:
    content = f.read()

annotations = [
    {"page": 1, "x": 100, "y": 100, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "blue"},
    {"page": 1, "x": 150, "y": 120, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "green"},
    {"page": 2, "x": 180, "y": 130, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "purple"},
    {"page": 2, "x": 220, "y": 155, "height": 22, "width": 30, "color": "red"},
]

clicked = pdf_viewer(content, width=800, annotations=annotations)
if clicked:
    show_popup()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Steps:

1. Run the app on Streamlit 1.53.0+.
2. Scroll the main page down to bring page 2 annotations into view.
3. Click any annotation. A `st.dialog` opens.
4. Close the dialog (X button or Escape).
5. Observe the main content scrolls back to the top.

Same steps on Streamlit 1.40.2 preserve the scroll position.

### Expected Behavior

title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
text:
Same steps on Streamlit 1.40.2 preserve the scroll position.

### Expected Behavior

After the dialog closes, the main content area (`section[data-testid="stMain"]`) should
retain the scroll position it had when the dialog was opened. In our Playwright harness:
scroll before click = scroll after dialog close (delta ≈ 0). This is exactly what happens
on Streamlit ≤ 1.40.2 on both Chromium and Firefox.

### Current Behavior

On Streamlit ≥ 1.41.0 the scroll position is disturbed after the dialog closes:

- **1.41.0 – 1.52.x, Firefox, with a custom component whose DOM has a `.scrolling-container`
  wrapper + overlay controls** — `stMain.scrollTop` is reset to `0` (full jump to top).
- **1.41.0 – 1.52.x, Chromium** — `stMain.scrollTop` shifts by ~20–30 px (minor but
  consistently wrong direction).
- **1.41.0 – 1.52.x, Firefox, with a minimal-DOM custom component (e.g. streamlit-pdf-viewer
  v0.0.25)** — scroll is preserved; the bug does not manifest.
- **≥ 1.53.0, both browsers, any custom-component DOM shape** — `stMain.scrollTop` is reset
  to `0`. No version of the downstream component escapes it.

Numeric evidence (same harness, `scrollTop=200` before the click):

title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
text:
Numeric evidence (same harness, `scrollTop=200` before the click):

| Streamlit | Component DOM shape | Browser  | `stMain.scrollTop` after close |
|-----------|---------------------|----------|--------------------------------|
| 1.40.2    | any                 | both     | 200 (expected)                 |
| 1.41.1    | v0.0.26 (wrapper)   | firefox  | **0**                          |
| 1.41.1    | v0.0.26 (wrapper)   | chromium | 174                            |
| 1.41.1    | v0.0.25 (minimal)   | both     | 200 (expected)                 |
| 1.53.0    | v0.0.25 (minimal)   | firefox  | **0**                          |
| 1.53.0    | v0.0.25 (minimal)   | chromium | **0**                          |
| 1.56.0    | any                 | both     | **0**                          |

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

### Evidence this is not a component-side problem

We instrumented the component's Vue hooks (`onMounted`, `onUnmounted`) and its resize /
render entry point (`handleResize`) with `console.log`. Through the entire dialog lifecycle
(click → dialog open → dialog close → scroll reset), **no component code runs**. The scroll
reset is observed with zero in-iframe JavaScript activity. We also experimentally removed
the ResizeObserver, all Vue watchers, and even the `.scrolling-container` wrapper — the
reset still happens on Firefox with Streamlit 1.41+ and on all browsers with 1.53+.

This places the root cause in Streamlit's host-page logic during script rerun, outside the
reach of any custom component.

### Suspected origin (1.41.0)

This commit was flagged by [USER] on the downstream thread as the probable source of the
1.41.0 regression:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/commit/96241e135e0a5597ff975c232fa2c44b45e71358

title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
text:

1.41.0 regression:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/commit/96241e135e0a5597ff975c232fa2c44b45e71358

It changed iframe handling for custom components. The 1.52 → 1.53 all-browser regression
would require a separate bisect by Streamlit maintainers.

### Environment

- Host: macOS 25.4 (darwin-arm64), Python 3.12
- Firefox 146.0.1, Chrome-for-Testing 145.0.7632.6 (both via Playwright 1.58 headless)
- streamlit-pdf-viewer 0.0.25 and 0.0.26 (both reproduce with Streamlit 1.53.0+)

### Additional Information

### Related issues 

I searched existing `streamlit/streamlit` issues with multiple term combinations
(`scroll reset dialog custom component`, `iframe scroll position rerun`,
`page scroll reset rerun`, `custom component iframe rerun`,
`main page scroll top st.dialog component`, `scroll position lost after rerun`) and did
not find a duplicate. The closest adjacent issues are:

- #10756 (closed): *Custom components unmount and reload on switch_page* — same theme of
  iframe lifecycle surprises on rerun/navigation, different trigger (switch_page rather
  than dialog close).
- #14505 (open PR): *fix: reset dialog scroll position to top when reopened* — fixes the
  **dialog's internal** scroll, not the parent page scroll. Different scroll surface.
- #10701 (open): *Preserve Selection, Sorting and Scrolling Position in st.dataframe* —
  widget-internal scroll preservation, unrelated mechanism.

If this turns out to be a duplicate of an issue I missed, happy to consolidate.

### Links

- Downstream issue (full history, repro videos, user-reported workaround): https://github.com/lfoppiano/streamlit-pdf-viewer/issues/107

title: Parent-page scroll resets after closing `st.dialog` opened from a custom component (regression since 1.41.0, worsened at 1.53.0)
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a well-documented regression where the parent page's scroll position (`stMain.scrollTop`) resets to 0 after closing an `st.dialog` that was opened via a custom component's `setComponentValue`. The reporter identified two distinct regressions: 1. **v1.41.0** (Firefox-only, specific DOM shapes): Caused by commit `96241e1` which migrated iframe styles from global styles to per-component styled-components for `CustomComponent`. The new `StyledComponentIframe` toggles `display: "initial" | "none"` based on `componentReady`, which can cause layout recalculations that disturb scroll position when the iframe re-renders during a script rerun triggered by dialog close. 2. **v1.53.0** (all browsers, all component shapes): Likely compounded by changes to dialog identity handling (commit `5319def` — "Prevent `st.dialog` from showing elements from previous dialog") and the introduction of `TransientNode`/`ClearTransientNodesVisitor` which alter how the render tree is rebuilt during reruns. When the dialog closes and triggers a rerun, the combination of dialog node clearing and custom component iframe re-rendering causes the browser to reset `stMain`'s scroll position. Notably, Streamlit has no explicit scroll preservation logic for the main content area during reruns — scroll stability relies entirely on DOM stability, which these changes disrupted. ### Related Issues - **#6953** — [Page automatically scrolls itself when interacting with widgets](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6953): Same symptom of unexpected scroll position jumps during rerun/re-render cycles, though triggered by native widgets rather than custom components + dialog. - **#12716** — [Long dialog starts at the bottom](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12716): Related dialog scroll issue (dialog's *internal* scroll position), with an open fix PR [#14505](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14505) that adds `scrollTop` reset to the dialog container —
