Issue #16030: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, area:dependencies, status:confirmed, priority:P2, upstream, area:server

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit's pyproject.toml pins "websockets>=12.0.0". Version 16.1 of websockets (released July 9, 2026) introduced a change that blocks non-ASCII values in HTTP headers (see [changelog](https://websockets.readthedocs.io/en/stable/project/changelog.html#id2), "Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers").

This breaks the WebSocket handshake for setups where a reverse proxy / auth layer injects headers containing UTF-8 characters before the request reaches Streamlit — for example [Authelia](https://www.authelia.com/) forward-auth, which can inject a Remote-Name header containing the user's display name (e.g. accented characters, non-Latin scripts).

Since Streamlit's dependency constraint allows websockets to resolve to 16.1+, installing/upgrading Streamlit in a fresh environment can silently pull in a version that breaks WebSocket connections for any deployment relying on non-ASCII header values, with no warning at install time

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy Streamlit behind a reverse proxy (nginx/Traefik) with Authelia forward-auth, configured to forward Remote-Name, Remote-Email, etc. headers to the backend.
2. Ensure a user's Authelia display name contains a non-ASCII character (e.g. "François", "Müller", "田中").
3. Install/upgrade Streamlit in an environment where pip resolves websockets to >=16.1.
4. Log in as that user and attempt to load the app.

### Expected Behavior

title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
text:
### Expected Behavior

The WebSocket connection (/_stcore/stream) should be established successfully, as it was with websockets<16.1.

### Current Behavior

The WebSocket handshake fails because websockets 16.1 rejects the non-ASCII header value. The app gets stuck on "Please wait..." / the frontend logs a WebSocket connection failure, similar in symptom to issues like #8799.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian
- Browser: Chrome / Mozilla

### Additional Information

Workaround: pinning websockets<16.1 restores normal behavior.

Possible fixes on Streamlit's side:

- Tighten the websockets dependency constraint (e.g. >=12.0.0,<16.1) until this is addressed, or

- Percent-encode / sanitize header values Streamlit forwards or reads internally before they reach the websockets layer.

title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ### Issue analysis This is a **bug / upstream-dependency regression**. Streamlit's `lib/pyproject.toml` currently declares `websockets>=12.0.0,<17`, which still allows `websockets` to resolve to **16.1** (released 2026-07-09). That release "Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers", so any WebSocket handshake carrying a UTF-8 header value is now rejected. Streamlit doesn't import `websockets` directly — it's used as **uvicorn's WebSocket protocol implementation** (`ws="websockets-sansio"` for uvicorn ≥ 0.44.0, else `"auto"`), configured in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_server.py` (`_get_websocket_protocol`). The handshake header parsing therefore happens inside the `websockets` layer. When a reverse proxy / forward-auth layer (e.g. Authelia injecting a `Remote-Name` with accented or non-Latin characters) forwards a non-ASCII header, `websockets` 16.1 rejects it and the `/_stcore/stream` handshake fails, leaving the app stuck on "Please wait...". **Likely fixes** (as the reporter notes): tighten the constraint to exclude the broken range (e.g. `websockets>=12.0.0,<16.1` or skip 16.1) and/or sanitize/percent-encode forwarded header values before they reach the `websockets` layer. Note the concern is valid even with the existing `<17` cap, since 16.1 falls within it. ### Related Issues - [#8799](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8799) — "WebSocket header HTTP_SEC_WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL value changed ... which gives connection error" (closed). Directly referenced by this issue; same failure class of a WebSocket handshake failing due to a header value. - [#8188](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8188) — "Unnecessary failover on /_stcore/stream". Same symptom/deployment context: the `/_stcore/stream` WebSocket hangs/fails when running behind a reverse proxy. - [#12108](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12108) — "Frequent websocket connection drops ...". Same pattern of an upstream WebSocket-layer dependency change (Tornado 6.5.1) breaking WebSocket connectivity for users behind proxies/Nginx. --- *This is an automated triage comment using

title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
text:
[NONE] We are seeing the same symptom, but the immediate exception is in **uvicorn**, not in websockets itself.

**Environment where we reproduced it:**
- Streamlit 1.58.0 / 1.59.2
- uvicorn 0.51.0
- websockets 16.1
- Python 3.10 / 3.14
- Reverse proxy: nginx + Authentik, forwarding user display-name headers (e.g. `X-authentik-name: Céline`)

**Traceback:**
```
  File ".../uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py", line 196, in <listcomp>
    (key.encode("ascii"), value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape"))
UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode characters in position 4-5: ordinal not in range(128)
```

**What's happening:**
- `websockets` 16.x decodes incoming HTTP header values as ISO-8859-1 (latin-1). A byte like `0xE9` therefore becomes the character `é` (U+00E9) by the time uvicorn sees it.
- `uvicorn 0.51.0` then tries to build the ASGI `headers` list with `value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")`.
- For a real non-ASCII character such as `é` (U+00E9) this is impossible, so the WebSocket handshake aborts.

**Note on the workaround `websockets<16.1`:** pinning websockets may avoid websockets-side validation, but it did **not** fix the above `UnicodeEncodeError` for us, because the crash is in uvicorn's re-encoding of the header value.

**Manual workaround:**
In `uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py`, in `handle_connect`, change the header listcomp so values are encoded back with `latin-1` (which preserves the original bytes, because websockets decoded them with latin-1):

```python
(key.encode("ascii"), value.encode("latin-1"))
```

**Suggested fix:**
Uvicorn should encode WebSocket header values with `latin-1` (or at least preserve the ISO-8859-1 decoded bytes) when building the ASGI `scope` in `websockets_sansio_impl.py`.

[NONE] I think this issue can be closed in favor of https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/issues/3035, unless you want to keep it open until resolved in uvicorn.

title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ### ✅ Confirmed — reproduced end-to-end Reproduced on a clean environment. A fresh `pip install streamlit==1.58.0` silently resolves to the broken combination: - `streamlit==1.58.0`, `uvicorn==0.51.0`, `websockets==16.1` Streamlit 1.58 selects uvicorn's `websockets-sansio` protocol (uvicorn ≥ 0.44.0), so this is the affected path. **Repro:** raw WebSocket handshake to `/_stcore/stream` simulating a forward-auth proxy injecting a display-name header: | Header value | Result | |---|---| | `X-Authentik-Name: Celine` (ASCII) | `101 Switching Protocols` ✅ | | `X-Authentik-Name: Céline` (raw byte `0xE9`) | connection dropped, **no response** ❌ | Server traceback matches [USER]'s report exactly: ``` File ".../uvicorn/protocols/websockets/websockets_sansio_impl.py", line 196, in handle_connect (key.encode("ascii"), value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")) UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character '\xe9' in position 1: ordinal not in range(128) ``` ### Root cause (the precise regression) The changelog phrase *"Blocked non-ASCII values in Headers"* is a little misleading for this case — websockets 16.1's header-value regex `[\x09\x20-\x7e\x80-\xff]*` still **allows** high bytes, so `0xE9` passes through. The actual break is a change in how the value is **decoded**: - **websockets 16.0** — `http11.py`: `value = raw_value.decode("ascii", "surrogateescape")` → `é` becomes surrogate `U+DCE9`, which uvicorn's `value.encode("ascii", errors="surrogateescape")` round-trips cleanly back to `0xE9`. ✅ - **websockets 16.1** — `http11.py`: `value = raw_value.decode("iso-8859-1")` → `é` becomes the real char `U+00E9`, which uvicorn's surrogateescape re-encode **cannot** encode → `UnicodeEncodeError` → handshake aborts. ❌ (16.1's `parse_headers` docstring still claims *"Non-ASCII characters are represented with surrogate escapes,"* which no longer matches its own code — worth flagging upstream.) ### Two corrections/notes for triage 1. **Dependency constraint.** The current constraint (both

title: Streamlit websockets 16.1 issue
text: `UnicodeEncodeError` → handshake aborts. ❌ (16.1's `parse_headers` docstring still claims *"Non-ASCII characters are represented with surrogate escapes,"* which no longer matches its own code — worth flagging upstream.) ### Two corrections/notes for triage 1. **Dependency constraint.** The current constraint (both `develop` and 1.58.0) is `websockets>=12.0.0` with **no upper bound** — not `<17`. So 16.1 (and anything newer) is fully permitted, and fresh installs pull it. 2. **Workaround discrepancy resolved.** The reporter says pinning `websockets<16.1` fixes it; [USER] says it didn't. In this exact stack (streamlit 1.58.0 / uvicorn 0.51.0), **`websockets==16.0` makes the non-ASCII handshake succeed** (101, no crash) — so the pin *does* work here. [USER]'s result was likely a different websockets/uvicorn combination (Authentik + Python 3.10/3.14). ### Possible Streamlit-side mitigations - Add an upper bound / exclude the broken range in `lib/pyproject.toml` (e.g. `websockets>=12.0.0,!=16.1` or a tested cap), and/or - Track the upstream fix — this is fundamentally a websockets 16.1 ↔ uvicorn incompatibility (uvicorn should re-encode with `latin-1` to preserve the ISO-8859-1 bytes websockets now produces).

title: Parameter for `st.columns` to disable column stacking on mobiles
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a **feature request** (`type:enhancement`) asking for a way to control the automatic responsive behavior of `st.columns`, which currently stacks columns vertically on narrow (mobile/tablet) viewports. The proposal is a parameter (e.g. `disable_column_stacking`) to force columns to stay side-by-side, optionally allowing horizontal overflow instead of stacking. The responsive stacking is intentional behavior implemented on the frontend: in `StyledColumn` (`frontend/lib/src/components/core/Block/styled-components.ts`), a media query forces each column's `min-width` to roughly `100%` once the viewport drops below the `breakpoints.columns` threshold, so columns wrap onto their own rows. Any implementation of this request would need to expose an option to skip/override that media rule (and decide between overflow vs. horizontal scrolling). This is a highly requested, long-standing enhancement rather than a bug, so it likely needs product input on the API surface (a per-call parameter vs. a global config, and how it interacts with the existing flex/wrap layout system). ### Related Issues - [#5003 – Deactivate responsiveness of `st.columns`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5003): Near-duplicate and the most upvoted version of this request. title: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list
text:
Issue #16086: Add `allowed_dates` parameter to st.date_input to restrict selectable dates to a specific list
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.date_input

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, st.date_input only supports continuous date ranges via min_value and max_value. 
There is no way to restrict selectable dates to a specific list of valid dates, such as 
dates available in a dataframe. Adding an allowed_dates parameter would fill this gap.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when I need to show a date picker that only allows the user to select 
dates that exist in a dataset. For example, when a dataframe contains sales data only for 
specific dates, the current widget allows the user to select any date in the range, even 
dates with no data. This forces developers to use workarounds like st.selectbox, which 
lacks the calendar UI and date-picking experience that st.date_input provides.

### How?

Introduce a new parameter called `allowed_dates` in `st.date_input` with the following behavior:

- Accepts a list of datetime.date objects
- Disables all dates not present in the list in the calendar UI
- Example usage:

import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"date": ["2025-01-01", "2025-01-15", "2025-02-10"]})
df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"]).dt.date

selected = st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    allowed_dates=df["date"].tolist()
)

### Additional Context

title: pressing ESC clears the contents of multiselect
text:
Issue #16109: pressing ESC clears the contents of multiselect
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.multiselect, status:intended-behavior

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Pressing ESC clears the contents of a multiselect.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

options = st.multiselect("What are your favorite colors?", ["Green", "Yellow", "Red", "Blue"])
st.write("You selected:", options)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click on the multiselect to open it.
2. Select all options.
3. Press [ESC] to close the multiselect.
4. (Optional) Press [ESC] a few more times. 
5. Click on the multiselect to open it again.
6. Press [ESC] twice.
7. Click on the multiselect to open it again.
8. Select all options.
9. Click on the multiselect
10. Press [ESC] once

### Expected Behavior

If you press ESC (no matter how many times) when a multiselect has focus, the selected options remain the same.

### Current Behavior

Step 6: Pressing ESC twice clears the contents of the multiselect.
Step 10: Pressing ESC once clears the contents of the multiselect.

If the multiselect is initalized with a non-empty set of options, however, pressing ESC doesn't affect the selection.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.60.0
- Python version: 3.14

### Additional Information

See #15637.

title: pressing ESC clears the contents of multiselect
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Pressing `ESC` on an `st.multiselect` that has **no `default`** wipes the user's current selection instead of just dismissing the dropdown. This is a follow-up to #15637 / PR #15646, which only partially fixed the problem: the fix disables ESC-clearing when a default is provided, but leaves it enabled for multiselects without a default. **Root cause:** `st.multiselect` renders BaseWeb's `Select`, whose `escapeClearsValue` prop defaults to `true`. In `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/Multiselect/Multiselect.tsx` this is set conditionally: ```tsx escapeClearsValue={element.default.length > 0 ? false : !disabled} ``` Because the condition only checks `element.default` (the initial default), a multiselect created without a default still has `escapeClearsValue = true`. So when a user manually selects options and presses `ESC` (once when the dropdown is closed, or after closing an open dropdown), BaseWeb clears the whole selection. This exactly matches the reporter's observation that ESC only preserves the selection when the widget is initialized with a non-empty default. This is a frontend-only behavior; the fix would be to make `escapeClearsValue={false}` unconditionally (as is already done for the `MultiSelectCell` in the data editor at `MultiSelectCell.tsx:534`), or otherwise decouple ESC-clearing from the presence of a default. ### Related Issues - **#15637 – "pressing ESC clear the contents of multiselect"** (closed, same author): Direct predecessor of this report. It was closed by PR #15646, whose fix only covered the "has a default" case, so this issue is effectively a re-report for the "no default" case that remained broken. - **#12260 – "Regression: Selectbox/Multiselect keyboard focus not activating on mobile"**: Another `st.multiselect` keyboard-interaction

[CONTRIBUTOR] Thanks for the detailed repro, [USER] — we reproduced this on 1.60.0.

This is currently **intended behavior**: a widget created without a `default` is treated as "clearable," and pressing `ESC` on a clearable widget clears its value. This matches `st.selectbox` (a selectbox with no default also resets to empty on `ESC`). That's why PR #15646 — which fixed the *has-a-default* case from #15637 — deliberately left the no-default case clearing.

That said, we hear that ESC wiping a selection you built up manually is surprising, and our own data-editor multiselect never clears on ESC. We'll discuss internally whether to change this so ESC only dismisses the dropdown and never clears the selection.

title: st.table() / st.dataframe() / st.data_editor() causes fatal SIGSEGV (exit code 139) in PyArrow convert_column - process killed silently, no Python exception raised
text:
Issue #16111: st.table() / st.dataframe() / st.data_editor() causes fatal SIGSEGV (exit code 139) in PyArrow convert_column - process killed silently, no Python exception raised
Labels: type:bug, area:arrow, status:confirmed, priority:P1

### Summary

Calling st.table(), st.dataframe(), or st.data_editor() with a pandas DataFrame causes a fatal segmentation fault (SIGSEGV, exit code 139) that kills the entire Streamlit process. The crash originates inside PyArrow's convert_column C extension, called during Streamlit's internal DataFrame-to-Arrow serialization. No Python exception is raised. The process dies silently with no user-visible error. In containerized environments (Kubernetes/OpenShift) this triggers a pod restart.

### Steps To Reproduce

We were unable to produce a minimal example that reliably crashes in all environments. The crash is non-deterministic and appears to depend on the process memory state at the time of rendering. It reproduces consistently in our containerized Linux environment (OpenShift, Python 3.11) but not on a local Windows developer machine.

The code that triggers it in the enviroments:

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This DataFrame is rendered on every page rerun
df = pd.DataFrame({"Group": st.session_state.get("usergroup", [])})
st.table(df)  
```

or

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# DataFrame built from backend JSON response
rows = [{"col_a": "value", "col_b": None}, {"col_a": "other", "col_b": 3}]
df = pd.DataFrame(rows)  # object-dtype columns with None values
st.dataframe(df)  #
```

Steps To Reproduce

title: st.table() / st.dataframe() / st.data_editor() causes fatal SIGSEGV (exit code 139) in PyArrow convert_column - process killed silently, no Python exception raised
text:
Steps To Reproduce

1. Deploy a Streamlit 1.55.0 app to a Linux container (e.g. OpenShift/Kubernetes)
2. Navigate to a page that renders st.table() or st.dataframe() with a DataFrame that has object-dtype columns (e.g. built from pd.DataFrame(list_of_dicts) where some cells are None)
3. Trigger a Streamlit script rerun via a button click that loads new data into session state before the render
4. Observed: process dies with exit code 139, container restarts
5. Repeat the exact same steps - it works on the second attempt

### Expected Behavior

The DataFrame renders normally. If an internal serialization error occurs, Streamlit catches it and displays an error in the UI without killing the process.

### Current Behavior

The Python process is killed with SIGSEGV (exit code 139). Nothing appears in logs unless faulthandler is explicitly enabled at startup. With import faulthandler; faulthandler.enable() added, the crash trace is:

```
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

Current thread (most recent call first):
  File ".../pyarrow/pandas_compat.py", line 638 in convert_column
  File ".../pyarrow/pandas_compat.py", line 656 in dataframe_to_arrays
  File ".../streamlit/dataframe_util.py", line 839 in convert_pandas_df_to_arrow_bytes
  File ".../streamlit/dataframe_util.py", line 919 in convert_anything_to_arrow_bytes
  File ".../streamlit/elements/table.py", line 78 in marshall_table
  File ".../streamlit/elements/table.py", line 234 in table
```

The crash is non-deterministic: it only occurs on some reruns, always the first one after the pod/process starts, and does not occur on subsequent reruns with identical data and code. We have no confirmed explanation for the non-determinism beyond it appearing to depend on process memory state.

title: st.data_editor NumberColumn commits after first keystroke when a CJK IME (Japanese/Korean) is active — regression in 1.59.0+ (works in 1.58.0)
text:
Issue #16129: st.data_editor NumberColumn commits after first keystroke when a CJK IME (Japanese/Korean) is active — regression in 1.59.0+ (works in 1.58.0)
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.data_editor, feature:st.column_config, upstream, area:localization

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When editing a `NumberColumn` cell in `st.data_editor` while a CJK IME (Japanese / Korean input method) is active, the cell editor commits after the **first keystroke**, making it impossible to type multi-digit numbers (e.g. typing `15` commits `1`).

This is a **regression introduced between 1.58.0 and 1.59.0**: the same app and the same input method work correctly on 1.58.0. The bug persists in 1.60.0.

Typing the same digits with the IME switched to direct alphanumeric input works fine on all versions, which points to IME composition events (`compositionstart` / `isComposing`) not being handled by the cell overlay editor.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"Mon": [8], "Tue": [9]}, index=["item"])
df.index.name = "name"

edited = st.data_editor(
    df,
    num_rows="fixed",
    column_config={
        c: st.column_config.NumberColumn(c, min_value=0, step=1, format="%d")
        for c in df.columns
    },
)
st.write(edited)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: st.data_editor NumberColumn commits after first keystroke when a CJK IME (Japanese/Korean) is active — regression in 1.59.0+ (works in 1.58.0)
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. On macOS, enable a CJK input method (reproduced with Japanese and Korean IME).
2. Run the app above on Streamlit 1.59.0 or 1.60.0.
3. Double-click a number cell to open the cell editor.
4. With the IME **on**, type `15`.

### Expected Behavior

The cell accepts both keystrokes and commits `15` (this is the behavior on 1.58.0, and on 1.59.0+ when the IME is off / direct alphanumeric input is used).

### Current Behavior

The cell editor commits immediately after the first keystroke; the cell ends up with `1` and the editor closes. Multi-digit input is impossible while the IME is active.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Works in **1.58.0**, broken in **1.59.0** and **1.60.0**.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 and 1.60.0 (broken), 1.58.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.11 (Linux container / Railway) — also observed from macOS clients
- Operating System (client): macOS (multiple machines)
- Browser: not browser-specific in our testing (the determining factor is whether the IME is composing; direct alphanumeric input works on the same machines/browsers)

### Additional Information

title: st.data_editor NumberColumn commits after first keystroke when a CJK IME (Japanese/Korean) is active — regression in 1.59.0+ (works in 1.58.0)
text:
### Additional Information

- In production this hit users editing production-planning quantities: users typing numbers with a Japanese/Korean IME still enabled could only enter single-digit values.
- Workaround we use: switch the IME to direct alphanumeric mode before typing digits.
- This looks like the classic IME pitfall where key handling ignores `KeyboardEvent.isComposing` / composition events, so the first keystroke during composition is treated as a complete edit. Streamlit had a similar IME issue in another component in the past (#6988, `st.chat_input`).

title: Timer.run() receives an extra positional argument with Sentry ThreadingIntegration and st.fragment(run_every)
text:
Issue #16139: Timer.run() receives an extra positional argument with Sentry ThreadingIntegration and st.fragment(run_every)
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.fragment

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When Streamlit is used together with Sentry's default ThreadingIntegration, a periodically running fragment can fail with:

TypeError: Timer.run() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given

The error appears to be caused by an interaction between Streamlit's thread-state wrapper and Sentry's threading wrapper.

Streamlit stores the already-bound thread.run method and later forwards *args and **kwargs to it. Sentry's threading integration may invoke the replacement wrapper with the thread instance as a positional argument. That argument is then forwarded to the already-bound Timer.run method, resulting in the TypeError.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import sentry_sdk
import streamlit as st

sentry_sdk.init(
    dsn="YOUR_TEST_SENTRY_DSN",
)

[USER].fragment(run_every="1s")
def timer_fragment() -> None:
    st.write("Fragment executed")

timer_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Install the dependencies:

pip install streamlit==1.60.0 sentry-sdk

Create app.py:

import sentry_sdk
import streamlit as st

sentry_sdk.init(
    dsn="YOUR_TEST_SENTRY_DSN",
)

[USER].fragment(run_every="1s")
def periodically_updated_fragment() -> None:
    st.write("Fragment is running")

periodically_updated_fragment()

Run the application:

streamlit run app.py

Leave the application open while the fragment timer runs.

### Expected Behavior

st.fragment(run_every=...) should run normally when Sentry's default integrations are enabled.

Third-party wrappers around thread.run should not cause Streamlit to forward an extra thread instance to an already-bound run method.

### Current Behavior

title: Timer.run() receives an extra positional argument with Sentry ThreadingIntegration and st.fragment(run_every)
text:
### Expected Behavior

st.fragment(run_every=...) should run normally when Sentry's default integrations are enabled.

Third-party wrappers around thread.run should not cause Streamlit to forward an extra thread instance to an already-bound run method.

### Current Behavior

The background timer can fail with:

TypeError: Timer.run() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given
  File "streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner_utils/script_run_context.py", line ..., in _run_with_thread_state
    original_run(*args, **kwargs)

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.60.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux in the deployed environment
- Browser: Google Chrome

### Additional Information

The issue does not occur after adding ThreadingIntegration() to disabled_integrations.

A related earlier Streamlit change allowed the thread-state wrapper to accept *args and **kwargs, but forwarding those arguments to an already-bound Timer.run appears to introduce this follow-up incompatibility.

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Testing the new reproducing issues skill ([not merged yet](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16054)): ### Triage: confirmed 🐛 Thanks for the detailed report and the workaround script — reproduced and root-caused. **Live repro:** https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-16148 **Full investigation notes:** https://issues.streamlit.app/agent_wiki_explorer?file=pull-requests/16054/gh-16148-notes.md #### What's happening Every fullscreen-capable element (images, charts, dataframes, etc.) renders a **Fullscreen** button with a fixed accessible name `aria-label="Fullscreen"`. It never references the element it belongs to, so on a page with several images/charts a screen reader announces a list of identical "Fullscreen button" controls with no way to tell them apart. Confirmed on **1.57.0** with two captioned images — both buttons expose the same accessible name: | Image caption | Fullscreen button `aria-label` | | --- | --- | | Federal Command Center | `Fullscreen` | | DoD Network Architecture | `Fullscreen` | This is a longstanding behavior (the label is a frontend constant), so it's **not a regression** — it's present on `develop` too. #### Root cause The toolbar hard-codes the fullscreen action's label, which becomes the button's `aria-label`, and no element caption/title is plumbed through: - `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Toolbar/Toolbar.tsx` — `<ToolbarAction label="Fullscreen" … />` and `aria-label={label}` - Callers like `ImageList.tsx` already have the caption in scope but don't pass it to `<Toolbar>`. #### Likely fix Thread an optional accessible label through `Toolbar`/`ToolbarAction` and set it to something like `"Fullscreen: {caption}"` when a caption/title is available (keeping the visible tooltip short), falling back to plain "Fullscreen" otherwise. Issue #16181: st.selectbox in sidebar clipping/overflows instead of flipping up (regression in 1.59)
Labels: type:bug, area:layout, type:regression, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.selectbox, feature:st.sidebar

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In the sidebar when st.selectbox sits near the bottom, the component opens its dropdown downward and the options overflow past the bottom of the viewport instead of flipping upward. This changed between 1.58 and 1.59/1.60: in 1.58 the same app flips the dropdown upward so it stays on screen; in 1.59 it opens downward and overflows. This issue only occurs in the sidebar.

Observed rendered DOM difference (offered as evidence): in 1.58 the open listbox renders at the document root as a sibling of #portal (ul[data-testid="stSelectboxVirtualDropdown"]), so its placement is viewport-relative and it flips. In 1.59 the widget is a react-aria-ComboBox and the open listbox renders inside [data-testid="stSidebar"], which is position: relative, so it is anchored to the sidebar and opens downward only.

### Reproducible Code Example

title: st.selectbox in sidebar clipping/overflows instead of flipping up (regression in 1.59)
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ### Triage summary This is a confirmed-looking layout **regression** in the new (`react-aria-components`) `st.selectbox`/ComboBox introduced in 1.59. When a selectbox sits near the bottom of the **sidebar**, its dropdown opens downward and overflows past the viewport instead of flipping up as it did in 1.58. **Likely root cause:** the dropdown is positioned via Floating UI, but flipping is explicitly disabled inside the sidebar. In `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Dropdown/Selectbox.tsx` the positioning hook is called with: ```tsx const { refs, floatingStyles } = useFloatingOverlay({ open: true, placement: "bottom-start", offsetPx: convertRemToPx(theme.spacing.twoXS), flipOptions: isInSidebar ? false : undefined, // <-- disables flip in the sidebar matchTriggerWidth: true, }) ``` In `useFloatingOverlay` (`frontend/lib/src/hooks/useFloatingOverlay.ts`), `flipOptions === false` drops the `flip()` middleware entirely, so the popover can no longer flip to `top` when there isn't enough space below — it just opens downward and gets clipped. This matches the reporter's DOM observation that in 1.59 the listbox renders inside `[data-testid="stSidebar"]` (which is `position: relative`) rather than at the document root as a sibling of `#portal` like in 1.58. This flip-disabling was added in the Floating UI scroll-tracking change (#15638); it was presumably meant to avoid the popover escaping the sidebar's bounds (the BaseWeb `Multiselect` uses the analogous `ignoreBoundary: isInSidebar`), but it also unintentionally removed the upward-flip behavior. A fix likely needs to keep flip enabled while constraining/shifting the popover against the viewport rather than fully disabling `flipOptions` in the sidebar. ### Related Issues - [#12260 – Regression: Selectbox/Multiselect keyboard focus not activating on mobile](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12260): Another regression in the same

text:
Issue #16269: format_func does not keep the pill selected when the pill's text changes.
Labels: type:bug, area:widgets, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

In the first part of the code below, two interdependent "pills" components are created; the `format_func` adjusts the text displayed on the buttons to show the record count for each category.
When a category is selected in the first component, it updates the component below by filtering subcategories and changing the displayed text to reflect the record count for each subcategory.
However, when the category selection is cleared, the second component retains the value in `session_state` and the object's internal state, yet it does not visually appear selected, which misleads the user.
In this scenario, the subcategory component should appear selected, even though the displayed text has changed.

The second part uses the "same code" but without `format_func`: here, if you select a category, select a subcategory, and then deselect the category, the subcategory remains visually selected.

title: format_func does not keep the pill selected when the pill's text changes.
text:
The second part uses the "same code" but without `format_func`: here, if you select a category, select a subcategory, and then deselect the category, the subcategory remains visually selected.

```
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(
        [
            {"id": 1, "name":"name a","category": "A","category_b": "D"},
            {"id": 2, "name":"name b","category": "A","category_b": "D"},
            {"id": 3, "name":"name c","category": "B","category_b": "D"},
            {"id": 4, "name":"name d","category": "B","category_b": "E"},
            {"id": 5, "name":"name e","category": "C","category_b": "E"},
```

title: format_func does not keep the pill selected when the pill's text changes.
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ### Summary This is a `st.pills` bug (also applies to `st.segmented_control`, which shares the same `ButtonGroup` implementation): when `format_func` output for the currently-selected option changes between reruns (here the record count in the label changes as `df` is filtered), the pill visually appears **deselected**, even though `session_state` and the return value still hold the correct underlying value. The reporter's second example without `format_func` works, isolating `format_func` as the trigger. ### Potential root cause Since the 1.54 refactor, these button-group widgets identify/track the selected option by its **formatted display string** rather than by the underlying value: - Frontend (`frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/ButtonGroup/ButtonGroup.tsx`) stores the widget value as the formatted content string and highlights selection via `contentStringsToIndices(options, value)`. When `format_func` output changes (e.g. `"D (2)"` → `"D (3)"`), the stored string no longer matches any current option's content, so `selectedKeys` is empty and nothing renders as selected. - Backend (`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/button_group.py`) maps wire values via `formatted_option_to_option_index`, and only preserves the *value* through `session_state_fallback` — which is why `session_state`/the return value stay correct while the visual selection is lost. Note there is already substantial handling for dynamic `format_func`/option changes in recent versions — the `session_state_fallback` + `set_value` re-serialization added in #15522 (shipped in 1.60.0) and the dynamic-options support in #13684. The report was filed without a version, so the team should confirm the exact Streamlit version and whether this still reproduces on the latest release; this may be a remaining edge case in the interdependent (parent→child) pills flow rather than a fully open regression. ### Related

title: `st.download_button` rejects documented `io.StringIO` data
text:
Issue #16270: `st.download_button` rejects documented `io.StringIO` data
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.download_button

## Summary

`st.download_button` documents `io.StringIO` as a supported file-like value, and the public typing tests accept it, but the runtime raises `StreamlitAPIException`. This affects both eager values and deferred callables because they share the same data conversion helper.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
import io

import streamlit as st

st.download_button("Download", data=io.StringIO("hello"))
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the example as `app.py`.
2. Run `streamlit run app.py`.
3. Observe the exception while the download button is created.

## Expected Behavior

The download button is rendered and downloads `hello` as `text/plain`, matching the documented `io.StringIO` support.

## Current Behavior

Streamlit raises:

```text
streamlit.errors.StreamlitAPIException:
Invalid binary data format: <class '_io.StringIO'>
```

`convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` handles `str` and the concrete `io.TextIOWrapper`, but not `io.StringIO`. The public `DownloadButtonDataType` and typing test already accept `io.StringIO`.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: current `develop` (`1.60.0`)
- Python version: 3.11.15
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: not applicable; the exception occurs during script execution

## Additional Information

A focused fix and regression test are available in [ShiroKSH/streamlit@e4e7da440](https://github.com/ShiroKSH/streamlit/commit/e4e7da4400646822221cbdeb9423467d0ce4264b). It reads `io.StringIO` with `getvalue()`, matching the existing `io.BytesIO` behavior without changing the stream cursor.

Validated with:

- `make check`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/runtime/download_data_util_test.py -q`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/elements/download_button_test.py -q`
- `uv run pytest lib/tests/streamlit/runtime/media_file_manager_test.py -k execute_deferred -q`

title: `st.download_button` rejects documented `io.StringIO` data
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a **bug**: `st.download_button` advertises `io.StringIO` as a supported `data` value (docstring, the public `DownloadButtonDataType` alias via `TextIO`, and the `button_types.py` typing test all accept it), but passing one raises `StreamlitAPIException: Invalid binary data format: <class '_io.StringIO'>` at runtime.

The root cause is in `convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` (`lib/streamlit/runtime/download_data_util.py`). It only handles text streams via `isinstance(data, io.TextIOWrapper)`, but `io.StringIO` is a *sibling* subclass of `io.TextIOBase` — it is **not** an `io.TextIOWrapper` — so it never matches the text branch (nor any `bytes`/`io.BytesIO`/`io.RawIOBase` branch) and falls through to `raise unsupported_error`. Because both the eager and deferred (callable) code paths in `button.py` route through this same helper, `io.StringIO` fails in both cases. The reporter's linked patch fixes this by reading `io.StringIO` via `getvalue()`, mirroring the existing `io.BytesIO` handling. A broader alternative would be to match `io.TextIOBase` so any text stream is covered.

### Related Issues

- [#14159 — st.download_button generate file_name and mime from io.FileIO](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14159): Also concerns how `st.download_button` handles file-like objects and MIME inference in the same `convert_data_to_bytes_and_infer_mime` code path; both point at gaps in the supported-`io.*`-types handling.
- [#5053 — Deferred data for download button](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5053): Introduced the deferred-callable path that shares the same data-conversion helper affected by this bug.

---

title: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
text:
Issue #16281: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.container, feature:st.status, feature:st.fragment, area:execution-model

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a fragment calls `.status()` on a container that was declared outside the fragment, and then opens that status block a second time with a separate `with` statement, the app crashes to a blank page with `Uncaught Error: Cannot set a node at a delta path`. The status container re-emits its own block at the wrong delta path, which destroys an intermediate container in the frontend element tree, so the next element written inside it has no parent. This is a regression: it works in 1.58.0 and fails in every version from 1.59.0 onward.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-16281)

```Python
import streamlit as st


[USER].fragment
def frag(outside):
    block = outside.status("query")
    with block:
        st.code("first")
    with block:  # second, separate `with` on the same status block
        st.text("second")


st.title("Repro")
frag(st.container())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Save the example above and run it with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open the app in a browser and open the developer console.
3. No interaction is needed. The crash happens during the initial page load.

### Expected Behavior

title: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
text:
The regression enters in 1.59.0. No released version fixes it, and the nightly above still fails.

#### The delta stream

These are the deltas the backend emits for the example above on the first script run. The defect is the sixth delta:

```
[0, 1]           block=flex_container   fragment=-      <- the outside container
[0, 2]           block=flex_container   fragment=X      <- the fragment's own container
[0, 1, 0]        block=transparent      fragment=X      <- outside-write wrapper
[0, 1, 0, 0]     block=expandable       fragment=X      <- the status, inside the wrapper
[0, 1, 0, 0, 0]  element=code           fragment=X      <- first `with` write
[0, 1, 0]        block=expandable       fragment=X      <- BUG: re-emitted at the wrapper's path
[0, 1, 0, 0, 1]  element=text           fragment=X      <- crashes here
```

The sixth delta replaces the `transparent` wrapper at `[0, 1, 0]` with an `expandable` block. `AppRoot.addBlock` only inherits the existing children when the block type matches (`frontend/lib/src/render-tree/AppRoot.ts:469`), and `transparent` is not `expandable`, so the frontend drops the whole subtree. The next delta targets `[0, 1, 0, 0, 1]`, its parent at `[0, 1, 0, 0]` no longer exists, and the visitor throws.

#### Root cause

`StatusContainer._create` captures the delta path for later re-emits from the **parent's** cursor **before** the block is created (`lib/streamlit/elements/lib/mutable_status_container.py:81-91`):

```python
delta_path: list[int] = (
    parent._active_dg._cursor.delta_path if parent._active_dg._cursor else []
)

status_container = cast(
    "StatusContainer",
    parent._block(block_proto=block_proto, dg_type=StatusContainer),
)

# Apply initial configuration
status_container._delta_path = delta_path
```

Normally the parent cursor points at exactly the index where the new block lands, so the captured path identifies the status block correctly.

title: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
text:
Normally the parent cursor points at exactly the index where the new block lands, so the captured path identifies the status block correctly.

Since 1.59.0, a write from a fragment into a container declared outside that fragment is redirected into a per-fragment layout-transparent wrapper block. The status block therefore lands one level deeper than the captured path predicted, so `_delta_path` points at the wrapper instead of the status.

`update()` does not use the cursor. It builds a message and sets that stale path directly (`mutable_status_container.py:151`):

```python
msg.metadata.delta_path[:] = self._delta_path
msg.delta.add_block.CopyFrom(self._current_proto)
```

`__exit__` calls `update(state="complete")` whenever the state is still `running` (`mutable_status_container.py:185-204`), so an explicit `update()` call is not required to trigger this.

#### Scope of the trigger

Each row was checked in a browser against 1.59.1:

| Variant | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same code without the fragment | works |
| Fragment, status, one `with` block | works |
| Fragment, status, one `with` block plus a later `update()` | works |
| Fragment, status, **two separate `with` blocks** | **crash** |
| Outside container is `st.container`, `st.popover`, or `st.expander` | crash in all three |
| Inner block is `outside.container()` instead of `outside.status()` | works |

`st.status` is the element that matters, because it is the one that re-emits its own block from a stored path. The type of the outside container does not matter.

title: `st.status` created on a container outside a fragment corrupts the element tree and crashes the app with "Cannot set a node at a delta path"
text:
`st.status` is the element that matters, because it is the one that re-emits its own block from a stored path. The type of the outside container does not matter.

The one-`with` case still emits the misdirected delta and still replaces the wrapper, but nothing is written inside the block afterwards, so no delta is left without a parent and no crash is visible. The element tree is already wrong in that case, which means this defect can also corrupt a page silently.

#### Related work

The 1.59.0 change that introduces the redirection is the outside-container-writes work: #15541, #15545, #15598, #15620, and #15623.

This looks close to #12514 (fragments inside a shared container), but it is a different defect. #16171 is the fix for #12514 and it is present in the nightly listed above, which still reproduces this crash.

#### Possible fix

Capture `_delta_path` after the block is created, from the path `_block()` actually wrote to, rather than predicting it from the parent cursor beforehand. It may be worth auditing any other element that stores a delta path and later enqueues a message with it directly.

#### Workarounds

Both verified on 1.59.1:

- Write everything to the status inside a single `with` block.
- Create the status on a container declared inside the fragment, or use `st.expander` or `st.container` instead of `st.status`.

title: Port auto-increment feature not working after moving to starlette
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ### Summary This is a **regression on Windows** introduced by the Tornado → Starlette/Uvicorn server migration (v1.57). When the default port `8501` is already in use, Streamlit no longer auto-increments to the next free port; instead every process happily binds to `8501`. **Likely root cause:** The new server pre-binds its own socket in `_bind_socket()` and unconditionally sets `SO_REUSEADDR`: ```271:271:lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_server.py sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1) ``` On POSIX systems `SO_REUSEADDR` only permits rebinding sockets left in `TIME_WAIT`, but **on Windows it allows two active sockets to bind the exact same address/port simultaneously**. As a result the second `streamlit run` process binds `8501` successfully, `bind()` never raises `EADDRINUSE`, and the port-retry loop in `UvicornServer.start()` (`for attempt in range(MAX_PORT_SEARCH_RETRIES + 1)`, ~lines 354–392) never advances to the next port. The old Tornado server relied on `tornado.netutil.bind_sockets`, which on Windows uses `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` (and avoids `SO_REUSEADDR`), so conflicts were detected and auto-increment worked. The Windows-appropriate fix is to use `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` instead of `SO_REUSEADDR` on Windows. This is a bug/regression, not intended deprecation. ### Related Issues - [#15378 — Running Streamlit with Starlette in Corporate Network](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15378): Confirmed `type:regression` from the same Starlette/Uvicorn migration affecting the server on Windows (`area:windows`, `area:network`, `area:server`) — closest sibling in nature. - [#15022 — Intermittent `OSError: [WinError 121]` since upgrading to `v1.57.0`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15022): Another confirmed Windows-specific server regression introduced by the 1.57 Starlette/Uvicorn migration, pointing to Windows socket-handling differences in the new server. - [#9271 — auto-select next available port](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9271): Directly concerns the port auto-increment / free-port-search feature this issue reports as broken

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ### Triage summary This is a **dependency-compatibility bug** in Streamlit's web server, not a Community Cloud–specific problem — it affects any environment where a fresh install resolves Starlette to a newer release (Community Cloud just happens to auto-resolve the latest compatible versions). **Root cause:** Streamlit's custom gzip middleware (`lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_gzip_middleware.py`) subclasses and directly instantiates Starlette's *internal* `GZipResponder`/`IdentityResponder` classes, which are private implementation details rather than public API: ```python responder = _MediaAwareGZipResponder( self.app, self.minimum_size, compresslevel=self.compresslevel ) ``` `_MediaAwareGZipResponder` does not override `__init__`, so it inherits Starlette's constructor. A newer Starlette release changed `GZipResponder.__init__` to add a required keyword-only argument `thread_minimum_size`. Because the responder is instantiated without it, startup fails before any app code runs: ``` TypeError: GZipResponder.__init__() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'thread_minimum_size' ``` Streamlit's runtime dependency range in `lib/pyproject.toml` is `starlette>=0.46.0,<2`, so the incompatible Starlette version satisfies the upper bound (`<2`) and gets installed. This coupling to Starlette internals was introduced with the Starlette/Uvicorn server migration ([#14553](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14553)). **Workaround confirmed by multiple reporters:** pin `starlette<1.4.0` (e.g. `starlette==1.3.1`) in `requirements.txt`. **Suggested fix:** cap the Starlette upper bound below the breaking release (and/or make the middleware resilient to the changed responder signature, e.g. forward `thread_minimum_size` or stop relying on the private responder classes). ### Related Issues - [#15378 – Running Streamlit with Starlette in Corporate Network](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15378): Another `area:server` bug stemming from the Starlette/Uvicorn migration; related to server behavior introduced by the same migration, though a different symptom (WebSocket connectivity). - [#15022 – Intermittent `OSError: [WinError 121]` since upgrading to `v1.57.0`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15022): Also traces back

text: [COLLABORATOR] Thanks for the report. The report is for **1.48.1**. The current release is **1.61.1**. We removed Tornado in **1.57.0**. Because of that, item 1 is not correct for current releases. Most of the other items still need work. Item by item. **Item 2, WebSocket error messages. Confirmed bug.** Malformed protobuf frames bypass the app-error redaction path. Because of this, `client.showErrorDetails` does not apply. File paths and line numbers can leak. This is a bug. `client.showErrorDetails = "none"` still helps for application exceptions. It does not cover this path. **Item 5, WebSocket Origin validation. Partly valid.** `server.allowedHosts` was added in **1.61.0**. It validates the `Host` header on the WebSocket handshake. It still works when CORS is disabled. This helps with unexpected hostnames. It does not provide a strict `Origin` allow-list. `server.corsAllowedOrigins` only adds more allowed origins. It does not replace the built-in allowed set. `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `0.0.0.0`, and the server's internal and external IPs are still allowed. `server.enableCORS=false` also allows all origins. This needs a separate feature request. **Item 3, OS version disclosure. Partly overstated.** Streamlit does not send a kernel version or distro version here. The `server_os` field is only `platform.system().lower()`. On Linux, this value is `"linux"`. The same session message still exposes the full Streamlit version and full Python version to any client that can open the WebSocket. The Streamlit version is used for client auto-reload after a server upgrade. The Python version and OS name are used only for telemetry in the current frontend. **Item 1, `Server`

text: Python version to any client that can open the WebSocket. The Streamlit version is used for client auto-reload after a server upgrade. The Python version and OS name are used only for telemetry in the current frontend. **Item 1, `Server` header. Resolved as written, but still present.** On current releases, the header is `Server: uvicorn`. It is not `TornadoServer/6.x.x`. It does not include a version. Streamlit does not have a config option to remove it. The current workaround is to strip it at the proxy. **Item 4, `/_stcore/host-config`. Informational.** This endpoint returns mostly hardcoded open-source defaults and your configured `client.allowedOrigins`. It does not reveal deployment-specific secrets. For a non-embedded app, `client.allowedOrigins = []` is the correct setting. Do not block this endpoint on the default connection path. If you need to control it, override the response at the proxy and return valid JSON. **Next steps** We filed two issues: 1. [WebSocket protocol error path ignores `client.showErrorDetails` and leaks stack traces](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16391) 2. [`server.enableCORS=false` warning incorrectly says the value is overridden to true](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16390) Please split the other asks into separate issues: 1. Suppress the `Server` header 2. Add a strict WebSocket Origin allow-list 3. Suppress version and OS fields in the session message

Issue #16390: server.enableCORS=false warning incorrectly says the value is overridden to true
Labels: type:bug, area:security, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:config, area:server

## Checklist

## Summary

When XSRF protection is enabled and `server.enableCORS=false`, Streamlit logs a warning that says `server.enableCORS` is "being overridden to 'true'." The current code only logs the warning. It does not change the config value. This can make operators think that Origin checks are stricter than they are.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("hello")
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a config with `server.enableCORS=false`.
2. Leave `server.enableXsrfProtection=true` enabled.
3. Start the app.
4. Read the startup warning in the logs.
5. Inspect behavior or code paths and see that `server.enableCORS` is still treated as false.

## Expected Behavior

The warning text should describe the real behavior. If Streamlit says it overrides the option to true, the code should do that. Otherwise the warning should say that the setting stays false and that Origin checks are still wide open.

## Current Behavior

The warning says:

```text
Warning: the config option 'server.enableCORS=false' is not compatible with
'server.enableXsrfProtection=true'.
As a result, 'server.enableCORS' is being overridden to 'true'.
```

title: server.enableCORS=false warning incorrectly says the value is overridden to true
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a confirmed documentation/warning bug: when `server.enableXsrfProtection=true` and `server.enableCORS=false`, `_check_conflicts()` in `lib/streamlit/config.py` logs that `server.enableCORS` is being overridden to `true`, but it never updates the config value. Origin checks in `server_util.is_url_from_allowed_origins()` still short-circuit when `enableCORS` is false and allow all origins. The option docstrings for both `server.enableCORS` and `server.enableXsrfProtection` also incorrectly claim Streamlit enables both. Operators can therefore believe Origin protection is active when it is not—especially risky behind reverse proxies. Fix options: either actually override the setting, or correct the warning/docs to describe the real behavior.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386 — Parent enterprise DAST/security report this issue was split from; includes Origin-validation concerns that motivated the misleading-warning analysis.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6062 — Proposal to rename `server.enableCORS` to `server.enableCORSProtection`; same config area and naming confusion around what the option actually does.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16393 — Open fix PR titled “[fix] Correct the server.enableCORS=false startup warning,” already linked from #16386.

title: WebSocket protocol error path ignores client.showErrorDetails and leaks stack traces
text:
Issue #16391: WebSocket protocol error path ignores client.showErrorDetails and leaks stack traces
Labels: type:bug, area:security, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:config, area:server, feature:runtime

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

## Summary

When a malformed WebSocket `BackMsg` frame fails protobuf deserialization, Streamlit uses a path that bypasses uncaught app exception redaction. Because of this, `client.showErrorDetails` does not apply. Stack traces with file paths and line numbers can reach the client. I reproduced this on 1.61.1.

## Reproducible Code Example

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st

st.write("hello")

# send_malformed_frame.py
import asyncio
import websockets


async def main():
    async with websockets.connect(
        "ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream",
        subprotocols=["streamlit"],
    ) as ws:
        # b"\\xff" is not a valid BackMsg protobuf frame.
        await ws.send(b"\\xff")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `app.py` on Streamlit 1.61.1.
2. Set `client.showErrorDetails = "none"`.
3. In a second terminal, run `send_malformed_frame.py`.
4. The script connects to `ws://localhost:8501/_stcore/stream` with subprotocol `streamlit` and sends `b"\xff"`.
5. Observe that the script receives a `ForwardMsg` Exception payload.
6. Observe that the Exception payload contains `DecodeError` and a stack trace entry with an absolute file path.

## Expected Behavior

Protocol-level WebSocket errors should return a generic client error or close the connection. They should not expose stack traces, file paths, or line numbers to the client. `client.showErrorDetails` should not be bypassed.

## Current Behavior

The deserialization exception goes through `AppSession._create_exception_message()`. That method calls `exception_utils.marshall(...)` without `is_uncaught_app_exception=True`. The redaction logic does not run. On the event-loop thread there is no script run context, so traceback filtering does not remove internal frames. In my local repro, the returned Exception payload had message `Error parsing message with type 'BackMsg'`, type `DecodeError`, and a stack trace entry that exposed `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py`.

## Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

## Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Any
- Browser: N/A

## Additional Information

Split from [issue #16386](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386). This also affects the generic `AppSession.handle_backmsg()` exception path, not only protobuf deserialization failures.

title: WebSocket protocol error path ignores client.showErrorDetails and leaks stack traces
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Malformed WebSocket `BackMsg` frames (and other `handle_backmsg` failures) are reported via `AppSession._create_exception_message()`, which calls `exception_utils.marshall(...)` without `is_uncaught_app_exception=True`. Redaction gated on `client.showErrorDetails` only runs when that flag is set, so `DecodeError` messages, exception types, and stack frames (including absolute paths under `starlette_websocket.py`) are sent to the client even when `client.showErrorDetails = "none"`. The deserialization catch in `starlette_websocket.py` correctly routes to `handle_backmsg_deserialization_exception`, but the shared exception-marshalling path is the leak.

### Related Issues

- [#16386](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16386) — Parent security/DAST information-disclosure report; this issue was explicitly split out from it.
- [#12101](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12101) — Another gap where `client.showErrorDetails` does not cover all error/warning surfaces (warnings vs. this protocol-exception path).
- [#16203](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16203) — Related hardening of untrusted client/BackMsg handling (server-side validation), though focused on widget constraints rather than error redaction.

title: Custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`/`backgroundColor` not applied to derived `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`
text:
Issue #16398: Custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`/`backgroundColor` not applied to derived `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`
Labels: type:bug, feature:st.dataframe, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:theming, feature:st.code

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When you set a custom `theme.secondaryBackgroundColor` and/or `theme.backgroundColor` (but don't set `theme.codeBackgroundColor` / `theme.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`), code blocks and dataframe headers still use the default derived colors from the base theme instead of recomputing them from the custom colors.

By default, both `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` should be `bgMix` = a 50/50 mix of `backgroundColor` and `secondaryBackgroundColor`. That derivation happens correctly in `createEmotionColors`, but then gets overwritten with the base theme value.

### Reproducible Code Example

`.streamlit/config.toml`:

```toml
[theme]
backgroundColor = "#ffffff"
secondaryBackgroundColor = "#FAFAF9"
```

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.code("print('hello')")
st.dataframe({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set the theme config above
2. Run the app
3. Inspect the code block background color

### Expected Behavior

Code background should be the mix of `#ffffff` and `#FAFAF9`, i.e. roughly `#FDFDFC`.

### Current Behavior

Code background is `#F8F9FB`, which is the *default* `bgMix` (`mix(#ffffff, #f0f2f6, 0.5)`), ignoring the custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`.

Same issue for dataframe header background (`dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: develop
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

title: Custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`/`backgroundColor` not applied to derived `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`
text:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: develop
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

Root cause in `frontend/lib/src/theme/utils.ts` (`createEmotionTheme`):

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor =
  codeBackgroundColor ?? colors.codeBackgroundColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor =
  dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor ?? colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor
```

`colors` here is the *base* theme's colors, so when the config option isn't set, we throw away the correctly derived value from `createEmotionColors(newGenericColors)` and replace it with the base default.

Contrast with the correct pattern used for `link` / `codeTextColor` a few lines below:

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.link =
  linkColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.blueTextColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.codeTextColor =
  codeTextColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.greenTextColor
```

These two (`codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`) seem to be the only instances of this bug — other derived colors from `bgMix` (e.g. `darkenedBgMix*`) are not overwritten and should pick up the custom colors correctly.

Fix should be something like:

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor =
  codeBackgroundColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor =
  dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor ??
  conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor
```

title: bug: `st.pyplot` crashes with an opaque PIL error for `format="pdf"`, `"eps"`, `"ps"`, `"svgz"`
text:
Issue #16429: bug: `st.pyplot` crashes with an opaque PIL error for `format="pdf"`, `"eps"`, `"ps"`, `"svgz"`
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P4, feature:st.pyplot

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.pyplot` forwards `**kwargs` to `savefig`, so `format=` accepts anything Matplotlib supports. But only raster output survives the image path. `format="svg"` was fixed in #16283; the remaining vector formats still fail, and they fail with an error from inside PIL that names neither the format nor a way forward.

`svgz` is the odd one out: it is simply gzipped SVG, so it is renderable in principle — the gzip magic bytes just aren't recognised as SVG and get handed to PIL instead.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import streamlit as st

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3])

st.pyplot(fig, format="pdf")   # UnidentifiedImageError
st.pyplot(fig, format="eps")   # OSError
st.pyplot(fig, format="ps")    # OSError
st.pyplot(fig, format="svgz")  # UnidentifiedImageError
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run an app containing any one of the four calls above.
2. The app raises from inside PIL rather than reporting anything about the format.

### Expected Behavior

title: bug: `st.pyplot` crashes with an opaque PIL error for `format="pdf"`, `"eps"`, `"ps"`, `"svgz"`
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run an app containing any one of the four calls above.
2. The app raises from inside PIL rather than reporting anything about the format.

### Expected Behavior

- `svgz` should render, since it is gzipped SVG and SVG already renders.
- `pdf` / `eps` / `ps` cannot be rasterised without an external tool (Ghostscript or Poppler), which Streamlit does not bundle. These should fail with a clear message that names the format and points at `format="png"` or `format="svg"`.

### Current Behavior

Each format reaches PIL and raises there. Sniffing the buffer the way the current SVG check does shows why:

```
format  first bytes                        detected as SVG?  PIL result
png     b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n\x00\x00\x00\r'  False            OK
svg     b'<?xml versio'                     True             (bypasses PIL)
pdf     b'%PDF-1.4\n%\xac\xdc'              False            UnidentifiedImageError
eps     b'%!PS-Adobe-3'                     False            OSError
ps      b'%!PS-Adobe-3'                     False            OSError
svgz    b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x00p\xf0xj\x02\xff'  False            UnidentifiedImageError
```

`svgz` starts with the gzip magic `\x1f\x8b`, so the existing `<svg` / `<?xml` check cannot see the SVG inside it. `eps` and `ps` share the `%!PS-Adobe-3` prefix, so they are indistinguishable by magic bytes and are both PostScript.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No, this is a new problem.

Not a regression — these formats have never worked. #16283 fixed `format="svg"` only; this is the remainder of the same class of bug.

### Debug info

title: bug: `st.pyplot` crashes with an opaque PIL error for `format="pdf"`, `"eps"`, `"ps"`, `"svgz"`
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `st.pyplot` forwards `format=` to Matplotlib `savefig`, but after save only plain SVG is special-cased before the image path. In `lib/streamlit/elements/pyplot.py`, `marshall()` sniffs for `<svg` / `<?xml`…`<svg` and otherwise hands the buffer to `marshall_images` → PIL. That works for PNG/JPEG and for the SVG fix from #16283, but fails for `pdf`/`eps`/`ps` (opaque PIL/`OSError`) and for `svgz` (gzip magic `\x1f\x8b` hides the SVG). Expected fix: gunzip/`svgz` into the SVG path; reject unsupported vector formats with a clear error pointing at `png` or `svg`.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11489 — Same class of bug: `format="svg"` crashed in PIL because SVG bytes were treated as raster. Fixed by #16283; this issue covers the remaining formats.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16283 — The SVG sniff/bypass that left `pdf`/`eps`/`ps`/`svgz` on the broken PIL path.

No open duplicates found; #9660 (`st.pyplot` cold-start render failures) is unrelated.

text:
[COLLABORATOR] A bit of additional context here: the kwargs support in `st.pyplot` is something that we have intended to deprecate (and eventually remove) for a long time. We also had kwargs support for `st.plotly`, `st.altair_chart`, and `st.vega_lite_chart`, but removed it last year. Pyplot is the least important chart type; that's why we haven't done this deprecation yet. But instead of fixing up these aspects, we should just deprecate it and remove it in a couple of months.

A couple of related metrics: only ~0.7% of all `st.pyplot` uses pass in custom kwargs, and there has been only a single usage of `format` within the last couple of days.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Closing per [USER]'s comment on the fix PR (#16430): kwargs support in `st.pyplot` is planned for deprecation, so extending it to non-raster `format=` values isn't the right path forward. The upcoming deprecation of `**kwargs` on `st.pyplot` will retire this whole class of bug.

title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
text:
Issue #16474: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
Labels: type:bug, area:widgets, feature:st.slider

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.slider` accepts `date`/`datetime` bounds that the frontend cannot represent exactly, and silently snaps them to a different instant instead of reporting the problem. The `int` and `float` paths already validate and raise a helpful `StreamlitAPIException`; the timelike path does not.

Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and held in a JavaScript number on the frontend, so only about **1684-07-28 to 2255-06-05** round-trips exactly. Outside that, precision is lost.

`lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py` acknowledges the gap:

```python
elif all_timelikes:
    # No validation yet. TODO: check between 0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31
    pass
```

Worth noting the TODO's own target range is wrong — most of `0001`–`9999` is not representable, so validating to those limits would not have fixed it.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime as dt
import streamlit as st

# Silently accepted, but min_value cannot be represented exactly:
st.slider("historical", min_value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(1700, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(1600, 1, 1))

# Also silently accepted, both bounds unrepresentable:
st.slider("projection", min_value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1), max_value=dt.date(2400, 1, 1),
          value=dt.date(2300, 1, 1))

# Raises a bare OverflowError instead of a StreamlitAPIException:
st.slider("ancient", value=dt.date(1, 1, 1))
```

### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
text:
### Actual Behavior

Inspecting the serialized proto shows the bounds exceeding JavaScript's `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` with no error raised:

```
in-range 1900..2000      -> NO ERROR. min=-2208988800000000 max=946684800000000  JS-unsafe: none
historical 1600..1700    -> NO ERROR. min=-11676096000000000                      JS-unsafe: ['min']
far future 2300..2400    -> NO ERROR. min=10413792000000000 max=13569465600000000 JS-unsafe: ['min', 'max']
min date 0001..0002      -> OverflowError: date value out of range
```

Two distinct problems:

1. **Moderately out-of-range values are accepted and lose precision.** Years like 1600 or 2300 are ordinary in historical datasets and long-range projections, so this is not just an exotic edge case.
2. **Extreme values raise a bare `OverflowError`.** It comes from `prepared_value[0] - timedelta(days=14)`, which computes the *default* `min_value`/`max_value` even when the caller supplied both explicitly, and overflows next to `date.min`/`date.max`. This is not a `StreamlitAPIException`, so it surfaces as an unhandled Python error rather than actionable guidance.

### Expected Behavior

Out-of-range timelike bounds should raise a `StreamlitAPIException` naming the representable range, matching how the int and float paths already behave. Extreme values should produce that same message rather than an `OverflowError`.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduced at `f2648d7237`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: macOS 15.5

### Additional Information

Contrast with the existing int path, which is what the timelike path should mirror:

```
`max_value` (9007199254740992) must be <= (1 << 53) - 1
```

title: st.slider silently mis-represents dates outside the frontend number range
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a valid bug in `st.slider`'s date/datetime path. Timelike values are serialized as microseconds since the epoch and sent as JavaScript numbers, which only preserve exact integers within `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (~±2^53, roughly 1684–2255). Int/float sliders already reject out-of-range bounds via `JSNumber.validate_*_bounds`, but the timelike branch is explicitly a no-op (`# No validation yet`), so moderately out-of-range dates are accepted and silently lose precision. Separately, default `min_value`/`max_value` are always computed as `value ± timedelta(days=14)` before checking whether the caller supplied bounds, which raises a bare `OverflowError` near `date.min`/`date.max` instead of a `StreamlitAPIException`. Fixing this should validate the microsecond form against JS safe-integer limits (not the incorrect 0001–9999 TODO range) and avoid computing unused default bounds that can overflow.

### Related Issues

- [#7427](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7427) — `st.date_input` overflows when computing default selectable bounds near `datetime.max` (similar “default range buffer overflows date extrema” pattern; different widget).
- [#5099](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5099) — `st.slider` bounds-validation inconsistency vs `st.number_input` when `value` is outside `min`/`max` (related to slider bound checking, but not about JS safe-integer / date precision).

No duplicate found for silent JS-precision loss on date/datetime `st.slider` values.
