title: Add `dataframeHeaderTextColor` theme option for dataframe header text
text:
Issue #16478: Add `dataframeHeaderTextColor` theme option for dataframe header text
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.dataframe, feature:theming

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `dataframeHeaderTextColor` theme option to control the foreground (text) color of `st.dataframe` / `st.data_editor` column headers. Today `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` exists, but the header text color can't be customized — it's always derived from the body `textColor` (as `fadedText60`), so a custom/tinted/dark header background often results in weak or unreadable header text.

### Why?

Users can already set a custom header background via `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`, but there's no matching control for the header text. With a dark or strongly tinted header background, the faded, body-derived header text has poor contrast and can be hard to read. A dedicated `dataframeHeaderTextColor` lets the header background and foreground be styled together for a readable, on-brand look.

### How?

Add a theme config option, e.g.:

```toml
[theme]
dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor = "#1f2937"
dataframeHeaderTextColor = "#ffffff"
```

Implementation notes:
- Wire it through the dataframe's custom theme so it overrides the header text color instead of the hardcoded default.
- In the frontend this currently maps to the glide-data-grid `textHeader` (and likely `textGroupHeader`), which today is set to `theme.colors.fadedText60`:

```117:119:frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DataFrame/hooks/useCustomTheme.ts
      textHeader: theme.colors.fadedText60,
      textHeaderSelected: theme.colors.white,
      textGroupHeader: theme.colors.fadedText60,
```

- If unset, fall back to today's derived default (so nothing changes for existing apps).

### Additional Context

### Summary

When using `st.color_picker` the component does not work when it's inside `st.dialog`.  Clicking on the coloured square opens the color pallete, but any interaction with that pallete is imposible.

Putting the element inside a popover fixes the issue. I have tested `st.column`, `st.expander` and neither of them fix the issue like `st.dialog`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

[USER].dialog("Example dialog")
def example_dialog():
    color = st.color_picker("Color picker inside dialog")
    st.text(color)

    with st.popover("Example popover"):
        color = st.color_picker("Color picker inside dialog inside popover")
        st.text(color)


color = st.color_picker("Color picker inside dialog inside popover")
st.text(color)

st.button("Click me", on_click=example_dialog)
```

1. Create `st.dialog`
2. Create `st.color_picker` inside that dialog
3. Try to interact with the `st.color_picker`

The color pallete would be interactable with inside st.dialog.

### Current Behavior

Upon clicking on `st.color_picker` that is inside `st.dialog` the color pallete dropdown opens, but user cannot interact with it with mouse nor keyboard.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend bug: `st.color_picker` opens its palette inside `st.dialog`, but mouse and keyboard interaction with the palette fail. Likely root cause: `BaseColorPicker` mounts via `<FloatingPortal>` without `id={FLOATING_OVERLAY_PORTAL_ID}`, so the popover is not under the shared host tagged with `data-react-aria-top-layer` / `data-st-overlay-root`. React Aria’s dialog then treats that portal as outside the modal (often marking it `inert`), which matches “opens but cannot interact.” Nesting under `st.popover` can appear to work because popover already uses that portal host. The same fix pattern used for date_input / selectbox / popover-in-dialog overlays should apply here.

### Related Issues

- [#16005](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16005) — Popover content inside a dialog was unusable for the same React Aria overlay/`inert` reason; fixed by routing Floating UI portals through `FLOATING_OVERLAY_PORTAL_ID`. Closest prior art for this bug.
- [#15859](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15859) — `st.date_input` calendar rendered behind / unusable inside `st.dialog` (overlay stacking after the React Aria dialog migration). Same dialog + portaled overlay family.
- [#15599](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15599) — Selectbox dropdown behind `st.dialog` so clicks did not register. Same class of dialog overlay interaction issues.

No exact open duplicate found for `st.color_picker` specifically.

text:
Issue #16539: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.metric

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When an `st.metric` (that has previously been rendered with a sparkline and then again with no data) is re-rendered with `chart_data` going from empty/None (no sparkline) to a populated list (sparkline expected), the sparkline frequently fails to mount. The metric value and delta update correctly; only the embedded chart is missing. It reproduces reliably on the first
"no data -> data" transition and is unaffected by the data itself.

### Reproducible Code Example

title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
text:
### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Metric Chart Issue Demo", layout="wide")

# Realistic-looking weekly data (~52 weeks)
# fmt: off
CHART_DATA_WITH = [
    5, 8, 12, 7, 9, 15, 11, 13, 8, 10, 14, 6, 9, 11, 13, 7,
    10, 12, 8, 14, 9, 11, 7, 13, 10, 8, 12, 9, 11, 14, 7, 10,
    13, 8, 11, 9, 12, 7, 14, 10, 8, 13, 11, 9, 12, 7, 10, 14,
    8, 11, 13, 9,
]  # 52 values
# fmt: on

CHART_DATA_WITHOUT = []

st.title("Metric Chart Rendering Issue")

use_workaround = st.toggle("Enable Container Workaround", value=False)
st.caption("Toggle ON to see the mitigation that reduces (but doesn't eliminate) the issue")

# Dropdown (default to "With Data")
dataset = st.selectbox("Select Dataset", ["With Data", "Without Data"], index=0)

# Determine data based on selection
if dataset == "With Data":
    chart_1 = CHART_DATA_WITH
    chart_2 = [x * 2 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    chart_3 = [x * 0.5 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    chart_4 = [x * 1.5 for x in CHART_DATA_WITH]
    metric_val = 42
    delta_val = 5
else:
    chart_1 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_2 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_3 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    chart_4 = CHART_DATA_WITHOUT
    metric_val = 0
    delta_val = 0

# Generate timestamp for workaround keys
if use_workaround:
    base_timestamp = int(time.time() * 1000)

# Four metric cards - conditional rendering based on workaround toggle
if not use_workaround:
    # Path A: No workaround (default)
    col1, col2, col3, col4 = st.columns(4)

    with col1:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 1",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_1 if chart_1 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col2:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 2",
            value=int(metric_val * 2),
            delta=int(delta_val * 2),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_2 if chart_2 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col3:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 3",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_3 if chart_3 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col4:
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 4",
            value=int(metric_val * 1.5),
            delta=round(delta_val * 1.5, 1),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_4 if chart_4 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )
else:
    # Path B: With single-container workaround
    col1, col2, col3, col4 = st.columns(4)

    with col1, st.container(key=f"col1_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 1",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_1 if chart_1 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col2, st.container(key=f"col2_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 2",
            value=int(metric_val * 2),
            delta=int(delta_val * 2),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_2 if chart_2 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col3, st.container(key=f"col3_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 3",
            value=metric_val,
            delta=delta_val,
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_3 if chart_3 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

    with col4, st.container(key=f"col4_{dataset}_{base_timestamp}"):
        st.metric(
            label="Metric 4",
            value=int(metric_val * 1.5),
            delta=round(delta_val * 1.5, 1),
            delta_color="normal",
            chart_data=chart_4 if chart_4 else None,
            chart_type="bar",
            border=True,
        )

st.markdown("---")
st.markdown("""
### How to Reproduce

**Without Workaround (Toggle OFF - default):**
1. Start with "With Data" selected (default)
2. Switch to "Without Data" - charts should disappear
3. Switch back to "With Data" - **charts are expected to fail to appear**

**With Workaround (Toggle ON):**
1. Enable the "Container Workaround" toggle above
2. Repeat steps 1-3 - charts should appear more reliably (but may still occasionally fail)

---

**Expected**: Charts appear when switching to "With Data"  
**Actual (no workaround)**: Charts consistently fail to render after first transition  
**Actual (with workaround)**: Charts usually render, but may still occasionally fail

**Workaround**: Wrap each metric in a keyed container with a timestamp-based unique key. 
This forces Streamlit to create fresh component instances on each render, which appears 
to reduce (but not eliminate) the rendering issue.

---

**Environment**: Streamlit 1.57.0, 1.60.0, and 1.61.1 (reproduces on all)

**Other Mitigation Strategies Attempted:**
- Double-container wrapping (nested containers with unique keys) - slightly better than 
  single container
- Using `st.empty()` placeholders before containers - no improvement
- Session state counters for key generation - worse performance
- Explicit data validation (converting empty lists to None) - no improvement

The single-container workaround shown in this demo provides the best balance of simplicity 
and reliability improvement.
""")
```

title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

Instructions also included inline in code example to view while executing.

Steps (with the "Container Workaround" toggle OFF):

1. Load the page with "With Data" selected. All four metric cards show sparklines.
2. Select "Without Data". Charts clear; values go to 0. (expected)
3. Select "With Data" again. Values return, but the sparklines do NOT render.

Additional browser console check:

The sparkline renders as `[data-testid="stMetricChart"]` containing an `<svg>`.
Run in the browser console after step 3:

```
    (() => {
      const m = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="stMetric"]')];
      return {
        cards: m.length,
        withChart: m.filter(c => c.querySelector('[data-testid="stMetricChart"] svg')).length,
      };
    })()
```

Healthy: `withChart === cards`. Bug: `withChart < cards` (typically 0) after
the transition, even though the metric values are correct.

### Expected Behavior

- Expected: selecting "With Data" repopulates both the values and the sparklines. Continually going between data/no data should update the chart correctly each time
- Actual: values repopulate; sparklines are sometimes absent after the transition. Somewhat better with extra container hacks, but never 100% correct

### Current Behavior

title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
text:
### Current Behavior

All covered in the code, but in general:
* I display a few metric cards with data to start.
* Then I change to the card not being backed by any data by setting `chart_data` to None or an empty list (this is an approximation of what my app is doing, but gets the point across...I have data sometimes and then users can switch to selections that have no data for whatever reason). Everything works to here
* Then another selection adds data back to the the card. 
* Everything on the cards functions as expected except the sparkline chart. The chart may or may not re-render. In my experience, without any mitigation the chart will not re-render the vast majority of the time. With shenanigans like additional container indirection, it might re-render more often but never have I seen it work every time.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit: reproduced on 1.57.0, 1.60.0, and 1.61.1 (not fixed by the upgrades)
- Python: 3.13
- Browser: Chromium 149.0.7827.200 and Firefox 140.12.0esr (also observed in normal app use across browsers and operating systems including MacOS and Windows of various versions. I cannot tell you what browsers were involved there tho)
- OS: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 (Plow)

### Additional Information

title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
text:
### Additional Information

- Direction-specific: "no data -> data" fails; "data -> no data" is fine.
- Wrapping each metric in a keyed `st.container` with a per-run unique key reduces the failure rate but does not eliminate it. A second nested keyed container helps marginally more.
- Using a monotonic session-state counter for the keys made it worse, and converting empty lists to None had no effect - suggesting the issue is a frontend component-lifecycle timing race, not key collision or data handling.
- In case it's useful, in my case the dropdown selection would map to a DB query that is returned in a pandas dataframe. Once the query has been fetched once, it's cached for 24 hrs

title: st.metric sparkline (chart_data) fails to render after a no-data -> data transition
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend bug in `st.metric` sparklines: after a `chart_data` empty→populated transition, the metric value/delta update but the Vega-Lite chart often never remounts. Likely root cause is in `Metric.tsx` + `useResizeObserver`: the chart container is conditionally rendered only when `chartData.length > 0`, and `vega-embed` runs only when `chartWidth > 0`. On unmount (data→no-data), the ResizeObserver can clear width to the `-1` fallback, but its effect does not re-subscribe when the container remounts because dependencies stay unchanged—so width never becomes positive again and embed is skipped. That matches the direction-specific failure and why keyed-container remounts partially help. There is also no `vega-embed` cleanup/`finalize` on effect teardown.

### Related Issues

- [#13785](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13785) — Closed bug for `st.metric` + `chart_data` layout in horizontal containers; same sparkline feature surface (not a duplicate of this lifecycle bug).
- [#12859](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12859) — Similar “fails to render after mount/visibility transition” pattern (`st.pdf` in a collapsed expander), though for a different element.
- [#8495](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8495) — Original enhancement that introduced metric sparklines; useful historical context, not a duplicate.

No clear open duplicate of this empty→data sparkline remount failure was found.

title: Connection error
text:
[COLLABORATOR] [USER] which version of Streamlit are you using? This has been an issue in older versions but should be fixed in the latest version.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This report is the well-known **Cached ForwardMsg MISS** WebSocket error: the server sent a `ref_hash` for a cacheable delta, but the frontend `ForwardMsgCache` did not have that hash (`cd4746dc1df6dcfb073b12276a2c9e39`). That happens when `cached_message_hashes` in a rerun `BackMsg` is out of sync with the client cache — historically from a race where a previous run’s `scriptFinished` expired entries still referenced by a new run (fixed in PR #11302 / 1.45.1), and from Streamlit-in-Snowflake’s initial response cache serving refs to clients that never received the original payloads. The issue has no Streamlit version, repro, or environment, so it cannot be distinguished from those already-fixed cases versus a remaining desync. A maintainer already asked for the version; if this still happens on a current OSS release, a minimal repro (and whether it is OSS vs SiS) is needed.

### Related Issues

- [#11357](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11357) — Same `Cached ForwardMsg MISS` connection dialog; main tracking issue after the 1.45.1 patch, later closed as fixed (including SiS rollout).
- [#11299](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11299) — Original confirmed race with slider + large dataframe under network lag; closed by PR [#11302](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/11302), which ignores stale `scriptFinished` cache cleanup.
- [#15816](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15816) — Most recent identical sparse report (July 2026); closed as cannot-reproduce after no version or repro was provided.

title: `st.iframe` hardcodes the frame title, so every embed on a page has the same accessible name
text:
### Current Behavior

Both frames have the accessible name `st.iframe`. A screen-reader user tabbing the page hears "st.iframe, frame" twice and has nothing to tell the charts apart.

### Scope

All three embedding paths share the frame component and none accepts a title:

| API | accepts `title`? | rendered `title` |
|---|---|---|
| `st.iframe` | no | `st.iframe` |
| `st.components.v1.iframe` | no | `st.iframe` |
| `st.components.v1.html` | no | `st.iframe` |

Verified on **Streamlit 1.61.1** by rendering all three on one page: three frames, one distinct accessible name.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: not a factor — the title is emitted by the frontend, independent of the Python version
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

### Where it comes from

In the shipped frontend bundle the title is a literal in the element's props, immediately beside a prop that *is* forwarded from the component's arguments:

```js
title: `st.iframe`, tabIndex: e.tabIndex ?? void 0
```

So the plumbing to pass a value through already exists on this element; `title` simply is not wired to it.

### Suggested fix

Add an optional `title` to `st.iframe` (and the two `components.v1` entry points), forwarded to the element and defaulting to the current literal so nothing changes for existing apps.

### Workaround, and why it is not sufficient

title: `st.iframe` hardcodes the frame title, so every embed on a page has the same accessible name
text:
### Suggested fix

Add an optional `title` to `st.iframe` (and the two `components.v1` entry points), forwarded to the element and defaulting to the current literal so nothing changes for existing apps.

### Workaround, and why it is not sufficient

Placing an `st.caption` or a heading next to each embed gives a sighted-adjacent cue and helps somewhat. It does not fix the frame's own accessible name, which is what is announced when focus enters the frame and what appears in a screen reader's list of frames.

Related note: because the frame's name cannot be set, adding a tab stop on it with `tab_index=0` makes the situation worse rather than better — every stop announces "st.iframe" — so embedding libraries are pushed to leave the frame out of the tab order entirely.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a valid accessibility bug, not a duplicate. `st.iframe`, `st.components.v1.iframe`, and `st.components.v1.html` all render through the same frontend `IFrame` component, which hardcodes `title="st.iframe"`. An iframe’s accessible name comes from that attribute, so multiple embeds on one page are announced identically (WCAG 2.2 4.1.2). The IFrame protobuf currently only carries `src`/`srcdoc`, `scrolling`, and `tab_index` — there is no `title` field, and none of the three Python APIs accept one. `tabIndex` is already forwarded from proto to the element, so an optional `title` (defaulting to `"st.iframe"`) would follow the same pattern without changing existing apps. Custom components v1 already set `title={componentName}` on their iframes, so they are not affected in the same way.

- [#8399](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8399) — Broader request for basic web accessibility (page language, named structure). This iframe-title gap is a concrete instance of that theme.

title: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
text:
Issue #16611: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:app-testing, feature:st.navigation

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`AppTest.switch_page(page_path)` computes the target page hash from the page's **file
name**. But `st.navigation` identifies each `st.Page` by its **`url_path`**. When a page
sets a custom `url_path` that differs from its file name, the two hashes disagree:
`switch_page` sets a `_page_hash` that matches no registered page, and the script runner
**silently falls back to the default page** instead of navigating to the requested one (and
without raising).

This makes it impossible to test navigation to any page declared like
`st.Page("other.py", url_path="custom")`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
See below.
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Files (all in one directory):

`home.py`

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("HOME PAGE")
```

`other.py`

```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("OTHER PAGE")
```

`app.py`

```python
import streamlit as st

home = st.Page("home.py", default=True)
other = st.Page("other.py", url_path="custom")  # url_path != file name ("other")

st.navigation([home, other]).run()
```

`test_switch_page.py`

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest


def test_switch_to_page_with_custom_url_path():
    at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run()
    assert at.markdown[0].value == "HOME PAGE"

    at.switch_page("other.py").run()

    assert at.markdown[0].value == "OTHER PAGE"  # FAILS: is "HOME PAGE"
```

Run pytest:

```
$ pytest test_switch_page.py
E       AssertionError: assert 'HOME PAGE' == 'OTHER PAGE'
```

### Expected Behavior

title: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
text:
Run pytest:

```
$ pytest test_switch_page.py
E       AssertionError: assert 'HOME PAGE' == 'OTHER PAGE'
```

### Expected Behavior

`at.switch_page("other.py").run()` renders the `other` page (or, if the path can't be resolved to a registered page, raises a clear error).

### Current Behavior

The default page is rendered, silently.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.13.15
- Operating System: Linux (WSL2) — also expected on macOS/Windows; not platform-specific

### Additional Information

#### Root cause

`AppTest.switch_page` derives the hash from the file name
(`streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py`):

```python
page_path_str = str(full_page_path.resolve())
_, page_name = page_icon_and_name(Path(page_path_str))
self._page_hash = calc_hash(page_name)          # hash of the FILE NAME
```

but `st.navigation` registers each page under a hash derived from its `url_path`
(`streamlit/navigation/page.py`):

```python
[USER]
def _script_hash(self) -> str:
    return calc_hash(self._url_path)             # hash of the URL PATH
```

`self._url_path` defaults to the file-name-derived slug, so the two hashes coincide **only
when `url_path` is not overridden**. With a custom `url_path`, `calc_hash(page_name)`
matches no registered page, so the runner uses the default page instead.

#### Suggested fix

title: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
text:
`self._url_path` defaults to the file-name-derived slug, so the two hashes coincide **only
when `url_path` is not overridden**. With a custom `url_path`, `calc_hash(page_name)`
matches no registered page, so the runner uses the default page instead.

#### Suggested fix

Resolve the requested page against the app's registered navigation pages (via the
`PagesManager` / `st.navigation` result), matching by resolved script path, and use that
page's actual `_script_hash` (which respects `url_path`) for `_page_hash`. Because the
navigation config is only known once the app runs, this can be done by deferring resolution
to the next `run()` (store the requested path in `switch_page`, resolve it against the
freshly built pages when running).

At minimum — even without full resolution — `switch_page`/`run` should **raise a clear
error when the computed hash matches no registered page**, rather than silently rendering
the default page, so the failure is not hidden from test authors.

#### Workaround

Set `_page_hash` to the `url_path`-based hash directly for the affected pages:

```python
from streamlit.util import calc_hash

at._page_hash = calc_hash("custom")  # the page's url_path
at.run()
```

title: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16611)


[CONTRIBUTOR] `AppTest.switch_page()` hashes the **file-name slug** (`calc_hash(page_name)` from `page_icon_and_name`), while `st.Page._script_hash` hashes the page’s **`url_path`**. Those hashes match only when `url_path` is left as the inferred filename; a custom `url_path` produces a hash that matches no registered page. `PagesManager._resolve_page_script` then silently falls back to the default page (`send_page_not_found` only enqueues a proto; AppTest does not raise). This is a real testing-framework bug, not a product-API issue. A robust fix is to resolve the requested script path against pages registered by `st.navigation` and use that page’s `_script_hash`, and/or raise when the computed hash is unknown.

### Related Issues

- [#9446](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9446) — AppTest originally failed to render `st.navigation` pages at all (now closed; callable-page coverage landed). This issue is a remaining gap: file pages with a custom `url_path` still cannot be reached via `AppTest.switch_page()`.
- [#10572](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10572) — `st.switch_page` / `st.page_link` identify pages by `url_path` and can silently land on the wrong page instead of erroring. Same identity/fallback pattern as this AppTest hash mismatch.
- [#8154](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8154) — AppTest page-path resolution (relative `st.page_link` paths). Related AppTest multipage-path handling, not a duplicate.

title: Text overflow from expander container in sidebar
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16618)


[CONTRIBUTOR] Long unbreakable markdown (file paths in list items) overflows the bordered `st.expander` when it is placed in `st.sidebar`. This looks like a CSS min-content issue rather than an expander animation bug: markdown uses `overflow-wrap: break-word` (and `word-break: break-word` only on `p`, not `li`), which does not shrink a flex item’s min-content width, while the expander details panel is `overflow: visible` with no `min-width: 0`. Nested flex layout (sidebar → expander → block) then lets long tokens paint past the expander border. A likely fix is `overflow-wrap: anywhere` / `word-break` on list content plus containing overflow on the expander panel. `#12366` addressed the same wrapping class in bordered containers and shipped in 1.49, but this 1.52 sidebar+expander case still reproduces.

**Related issues:**
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12366 — Same long-token markdown overflow in a bordered container; closed by adding `overflow-wrap: break-word`, which appears insufficient inside the sidebar expander flex layout.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6394 — Long markdown (inline code) overflowing nested alert containers; same wrapping failure mode in a constrained parent.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9387 — Nested content overflowing the sidebar viewport (`st.popover`); related sidebar overflow, different mechanism (positioning vs. text wrapping).

title: Text overflow from expander container in sidebar
text:
[COLLABORATOR] **Note**: This is a markdown list sizing regression rather than an `st.expander` or sidebar bug. 
Top-level lists carry `width: fit-content`, which is floored at `min-content`, and the `overflow-wrap: break-word` above it does not reduce `min-content` width — so a list holding an item too long to fit is sized to that item and never wraps. Paragraphs have `width: auto` and are unaffected, which is why the prose wraps and only the bullets spill. Introduced by #13036 (`text_alignment`) and shipped in 1.52.0.
**Impacted**: any container narrower than the longest list item. The sidebar clips the overflow, so the text is lost rather than just misaligned. 
**Not impacted**: full-width lists, lists whose items fit, nested lists, and widget labels.

text:
Issue #16630: Typing issue for `st.selectbox` when `index: int | None` & `accept_new_options=False`
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.selectbox, area:typing

### Checklist

- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello!

When I use `st.selectbox` with an dynamic index which can be `int | None`, with the default for `accept_new_options` (so should be False), the return type includes `str`, so gives `T | str | None` instead of `T | None`...

### Reproducible Code Example

import streamlit as st
from typing_extensions import assert_type

index: int | None = None

3. notice the error: (first line)

  --> main.py:12:12

12 | assert_type(result, int | None)

text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16630)


[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a real typing bug in `st.selectbox`, not a pyrefly-only issue. Overloads distinguish `index: int` vs `index: None` and `accept_new_options: Literal[False]` vs `Literal[True]`, then fall through to a catch-all of `index: int | None` + `accept_new_options: bool` that returns `T | str | None`. When `index` is typed as `int | None` (and `accept_new_options` is omitted / `False`), pyrefly/pyright cannot match the narrower overloads and pick that catch-all, so `str` appears in the return type even though a new option cannot be entered. mypy often expands the `index` union across overloads and reports `T | None`, which is why it stays silent. Existing type tests only cover literal `index=None` / `index=0`. A fix is to add an overload for `index: int | None` with `accept_new_options: Literal[False]` returning `T | None` (before the catch-all) and cover it in `lib/tests/streamlit/typing/selectbox_types.py`.

### Related Issues

- [#15529](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15529) (closed) — Incomplete `st.slider` overloads for type checkers; same class of bug where a union argument misses a specific overload.
- [#13487](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13487) (closed) — Incomplete public API type hints (`st.date_input`) that type checkers reject despite valid runtime usage.
- No open duplicate of this `st.selectbox` + `index: int | None` overload gap was found.

title: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
text:
Issue #16631: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.download_button, area:server

### Summary

The media endpoint that serves `st.download_button` files builds its `Content-Disposition` header by interpolating the download filename into a quoted string, `filename="{filename}"`, whenever the name is latin-1 encodable. A double quote is latin-1 encodable, so any filename containing one closes the quoted parameter early and the rest of the name spills out as trailing tokens. The emitted header is not valid per RFC 6266, and the name the browser saves the file under is no longer the name the app set.

This needs nothing adversarial to hit. An ordinary filename like `5" x 7" print.jpg` (inch marks) is enough. The name reaches this sink from `st.download_button(file_name=...)`, and since 1.61.0 also from the filename inferred off an uploaded file when `file_name` is omitted.

The safe branch already exists in the same function: a name that is not latin-1 encodable takes `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}`, which percent-encodes and cannot break out. The bug is only which branch a name reaches. Streamlit's own dependency, Starlette, makes the correct choice for the same header in `FileResponse` (`starlette/responses.py`), selecting the quoted form only when `quote(filename) == filename`.

### Reproducible Code Example

Fully in-process against the real media route, no browser needed:

title: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
text:
### Reproducible Code Example

Fully in-process against the real media route, no browser needed:

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.testclient import TestClient
from streamlit.runtime.media_file_storage import MediaFileKind
from streamlit.runtime.memory_media_file_storage import MemoryMediaFileStorage
from streamlit.web.server.starlette.starlette_routes import create_media_routes

# An ordinary filename: a 5 inch by 7 inch print. The inch marks are
# double quotes, which are perfectly valid in a filename.
filename = '5" x 7" print.jpg'

storage = MemoryMediaFileStorage("/media")
file_id = storage.load_and_get_id(
    b"jpeg-bytes", "image/jpeg", MediaFileKind.DOWNLOADABLE, filename
)
client = TestClient(Starlette(routes=create_media_routes(storage, "")))
response = client.get(storage.get_url(file_id))
print(response.headers["content-disposition"])
```

The same header is produced end to end from an app, without touching internals:

```python
import streamlit as st

uploaded = st.file_uploader("upload")
if uploaded:
    # The inch marks in the file_name break the emitted header.
    st.download_button("download", data=uploaded, file_name='5" x 7" print.jpg')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `pip install streamlit==1.61.1`
2. Save the first snippet above as `repro.py`.
3. Run `python repro.py`.
4. Observe the printed header: `attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"`. The `filename` parameter is terminated by the first `"` after `5`, so the value a conforming parser reads is not the name the app set.

### Expected Behavior

A filename with characters that are not safe unescaped inside a quoted string (a double quote, a semicolon, a space) should still be carried faithfully in a valid header, using the RFC 5987 `filename*=` form, exactly as the non-latin-1 branch already does and as Starlette's `FileResponse` does:

```
attachment; filename*=utf-8''5%22%20x%207%22%20print.jpg
```

### Current Behavior

title: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
text:
```
attachment; filename*=utf-8''5%22%20x%207%22%20print.jpg
```

### Current Behavior

The name is interpolated into `filename="..."` verbatim, so the double quote closes the parameter:

```
attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"
```

That is not a valid RFC 6266 header: the quoted string ends at the first unescaped `"`, and everything after it is stray tokens. A name that also contains `;` can introduce additional `Content-Disposition` parameters, so the header's structure ends up controlled by the filename rather than by Streamlit.

Root cause, `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py` in `_media_endpoint`:

```python
try:
    filename.encode("latin1")
    disposition = f'filename="{filename}"'
except UnicodeEncodeError:
    disposition = f"filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}"
headers["Content-Disposition"] = f"attachment; {disposition}"
```

The branch is selected on latin-1 encodability, but the property that matters is whether the value is safe unescaped inside a quoted parameter, and `"`, `;` and space are all latin-1 encodable.

### Fix direction

Select the branch the way Starlette's `FileResponse` does in `starlette/responses.py`: emit the plain `filename="..."` form only when `quote(filename) == filename`, and fall back to `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}` otherwise. This is a strict superset of the current safe branch (every non-latin-1 name still percent-encodes) and additionally routes latin-1 names that need escaping onto the safe form. Plain ASCII names like `report.pdf` keep the quoted form unchanged.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1 (present since 1.60.0; also on current `develop`)
- Python version: 3.10 - 3.14
- Operating System: any
- Browser: n/a (backend header construction; the visible effect is the saved download name)

title: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `st.download_button` serves files from the media endpoint, which builds `Content-Disposition` in `_media_endpoint` (`lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py`). Latin-1-encodable names are interpolated as `filename="{filename}"` with no escaping; only non-latin-1 names take the RFC 5987 `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}` form. A `"` is latin-1, so names like `5" x 7" print.jpg` emit `attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"`, which is not a valid RFC 6266 header and causes the browser to save the wrong name. The same path also accepts inferred names from file objects (since 1.61.0 / #14159), so this is not limited to an explicit `file_name=`. Existing tests cover the utf-8 branch and a space-containing quoted name, but not `"`. The latin-1 vs utf-8 split was added in #5465 to fix #5434; the missing piece is treating quoted-string-unsafe characters the way Starlette's `FileResponse` does (`quote(filename) == filename`).

### Related Issues

- [#5434](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5434) (closed) — Non-latin-1 `file_name` values crashed header encoding. PR [#5465](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/5465) added the latin-1 / `filename*=` split that this report shows is too narrow.
- [#5566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5566) (closed) — Docs discussion of RFC 6266 filename handling for `st.download_button`. Explicit `file_name` values are still passed through without escaping at the header boundary.
- [#14159](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14159) — Infer `file_name` from file-like `data.name`. That inference is now landed, so uploaded / on-disk names (which can contain `"`) also reach this header.

No duplicate of this specific quoted-string bug was found.

title: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
text:
[NONE] The triage analysis matches what I found, including the fix direction. I have that change ready on a branch:

[develop...skraft9:streamlit:fix/media-content-disposition-filename-escape](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/compare/develop...skraft9:streamlit:fix/media-content-disposition-filename-escape)

It selects the disposition branch on quoting safety (`quote(filename) == filename`), matching Starlette's `FileResponse`, rather than on latin-1 encodability. This is a strict superset of the current safe branch, so non-latin-1 names still percent-encode, latin-1 names that need escaping now take the `filename*=` form, and plain ASCII names like `report.pdf` keep the quoted form unchanged. It also drops the `try/except UnicodeEncodeError` in favor of the single equality test.

title: Guest-to-host messages are only posted to window.parent, so a same-window embed host never receives them (METRICS_EVENT is dropped)
text:
Issue #16644: Guest-to-host messages are only posted to window.parent, so a same-window embed host never receives them (METRICS_EVENT is dropped)
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:embedding

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`HostCommunicationManager.sendMessageToHost` posts only to `window.parent`. When Streamlit is
embedded such that the host code runs *in the app's own window* (an in-iframe embed
preamble/adapter, rather than in the parent frame), no guest-to-host message reaches the host,
because `window.parent` is a third-party page in this case.

`GUEST_READY` is the one exception: `openHostCommunication` additionally posts it to the app's
own window. Every other message, notably `METRICS_EVENT`, has no such path, so embedded apps
report app-load state correctly but emit **no metrics at all** to the host.

Notably, the library already assumes this topology in the opposite direction:
`receiveHostMessage` explicitly trusts same-window self-posts, with the comment
"an in-iframe embed preamble ... when there is no trusted parent frame to relay them
(`window.parent` is a third-party page)". Only the guest-to-host direction is missing it.

### Root cause

`frontend/lib/src/hostComm/HostCommunicationManager.tsx`

```ts
// :186 — parent only
public sendMessageToHost = (message: IGuestToHostMessage): void => {
  window.parent.postMessage(this.buildVersionedMessage(message), "*")
}

// :116-121 — the only same-window dispatch, GUEST_READY exclusive
if (window !== window.parent) {
  window.postMessage(this.buildVersionedMessage(guestReadyMessage), window.location.origin)
}
```

1. Embed a Streamlit app in a cross-origin page, with host code running inside the app's own
   window (i.e. the host listens via `window.addEventListener("message", ...)` in the app frame,

2. Set `metricsUrl: "postMessage"` in the host config and leave `browser.gatherUsageStats` at

`pageProfile`) along with the other guest-to-host messages.

**Actual:** only the *parent* frame receives them. The in-window host receives `GUEST_READY`
and nothing else.

### Expected Behavior

When Streamlit is embedded such that the host code runs inside the app's own window (an
in-iframe embed preamble/adapter rather than code in the parent frame), the host should receive
all guest-to-host messages — including METRICS_EVENT (`viewReport`, `updateReport`,
`pageProfile`) when the host config sets `metricsUrl: "postMessage"`.

### Current Behavior

`sendMessageToHost` posts only to `window.parent`, which in the embedding case is the third-party
embedding page and not the host. So the in-window host receives nothing.

### Current Behavior

`sendMessageToHost` posts only to `window.parent`, which in the embedding case is the third-party
embedding page and not the host. So the in-window host receives nothing.

The single exception is GUEST_READY, which `openHostCommunication` additionally posts to the
app's own window. The result is that app-load/readiness signalling works, while every other
message is silently invisible to the host, most visibly METRICS_EVENT, so embedded apps report
no usage metrics at all despite `browser.gatherUsageStats` being true and `metricsUrl` being
correctly set to "postMessage".

`pageProfile` all arrive at the parent frame, and only GUEST_READY arrives in the app's own
window. MetricsManager itself behaves correctly: it takes the `postMessageEvent` branch and
builds the event; the message is just delivered to a window the host is not in.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a real guest-to-host delivery bug in `HostCommunicationManager.sendMessageToHost`: it only `postMessage`s to `window.parent`. In the in-iframe embed topology (host preamble in the app frame; `window.parent` is a third-party page), that means the host never sees guest messages. `GUEST_READY` is the only exception — `openHostCommunication` also posts it to the app’s own window — which is why readiness works while `METRICS_EVENT` (`viewReport` / `updateReport` / `pageProfile`) and every other guest-to-host type are dropped. `MetricsManager` is not at fault: with `metricsUrl === "postMessage"` it correctly calls `sendMessageToHost`. The host-to-guest path already trusts same-window self-posts (`receiveHostMessage`), so the gap is one-directional. A same-window echo of all guest-to-host messages is a reasonable fix, but it must be tagged (e.g. `isGuestToHostEcho`) because `UPDATE_HASH` exists in both directions and would otherwise be executed as a host command if the app origin is allow-listed. `sendMessageToSameOriginHost` has the same parent-only limitation (used for `REDIRECT_TO_URL`).

### Related Issues

- [PR #14790](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14790) — added the same-window `GUEST_READY` dispatch this issue wants generalized to all guest-to-host messages.
- [PR #16327](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16327) — the host-to-guest counterpart: trusts same-window self-posts so an in-iframe preamble can deliver `SET_AUTH_TOKEN` when the parent is untrusted.
- [PR #15800](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15800) — the source/`isTrusted` guard that made untagged self-posts unsafe; any echo of guest-to-host traffic has to be ignored by `receiveHostMessage`.

No duplicate open issues found.

text:
class SingletonMeta(type):
    """
    A thread-safe implementation of Singleton using a metaclass.
    """
    _instances = {}
    _lock: threading.Lock = threading.Lock()

    def __call__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
        # Double-checked locking pattern to prevent unnecessary lock acquisition
        if cls not in cls._instances:
            with cls._lock:
                # The first thread to acquire the lock creates the instance
                if cls not in cls._instances:
                    instance = super().__call__(*args, **kwargs)
                    cls._instances[cls] = instance
        return cls._instances[cls]

class DatabaseConnectionPool(metaclass=SingletonMeta):
    """
    Example usage: A database connection pool that must only have one instance.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.connection_string = "postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/mydb"
        self.is_connected = False
        print("Initializing Database Connection Pool...")

    def connect(self):
        if not self.is_connected:
            print(f"Connecting to {self.connection_string}")
            self.is_connected = True

# Usage Example
if __name__ == "__main__":
    def get_db_instance():
        db = DatabaseConnectionPool()
        print(f"Instance ID: {id(db)}")

    # Launching multiple threads to test thread safety
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=get_db_instance) for _ in range(5)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join()

title: is_mem_address_str() fails on uppercase hex addresses, breaking st.write() and st.help() object rendering on Windows
text:
Issue #16674: is_mem_address_str() fails on uppercase hex addresses, breaking st.write() and st.help() object rendering on Windows
Labels: type:bug, area:windows, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.help, feature:st.write

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`is_mem_address_str()` in `lib/streamlit/string_util.py` matches memory-address reprs with the regex `^\<[a-zA-Z_]+[a-zA-Z0-9<>._ ]* at 0x[0-9a-f]+\>$`. The address group only accepts **lowercase** hex digits. On Windows, CPython formats object addresses with **uppercase** hex (e.g. `<__main__.Foo object at 0x0000027B0C1B1550>`), so the function returns `False` for essentially every real object repr on that platform.

Both callers of this helper then take the wrong branch: `st.write(obj)` stops routing plain objects to the object-help view and prints the raw memory address instead, and `st.help()` renders memory addresses as member values while dropping those members' docstrings.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st


class Foo:
    """A Foo."""

    x = 1

    [USER]
    def e(self):
        "Property e"
        return 5


st.write(Foo())   # expected: rich object-help view. On Windows: raw memory address as inline code.
st.help(Foo)      # expected: property `e` documented. On Windows: "<property object at 0x...>".
```

Minimal check of the helper itself:

```python
from streamlit.string_util import is_mem_address_str


class Foo:
    pass


print(repr(Foo()))                  # <__main__.Foo object at 0x0000023FFDF98AD0>
print(is_mem_address_str(repr(Foo())))          # False   <-- should be True
print(is_mem_address_str("<foo blarg at 0x15ee6f9a0>"))  # True (lowercase only)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: is_mem_address_str() fails on uppercase hex addresses, breaking st.write() and st.help() object rendering on Windows
text:
Minimal check of the helper itself:

```python
from streamlit.string_util import is_mem_address_str


class Foo:
    pass


print(repr(Foo()))                  # <__main__.Foo object at 0x0000023FFDF98AD0>
print(is_mem_address_str(repr(Foo())))          # False   <-- should be True
print(is_mem_address_str("<foo blarg at 0x15ee6f9a0>"))  # True (lowercase only)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. On Windows, run either snippet above (or just the plain-Python helper check — no browser needed).
2. Observe that `is_mem_address_str` returns `False` for a repr it is explicitly designed to detect.

### Expected Behavior

`is_mem_address_str()` should recognize a CPython memory-address repr regardless of the hex casing produced by the platform's C runtime. Consequently:

- `st.write(obj)` renders the object-help view for an object with no other special handling.
- `st.help(SomeClass)` shows the property's docstring and leaves the value slot empty rather than printing a memory address.

### Current Behavior

On Windows (verified with `AppTest`):

```
markdown elements: ['`<__main__.Foo object at 0x0000027B0C1B1550>`']
help elements    : 0
```

`st.help` on a class with a `[USER]`:

```
name='e' type='property' value='<property object at 0x000002500A1F3240>' doc=''
```

versus the same class instance, which takes the other code path and is correct:

```
name='e' type='property' value='' doc='Property e'
```

The repository's own tests catch this — they currently fail on Windows for exactly this reason:

- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_obj_instance` → `AssertionError: Expected 'help' to be called once. Called 0 times.`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_repr_html`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_repr_html_no_html_tags_in_string`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_repr_html_not_callable`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/help_test.py::StHelpTest::test_class_members` → `assert '<property ob...>' == ''`

They pass on Linux/macOS because glibc's `%p` formatting yields lowercase hex, which is why CI has not caught it.

### Root Cause

`lib/streamlit/string_util.py:250-252`

title: is_mem_address_str() fails on uppercase hex addresses, breaking st.write() and st.help() object rendering on Windows
text:
They pass on Linux/macOS because glibc's `%p` formatting yields lowercase hex, which is why CI has not caught it.

### Root Cause

`lib/streamlit/string_util.py:250-252`

```python
_OBJ_MEM_ADDRESS: Final = re.compile(
    r"^\<[a-zA-Z_]+[a-zA-Z0-9<>._ ]* at 0x[0-9a-f]+\>$"
)
```

`[0-9a-f]+` cannot match `0000027B0C1B1550`.

### Suggested Fix

Accept both casings, e.g. `[0-9a-fA-F]+` (or add `re.IGNORECASE`).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `is_mem_address_str()` returns `True` for uppercase-hex reprs such as `<__main__.Foo object at 0x0000027B0C1B1550>`.
- [ ] `st.write(obj)` produces a help element (not a markdown memory address) on Windows.
- [ ] `st.help(SomeClass)` no longer renders `<property object at 0x...>` and preserves property docstrings.
- [ ] A regression test covers an uppercase-hex address string so the behavior is asserted independently of the host platform.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Unknown — the regex appears long-standing.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: n/a (reproduced headlessly via `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest` and direct function calls)

### Additional Information

The two affected call sites are `lib/streamlit/elements/help.py:482` and `lib/streamlit/elements/write.py:576`.

text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] I have a fix with tests ready, but this repository limits opening pull requests to collaborators, so I can't submit it as a PR. Posting the patch here in case a maintainer wants to pick it up.

Branch: https://github.com/rajarshidattapy/streamlit/tree/fix/mem-address-regex-uppercase-hex

The library change is one character class:

```diff
+# CPython renders the address with the platform C runtime's pointer format, which
+# is lowercase hex on glibc but uppercase hex on Windows, so accept both.
 _OBJ_MEM_ADDRESS: Final = re.compile(
-    r"^\<[a-zA-Z_]+[a-zA-Z0-9<>._ ]* at 0x[0-9a-f]+\>$"
+    r"^\<[a-zA-Z_]+[a-zA-Z0-9<>._ ]* at 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+\>$"
 )
```

Plus two tests in `lib/tests/streamlit/string_util_test.py`: a parameterized case covering both hex casings and three non-address strings, and one that asserts against a repr produced by the running interpreter, so the behavior stays pinned on whichever platform CI runs.

Verification on Windows (Python 3.13.6, `develop` @ `2ac0d77d3`):

- The five existing tests named in the issue now pass: `write_test.py::test_obj_instance`, `::test_repr_html`, `::test_repr_html_no_html_tags_in_string`, `::test_repr_html_not_callable`, and `elements/help_test.py::StHelpTest::test_class_members`.
- Full `string_util_test.py` passes (111 tests); `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.
- `st.write(Foo())` now emits a `help_info` element instead of rendering a raw memory address as markdown.

title: is_mem_address_str() fails on uppercase hex addresses, breaking st.write() and st.help() object rendering on Windows
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a Windows-only bug in `is_mem_address_str()` (`lib/streamlit/string_util.py`). The `_OBJ_MEM_ADDRESS` regex uses `[0-9a-f]+`, so it fails on CPython's uppercase `%p` addresses (e.g. `0x0000027B0C1B1550`). `st.write()` then treats a default object `str()` as markdown instead of routing to the help view, and `st.help()` shows memory addresses as member values (dropping property docstrings). Existing tests (`write_test.py::test_obj_instance`, `help_test.py::test_class_members`) already encode the expected behavior but use live host `repr()`s, so they fail on Windows and pass on Linux/macOS CI. There is no dedicated `is_mem_address_str` unit test covering uppercase hex. The one-character-class fix (`[0-9a-fA-F]+`) plus a platform-independent uppercase-hex case looks correct; the reporter also posted a ready patch.

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
text:
Issue #16675: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.slider

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`_slider()` tries to swap reversed bounds with two sequential statements, but the second one reads the variable the first one just overwrote:

```python
# lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py:1081-1083
# Ensure that min <= value(s) <= max, adjusting the bounds as necessary.
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)   # <-- min_value is already the new (smaller) value
```

After line 1082, `min_value` is `min(a, b)`, so line 1083 evaluates `max(min(a, b), b)`, which is always `b`. The original `min_value` can never become the upper bound, so the intended swap never happens. Depending on what `value` is, this silently produces a wrong range or raises an exception quoting numbers the user never passed.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

# 1. Bounds silently reinterpreted
st.slider("a", 10, 1)                                  # -> range 1..10, value 10

# 2. Upper bound silently invented from `value`
st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)     # -> range 1..5  (max_value=1 is gone)

# 3. Spurious exception quoting numbers the user never passed
st.slider("c", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=1)     # -> StreamlitAPIException
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any of the three lines above.
2. Compare the resulting slider bounds against the arguments passed.

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any of the three lines above.
2. Compare the resulting slider bounds against the arguments passed.

### Expected Behavior

Either of the following would be self-consistent:

- Reject reversed bounds with a clear error naming the two values the caller actually supplied, the way `st.date_input` already does:
  > The `min_value`, set to 2024-01-02, shouldn't be larger than the `max_value`, set to 2024-01-01.
- Or genuinely swap them, so `st.slider("a", 10, 1)` yields a `1..10` slider — which is what the code comment says it intends.

Today it does neither reliably.

### Current Behavior

Verified with `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`:

```
slider(min=10, max=1)            -> min=1.0 max=10.0 value=10
slider(min=10, max=1, value=5)   -> min=1.0 max=5.0  value=5
slider(min=10, max=1, value=1)   -> RAISED: Slider `min_value` must be less than the `max_value`.
                                            The values were 1 and 1.
```

Note case 3: the user passed `10` and `1`, but the error reports "The values were 1 and 1" — both numbers have been overwritten by the faulty normalization. Case 2 is the most damaging, because it silently produces a slider whose upper bound (`5`) was never supplied as a bound at all; it leaked in from `value`.

Isolating just the two lines:

```python
min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 1     <-- current behavior

min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 10    <-- intended
```

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
text:
The `min_value == max_value` guard at line 1137 then fires on values that are an artifact of this bug rather than of user input, and it only catches the case where the corruption happens to collapse both bounds to the same number — which is why `st.slider("x", 5, 5)` errors while `st.slider("x", 10, 1)` does not.

### Suggested Fix

Assign both bounds simultaneously (or compute the max from the original value):

```python
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
```

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)` no longer produces a slider whose upper bound came from `value`.
- [ ] Reversed bounds either swap correctly or raise an error that quotes the values the caller actually passed.
- [ ] Test coverage for reversed `min_value`/`max_value` with `value` below, inside, and above the range.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (logic is platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a (reproduced headlessly via `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`)

### Additional Information

Related but distinct: #5099 covers `value` falling outside `(min_value, max_value)`. This report is specifically about the bound-normalization statements corrupting `min_value`/`max_value` themselves.

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] I have a fix with tests ready, but this repository limits opening pull requests to collaborators, so I can't submit it as a PR. Posting the patch here in case a maintainer wants to pick it up. Branch: https://github.com/rajarshidattapy/streamlit/tree/fix/slider-reversed-bounds-normalization The library change assigns both bounds at once, so the swap reads the original `min_value`: ```diff # Ensure that min <= value(s) <= max, adjusting the bounds as necessary. -min_value = min(min_value, max_value) -max_value = max(min_value, max_value) +# Assign both at once so the swap reads the original min_value; assigning +# min_value first would leave max_value unable to take the original min. +min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value) ``` I went with completing the swap rather than raising on reversed bounds, since that is what the existing comment ("adjusting the bounds as necessary") and the neighbouring `start > end` swap already intend. Rejecting reversed bounds instead would be a behaviour change worth deciding separately. Added to `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/slider_test.py`: - `test_reversed_bounds_are_swapped` — parameterized over `value` omitted / at min / inside range / at max, asserting `c.min == 1` and `c.max == 10` in every case. The `value_inside_range` case is the one that previously produced a `1..5` slider, with the upper bound leaking in from `value`. - `test_reversed_bounds_do_not_collapse_to_equal_values` — covers the float case that previously raised `Slider min_value must be less than the max_value. The values were 1 and 1`. Behaviour before and after, via `AppTest` (Python 3.13.6, `develop` @ `2ac0d77d3`): | call | before | after | | --- |

Behaviour before and after, via `AppTest` (Python 3.13.6, `develop` @ `2ac0d77d3`): | call | before | after | | --- | --- | --- | | `st.slider("a", 10, 1)` | `min=1 max=10 value=10` | `min=1 max=10 value=10` | | `st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)` | `min=1 max=5 value=5` | `min=1 max=10 value=5` | | `st.slider("c", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=1)` | raised `The values were 1 and 1` | `min=1 max=10 value=1` | The existing `test_max_min` and `test_min_equals_max` still pass, so equal bounds are still rejected and the previously-passing reversed case is unchanged.

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a real backend bug in `_slider()` bound normalization, not a frontend or widget-state issue. In `lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py`, reversed bounds are meant to be swapped (`min_value = min(...)` then `max_value = max(...)`), but the second assignment reads the already-overwritten `min_value`, so `max_value` always collapses to the original `max_value`. After that, the existing “expand bounds to include `value`” logic can invent an upper bound from `value` (`min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5` → range `1..5`) or make both bounds equal and raise `The values were 1 and 1` for inputs the user never passed. Existing `test_max_min` only covers the case where `value` equals the original min, which accidentally restores the lost bound, so the tests never caught this. A simultaneous swap (`min_value, max_value = min(...), max(...)`) matches the current comment and the range-handle swap a few lines below; alternatively, `st.date_input` / `st.datetime_input` already reject reversed bounds with the original values quoted. The reporter also posted a ready-to-apply patch in the issue thread.

### Related Issues

- [#5099](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5099) — Confirmed `st.slider` behavior of expanding `min_value`/`max_value` to include an out-of-range `value`. Distinct from this report (which is about the failed bound swap itself), but it is the neighboring code path that turns the corrupted bounds into a silently wrong range.

No duplicate of this reversed-bounds assignment bug was found among open issues.

title: Stray 's' in config deprecation warning also disables textwrap.dedent(), leaving the message indented
text:
Issue #16676: Stray 's' in config deprecation warning also disables textwrap.dedent(), leaving the message indented
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P4, feature:config, area:backend

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `ConfigOption.set_value()`, the deprecation warning for a not-yet-expired config option opens its f-string with a stray `s` character:

```python
# lib/streamlit/config_option.py:285
get_logger(__name__).warning(
    textwrap.dedent(
        f"""s
        ════════════════════════════════════════════════
        {self.key} IS DEPRECATED.
```

This has two effects. The obvious one is a literal `s` printed at the start of the warning. The subtler one is that `textwrap.dedent()` silently stops working: `dedent` strips the longest common leading whitespace across all non-blank lines, and `s` is a line with **zero** indentation, so the common prefix becomes `""` and nothing is stripped. Every subsequent line keeps its 20 spaces of source indentation.

The sibling "expired" branch a few lines above is written correctly and dedents as intended, which makes the difference easy to see side by side.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import logging

from streamlit.config_option import ConfigOption

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s|%(message)s")

opt = ConfigOption(
    "test.notexpired",
    description="d",
    default_val="",
    deprecated=True,
    deprecation_text="Use something else.",
    expiration_date="2999-01-01",
)
opt.set_value("x", "some_file.toml")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the snippet above (any deprecated config option whose `expiration_date` is in the future takes this branch).
2. Compare the output with the expired branch (set `expiration_date="2020-01-01"`).

### Expected Behavior

title: Stray 's' in config deprecation warning also disables textwrap.dedent(), leaving the message indented
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Confirmed bug in `ConfigOption.set_value()` (`lib/streamlit/config_option.py`). The not-yet-expired deprecation warning opens as `f"""s` instead of `f"""`. That leftover `s` is a conversion leftover from PR #10133 (commit `7a7ddbb`), which rewrote `%(key)s` percent-format placeholders into f-strings and accidentally kept the `%s` conversion character. Because `s` is an unindented first line, `textwrap.dedent()` finds no common leading whitespace and leaves the rest of the banner indented. The expired-option branch immediately above is written correctly. Existing tests (`test_deprecated_unexpired`) call `set_value()` but never assert the warning text, so this slipped through. Impact is currently low: the only deprecated option (`mapbox.token`) is already expired and takes the other branch. Fix is to delete the stray `s` and assert the warning message (no leading `s`, flush-left like the expired error).

### Related Issues

- [#16678](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16678) — Companion report on the same `ConfigOption` deprecation path: `mapbox.token` is past its `expiration_date`, so users currently see the expired **ERROR** instead of this warning. Extending that date would immediately expose this formatting bug.
- [#12743](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12743) (closed) — Separate `feature:config` bug where deprecation warnings were still shown because `client.showErrorDetails` did not parse string values. Same warning surface, different cause.

No duplicate of the stray-`s` / `dedent()` failure was found.

title: StreamlitInvalidColorError message renders as one run-on line because bullets lack newlines
text:
Issue #16677: StreamlitInvalidColorError message renders as one run-on line because bullets lack newlines
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.map, feature:builtin-charts, area:backend

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`StreamlitInvalidColorError` builds its message from implicitly concatenated string literals, but the literals that introduce the bullet list have no separating newline:

```python
# lib/streamlit/errors.py:589-592
"This does not look like a valid color: {color}.\n\n"
"Colors must be in one of the following formats:"
"* Hex string with 3, 4, 6, or 8 digits. Example: `'#00ff00'`"
"* List or tuple with 3 or 4 components. Example: `[1.0, 0.5, 0, 0.2]`",
```

Python concatenates these into a single line, so the two bullets never start a new line. Because the message is rendered as Markdown, the `*` characters do not become a list — they appear as literal asterisks mid-sentence.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.map(
    {"lat": [37.77], "lon": [-122.4]},
    color="not-a-color",
)
```

Or directly:

```python
from streamlit.elements.lib.color_util import to_int_color_tuple

to_int_color_tuple("red")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Pass any invalid color to an API that validates colors (`st.map(color=...)`, `st.scatter_chart(color=...)`, etc.).
2. Read the resulting error message.

### Expected Behavior

One of the following, consistently:

title: mapbox.token deprecation expired 2026-05-01: logs "IS NO LONGER SUPPORTED" while the option still works
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `mapbox.token` was deprecated in #11231 with `expiration_date="2026-05-01"`. That date is now in the past, so `ConfigOption.is_expired()` is true and setting the option logs **ERROR** `IS NO LONGER SUPPORTED`. Expiration only changes the log text: the option is still registered, still readable via `config.get_option("mapbox.token")`, and still applied in `st.map`, `st.pydeck_chart`, and `_fix_pydeck_mapbox_api_warning()` (which copies it into `MAPBOX_API_KEY`). Unit tests still assert the token is forwarded to the proto. There is no CI check that a deprecated option’s expiration date has passed, so this drifted without a corresponding removal. Fix is to either remove the option (and stop reading it) or push the expiration date so the message matches current behavior.

- [#11399](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11399) — Closed `st.map` bug where `mapbox.token` was not applied. Maintainers confirmed the token should still be honored if set, and noted the option was already deprecated in favor of `MAPBOX_API_KEY`. Shows the option is still a live fallback, not a no-op.

title: Python unit tests are not portable to Windows (path separators, NamedTemporaryFile reopen, registry-dependent MIME type)
text:
Issue #16679: Python unit tests are not portable to Windows (path separators, NamedTemporaryFile reopen, registry-dependent MIME type)
Labels: type:bug, area:windows, status:confirmed, priority:P4, area:contribution

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Running the Python unit suite on Windows produces a large number of failures that are caused by the tests themselves rather than by the library. `CONTRIBUTING.md` does not restrict development to POSIX, so a contributor on Windows currently cannot use a green suite as a baseline.

This report covers three failures whose root cause I isolated precisely. (Two other clusters are excluded on purpose: the `write_test.py` / `help_test.py` failures belong to a separate library bug I filed about `is_mem_address_str`, and the `metrics_util_test.py` cluster is caused by the tests reading the developer's real home directory, which is a distinct test-isolation concern.)

### Steps To Reproduce

```console
$ uv run pytest lib/tests/ -q
```

on Windows.

### Failures and root causes

**1. `lib/tests/streamlit/components/v2/test_component_registry.py::test_resolve_glob_pattern_direct`**

The assertion compares a native path string against a POSIX-normalized one:

```python
assert str(resolved.resolve()) == Path(test_file).resolve().as_posix()
```

`str(Path)` yields `C:\Users\[HOME]\test-pattern.js` while `.as_posix()` yields `C:/[HOME]/test-pattern.js`. These coincide only on POSIX.

```
AssertionError: assert 'C:\\Users\\a...st-pattern.js' == 'C:/[HOME]
```

Fix: compare like with like — either `.as_posix()` on both sides or `Path(...) == Path(...)`.

**2. `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/video_test.py::VideoTest::test_st_video_subtitles_path`**

title: Python unit tests are not portable to Windows (path separators, NamedTemporaryFile reopen, registry-dependent MIME type)
text:
`str(Path)` yields `C:\Users\[HOME]\test-pattern.js` while `.as_posix()` yields `C:/[HOME]/test-pattern.js`. These coincide only on POSIX.

```
AssertionError: assert 'C:\\Users\\a...st-pattern.js' == 'C:/[HOME]
```

Fix: compare like with like — either `.as_posix()` on both sides or `Path(...) == Path(...)`.

**2. `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/video_test.py::VideoTest::test_st_video_subtitles_path`**

The test writes to a `NamedTemporaryFile` and, while it is still open, passes its path to `st.video(...)`, which reopens it. Windows does not permit reopening a still-open `NamedTemporaryFile`:

```
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'C:\\Users\\...\\tmpyltckifk.vtt'
lib\streamlit\elements\lib\subtitle_utils.py:121: PermissionError
```

Fix: close the handle (or use `delete=False` / a `TemporaryDirectory`) before handing the path to code that opens it.

**3. `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/download_button_test.py::DownloadButtonTest::test_file_object_infers_file_name_and_mime`**

The test asserts a specific MIME type for `.csv`:

```
AssertionError: assert 'application/vnd.ms-excel' == 'text/csv'
```

`mimetypes.guess_type()` consults the Windows registry (`HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT`), where `.csv` is commonly mapped to `application/vnd.ms-excel` on machines with Excel installed. The expected value therefore depends on the host's registry rather than on Streamlit.

Fix: register the expected mapping in the test (or in library setup) via `mimetypes.add_type("text/csv", ".csv")`, or assert against `mimetypes.guess_type` rather than a hard-coded string.

### Expected Behavior

`uv run pytest lib/tests/` passes on Windows, or the supported development platforms are stated explicitly in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### Current Behavior

A full run reports **59 distinct test failures (95 including subtests)**, of which the three above are cleanly attributable to non-portable test code.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three tests above pass on Windows without weakening what they assert.
- [ ] Optionally, a Windows job in CI (even a subset) to keep the suite portable.
