title: Python unit tests are not portable to Windows (path separators, NamedTemporaryFile reopen, registry-dependent MIME type)
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a **test-portability** bug: three Python unit tests fail on native Windows because of host-specific assumptions, not because the corresponding library APIs are broken. The cited assertions and call sites match the current code: `test_resolve_glob_pattern_direct` compares `str(Path.resolve())` (native separators) to `.as_posix()`; `test_st_video_subtitles_path` leaves a `NamedTemporaryFile` open and then reopens it via `subtitle_utils._handle_string_or_path_data` (Windows `PermissionError`); and `test_file_object_infers_file_name_and_mime` hard-codes `text/csv` while `_maybe_infer_file_info` uses `mimetypes.guess_type()`, which on Windows can return `application/vnd.ms-excel` from the registry. Neighboring tests already use `NamedTemporaryFile(..., delete=False)` for the reopen case. Native Windows is not the primary contrib environment (`CONTRIBUTING.md` points people at the devcontainer / WSL), so a full Windows CI job is optional; the three test fixes themselves look small and well-scoped.

### Related Issues

- [#16674](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16674) — Same Windows pytest run and author. That issue is the **library** hex-casing bug that causes `write_test.py` / `help_test.py` failures; this issue is the remaining **test-only** cluster they split out.
- [#14159](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14159) — `st.download_button` filename/MIME inference from file objects. `test_file_object_infers_file_name_and_mime` was added for that behavior and is the MIME assertion that depends on the host `mimetypes` database.
- [#11740](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11740) — Contribution-docs follow-up for developing Streamlit on Windows via WSL. Same area (Windows contributor workflow), not a duplicate of these test assertions.

No duplicate of this specific three-test report was found.

title: Broken relative link in .github/copilot-instructions.md and stale knip ignoreDependencies entries
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Two confirmed repo-hygiene bugs, not product regressions.

**1. Broken Copilot link.** `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is generated from root `AGENTS.md` by `scripts/generate_agent_rules.py`, which copies the body verbatim. The debugging-skill link is valid from the repo root but resolves to the non-existent `.github/.claude/skills/debugging-streamlit/SKILL.md` on GitHub. Patching only the generated file will be overwritten on the next `generate_agent_rules.py` run; the durable fix is to rewrite relative links in the generator (or avoid a relative Markdown link in `AGENTS.md`). The same unadjusted path is also copied into `.cursor/rules/overview.mdc`.

**2. Stale Knip ignores.** `frontend/knip.json` still lists `[USER].gl/extensions`, `[USER].gl/widgets`, and `react-responsive-carousel` in `ignoreDependencies`. Those pins remain in `frontend/lib/package.json` (Vite/Deck.gl peers and a Glide Data Grid peer, added in #16593). Knip now reports the ignores as unused configuration hints, so they can be dropped without changing the dependency list.

No duplicate of this report. Closely related prior work: [#16593](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16593) (introduced the Knip ignores).

### Related Issues

No closely related open issues found. The contribution-docs issues below share the area but not the defects:

- [#11740](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11740) — contributor-guide updates (WSL build notes), not agent-rule generation or Knip config.
- [#14097](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14097) — VS Code debug launch configs; adjacent to the debugging skill the broken link points at, but a different request.

### Summary

I used uv to install streamlit 1.62.0.

```Python
from datetime import datetime
import streamlit as st

a = st.date_input("Input:", min_value=datetime(2024,8,3), max_value=datetime(2025,2,3), value=None)
st.write(a)

]
```

2. Run `uv sync` to set up environment
3. Run the app with `uv run streamlit run main.py`
4. On the app page, select the date input.

### Expected Behavior

The date input dropdown should open in February, 2025. When the 1st of February is selected, the input should display 2025/02/01. If the year in the dropdown menu is selected, it should display a list of 2024 and 2025.

### Current Behavior

If the year in the dropdown menu is selected, it displays a list of only 2024. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.62.0 - Python version: 3.13.14 - Operating System: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (running in WSL) - Browser: Google Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

title: st.date_input dropdown showing the wrong year in constrained range
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend bug in the `st.date_input` calendar header: when `min_value`/`max_value` span a year boundary and the max date’s month/day is earlier than the min date’s (here `2024-08-03` → `2025-02-03`), the popover grid is on February 2025 but the header shows **February 2024**, and the year dropdown lists only **2024**. Selecting a day still commits the correct 2025 date, so the value path is fine; only the month/year picker UI is wrong. The same header is shared with `st.datetime_input`. Likely cause: React Aria’s `CalendarYearPicker` (`useCalendarYearPicker`, `react-aria-components` 1.20.0) builds year options by starting at `minValue` and adding one year at a time until the date exceeds `maxValue`. `2024-08-03 + 1 year` is `2025-08-03`, which is after `2025-02-03`, so 2025 is never added. Streamlit then renders the year trigger from that item list (`CalendarPopoverHeader`), so it stays on the only remaining year (2024) even while the calendar grid shows February 2025. There is already a local workaround in `CalendarPopoverHeader` for a related RAC year-picker bug (stale month on controlled `focusedValue`), but it does not fix year-list generation. A secondary Streamlit issue: `getInitialFocusedDate` clamps to `minDate` but not `maxDate`, so with `value=None` and today after the max, the focused date starts out of range. ### Related Issues - [#9667](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9667) — Same class of year-dropdown failure when the allowed range crosses a year boundary (years missing/disabled). Filed against the old Baseweb picker and closed after the RAC migration; this issue is the RAC equivalent, not a duplicate. - [#9922](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9922) — Year options

title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
text:
Issue #16697: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
Labels: type:bug, feature:st.file_uploader, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.camera_input, feature:st.chat_input, area:server, feature:st.audio_input, area:integrations

**Summary**

File uploads under ~10KB hang indefinitely (eventually timing out client-side) when `sentry_sdk.init()` is called in the same process, before Streamlit's own event loop is created, and Streamlit is then started in that process (e.g. via `streamlit.web.cli.main()` after rewriting `sys.argv`, rather than a fresh `streamlit run` subprocess). Uploads over ~10KB are unaffected. This reproduces with no application code beyond a single `st.file_uploader()`.

This in-process launch pattern is common for wrapper entrypoints that do setup (init error tracking, run DB migrations, etc.) before starting Streamlit without spawning a new OS process.

**Reproducible Code Example**

```python
"""
pip install streamlit==1.61.1 sentry-sdk==2.61.1
python repro.py
Then open http://localhost:8501 and upload a file smaller than ~10KB.
"""
import sys
import pathlib

pathlib.Path("app.py").write_text('''
import streamlit as st
uploaded = st.file_uploader("pick a file")
if uploaded is not None:
    st.write(f"Got {uploaded.name}, {len(uploaded.getvalue())} bytes")
''')

import sentry_sdk
sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None)  # comment this line out and the hang disappears

from streamlit.web import cli
sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", "app.py"]
sys.exit(cli.main())
```

**Steps To Reproduce**

1. `pip install streamlit==1.61.1 sentry-sdk==2.61.1`
2. Save the snippet above as `repro.py`, run `python repro.py`
3. Open `http://localhost:8501`, upload any file smaller than ~10KB (e.g. a 300-byte CSV)
4. Upload hangs indefinitely. Comment out `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None)` and it succeeds instantly. Upload a file larger than ~10KB and it succeeds either way.

**Expected Behavior**

title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
text:
**Expected Behavior**

Upload completes regardless of file size or whether Sentry was initialized in-process before Streamlit started.

**Current Behavior**

Small uploads hang. Root-caused to Sentry's `StarletteIntegration` (enabled by default) — confirmed via `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None, disabled_integrations=[StarletteIntegration()])` (succeeds) vs. `disabled_integrations=[ThreadingIntegration()]` (still hangs — ruling out threading despite superficial similarity to #15374 / #16139, both of which are already fixed in this version and don't apply since this repro has no `st.fragment(run_every=...)`). `StarletteIntegration` instruments Starlette's ASGI request lifecycle, and the hang lives inside Starlette's own multipart parser — Sentry wraps exactly the layer that breaks.

**Is this a regression?**

Not tested on older versions — can test if useful.

**Debug info**

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: macOS (also reproduces in a Linux container)
- sentry-sdk version: 2.61.1

**Additional Information**

Fuller repro with isolation scripts (control, all-integrations-disabled, Starlette-only-disabled) and sample CSVs: https://gist.github.com/tbrambor/d41b40950a0061ca404fc0d67e4768ed

title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
text:
[NONE] Found the precise mechanism, which also explains the exact ~10KB boundary — filed against sentry-python since it's really their code path: https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/7285

In short: `StarletteIntegration.patch_request_response()` wraps every route endpoint (including `_upload_put`). Before the handler runs, Sentry's `StarletteRequestExtractor.extract_request_info()` calls `await request.body()`/`.form()` whenever `content_length` is within its default `max_request_body_size` ("medium" → `content_length <= 10_000` bytes) — this fully drains the ASGI `receive()` channel purely to populate breadcrumb/event data.

`_upload_put` (`streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py`) then builds its own `StarletteRequest(request.scope, limited_receive)` to enforce a streaming size cap, where `limited_receive` calls `await request.receive()` directly — the same raw ASGI channel Sentry already drained. That second read blocks forever (no more body left, no disconnect coming on a keep-alive connection), which is the hang.

For uploads over 10,000 bytes, Sentry's size check skips body capture entirely, so the channel is untouched and the upload succeeds — matching the exact size boundary seen in testing.

This isn't really fixable from Streamlit's side alone — any ASGI middleware that reads the body first (not just Sentry) would break `_upload_put`'s manual receive the same way, since it isn't going through Starlette's own cached `Request.body()`/`.stream()`. Flagging here for visibility in case a defensive fix on this side (e.g. checking whether the body was already consumed, or reusing the original request via `Request.stream()`/cached body when available) is worth considering regardless of how the Sentry side lands.

title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
text: [COLLABORATOR] Confirmed, and your root-cause analysis is exactly right — thank you, the write-up made this quick to verify. Editing this comment to keep everything in one place now that we've implemented a fix; the mechanism section is unchanged, the "which middleware patterns break" characterization is corrected, and the open question about Sentry's `Request` instance is resolved. **Mechanism** Confirmed against Starlette 1.6.0: `Request.body()` caches into `self._body` **per instance**, and `stream()` only consults `hasattr(self, "_body")`. Because `_upload_put` constructs a *new* `StarletteRequest(request.scope, limited_receive)` whose `limited_receive` calls the raw `request.receive()`, it can never see that cache. The second read then blocks forever on a keep-alive connection. Reproduced with no `sentry_sdk` installed at all, using a stand-in that reads the request body before the handler runs: ``` CASE 1: no middleware reading the body (control) RESULT: completed, status=204 CASE 2: middleware reads body first (models Sentry StarletteIntegration) middleware pre-read 159 bytes of body RESULT: *** HUNG *** (timed out after 3s; receive() called 2x) ``` **It's a regression in 1.61.0** You mentioned you hadn't tested older versions, so: the `limited_receive` pattern was introduced in #16207 ("Enforce upload size limit while streaming body"), which shipped in **1.61.0**. Before that, the handler called `await request.form()` on the *original* request, which is cache-aware. Same drained-channel scenario against the old code path: ``` OLD (pre-#16207) `await request.form()`: OK -> ['foo.txt'] (receive calls: 1) ``` So 1.60.x and earlier are unaffected, and 1.61.0 onward is broken. **Which patterns actually break (correcting an earlier overstatement)** An earlier version of this

title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
text: Sentry does read from the same `Request` instance, so a cache-aware read is sufficient and no buffering workaround is needed. In `sentry_sdk.integrations.starlette`, `_wrap_async_handler` does `request = args[0]` and then `StarletteRequestExtractor(request)`; the extractor's `form()` deliberately calls `await self.request.body()` first (with a comment noting Starlette doesn't cache `form()` the way it caches `body()`). Verified against sentry-sdk 2.68.1. The ~10KB boundary is `request_body_within_bounds` under the default `max_request_body_size="medium"`, matching your numbers exactly. **The fix** `_upload_put` now reads through the original request's `stream()` — which replays Starlette's cached body when present — instead of the raw `receive()` channel, while still counting bytes to preserve #16207's streaming size cap. That cap exists to stop an oversized upload from being buffered in memory or spooled to disk before the size check runs, so we didn't want to trade this hang for that. Verified end to end against real sentry-sdk 2.68.1 + uvicorn: the sub-10KB upload that previously hung now returns 204, and the >10KB case is unchanged. One behavior change worth noting: a body consumed without being cached now returns a clear 400 rather than hanging or surfacing an opaque 500. **Triage** Confirmed bug, prioritized as a regression affecting `st.file_uploader`, `st.chat_input` attachments, `st.camera_input`, and `st.audio_input` — all four share the `/_stcore/upload_file` route. The silent-hang failure mode with no error or log makes this disproportionately hard to diagnose, which we weighted in. title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `st.file_uploader` hangs on uploads under ~10KB when `sentry_sdk.init()` runs in the same process before Streamlit starts. Sentry’s default `StarletteIntegration` drains the ASGI body (via `request.body()` / `.form()`) for requests with `content_length <= 10_000`. `_upload_put` in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py` then wraps `request.receive()` in `limited_receive` and builds a **new** `StarletteRequest` for multipart parsing, which does not see Starlette’s cached body. The second `receive()` blocks indefinitely on a keep-alive connection. Uploads over ~10KB skip Sentry body capture, matching the reported boundary. The same `/_stcore/upload_file` route is used by `st.camera_input` and `st.chat_input` attachments. Workaround: disable `StarletteIntegration` (or avoid in-process Sentry init). A Streamlit-side defensive fix would reuse the original request’s cached body / `Request.stream()` instead of a raw second `receive()`.

### Related Issues

- [#16139](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16139) — Closed. Another in-process `sentry_sdk.init()` interaction with Streamlit (ThreadingIntegration + `st.fragment(run_every)`). Different mechanism; the reporter correctly ruled this out.
- [#15374](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15374) — Closed. Sentry/threading wrapper clash around `add_script_run_ctx` in 1.58.0. Same “Sentry instruments Streamlit in-process” class of bug, not a duplicate of this hang.
- Upstream: [getsentry/sentry-python#7285](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/7285) — Reporter’s Sentry-side write-up of the body-drain + second `receive()` hang.

No open Streamlit duplicates found. Other `st.file_uploader` timeout issues (e.g. [#11419](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11419)) are unrelated client/mobile timeouts.

title: Support inline tooltips in Markdown (hover text), e.g. via a `:tooltip[...]` directive
text:
Issue #16729: Support inline tooltips in Markdown (hover text), e.g. via a `:tooltip[...]` directive
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:markdown

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a way to include inline text in Markdown that shows a tooltip when hovered — like abbreviations/glossary terms with an explanation on hover. This could be exposed as a new Markdown directive, and #12474 (show footnotes as tooltips) could be generalized to cover this.

### Why?

It's common to want to annotate a word or phrase with extra context that appears on hover — glossary terms, acronym expansions, definitions, or short explanations — without cluttering the main text. Today there's no native way to do this in Streamlit Markdown; users resort to raw HTML (`<abbr>`/`title`) which is limited and not always allowed. A first-class inline tooltip makes docs, dashboards, and explanatory text much richer.

### How?

Add a Markdown directive for inline tooltips, where the bracketed text is displayed and the `text` attribute is shown on hover:

```
The :tooltip[HTML]{text="Hyper Text Markup Language"} specification...

:tooltip[Streamlit]{text="Open-source app framework for Machine Learning and Data Science teams."}
```

title: Support inline tooltips in Markdown (hover text), e.g. via a `:tooltip[...]` directive
text:
Add a Markdown directive for inline tooltips, where the bracketed text is displayed and the `text` attribute is shown on hover:

```
The :tooltip[HTML]{text="Hyper Text Markup Language"} specification...

:tooltip[Streamlit]{text="Open-source app framework for Machine Learning and Data Science teams."}
```

Notes:
- The visible text (`[...]`) renders inline; hovering shows the tooltip `text`.
- Works wherever Streamlit Markdown is rendered (`st.markdown`, `st.write`, captions, etc.).
- Consider whether the tooltip `text` itself supports Markdown.
- **Alternative / complementary:** generalize #12474 (footnotes → tooltips). Markdown footnotes could render as hover tooltips, giving a standard-Markdown path to the same result; the `:tooltip[...]` directive is the more explicit, inline alternative.

### Additional Context

- Related: #12474 (show markdown footnotes as tooltips) — this issue proposes a more generic, directive-based approach to inline hover text.

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
text:
Issue #16732: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, feature:custom-components, status:confirmed, priority:P3, area:execution-model

### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
text:
### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

### Expected Behavior

Every value the mounted component sends is readable on the following script run. The explicit `key` makes the element id stable, so a changing `data` payload should not affect delivery.

### Current Behavior

About 25% of values are never delivered. Verified as lost rather than late by scanning the full backend log after all clicks — 0 arrived in a later run.

The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
text:
The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

Three controls on the same harness came out clean. They do not isolate the bug to trigger-on-mount — see Additional Information — but they do narrow which write path is affected:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` on mount, same conditions | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, stable `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, churning `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| **`setTriggerValue` on mount, churning `data`** | **5 of 21 lost** |

### Additional Information

**Mechanism.** `setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`makeTriggerAggregatorId` → `$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`) and the flush is deferred to a `setTimeout(…, 0)` macrotask. `App.removeInactiveWidgetState()` runs from the `ScriptFinished` → `clearStaleNodes` setState callback and deletes every widget state whose id is not an active *element* id — the aggregator id never is, because it isn't part of the element tree. When that lands before the flush, the trigger is deleted but the rerun is still sent (`sendUpdateWidgetsMessage` uses unfiltered `createWidgetStatesMsg()`), so the script reruns with no trigger.

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
text:
Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path: the component's `default function` runs behind `await loadAndRunModule(...)` (dynamic `import()` of a blob URL), so it executes a macrotask or more after the commit that mounted it. This also explains the control table — `setStateValue` is immune because it writes the component's real element id, and the event-handler controls passed because letting the app settle means `removeInactive` has already run.

**The `_pending_resets` theory is ruled out.** It is only populated by `mark_page_switch_drops`, which runs on page transitions and skips widgets whose recorded page is the current page, so a single-page app never populates it. (For the record, the original hypothesis was that `_pending_resets` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py` discarded a frontend-resent value on re-registration, which would have made this by design.)

**Related blind spot.** The same synthetic id is invisible to other active-id filters, not just this one: `App.tsx` `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which would likewise drop a pending aggregator. Reaching it would require a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible, so no change is planned there. Recorded as an observation only.

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
text:
**Scope of what was tested.** Measured against this repro on one machine, 235 trials total. It establishes this race as the cause of the loss seen here; it does not rule out other trigger-loss paths. The same race also appears to explain the recurring `bidi_components/basics_test.py::test_trigger_interactions` CI flake — the failure signature (counts unchanged plus `Result` reset to `None`) is what a trigger-less rerun produces — but that link is inferred from the signature, not directly observed. Two prior automated PRs (#14542, #14843) misattributed that flake to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts.

**Open question for Components V2** (replacing the original question here, which is now answered — the drop is a race, not intentional): should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern at all? Fixing the race makes it reliable, but it fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That is a semantics decision independent of this bug, and it determines whether this issue closes as fixed or splits into a fix plus a documentation/warning change.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (released wheel, production frontend build)
- Python version: 3.11 · macOS · Chromium
- The ~25% figure is one 21-trial sample on a single machine; treat it as "roughly a quarter" rather than a precise rate.

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a real Components V2 race, not identity churn and almost certainly not `_pending_resets`. With an explicit `key`, the element id stays stable (`key_as_main_identity=True`), but `useHandleJsContent` still re-runs the default export whenever `data` changes. A mount-time `setTriggerValue` then has to win a one-shot delivery race: the value is stored under the synthetic trigger-aggregator id (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<id>__events`), flushed on `setTimeout(0)`, deleted from client widget state, and cleared again by `_reset_triggers()` at the end of every script run. That aggregator id is not in the render tree, so `removeInactiveWidgetState()` on `ScriptFinished` can delete a pending trigger before the macrotask flush sends it. `_coalesce_widget_states` also preserves `trigger_value` / `chat_input_value` across queued reruns but not `json_trigger_value`, so a second widget-update message can overwrite a just-queued CCv2 trigger. Both fit the controls: `setStateValue` lives on the element id and persists; event-handler triggers fire after the app has settled. `_pending_resets` is page-scope persist-state tracking and is not involved in this repro. Mount-time triggers are still a poor fit for Streamlit's model (use `setStateValue` for init data), but silent ~25% loss with a stable key is a bug, not intended discard-on-re-register. ### Related Issues - [#14710](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14710) — Parent investigation this was split from. Most of that report is by-design (unkeyed `data` in identity, trigger reset after each run, first-run empty result). This issue is the remaining genuine drop with a stable `key`. - [#8041](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8041) — Older Components V1 “not ready on first load / retry” request. Same class of mount-time value timing, different API. - [#10102](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10102)

title: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell
text:
Issue #16770: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell
Labels: type:bug, area:docker, area:deployment, area:server, area:integrations

Not a reproducible bug report — a signal from population data that may point at one, and I can't tell from the outside whether the cause is Streamlit or the Hugging Face runtime image.

I enumerated the complete public Hugging Face Spaces catalogue (1,458,692 Spaces) using the `runtime.stage` field HF exposes, and split permanent failures by SDK and creation year.

**`BUILD_ERROR` is falling for every SDK — that part looks healthy.** But `RUNTIME_ERROR` diverges sharply for Streamlit in the 2026 cohort:

| SDK | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **streamlit** | 18.1% | **12.4%** | **31.7%** |
| gradio | 47.1% | 27.0% | 20.8% |
| docker | 31.6% | 19.5% | 20.5% |

Gradio and Docker fell or stayed flat over the same period. Streamlit's rate went from 12.4% to 31.7%.

The failure mode also inverted. Among broken Streamlit Spaces created in 2025: 7,991 `BUILD_ERROR` vs 4,582 `RUNTIME_ERROR`. In 2026: **653 `BUILD_ERROR` vs 5,614 `RUNTIME_ERROR`.** Builds started succeeding and apps started crashing instead.

**Checks I ran before posting, because the obvious explanations would each invalidate this:**

title: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell
text:
**Checks I ran before posting, because the obvious explanations would each invalidate this:**

- *Bulk uploaders?* No. The top-10 authors account for 2.3% of the 2026 Streamlit cohort, and excluding them entirely moves the rate from 36.6% to 37.1%. It is spread across 12,432 distinct authors.
- *Just young Spaces still settling?* Newer cohorts are consistently *less* broken across every SDK, so a worse young cohort runs against the trend rather than with it. Separately, 300 error-state Spaces re-queried individually with retries were 300/300 still broken with none recovered, so these are not transient.
- *An age artifact?* Age-standardising Streamlit to Gradio's creation-year distribution moves it 43.50% → 41.16%, so the cohort effect here isn't age composition.

**What I can't determine from outside:** whether this is a Streamlit change, a change in the Streamlit runtime image HF builds, or an interaction between the two. HF controls the Space container, so it may not be yours at all — I've filed the general Spaces census with them separately at huggingface/hub-docs#2743.

If it is useful, I can produce the list of affected Space IDs so someone can look at actual tracebacks, which is the thing this analysis can't reach.

Data (1.46M rows, one row per Space): https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ashsinha1/hf-spaces-census
Method and code: https://github.com/ashishsinha1602/dataset-integrity-audit

title: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell

title: Runtime errors in Streamlit apps on HF Spaces rose 12.4% → 31.7% for the 2026 cohort while other SDKs fell
text: Tornado→Starlette cutover (May 2026) is *five months after* the window opens, and by May 2026 the rate is already falling. - The Starlette 1.4.0 `GZipResponder` crash (Aug 2026, #16341) is *after* the window closes. Neither timing fits. Whatever this was appears to have started around Nov 2025 and been resolved around May–June 2026. **The caveat that cuts the other way, stated plainly:** this is a single snapshot (28 Aug 2026) bucketed by creation date, so the falling tail is confounded — Spaces created in June–August 2026 are only weeks old and may simply not have had time to break. title: Clarify st.number_input return type when value= int | None
text:
Issue #16773: Clarify st.number_input return type when value= int | None
Labels: type:bug, status:intended-behavior

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Passing a typed variable of int | None to the value parameter for number_input returns a float | None type.

I expected this to be int | None, and that this is how you are expected to create an empty input field, that accepts integers only, assuming the step parameter would default to 1, but it appears that strictly requires value to be int.

If you set step=1, then static type checking works as expected, resolving to int | None.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

default_value: int | None = None

number = st.number_input(
    "Input number",
    value=default_value,
)

if number:
    assert isinstance(number, int)
    print('Number is an int')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run example
2. Input number

### Expected Behavior

Prints 'Number is an int'

### Current Behavior

Assertion fails.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Edge

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: Clarify st.number_input return type when value= int | None
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16773)


[COLLABORATOR] This is expected behavior, not a typing bug we can fix with overloads.

`st.number_input` infers int vs float from the runtime values of `value` / `min_value` / `max_value` / `step`. A variable annotated `int | None` is just `None` at runtime, so with no other int args the widget is a float input and returns `float | None`. Type checkers follow that: the union splits into `value: int` → `int` and `value: None` → `float | None`, which is `int | float | None` (often shown as `float | None`). An overload that reported `int | None` would disagree with runtime.

Workarounds for an empty integer input:

```python
number = st.number_input("Input number", value=default_value, step=1)
# or min_value=0 / max_value=... as int
```

If you only need the annotation to be `int | None` and already know the widget is an int (e.g. you passed `step=1`):

```python
from typing import cast

number = cast(int | None, st.number_input("Input number", value=default_value, step=1))
```

`cast` alone does not change the runtime type. Without an int `step` / `min_value` / `max_value`, entered values are still floats.

text:
Issue #16841: st.multiselect no longer inserts the first filtered option on Enter (works in 1.49.1, not in 1.62.0)
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, area:frontend, area:widgets, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.selectbox, feature:st.multiselect, area:accessibility

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In `st.multiselect`, typing a few letters and pressing Enter used to insert the first filtered option. Since the react-aria migration it inserts nothing: no option is marked as the user types, so Enter has nothing to commit and simply closes the list.

`st.selectbox` still commits its first filtered option on Enter, which is why this reads as an oversight rather than a decision, but I may be wrong about that and would rather ask than assume.

Filing it because the same migration produced #16003 (fuzzy search became contiguous-substring matching), which was accepted as a regression, and this is the same shape of quiet behaviour loss.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

picked = st.multiselect("Multi", ["Person", "Organization", "Department", "Role", "Project"])
st.write("multiselect:", picked)

one = st.selectbox("Single", ["Person", "Organization", "Role"], index=None)
st.write("selectbox:", one)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click the multiselect and type `Pe`.
2. Press Enter.
3. Do the same in the selectbox below it.

### Expected Behavior

Enter inserts `Person`, the first filtered option, as it did in 1.49.1 and as the selectbox still does in 1.62.0.

### Current Behavior

title: st.multiselect no longer inserts the first filtered option on Enter (works in 1.49.1, not in 1.62.0)
text:
### Expected Behavior

Enter inserts `Person`, the first filtered option, as it did in 1.49.1 and as the selectbox still does in 1.62.0.

### Current Behavior

Enter clears the text and closes the list, and nothing is selected.

Comparing the same script on both versions, in the DOM after typing `Pe`:

| | 1.49.1 | 1.62.0 |
|---|---|---|
| options offered | Person, Project, Department | same (the fuzzy filter is unchanged) |
| first option | `aria-selected="true"`, tinted row | nothing marked, no `aria-activedescendant` |
| Enter | inserts Person | inserts nothing |
| extra row | none | `Select N matches`, keyed `__select_matches__` |
| selectbox, Enter | - | inserts the first option |

The arrow keys reach the option, but the first ArrowDown lands on the new `Select N matches` row, so the natural keyboard recovery (ArrowDown, Enter) selects *every* match rather than the one that was wanted. It takes ArrowDown twice.

I could not find a prop in React Aria's ComboBox for list autocomplete with automatic selection, so I appreciate this may not be a small change. The WAI-ARIA APG lists both automatic and manual selection as valid patterns, so this is a design question as much as a bug, which is why the question is in the summary.

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

text: [COLLABORATOR] Hi [USER] - thanks for your thorough submission, it was very helpful! Upgrading to `1.63.0` plus one parameter gets you the `1.49.1` behavior back: ```python st.multiselect("Multi", options, select_all=False) ``` Typing `Pe` then Enter inserts `Person`, as it used to. Some background on why the parameter is needed. 1.63.0 changed Enter from a no-op to "commit the first visible row." When 2+ options match, that first row is `Select N matches` — so on the defaults, typing `Pe` (which fuzzy-matches Person, Project and Department) now selects all three, while typing `Per` (one match) inserts just `Person`. Enter activating the bulk row is the intended default rather than an oversight, and the new `select_all=False` is the opt-out that hides that row entirely. That came out of #16537. Your second observation is the part that's still open, and you're right about it. 1.63.0 does mark the Enter target visually as you type — `Select 3 matches` on the defaults, or the first match with `select_all=False` — but nothing is exposed to assistive tech until you press an arrow key. The highlight is plain CSS on `[aria-posinset='1']`; React Aria's `focusedKey` is still null, so the input carries no `aria-activedescendant` and no option carries `aria-selected="true"`. Press ArrowDown and ARIA catches up correctly, but that first ArrowDown lands on the bulk row, which is exactly why reaching the highlighted match takes two presses. In 1.49.1 the first filtered option carried `aria-selected="true"` while typing, so what regressed is specifically that a screen reader can no longer

title: st.multiselect no longer inserts the first filtered option on Enter (works in 1.49.1, not in 1.62.0)
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a keyboard regression in `st.multiselect` after the BaseWeb → React Aria ComboBox migration ([#16175](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16175), shipped in 1.61). RAC does not auto-focus a list item while typing (`focusedKey` stays null, no `aria-activedescendant`), so in **1.62.0** Enter is a no-op: the filter is cleared and the menu closes without selecting anything. `st.selectbox` still commits its first filtered option via a dedicated Enter handler, which is why the widgets now diverge.

**1.63.0** ([#16673](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16673)) replaced that no-op with “unfocused Enter commits the first visible row.” When two or more options match, that first row is `Select N matches` (`__select_matches__`), not the first option as in 1.49.1. Product approved this default; `select_all=False` restores type-then-Enter of the first match. Skipping the bulk row on Enter was explicitly rejected. A remaining gap is visual/ARIA highlighting: the first row is CSS-highlighted via `aria-posinset`, but RAC `focusedKey` / `aria-activedescendant` is still a TODO, so ArrowDown still lands on the bulk row first.

### Related Issues

- [#16537](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16537) — Same type-then-Enter vs “Select N matches” request. Closed by [#16673](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16673), which added `select_all=False` as the opt-out that restores first-match Enter.
- [#16003](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16003) — Cited by the reporter. Another quiet behavior loss from the React Aria ComboBox migration (selectbox fuzzy search), same class of regression.
- [#15697](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15697) — Open enhancement for customizable selectbox/multiselect keyboard navigation; related interaction surface, not a duplicate of this Enter/filter bug.

title: st.data_editor NumberColumn: typing a value starting with "." (no leading zero) drops the decimal point and reads digits as a whole number
text:
Issue #16909: st.data_editor NumberColumn: typing a value starting with "." (no leading zero) drops the decimal point and reads digits as a whole number
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.data_editor, feature:st.column_config, upstream

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a NumberColumn cell is selected and you type a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.01`), the `.` is silently dropped and the remaining digits are committed as a whole number — `.01` becomes `1`, `.07` becomes `7`. Typing the same value with a leading zero (`0.01`) works correctly, and **pasting** `.01` into the cell also works correctly. So this is specific to the character-by-character typed-entry path.

Impact
This is a real-world data-entry trap: any user in the habit of typing .01-style shorthand (common for percentage/margin fields) silently enters a value the cell just shows a plausible-looking wrong number.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
df = pd.DataFrame({"Customer": ["A", "B"], "Margin": [12.0, 8.0]})
st.data_editor(
    df,
    column_config={
        "Margin": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Margin", format="%.4f", step=0.0001),
    },
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Click the Margin cell for row A (shows 12.0000).
Type .07 (as literal keystrokes: ., 0, 7).
Press Enter.

### Expected Behavior

Expected: cell shows 0.0700.

### Current Behavior

Actual: cell shows 7.0000.

### Is this a regression?

title: st.data_editor NumberColumn: typing a value starting with "." (no leading zero) drops the decimal point and reads digits as a whole number
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend bug in `st.data_editor` `NumberColumn`: typing a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.07`) silently drops the decimal, so the remaining digits commit as an integer (`7.0000` instead of `0.0700`). Pasting `.01` and typing `0.01` both work, which matches the two different input paths. Streamlit’s own parsers are not the problem — `toSafeNumber` / `NumberColumn.getCell` already accept leading-dot strings such as `".1312314"` (covered by unit tests), and paste goes through `getCell` with the full string. Typed entry instead uses Glide Data Grid’s built-in `GridCellKind.Number` overlay (`react-number-format`), which Streamlit does not replace (`useCustomEditors` returns `undefined` for number cells). That overlay is a controlled numeric input that reports a JS `floatValue` on every keystroke; a lone `.` is not a valid number, so the decimal is discarded and later digits are read as a whole number. A fix would keep the in-progress text (similar to `st.number_input`’s `formattedValue`) or patch the overlay so incomplete input like `.` / `.0` is preserved. ### Related Issues - [#16129](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16129) — Same Glide `NumberColumn` overlay editor; IME composition committed after the first keystroke. Streamlit already patches that overlay for #16129, so this is another overlay typing-path bug rather than a `getCell` parsing issue. - [#12886](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12886) — Similar “decimal disappears while typing” symptom in `st.number_input` (`1.0` collapsing to `1`). Related UX, but a different widget and input implementation; not a duplicate. - [#11519](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11519) — Another `NumberColumn` editing-path numeric distortion (`4.52` rounding to `4.51` with `step`/`format`). Same feature area, different failure mode. No exact duplicate

title: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
text:
Issue #16931: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
Labels: type:bug, area:security, status:confirmed, priority:P3, area:contribution

**Description**

`scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` builds a `grep` command by interpolating snapshot
filenames from the working tree into a shell string that is then executed with
`shell=True`, so shell metacharacters in committed snapshot filenames execute
arbitrary commands when the script is run.

In `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` (lines 225-228):

```python
cmd = f'grep -r --include="*.py" "{snapshot_name}" e2e_playwright/'
result = subprocess.run(
    cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
)
```

The `snapshot_name` is derived from on-disk filenames (lines 288-311):

```python
for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(snapshot_root):  # e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux
    for filename in filenames:
        if filename.endswith(".png"):
            all_snapshot_files.append(os.path.join(dirpath, filename))
...
snapshot_name = re.sub(r"\[.*\]\.png$", "", filename)
```

`filename` comes straight from the repository working tree (the snapshot PNGs
are committed to git), so anyone whose snapshot file gets merged controls part
of the command string. Because the value is placed inside double quotes,
`/bin/sh` still interprets `"`, `;`, `|`, `$()` and backticks — for example a
file named `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "[chromium].png` is reduced to the
snapshot name `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "` and produces

    grep -r --include="*.py" "st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "" e2e_playwright/

which runs `touch /tmp/pwned` as a separate command. The remaining grep then
searches for the same injected string, keeping the script's normal flow intact.

**Trigger scenario**

title: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
text:
grep -r --include="*.py" "st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "" e2e_playwright/

which runs `touch /tmp/pwned` as a separate command. The remaining grep then
searches for the same injected string, keeping the script's normal flow intact.

**Trigger scenario**

1. A PR adds (or renames) a snapshot file under
   `e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/` with a filename containing shell
   metacharacters (the name is visible in the diff, but its effect is easy to
   miss in review).
2. The PR is merged.
3. A maintainer runs `python scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` locally, or CI runs
   it in `--ci` mode — both paths execute the grep above.
4. The injected command executes in the maintainer's environment / CI runner.

**Impact**

Arbitrary command execution in the environment of whoever runs the cleanup
script. In practice the attacker already needs write access to the repository
(a merged PR), so I'd class this as a hardening issue rather than a security
vulnerability — which is why I'm opening a regular issue instead of using a
security channel. Still, it's an easy footgun to eliminate: the `find` call a
few lines above (lines 157-160) also uses `shell=True` (its string is static,
so it is harmless, but it could be cleaned up in the same pass).

**Suggested fix**

Drop the shell entirely and pass an argument list, keeping `--` to avoid
option injection:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["grep", "-r", "--include=*.py", "--", snapshot_name, "e2e_playwright/"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
)
```

Optionally validate the name as defense in depth, e.g.
`re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+", snapshot_name)` (or use `shlex.quote()` if a
shell must be kept).


Optionally validate the name as defense in depth, e.g.

title: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` interpolates snapshot PNG basenames into a `grep` command string and runs it with `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. The names come from `os.walk` of `e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/` after only stripping a `[browser].png` suffix, so shell metacharacters in a snapshot filename can break out of the double quotes and run extra commands. This is confirmed in `search_for_snapshot_name` (around lines 225–228). The nearby `find` call also uses `shell=True`, but its command string is static. Impact is limited to whoever runs the script: maintainers locally, and CI via `.github/workflows/snapshot-hygiene.yml` (including on PRs that change `e2e_playwright/**`, so a merge is not required for CI execution). This is maintainer/CI hardening rather than a user-facing Streamlit vulnerability. Passing an argv list (with `--`) instead of a shell string is the correct fix.

### Related Issues

- [#16691](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16691) — Defense-in-depth against interpolating filenames into a protocol field. Same class of unescaped-filename issue, different surface (`st.file_uploader`, not this script).
- [#16631](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16631) — Interpolating a filename containing quotes into a `Content-Disposition` header without escaping. Related interpolation bug, not a duplicate.

No existing issues track `snapshot_cleanup.py` or this `shell=True` grep path.

title: Scroll to st.chat_input
text:
Issue #16977: Scroll to st.chat_input
Labels: type:bug, area:layout, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.chat_input

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Placing `st.chat_input` inside `st.bottom` causes an otherwise non-chat page to scroll to the bottom immediately on initial load, without any user interaction or chat messages. This hides the heading and initial content when using the bottom container for a persistent assistant alongside a dashboard. Replacing only `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input` prevents the unsolicited scrolling.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Dashboard heading")
for number in range(30):
    st.write(f"Dashboard row {number}")

with st.bottom:
    st.chat_input("Ask about the dashboard")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install `streamlit==1.63.0` and run the example with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open a fresh browser tab/context with a viewport around 1280 x 720, so the main content exceeds the viewport height.
3. Do not click, type, or scroll. Wait for rendering to settle.
4. Observe that the main page has scrolled to the bottom and the dashboard heading is offscreen.
5. As a control, replace `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input`, restart/reload in a fresh browser context, and observe that the page stays at the top.

No custom CSS, JavaScript, Snowflake connection, fragments, tabs, navigation, or third-party component is needed to reproduce this.

### Expected Behavior

title: Scroll to st.chat_input
text:
No custom CSS, JavaScript, Snowflake connection, fragments, tabs, navigation, or third-party component is needed to reproduce this.

### Expected Behavior

An initial dashboard load should remain at the top. A bottom-docked input should not make non-chat content above it auto-scroll before any conversation exists. If automatic scrolling is intentional for chat-first apps, an opt-out for this mixed dashboard/assistant use case would be helpful.

### Current Behavior

The page scrolls to the bottom on its own. In three fresh Chrome contexts per variant, measured after rendering settled at a 1280 x 720 viewport:

| Bottom widget | Main scrollTop | Main scrollHeight | Main clientHeight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `st.chat_input` (all 3 runs) | 843 | 1563 | 720 |
| `st.text_input` (all 3 control runs) | 0 | 1573 | 720 |

The scroll position was read from the main scrollable section (`section.stMain`), not `window.scrollY`. No Streamlit exception was displayed. Measurements used Playwright with installed Chrome in headless mode; the same symptom was first noticed in interactive Chrome in a larger app.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0 (also the latest GitHub release at the time of filing)
- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS 26.6, ARM64
- Browser: Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83
- Deployment: local `streamlit run`, default theme for the minimal example

### Additional Information

_No response_

[CONTRIBUTOR] Placing `st.chat_input` in `st.bottom` (or calling it at the main-app root, which enqueues it there) is currently treated as a chat layout: `AppView` swaps `stMain` for `ScrollToBottomContainer`, and `useScrollToBottom` sets stickiness on first load so the main section animates to the bottom. That matches the control in the report (`st.text_input` in `st.bottom` does not activate this path) and the e2e guard that only skips auto-scroll when the bottom container has no chat input. The behavior is intentional for chat-first apps (kept on purpose in the `st.bottom` public API work), but it is a poor default for mixed dashboard + assistant pages because the heading and initial content are scrolled offscreen before any messages exist. A fix would likely mean not auto-scrolling on initial load unless chat content is present, or adding an explicit opt-out.

### Related Issues

- [#13249](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13249) — Same auto-scroll / stick-to-bottom machinery on containers; related UX for users who need control over when the view jumps to the latest content.
- [#8363](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8363) — Open report of unexpected main-area scroll interaction when `st.chat_input` / `st.chat_message` are present (jitter rather than a one-shot jump to the bottom).
- [#8836](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8836) — Original request for “scroll to bottom” chat/log behavior; that feature is what this dashboard layout is hitting on load.

[CONTRIBUTOR] `st.App` is an ASGI wrapper around Starlette (composition, not a subclass), so OpenTelemetry's `StarletteInstrumentor.instrument_app()` fails with `AttributeError: 'App' object has no attribute 'add_middleware'`. Middleware is accepted only at construction (`App(..., middleware=[...])`) and applied later when the inner Starlette app is built lazily on the first ASGI call; there is no `add_middleware` (or `router` / `user_middleware`) surface for post-construction instrumentors. The working uvicorn path in the report uses vanilla `starlette.applications.Starlette`, not `st.App` — `uvicorn home:app` with `st.App` would hit the same error at import time. A likely fix is to add a Starlette-compatible `add_middleware` that appends to `_user_middleware` before the inner app is built; full OTEL compatibility may also need other Starlette attributes that instrumentors inspect. Passing OTEL's ASGI middleware via the constructor is a possible workaround today.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9159 — Open request for first-class OpenTelemetry / observability support; this report is a compatibility gap while trying to use existing Starlette OTEL instrumentation with `st.App`.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11126 — DataDog auto-instrumentation request; same class of third-party ASGI/Starlette instrumentors expecting a real Starlette (or similarly introspectable) app.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13600 — Starlette/ASGI `st.App` introduction (closed RFF). Documents custom middleware as a supported `App` feature, but only via the constructor, which is what OTEL's `instrument_app()` does not use.

```Python
st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

title: Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a regression from 1.57.0 to 1.58.0: a dialog opened from a button inside `[USER].fragment(run_every=...)` stays on screen after the parent fragment auto-reruns, but clicks inside it stop working and the backend logs `The fragment with id ... does not exist anymore`. `[USER].dialog` is implemented as a nested fragment of the caller (`_fragment` wrapping the dialog body). Because the repro only calls `show_dialog()` on the button-click run, the parent `run_every` rerun never re-registers that nested fragment. Since 1.58.0 (PR #15130, the #15084 stale auto-rerun fix), `ScriptRunner` evicts descendants that were not re-registered via `clear_stale_descendants`. The frontend still shows the modal because dialogs live on `event_dg` (outside the parent fragment tree) and keep `isOpen` in React state. Later widget clicks send a fragment rerun for the evicted id; `AppSession.request_rerun` then drops the request at the `fragment_storage.contains` check. A likely fix is to keep an open dialog fragment across parent fragment reruns (or not treat dialogs as evictable descendants), rather than closing leftover UI. ### Related Issues - [#15084](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15084) — Nested `run_every` fragments crashing when an ancestor stopped rendering them. The 1.58.0 descendant-eviction fix for this is the likely source of this regression; dialogs are nested fragments that are *intentionally* not re-called on later parent runs. - [#16708](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16708) — Nested `run_every` fragment remains on screen with stale content after it is no longer rendered. Same leftover-UI class of bug (backend eviction vs. frontend still showing the subtree), though that report is about fragment containers rather than dialogs. - [#10283](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10283) —

title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
text:
Issue #17029: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.metric, area:ai

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

This is a documentation inconsistency, not a runtime bug. The behavior is by design (#15790, closing #15005), and this report does not ask to change it. It asks for the two places that describe `delta` to match it.

The `delta` docstring gives four unqualified rules ([metric.py lines 150-158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L150-L158)): no arrow for `None` or an empty string, "if the delta is zero, no arrow is shown and the delta is gray", red and down for "a negative number or starts with a minus sign", otherwise green and up. `delta_color="normal"` repeats "gray when zero" ([metric.py line 170](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L170)) and `delta_arrow="auto"` says "no arrow is shown if `delta` is zero" ([metric.py line 269](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L269)). Those rules treat strings as first-class input (the minus-sign branch exists only for strings), so a reader expects a zero-valued string such as `"0%"` or `"+0.0%"` to be "zero".

title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
text:
The implementation defines zero for strings as the literal `"0"` only ([metric.py lines 598-604](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L598-L604)), with the comment "other numeric-looking strings (e.g. `"0.0"`, `"0%"`) stay positive". #15790 added that deliberately, on the basis that string deltas are opaque display text, and locked it in with an anti-regression test. The docstring was not updated to say so, which is the gap.

The packaged `developing-with-streamlit` skill widens the gap in practice. Every `st.metric` example in it passes `delta` as a pre-formatted string: [dashboards.md line 17](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L17), [dashboards.md lines 47-49](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L47-L49), and [data-display.md line 363](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/data-display.md?plain=1#L363). The skill never mentions zero, so it does not contradict anything, but an agent that follows its examples and then reads the docstring's "gray when zero" will format a flat period as `"0%"` and get a green up-arrow.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
For reference only. This shows the designed behavior, not a bug; it is here so the mismatch with the docstring wording can be seen without reading the source.


import streamlit as st

col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3)
# What the skill's examples lead to for a flat period:
col1.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "0%")        # green up-arrow
col2.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "-0.0%")     # red down-arrow
# What actually renders neutral:
col3.metric("Orders (numeric)", 1400, 0, delta_description="vs last month")

"I.e.:"

from streamlit.elements.metric import _is_zero_delta
for delta in ["0", "0%", "+0.0%", "-0.0%", 0]:
    repr(delta), _is_zero_delta(delta)
# '0' True
# '0%' False
# '+0.0%' False
# '-0.0%' False
# 0 True
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
text: ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Read the `delta` docstring's "if the delta is zero" rule and `delta_color="normal"`'s "gray when zero". 2. `streamlit run` or `uv run streamlit run` the snippet. 3. Compare the first two tiles with the third / see the debug output beneath it. ### Expected Behavior Documentation that states the actual rule: 1. In the `delta` docstring (and the `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` mentions of zero), say that a string delta is displayed as-is and that only the literal string `"0"` is treated as zero; other zero-like strings follow the sign rule (leading minus is negative, anything else is positive). One sentence is enough. 2. In the packaged skill, either show at least one example with a numeric `delta` and qualifier text in `delta_description=`, or add a one-line note next to the string examples that string deltas are never treated as zero. ### Current Behavior The docstring says zero deltas are gray with no qualification about strings. `"0%"` renders as a positive delta with a green up-arrow and `"-0.0%"` as a negative delta with a red down-arrow, which is the designed behavior. The skill's examples are all strings and say nothing about zero. For at-a-glance reference: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
text: For at-a-glance reference: ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. Not a regression and not a behavior change request. Verified on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing): the docstring text, the skill examples, and `_is_zero_delta` are identical in both, and unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information The behavior was settled in #15790: the PR description lists an anti-regression test that `"0.0"`, `"+0"` and `"0%"` "stay green/up", and review confirmed the numbers-versus-strings split as intended. Nothing here asks to reopen that; it asks for the docstring and the skill to describe it. `format=` is not a way around the string question: it is one format applied to both `value` and `delta`, and `"percent"` multiplies by 100, so a tile whose value is a count and whose delta is a percent change cannot be served by a single `format=`. Numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` is the pattern that works, and it is the one the skill could show.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a documentation mismatch, not a runtime defect. `_is_zero_delta` in `lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py` treats a numeric `0` (including `0.0` / `Decimal("0")`) and only the literal string `"0"` as zero; other zero-looking strings such as `"0%"`, `"0.0"`, and `"+0"` stay positive, and a leading minus (e.g. `"-0.0%"`) is negative. That split was intentional in #15790 (closing #15005) and is locked in by `test_zero_like_strings_keep_positive_direction`. The `delta` / `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` docstrings still say an unqualified “gray when zero,” and every `st.metric` example in the bundled `developing-with-streamlit` skill passes a pre-formatted string `delta`, so an agent that formats a flat period as `"0%"` gets a green up-arrow. The requested fix is to state the string rule in the docstring and show a numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` (or a one-line note) in the skill.

### Related Issues

- [#15005](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15005) (closed by [#15790](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15790)): original request for gray/no-arrow zero deltas. That PR introduced the numbers-vs-strings split and the anti-regression tests; this issue is the leftover docstring/skill gap from that change, not a request to reopen the behavior.
- [#4775](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4775) (closed): string deltas still get an up-arrow (e.g. `"No difference compared to last month"`). Same opaque-string rule; later addressed for control via `delta_arrow`, not by parsing zero-like strings.
- [#13690](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13690) (closed): added `delta_description`, which is the pattern this report recommends for a numeric zero delta with qualifier text instead of stuffing `"0%"` into `delta`.

title: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
text:
Issue #17074: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, area:styling, status:cannot-reproduce, feature:st.segmented_control, feature:st.pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

On fresh page load (before any user interaction), st.pills (multi-select mode) renders ALL options with the "selected" purple-outline style in Safari, even though no option is selected — the underlying server-side state (default=None) is correctly empty. The visual bug appears specifically in real Safari and does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit engine.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

selected = st.pills(
    "Filter",
    options=["Option A", "Option B", "Option C"],
    selection_mode="multi",
    default=None,
)
st.write(selected)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app fresh in Safari (macOS or iOS) — a new tab/window, not a warm reload.
2. Before clicking anything, observe the st.pills widget with selection_mode="multi" and default=None.
3. All options render with the "selected" purple-outline styling, even though nothing has been selected yet.
4. The underlying state is correct (st.write(selected) shows an empty list) — this is a visual-only bug.
5. Does NOT reproduce in Chromium or in Playwright's WebKit engine — only in real Safari.

### Expected Behavior

On fresh load with default=None, all pill options should render in the plain/unselected style, matching the actual empty selection state.

### Current Behavior

title: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
text:
### Expected Behavior

On fresh load with default=None, all pill options should render in the plain/unselected style, matching the actual empty selection state.

### Current Behavior

All pill options render in the "selected" style (purple outline/fill) on fresh page load in Safari, despite no option being selected and the server-side value correctly being an empty list.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: (from your requirements.txt / Railway build — Claude Code can confirm the exact version)
- Browser: Safari (macOS) — reproduces on real Safari; does not reproduce in Chromium or Playwright's WebKit
- OS: macOS

### Additional Information

Extracted the relevant CSS from the live page's compiled stylesheet:
[data-selected]:not([data-disabled]) { background-color: rgba(79,70,229,0.1); border-color: rgb(79,70,229); color: rgb(79,70,229); }

This appears to be an attribute-presence selector issue: in Chromium/WebKit-via-Playwright, react-aria (the underlying ToggleButtonGroup implementation) correctly omits the data-selected attribute entirely on unselected buttons, so the selector doesn't match. It's possible real Safari's DOM/CSS engine handles react-aria's attribute timing differently on initial paint, causing data-selected to be briefly (or persistently) present on all buttons before Safari's own attribute-removal logic runs — worth investigating from the react-aria/Safari interaction side.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Visual-only Safari bug: on a cold load, multi-select `st.pills` with `default=None` paints every option with the primary selected style even though widget state is correctly empty. This is plausible in code: after the BaseWeb → React Aria migration, `StyledPillsToggleButton` (and the shared `st.segmented_control` styles) key off the presence selector `[data-selected]:not([data-disabled])`. CSS `[data-selected]` matches any present attribute, including `data-selected="false"` or `""`, so a Safari/react-aria first-paint quirk that leaves that attribute on unselected `ToggleButton`s would produce exactly this screenshot while Chromium and Playwright WebKit (not real Safari) stay clean. The hosted repro not reproducing is consistent with that. Worth checking `st.segmented_control` in real Safari the same way, and inspecting whether unselected buttons have `data-selected` / `data-selected="false"` in the DOM.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12802 — Same `ToggleButtonGroup` CSS surface (`[data-selected]` / hover adjacency) for `st.segmented_control`; not a duplicate, but the closest existing styling bug on this component.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12912 — Selected *appearance* of `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control` diverging from the actual value (disabled case). Same class of visual/state mismatch, different trigger.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12388 — Earlier report that pills hide the selected style when `disabled=True`; inverse of this issue (selected look missing vs. selected look on everything), same widget.

No duplicate of the Safari cold-load “all pills look selected” report was found.

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Thanks for the detailed report — the CSS you extracted was genuinely useful in narrowing this down. I spent some time trying to reproduce it in real Safari and wasn't able to, so I want to share exactly what I tried in case it helps us find the difference between our setups. **What I tested:** Streamlit 1.64.0 (your reported version) in a clean venv, your snippet verbatim, with `primaryColor = "#4F46E5"` set so the selected style matches the indigo in your CSS. Real Safari 26.6.2 on macOS 26.7 — not Playwright's WebKit, since your report rules that out. Three loads: a first-ever visit to the URL, a warm reload, and one on a separate origin so every asset was refetched cold. On all three, the three `default=None` pills rendered plain: no `data-selected` attribute, `aria-pressed="false"`, and a neutral `rgba(49,51,63,0.2)` border rather than the indigo one. **Why I trust that negative result:** a "nothing found" outcome is only as good as the detector, so the same page also had a second pills widget with `default=["Ctrl A"]` as a control. That button reported `data-selected` present with `background-color: rgba(79,70,229,0.1); border-color: rgb(79,70,229); color: rgb(79,70,229)` — exactly the CSS you quoted. So the check does see the attribute and the indigo styling when they're really there; the `default=None` pills simply didn't have either. I also sampled every animation frame from before React first rendered through several seconds after, specifically to catch a transient flash on first paint, and there were zero frames where an unselected

title: Pills/ToggleButtonGroup: all options render with "selected" style on fresh page load in Safari
text: there; the `default=None` pills simply didn't have either. I also sampled every animation frame from before React first rendered through several seconds after, specifically to catch a transient flash on first paint, and there were zero frames where an unselected pill carried the attribute. **On the attribute-timing theory:** I don't think this one can be it, unfortunately. In the shipped bundle react-aria emits the attribute as `data-selected={isSelected || undefined}`, and React removes rather than sets an attribute whose value is `undefined`. So `data-selected=""` or `data-selected="false"` never exists on an unselected button in any engine — there's no attribute present for `[data-selected]` to match, and no window for Safari to remove it late. Related: the compiled rule on the page is class-scoped (`.st-emotion-cache-XXXX[data-selected]:not([data-disabled])`) rather than the bare `[data-selected]` selector, though that's secondary to the attribute never being there. Since you're clearly seeing it, I suspect something in your app that the minimal snippet doesn't have. Two things would help a lot: - Your exact Safari version, and whether it was macOS or iOS. I could only test 26.6.2 on macOS, and I don't have an iOS device to check. - Whether the app has any custom CSS, a theme beyond `primaryColor`, or custom components. This follows on from the question above — anything injecting styles that match `.stButtonGroup button` could paint the pills without any `data-selected` involved. https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/compare/develop...acsarthur3333:streamlit:fix-global-hotkeys-missing-key
