title: GlobalHotkeys crashes on keydown/keyup events without a key
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `GlobalHotkeys` listens on `document` for `keydown`/`keyup` and immediately calls `normalizeKey(event.key)`, which does `key.toLowerCase()`. Real `KeyboardEvent`s always have a string `key` (empty string if unspecified), so normal typing is fine. A plain `Event("keydown")`/`Event("keyup")` has no `key`, so the handler throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')`. That can happen with synthetic events from hosts, extensions, or test harnesses. The component was introduced in #16655 as a `react-hot-keys` replacement and has no guard; widget shortcut code already uses `event.key ?? ""`. Guarding `typeof event.key !== "string"` in both handlers (and covering keyless events in `GlobalHotkeys.test.tsx`) is the right fix. Note: `Dialog.tsx` also calls `e.key.toLowerCase()` unguarded on capture-phase `keydown`.

### Related Issues

- [#16608](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16608) — Same `GlobalHotkeys` document listeners for the `r`/`c` app shortcuts; different bug (shortcuts firing inside custom components) but the same event path.
- [#16954](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16954) — Request to change the clear-cache `c` shortcut, which is dispatched through this same `GlobalHotkeys` handler.
- [#13112](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13112) — Broader request for app-level keyboard shortcuts; not a duplicate, but it would share this document-level key handling.

title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
text:
Issue #17093: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
Labels: type:bug, area:widgets, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.number_input, feature:st.session_state

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

The bug does not happen if `persist_state="page"` is passed to `number_input`.

Possibly related: #15660 seems to have fixed a similar bug for when persist_state is passed, but not for when persist_state=None.

title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] **If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17093)


[CONTRIBUTOR] When a keyed widget is first rendered on a later run than the one that wrote its `st.session_state` default (e.g. `setdefault` while the widget is hidden behind a toggle), the backend returns that stored value but the frontend mounts at the widget element default. A follow-up rerun then writes the frontend default back into session state, so the programmatic value is lost. Root cause: `SessionState.register_widget` only sets `value_changed=True` for same-run assignments (`is_new_state_value`) or for `persist_state` remounts (`restored_persisted_value` from PR #15660). For `persist_state=None`, a previous-run user-key value in `_old_state` is resolved on the Python side but never sent via `set_value`, so `st.number_input` (and other widgets) render `0.00` / empty while returning `100.0`. Passing `persist_state="page"` works because that path already tells the frontend to adopt the backend value.

### Related Issues

- [#5620](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5620) — Likely duplicate: a keyed `st.text_input` revealed by a checkbox does not load a `session_state` value set on a prior run.
- [#9082](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9082) — Same `setdefault` + conditional-widget pattern; the first-rendered widget gets the default, later-revealed widgets do not, and hiding them can clear session state.
- [#16388](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16388) — Related frontend/backend split for keyed widgets, but triggered by deleting a session-state key rather than delayed first mount.

title: Support for websockets >= 17.x
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] I think this is more of an enhancement, but looking into bumping the supported version. 

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a packaging enhancement, not a Streamlit runtime bug. Streamlit 1.64.0 (and current `develop`) declares `websockets>=12.0.0,<17` in `lib/pyproject.toml`, so `pip install streamlit==1.64.0 "websockets>=17.1"` cannot resolve. The `<17` cap was added in #15948 as the standard “next unreleased major” bound; Streamlit does not import `websockets` in production code and instead uses it as uvicorn’s WebSocket implementation (`ws="websockets-sansio"` in `starlette_server.py`). Bumping to `<18` is reasonable once 17.x is verified with that uvicorn path. That check matters because #16030 showed websockets 16.1 broke non-ASCII handshake headers, and the `websockets` maintainer planned to reintroduce that change as a documented break in 17.0 pending an uvicorn fix ([Kludex/uvicorn#3035](https://github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/issues/3035)). The lockfile is still on `websockets==16.1.1`.

### Related Issues

- [#16030](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16030) — Closed regression where websockets 16.1 broke WebSocket handshakes with non-ASCII proxy/auth headers. Directly relevant: the 17.x major was called out as the version that would reintroduce that breaking change, so compatibility with uvicorn must be confirmed before raising Streamlit’s cap.
- [#15421](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15421) — Same class of request: raise a server-stack dependency bound (`starlette`) so Streamlit can install alongside a newer major.
- [#15022](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15022) — Windows `WinError 121` noise in the uvicorn/websockets read loop after the Starlette migration. Not a duplicate, but it is another signal that WebSocket-layer upgrades in this stack need careful validation.

title: Dialog crashes on keydown events without a key
text:
Issue #17107: Dialog crashes on keydown events without a key
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P3

### Summary

`st.dialog` with `dismissible=False` attaches a capture-phase document `keydown` listener that calls `e.key.toLowerCase()` without checking that `key` is a string. A synthetic `keydown` with no `key` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')`.

This is the same event class as #17082 (`GlobalHotkeys`), but a separate listener. #17082 / PR #17105 only guards `GlobalHotkeys`. The dialog handler still throws while a non-dismissible dialog is open.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Open a non-dismissible dialog (`st.dialog(..., dismissible=False)`).
2. Dispatch:

```js
document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keydown"))
```

Expected: ignored (there is no key to match as `r`).
Actual: uncaught TypeError from `Dialog.tsx` `handleRKeySuppress`.

### Notes

- The listener is only attached while a non-dismissible dialog is open (`capture=true`).
- Do not `preventDefault` / `stopImmediatePropagation` when there is no string `key` — that would treat the event as an R-key suppress.
- Related: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17082
- Related PR: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17105

title: st.button lost callback from a fragment > dialog > fragment
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a regression in the `fragment → dialog → fragment` nesting: the Increment button stays visible, but its click never reruns the inner fragment. `[USER].dialog` is itself a `_fragment`. The repro opens that dialog from a fragment widget’s `on_click`, so the dialog (and the nested `[USER].fragment` inside it) are registered during the callback. Since #16141 (in 1.64), callbacks bind `ThreadState.fragment_id` to the opener widget’s fragment, so those dialog/inner fragments become **descendants of the opener**. The opener then still does its default fragment rerun without calling the dialog again; `clear_stale_descendants` evicts the nested callables while the modal remains on `event_dg`. Later clicks send the evicted id and `AppSession.request_rerun` drops them. In 1.59.2 callbacks did not set `fragment_id`, so the dialog was registered as a root fragment and survived. A fragment `key` would not fix this. [#17039](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17039) (full-app-scoped dialog lifetime) likely covers this on `develop`, but its e2e opens the dialog from `if st.button()` rather than `on_click`, so that path should still be verified. ### Related Issues - [#17011](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17011) — Same eviction class: a dialog opened from a fragment stays on screen after the parent fragment reruns, but clicks stop working. Closed by #17039; this report is the `on_click` + nested inner fragment variant. - [#8591](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8591) — Opening a dialog from a button `on_click` historically made later dialog button clicks fail with a missing fragment id. [CONTRIBUTOR] Thanks for the report [USER] 

This is the same bug as #17011. The fix is already on develop in #17039 ([Preserve dialogs across parent fragment reruns](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17039)). We re-ran this issue’s repro against current develop after that merge: Increment updates Count as expected.

It will ship in the next release after 1.65 (next week). Until then, a workaround is to open the dialog from the parent fragment body (e.g. a session-state flag) rather than from on_click, so the dialog fragment is re-registered on the parent rerun.

For example:

```
[USER].fragment
def counter_dialog():
    [USER].dialog("Counter", width="small")
    def _open_dialog():
        if "count" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.count = 0
        st.metric("Count", st.session_state.count)
        if st.button("Increment", type="primary"):
            st.session_state.count += 1
            st.rerun(scope="fragment")
    # Open from the fragment body, not on_click.
    if st.button("Open Counter"):
        st.session_state.show_counter = True
    if st.session_state.get("show_counter"):
        _open_dialog()
counter_dialog()
```

This workaround is included in the repro app as well: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-17112

title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
text:
Issue #17119: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
Labels: type:bug, area:widgets, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.session_state

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

title: `aria-expanded` on elements with no role: sidebar `<section>` and `st.date_input` field fail axe `aria-allowed-attr` (WCAG 4.1.2)
text:
Issue #17126: `aria-expanded` on elements with no role: sidebar `<section>` and `st.date_input` field fail axe `aria-allowed-attr` (WCAG 4.1.2)
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, priority:P3, feature:st.date_input, feature:st.sidebar, area:accessibility, feature:st.datetime_input

### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
Every page of an app with a sidebar fails axe-core's `aria-allowed-attr` rule (impact: critical, WCAG 2.0 A,
SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value), and so does every `st.date_input`. In both cases `aria-expanded` is set on an
element whose role does not support it:

1. The sidebar is rendered as a plain `<section>` with no accessible name, so it has no landmark role that
   supports `aria-expanded`. `frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/Sidebar.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~265):
   `aria-expanded={!isCollapsed}` on the `Resizable` rendered as `StyledSidebar`.
2. The date input's field is a `<div>` with no role carrying `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`.
   `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DateInput/SingleDateInput.tsx` (1.64.0, line ~553); the same pattern
   is in `RangeDateInput.tsx`.

Assistive technology ignores (or mis-announces) state on an element it cannot map to a role, so the
expanded/collapsed state is not conveyed, and automated audits (axe, Lighthouse) report a critical failure
that app authors cannot fix from Python.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import datetime
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.sidebar.write("Sidebar content")
st.date_input("Start date", datetime.date(2026, 1, 1))
st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": ["x", "y", "z"]}))
```

title: `aria-expanded` on elements with no role: sidebar `<section>` and `st.date_input` field fail axe `aria-allowed-attr` (WCAG 4.1.2)
text:
(At 390px the sidebar starts collapsed and the same node reports `aria-expanded="false"`.)

### Suggested fix
- **Sidebar:** put the state on the control, not the region. Remove `aria-expanded` from the `<section>`;
  set `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls="<sidebar id>"` on the collapse/expand buttons
  (`stSidebarCollapseButton` / `stExpandSidebarButton`), which already carry `aria-label`s since #14563.
  Optionally give the section an accessible name (`aria-label="Sidebar"`) so it becomes a `region` landmark.
- **Date input:** follow the React Aria DatePicker pattern the widget is now built on: the field is
  `role="group"` (labelled by the widget label) and the popup state lives on the element that opens the
  calendar. Either move `aria-haspopup` / `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` / `aria-keyshortcuts` to a
  calendar toggle `<button>`, or, if the whole field must stay the trigger, give it a role that supports
  them. (It contains spinbuttons, so `role="button"` would nest interactive content; a separate button is
  the clean option.)

### Is this a regression?
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No — sidebar has had it for several releases; the date input form arrived with the non-BaseWeb
  DateInput (#16460, 1.62).

text:
Issue #17127: `st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)
Labels: type:enhancement, area:frontend, feature:st.dataframe, feature:st.data_editor, area:accessibility

### Checklist
- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary
The hover toolbar that `st.dataframe` draws (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen)
renders each button at 22.4 x 22.4 CSS px, and the buttons sit next to each other, so axe-core's
`target-size` rule (impact: serious, WCAG 2.2 AA, SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)) fails. Cause:
`StyledElementToolbarButton` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/BaseButton/styled-components.ts`
(1.64.0, line ~524) sets `padding: theme.spacing.twoXS` and `minHeight: "unset"` around a small icon.

### Reproducible Code Example
Same app as above (the `st.dataframe` line is enough).

### Steps To Reproduce
1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Hover the dataframe so the toolbar appears.
3. Run axe-core 4.13 with the `wcag22aa` tag.

### Expected Behavior
Each toolbar button is at least 24 x 24 CSS px (or spaced so a 24px circle around each does not overlap
another target).

### Current Behavior

```
target-size (serious, wcag22aa, wcag258) — 4 nodes
<button kind="elementToolbar" data-testid="stBaseButton-elementToolbar" aria-label="Show/hide columns" class="st-emotion-cache-18ac3gt eqzt73c20">
  Target has insufficient size (22.4px by 22.4px, should be at least 24px by 24px)
<button ... aria-label="Download as CSV" ...>   (same)
<button ... aria-label="Search" ...>            (same)
<button ... aria-label="Fullscreen" ...>        (same)
```

title: `st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)
text:
### Suggested fix
Give `StyledElementToolbarButton` `minWidth: "1.5rem"` and `minHeight: "1.5rem"` (24px) instead of
`minHeight: "unset"`, or raise the padding one step. The toolbar is already an overlay above the element,
so the extra 1.6px per button does not move page layout. The same styled button is used by other element
toolbars (charts, `st.data_editor`), which would all pass with the one change.

In the same minimal app, axe also reports `target-size` on the `st.date_input` month/day spinbutton
segments (17.9 x 19.6px); that may deserve its own look but is secondary.

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No.

- Python version: 3.12
- OS: Linux (CI) and Windows 11

title: `st.dataframe` toolbar buttons are 22.4px, below the WCAG 2.2 24px minimum target size (axe `target-size`)
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a WCAG 2.2 AA bug: `st.dataframe` hover-toolbar buttons (Show/hide columns, Download as CSV, Search, Fullscreen) measure **22.4×22.4 CSS px**, below the 24px minimum in SC 2.5.8 (`axe` `target-size`). The reported cause is confirmed in `StyledElementToolbarButton` (`frontend/lib/src/components/shared/BaseButton/styled-components.ts`): it sets `minHeight: "unset"` and `padding: theme.spacing.twoXS` (0.25rem / 4px) around a `md` icon (`0.9rem` / 14.4px), which is exactly 22.4px, and adjacent buttons have no extra margin. The same `ToolbarAction` / `ELEMENT_TOOLBAR` button is reused by other element toolbars (data editor, charts, images, code copy, etc.), so raising `minWidth`/`minHeight` to `1.5rem` (or equivalent padding) would fix all of them. The secondary `st.date_input` spinbutton finding is a separate widget and should be tracked on its own issue.

Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, feature:st.dataframe, status:confirmed, priority:P3

### Checklist

- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The example in https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe titled: "Example 2: Programmatically set selections" does not work if we try with empty selections.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from numpy.random import default_rng as rng

df = pd.DataFrame(rng(0).standard_normal((12, 5)), columns=["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"])

if st.button("Select the first row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [0], "columns": [], "cells": []}}
if st.button("Select no row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}

event = st.dataframe(
    df,
    key="data",
    on_select="rerun",
    selection_mode=["single-row"],
)

st.code(event.selection)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Select a row
3. Click on the button "Select the first row", it works as expected
4. Select a row again
5. Click on the button "Select no row", the dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection.

### Expected Behavior

The row selection should match the dataframe selection state and be empty.

### Current Behavior

The dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection and is not empty.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

title: Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Assigning an empty dataframe selection via `st.session_state` (for example `{"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}`) updates the Python return value, but the Glide Data Grid UI keeps the previous row highlight. Non-empty programmatic selections in the same docs example work. Backend validation already accepts empty selections and, on `value_changed`, writes them to the one-shot `selection_state` proto field. The frontend parser is also written to return an empty `GridSelection` (not `undefined`) so clearing can work, but `DataFrame` never asserts that applying that empty state actually unchecks rows. The existing e2e clear test only checks the Python markdown output, not the canvas, which matches this backend/UI split. A likely apply-path gap is that empty selection JSON is always the same string, so `processedSelectionStateRef` can skip a later clear, and/or Glide does not visually honor a controlled empty selection after a rerun in `single-row` mode. ### Related Issues - [#14454](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14454) — Previous bug in the same programmatic-selection path (`selection` key / `AttributeError`). Same session-state API; that issue was about applying selections, this one is about clearing them. - [#10128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10128) — Original request to pre-set dataframe selections via session state (shipped in #13594). This report is a gap in that feature: empty selections are a documented way to clear. - [#16388](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16388) — Similar backend/frontend split: Python reflects the cleared widget value while the UI keeps the stale one. title: Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection
text:
[NONE] Hello, I'd like to work on this issue. 

I've reproduced the bug where programmatically passing an empty selection (`{"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}`) updates the backend session state but fails to clear the active selection in the frontend UI. 

I'm planning to investigate the state reconciliation in the dataframe frontend component (`frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DataFrame/`) to see if empty arrays are being evaluated as falsy or skipped during state updates.

Could you please assign this issue to me?

title: Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection
text:
[NONE] This also affects repeated **non-empty** assignments, which may help narrow the investigation.

With the unmodified Streamlit 1.64.0 wheel in Chrome on macOS, using the example above and keeping `key="data"` unchanged:

| Sequence | Python `event.selection.rows` | Visible selected row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select a row, then click “Select no row” for the first time | `[]` | None |
| Select another row, then click “Select no row” again | `[]` | Previous row remains checked |
| Click “Select the first row” | `[0]` | First row |
| Select the second row in the grid, then click “Select the first row” again | `[0]` | Second row remains checked |

The first clear does remove the checkbox/highlight, so this is not simply empty arrays being ignored by the grid.

In [DataFrame.tsx at 1.64.0](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1.64.0/frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DataFrame/DataFrame.tsx#L661-L692), `processedSelectionStateRef` retains the last programmatic JSON string. The early return for an absent one-shot `selectionState` does not clear that ref. This appears consistent with both repeated-value failures: the same later command is skipped before parsing/applying it.

A regression check should include both `clear → user selects → clear` and `[0] → user selects [1] → [0]`, asserting the grid's selected row as well as the Python output. I haven't validated a source fix.

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
text:
Issue #17215: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
Labels: type:bug, feature:custom-components, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.fragment, area:backend, area:execution-model

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A Custom Components v2 (CCv2) `setTriggerValue` call is silently lost when its rerun request is still queued and another widget update arrives before the script runner picks it up: the `on_<event>_change` callback never runs and `result.<event>` is never set. `st.button` survives the identical sequence. With default settings this affects components inside `[USER].fragment`, and with `runner.fastReruns = false` it also affects full-app reruns.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time

import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("log", [])

probe = st.components.v2.component(
    "trigger_probe",
    html="<button id='fire'>Fire component trigger</button>",
    js="""
export default function (component) {
  const { parentElement, setTriggerValue } = component;
  parentElement.querySelector("#fire").onclick = () => setTriggerValue("fired", Date.now());
}
""",
)


[USER].fragment
def panel():
    # result.fired only exists for events with an on_<event>_change callback.
    result = probe(key="probe", on_fired_change=lambda: None)
    if result.fired:
        st.session_state.log.append("component trigger received")
    if st.button("st.button"):
        st.session_state.log.append("st.button click received")
    st.text_input("Other widget", key="other")
    st.write("Received:", st.session_state.log)
    time.sleep(5)  # a slow fragment, so the next requests queue up


panel()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. `streamlit run app.py` and wait for the first run to finish (about 5 s).
2. Click **Fire component trigger** while the app is idle. `Received:` shows `component trigger received`. This is the control.
3. Type `a` into **Other widget** and press Enter. The fragment reruns and sleeps for 5 s.
4. Within those 5 s, click **Fire component trigger**, then replace the text in **Other widget** with `b` and press Enter.
5. Wait for the fragment to finish.
6. Repeat steps 3–5, but click **st.button** instead of **Fire component trigger**.

### Expected Behavior

After step 5 the log gains a second `component trigger received`, the same way step 6 adds `st.button click received`.

### Current Behavior

After step 5 the log still holds only the control entry: the trigger fired in step 4 never reaches Python, although the text input's new value is applied. After step 6, `st.button click received` is appended as expected.

A full-app version of the script (the same body without `[USER].fragment`) behaves the same way when started with `--runner.fastReruns false`.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: macOS 27.0
- Browser: Chromium 152

### Additional Information

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
text:
- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: macOS 27.0
- Browser: Chromium 152

### Additional Information

**Why it happens.** `AppSession.request_rerun` stops the current runner and starts a new one only when `runner.fastReruns` is on and the request has no `fragment_id`. A widget-triggered fragment rerun (or any rerun when `fastReruns` is off) is handed to the existing `ScriptRunner`. A fragment rerun also does not preempt the running script (`_fragment_run_should_not_preempt_script`), so it waits in the queue. If a rerun request is already queued, `ScriptRequests.request_rerun` merges the two requests with `_coalesce_widget_states(old, new)`. That keeps the newer message's widget states and carries forward only `trigger_value` and `chat_input_value` from the older one.

A CCv2 trigger is a `json_trigger_value` on the component's synthetic aggregator ID (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<id>__events`). The frontend deletes trigger values once it has sent them, so the newer message never contains the trigger, and the merge drops it.

`string_trigger_value`, used by `st.menu_button` and `st.column_config.ButtonColumn`, is missing from the same list. Checking `_coalesce_widget_states` directly on 1.64.0, with a queued trigger of each type followed by a newer message for another widget:

| Queued trigger type | Kept after the merge |
|---|---|
| `trigger_value` (`st.button`) | yes |
| `chat_input_value` (`st.chat_input`) | yes |
| `string_trigger_value` (`st.menu_button`, `ButtonColumn`) | no |
| `json_trigger_value` (CCv2 `setTriggerValue`) | no |

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
text:
| Queued trigger type | Kept after the merge |
|---|---|
| `trigger_value` (`st.button`) | yes |
| `chat_input_value` (`st.chat_input`) | yes |
| `string_trigger_value` (`st.menu_button`, `ButtonColumn`) | no |
| `json_trigger_value` (CCv2 `setTriggerValue`) | no |

I reproduced the CCv2 case in the browser. The `string_trigger_value` row is from the function-level check only.

**Suggested fix.** 1.64.0 already has `_TRIGGER_PROTO_FIELDS` and `_has_active_trigger_value`, and `_coalesce_replay_trigger_states` uses them. `_coalesce_widget_states` could apply its existing carry-forward rule to every active trigger type through the same helper, instead of the hard-coded two-item list. When both messages carry a `json_trigger_value` for the same aggregator ID, concatenating the two event lists would keep both events. A rough sketch:

```python
import json  # not imported in script_requests.py today


def _trigger_events(state):
    events = json.loads(state.json_trigger_value)
    return events if isinstance(events, list) else [events]


# In _coalesce_widget_states, replacing the loop over the two-item list:
for old_state in old_states.widgets:
    if not _has_active_trigger_value(old_state):
        continue
    trigger_type = old_state.WhichOneof("value")
    new_state = states_by_id.get(old_state.id)
    if new_state is None or (
        new_state.WhichOneof("value") == trigger_type
        and not _has_active_trigger_value(new_state)
    ):
        # Today's rule, applied to every trigger type.
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = old_state
    elif trigger_type == "json_trigger_value" == new_state.WhichOneof("value"):
        # Both messages carry CCv2 events for one aggregator: keep both lists.
        merged = WidgetState()
        merged.CopyFrom(new_state)
        merged.json_trigger_value = json.dumps(_trigger_events(old_state) + _trigger_events(new_state))
        states_by_id[old_state.id] = merged
```

title: Custom Components v2 trigger is silently lost when another widget updates while its rerun is queued
text:
With this patched in at startup on 1.64.0, the browser repro above passes: the trigger fired in step 4 reaches Python, and the text input's new value is applied too. At the function level it keeps all four trigger types from the table and merges two events sent to one aggregator into a single list.

**Related.** The automated triage comment on #16732 (mount-time `setTriggerValue` dropped) noted this gap. The fix that closed it, #16833, made one non-test change, to `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive` in the frontend, so this backend path is unchanged. #16765 added the replay-trigger helpers that the fix above could reuse. The tech spec in the open spec PR #16763 (session-owned rerun mailbox) lists all four trigger types as ones that "may not be dropped by coalescing" and calls this the carry-forward already implemented. In 1.64.0, `_coalesce_widget_states` carries two of them. The same two-item list is on `develop` as of 2026-10-01 and in 1.52.0, so this is not a regression.

[CONTRIBUTOR] CCv2 `setTriggerValue` events are dropped when a later widget update coalesces with a still-queued rerun. `_coalesce_widget_states` in `script_requests.py` only carries forward `trigger_value` (`st.button`) and `chat_input_value`, so `json_trigger_value` (CCv2) and `string_trigger_value` (`st.menu_button`, `ButtonColumn`) are overwritten after the frontend has already deleted them. This is the default path inside `[USER].fragment` (fragment reruns do not preempt the running script) and also affects full-app reruns when `runner.fastReruns` is false. The likely fix is to reuse `_has_active_trigger_value` / `_TRIGGER_PROTO_FIELDS` in that merge and concatenate CCv2 event lists when both messages carry events for the same aggregator. This is not a regression; #16833 fixed a different, frontend path for dropped CCv2 triggers.

### Related Issues

- [#16732](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16732) — Closest sibling: CCv2 `setTriggerValue` was dropped on remount via frontend `removeInactive`. Closed by [#16833](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16833), which did not change `_coalesce_widget_states`.
- [#14710](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14710) — Open CCv2 report of trigger/result values not reliably reaching Python across remounts and rapid reruns; overlapping symptoms, different root cause.
- [#11030](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11030) — Fragment widget interactions queue instead of interrupting, which is the default window in which this coalescing drop occurs.

Issue #17216: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances Labels: type:bug, feature:custom-components, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:app-testing ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary An app that imports an inline `st.components.v2.component(...)` from another module works under `streamlit run`, but in a test suite only the first `AppTest` that imports that module can render it: every later `AppTest` in the same Python process records `StreamlitAPIException: Component '' is not registered.` in `at.exception`. If anything imports the module before the first `AppTest` runs (a `conftest.py`, another test), that one fails too, so results depend on test order. A component defined in the script body itself is not affected, because it registers again on every run. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python # my_component.py import streamlit as st greeting = st.components.v2.component("greeting", html="

hi

") # app.py from my_component import greeting greeting(key="g") # test_app.py from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest def test_first_apptest_renders_the_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value def test_second_apptest_renders_the_same_component(): at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run() assert not at.exception, at.exception[0].value ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Put the three files in one directory. 2. Run `pytest test_app.py`. ### Expected Behavior Both tests pass, the same way `streamlit run app.py` renders the component every time. ### Current Behavior ``` E AssertionError: Component 'greeting' is not registered. 1 failed, 1 passed ```

title: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances
text:
### Expected Behavior

Both tests pass, the same way `streamlit run app.py` renders the component every time.

### Current Behavior

```
E       AssertionError: Component 'greeting' is not registered.
1 failed, 1 passed
```

The first test passes and the second fails. Each test passes when run on its own. If `import my_component` is added at the top of `test_app.py`, both fail.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0 (also reproduced on 1.63.0)
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: macOS 27.0
- Browser: n/a (AppTest)

### Additional Information

**Why it happens.** `st.components.v2.component()` registers the definition once, when it is called (normally at module import), into `get_bidi_component_manager()`. That is the active runtime's registry, or a throwaway local `BidiComponentManager` when no runtime exists. `AppTest` creates one `BidiComponentManager` per instance (reused across that instance's reruns) and only runs `discover_and_register_components()` on it, which scans installed component packages. Python caches the module, so later instances never re-run the `component()` call, and the name is missing from their registry.

**Workaround.** Make the module re-import inside each test's run:

```python
# conftest.py
import sys

import pytest


[USER].fixture(autouse=True)
def reimport_component_module():
    sys.modules.pop("my_component", None)
```

With this fixture both tests pass. Replacing the component callable with a stub in tests also works.

title: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances
text:
**Workaround.** Make the module re-import inside each test's run:

```python
# conftest.py
import sys

import pytest


[USER].fixture(autouse=True)
def reimport_component_module():
    sys.modules.pop("my_component", None)
```

With this fixture both tests pass. Replacing the component callable with a stub in tests also works.

**Suggested fix.** `_mount_component` closes over only `component_key` and `isolate_styles`, but `_create_component_callable()` has the raw `html`, `css` and `js` in scope. If it kept them, `_mount_component` could register the definition into the current registry when the name is missing there, before mounting. File-backed definitions would need their paths resolved against that registry. Alternatively, keep a process-level record of inline definitions and seed each new `AppTest` registry from it.

**Related.** #15484 (AppTest did not discover installed CCv2 components) and #14274 (AppTest `TypeError` with CCv2) are both closed. #14274's reproducer used this same imported-module pattern with a single test. The regression test added with its fix (#14301) defines the component inside `AppTest.from_function`, so it registers again on every run and does not cover this case.

title: AppTest: an `st.components.v2` component defined in an imported module is "not registered" in later AppTest instances
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a real `AppTest` isolation bug for inline `st.components.v2` components defined in an imported module. `st.components.v2.component()` registers once at import time into `get_bidi_component_manager()`, which is the active runtime’s `BidiComponentManager` (or a throwaway local manager if no runtime exists). title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
text:
Issue #17249: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.session_state, feature:app-testing, area:backend, area:execution-model

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
text:
### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
text:
### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a bug in `AppTest`, reproduced on Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0: a keyed widget with `persist_state="page"` keeps its value while hidden, then comes back empty when shown again, even though the test never changes pages. A browser session keeps the value, and `persist_state="session"` keeps it in `AppTest`. `AppTest._run()` builds a new `PagesManager` on every run, and that manager's current page hash starts as `""`. `ScriptRunner` compares that empty hash with the target page (the main-script hash when no page was requested), treats the rerun as a page change, and runs page-change widget cleanup before `ScriptRunContext.reset()` installs the real page hash. Page-scoped persistence then sees a different page and drops the preserved value, including the pending reset that makes the remounted widget ignore its stored value. A contributor reproduced this on `develop`; seeding the new manager with the requested hash stops the false page change, but that also makes the current and requested hashes identical after `switch_page()`, so the pre-run cleanup that should drop page-scoped state before the new page registers widgets would be skipped. The seed needs to be the page from the previous run, with the requested hash passed separately. ### Related Issues No duplicates found. These are nearby, with different failures: - [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) — `AppTest` can hit a session-state `KeyError` when conditional inputs disappear on rerun. Same test runner and dynamic widget tree; this issue drops a page-persistent value with no exception. - [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) — `AppTest` raises `KeyError` when a rerun adds widgets and updates others.

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] ## Verification: confirmed Reproduced on the reported 1.65.0 from PyPI and on `develop` (192c914271), macOS/arm64 with Python 3.12. Page-scoped persistence therefore sees a different page on each rerun and drops the value — which is

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
text:
[NONE] I reproduced this on Python 3.13 / Windows against `develop`, and I think I've found the cause.

**Root cause**

`AppTest._run()` builds a new `PagesManager` on every run, and its `_current_page_script_hash` starts out empty. `ScriptRunner` compares that against the requested page hash, sees a mismatch, and does the page-change cleanup. That cleanup drops page-persistent widget state. A browser session keeps one `PagesManager`, so it doesn't hit this, and `persist_state=session` isn't affected.

**Observed with the repro from the issue**

- Before: hidden state is `'SKU-42'`, but after showing the input again its value is `''`, with no exceptions.
- After the change below: hidden state is `'SKU-42'` and the shown value is `'SKU-42'`.

**Possible fix** in `lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py`, right after the `PagesManager` is constructed in `_run()`:

```python
pages_manager.set_current_page_script_hash(
    self._page_hash or pages_manager.main_script_hash
)
```

This marks the fresh manager as already on the current page. `switch_page()` still sets `self._page_hash`, so real page switches are still treated as page changes.

**Regression test** (`app_test_test.py`): toggle a `persist_state=page` text input, enter a value, hide it, show it again, and assert the value is preserved.

I ran the new test and the other AppTest tests, including the `switch_page` ones, and they pass. One existing test, `test_switch_page_uses_paths_relative_to_main_script`, fails on Windows with and without this change because of path escaping in its error-message assertion, so it is unrelated.

I know external PRs are paused, so I'm posting this as a diagnosis. I can share the patch if it's useful.

title: Button in horizontal container shows native browser title tooltip even when the label is not truncated
text:
Issue #17264: Button in horizontal container shows native browser title tooltip even when the label is not truncated
Labels: type:enhancement, area:frontend, area:widgets, feature:st.container, feature:st.columns, feature:tooltip, feature:st.button

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Starting with Streamlit 1.62.0, a button inside **st.container(horizontal=True)** (or placed directly in a column) gets an HTML **title** attribute on its label when **help** is not set. Hovering the label then shows the browser's native tooltip.

According to the **wrap** docstring, this is meant to "reveal the full label" when it's truncated with an ellipsis. However, the **title** is added even when the label fits and nothing is truncated. The result is an unexpected, unstyled tooltip on every short button in a horizontal layout. It also looks inconsistent next to Streamlit's own **help** tooltip, which has a different style and position.

### Reproducible Code Example

title: Button in horizontal container shows native browser title tooltip even when the label is not truncated
text:
### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

LONG_LABEL = "This is a very long button label " * 6

# 1. Unexpected: native tooltip although the label is not truncated
with st.container(horizontal=True):
    st.button("Short label")

# 2. Truncated label: here the native tooltip is useful
with st.container(horizontal=True):
    st.button(LONG_LABEL)

# 3. wrap=True: label wraps, no native tooltip
with st.container(horizontal=True):
    st.button(LONG_LABEL, wrap=True, key="wrapped")

# 4. Vertical container: no native tooltip
with st.container(horizontal=False):
    st.button("Short label", key="vertical")

# 5. help set: Streamlit tooltip only
st.button("With help", help="This is a button with a tooltip")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above with **streamlit run app.py**.
2. Hover the mouse over the text of the first button ("Short label") and wait about one second.

### Expected Behavior

No tooltip should appear, because the label is fully visible and **help** is not set. The native **title** tooltip should appear only when the label is actually truncated, as in case 2.

### Current Behavior

The browser's native tooltip (rectangular, below and to the right of the cursor) shows the label text even though nothing is truncated. The button in the vertical container (case 4) does not show it.

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0 (also reproduced on 1.62.0)
- Python version: 3.12.8
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome 154.0.8037.95 (64-bit)

### Additional Information

### Debug info

- Python version: 3.12.8
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome 154.0.8037.95 (64-bit)

### Additional Information

**Button** passes **addTitleTooltip = !wrap && !help** to the label component. In the 1.65.0 bundle, the hook that handles this flag (minified, in **StreamlitMarkdown.*.js**) always sets **title** to the label's text content. It does not check whether the text overflows (for example **el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth**).

A possible fix is to set **title** only when the label is truncated, and re-check it with a **ResizeObserver** alongside the existing **MutationObserver**. The same hook appears to be used by **st.checkbox**, **st.popover** and markdown with **wrap=False**, so these may be affected too.

Workaround: pass **wrap=True** to the button.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This matches a documented limitation of the `wrap` behavior added in 1.62 ([#16325](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16325)), rather than an accidental title being attached. Inside `st.container(horizontal=True)`, and for a button placed directly in a column, `useResolvedWrap` treats the default `wrap=None` as no-wrap. `Button` then sets `addTitleTooltip` whenever that resolved wrap is false and `help` is unset. `useLabelTitleTooltip` always copies the rendered plain-text label onto a native HTML `title` and never checks overflow (`scrollWidth` vs `clientWidth`) or listens for resize. The horizontal-wrap product spec records this as an accepted trade-off ("Tooltip for the full label") and defers a follow-up, "Styled, only-when-clipped label tooltip", that would measure truncation and use the styled tooltip. The same hook is shared by the other button-like controls, `st.checkbox` / `st.toggle`, and `wrap=False` text, so those surfaces show the same native tooltip. `wrap=True` or a `help` string avoids the native title on buttons.

### Related Issues

No duplicate of this report was found. The two closest open issues are adjacent tooltip and truncation requests:

- [#16348](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16348) — Long `st.selectbox` labels are clipped with no way to read the full text. Same "reveal the label only when it does not fit" need, but a different widget and the opposite gap (no tooltip today).
- [#12649](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12649) — `st.button` `help` tooltips are hover-only and do not appear on mobile. Related button-tooltip UX, not the native `title` path used for unwrapped labels.

title: Unknown-attribute lookup on streamlit imports modules since 1.65 (breaks iteration over sys.modules)
text:
Issue #17298: Unknown-attribute lookup on streamlit imports modules since 1.65 (breaks iteration over sys.modules)
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, status:confirmed, priority:P3, area:backend

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

### Summary

Since 1.65.0, looking up any unknown attribute on the `streamlit` module (even `hasattr(st, "x")` or `getattr(st, "x", None)`) imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` and `difflib`. Code that iterates over `sys.modules` while probing module attributes then fails with `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. This broke our whole test suite at setup after upgrading from 1.64.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import sys
import streamlit

[m for m in sys.modules.values() if getattr(m, "date", None) is not None]
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the script above in a fresh interpreter with streamlit 1.65.0.

### Expected Behavior

As in 1.64.0: the lookup returns the default, and no module is imported.

### Current Behavior

```
RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
```

The module `__getattr__` added in #16912 imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` on every miss, including lookups that only probe with a default:

```python
import sys, streamlit
before = set(sys.modules)
hasattr(streamlit, "date")                 # False, as expected
print(sorted(set(sys.modules) - before))   # ['difflib', 'streamlit.command_suggestions']
```

### Is this a regression?

Yes, this used to work in a previous version (1.64.0).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0
- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

The pattern is common in test suites: a pytest fixture scans the loaded modules to patch a name (here, freezing `date.today()`). We have fixed our side by iterating over `list(sys.modules.values())`, since iterating over the live dict is fragile in general. But a plain `hasattr` or `getattr(..., default)` now has an import side effect. Some possible ways to avoid it:

- import `streamlit.command_suggestions` eagerly (or once, at first use outside `__getattr__`);
- only build suggestions when the `AttributeError` is actually raised to user code, not on probes;

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17298)


[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a regression in 1.65.0 (working in 1.64.0), introduced by #16912. `lib/streamlit/__init__.py` defines a module `__getattr__` that lazy-imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` so a missing `st.*` name can raise `AttributeError` with a removal note or typo suggestion. `hasattr` and `getattr(obj, name, default)` both call `__getattr__` and then swallow `AttributeError`, so a probe that should only return false or the default still runs that import. `command_suggestions.py` imports `difflib` at module scope, which inserts `streamlit.command_suggestions` and `difflib` into `sys.modules`. Code that iterates the live `sys.modules` mapping while probing attributes then raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. `command_suggestions` does not import Streamlit at module level, so loading it while `streamlit` itself is imported, instead of inside `__getattr__`, would stop those probes from mutating `sys.modules`.

### Related Issues

No duplicate or closely related issues were found. Searches for `sys.modules` iteration failures, `hasattr` side effects, and the command-suggestion error path only match this report. The behavior comes from #16912, which is not linked to another issue.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a regression in `st.pydeck_chart` hover tooltips. On 1.65.0 the tooltip is drawn far above the hovered object and often off-screen; the same app is correct on 1.64.0. The new `alt` parameter (#17086) only sets an accessible name and does not affect placement.

1.65.0 bumped `[USER].gl/*` from 9.3.11 to 9.4.0 (#16924). deck.gl 9.4 (`TooltipWidget.onHover`, visgl/deck.gl#10491) positions the tooltip at `info.x/y` plus `getCanvasBounds()`, which is the canvas rectangle minus the `.deck-widgets-root` rectangle. `[USER].gl/react` renders that root as an unstyled sibling after `.deck-events-root` (`height: 100%`). The root therefore sits at the bottom of the chart, while the tooltip is absolutely positioned against the chart wrapper. For the default 500px chart that subtracts about one chart-height from the tooltip `translateY`, which matches a tooltip landing far above the cursor. Streamlit’s `createTooltip` in `useDeckGl.tsx` only supplies text or HTML; it does not set coordinates.

### Related Issues

No open issue looks like a duplicate of this positioning regression.

- [#2242](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2242) is an older, closed report about pydeck tooltips together with a basemap when embedding deck HTML. It is a different problem and should not be treated as a duplicate.

Issue #17338: Main scroll region (`stMain`) takes keyboard focus with no visible focus indicator
Labels: type:enhancement, area:frontend, area:styling, area:accessibility

### Checklist

- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`section[data-testid="stMain"]` is a Tab stop, which is right for keyboard scrolling (axe `scrollable-region-focusable`). But when it has focus it shows no indicator: `outline-style: none` and `box-shadow: none`. On every page, the Tab stop after the header is invisible, which fails WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st


def home():
    st.title("Home")
    st.button("First button")
    st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": ["x", "y", "z"]}))
    st.button("Last button")


pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "": [st.Page(home, title="Home")],
        "Group": [
            st.Page(lambda: st.write("B"), title="Page B", url_path="b"),
            st.Page(lambda: st.write("C"), title="Page C", url_path="c"),
        ],
    },
    position="top",
)
pg.run()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Press Tab from the top of the page. Stops 1–4 are the top-nav items, Deploy and Main menu (Main menu shows a box-shadow ring).
3. Press Tab once more.

### Expected Behavior

A `:focus-visible` indicator on the main region, such as the ring other controls use.

### Current Behavior

Stop 5 is `stMain`, with `outline: none` and `box-shadow: none`. Nothing on screen shows where focus is.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

title: Main scroll region (`stMain`) takes keyboard focus with no visible focus indicator
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] `section[data-testid="stMain"]` is a tab stop on purpose. `AppView` renders the main scroll container (`StyledAppViewMain`, or `ScrollToBottomContainer` when an auto-positioned chat input is present) with `tabIndex={0}` so arrow keys can scroll it, which satisfies the axe `scrollable-region-focusable` rule. That element then clears the browser outline in `frontend/app/src/components/AppView/styled-components.ts` (`&:focus { outline: "none" }`) and has no `:focus-visible` rule that draws `theme.shadows.focusRing`, the ring used by code blocks and widgets. Global styles only suppress outlines on `[tabindex="-1"]` elements that are not `:focus-visible`, so the invisible stop comes from this component style. The `tabIndex` is applied even when `disableScrolling` sets `overflow: hidden`. This matches the report on 1.65.0 and 1.61.1 and is longstanding behavior (the outline suppression dates to 2020), so it is a bug rather than a regression.

### Related Issues

- [#17337](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17337) — Same reporter and the same repro app, filed with this issue. The `st.dataframe` toolbar stays in the tab order at `opacity: 0` during keyboard focus, which is a separate WCAG 2.4.7 failure on a different element.
- [#17339](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17339) — Same keyboard pass through top navigation. A section dropdown in `st.navigation(position="top")` does not move focus into the open menu or respond to arrow keys, so its items come after every other control (WCAG 2.4.3). Those nav items are the tab stops immediately before `stMain` in this report.

title: getCookie throws SecurityError in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so the websocket never opens
text:
Issue #17402: getCookie throws SecurityError in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so the websocket never opens
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, area:network, status:needs-triage, feature:embedding

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit can't open its websocket when the app runs in an iframe sandboxed without `allow-same-origin`. That frame's document has an opaque origin, and reading `document.cookie` there throws `SecurityError`. `getCookie` in `frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts` reads it without a try/catch. `WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens` calls `getCookie("_streamlit_xsrf")` on every connect, even after `claimHostAuthToken()` has returned a token. The error makes `connectToWebSocket` reject before the handshake starts, and the frame stays blank.

`localStorageAvailable()`, a few lines below `getCookie`, already wraps its storage access in a try/catch. The cookie helpers need the same guard.

We sandbox each embedded app without `allow-same-origin` so that it gets its own opaque origin and can't reach the parent page or another embedded app.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
`app.py`:


import streamlit as st
st.write("hello from streamlit")


`host/index.html`:


<!doctype html>
<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src="http://localhost:8599/" width="800" height="400"></iframe>
```

### Steps To Reproduce

title: getCookie throws SecurityError in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so the websocket never opens
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `streamlit run app.py --server.port 8599 --server.enableCORS false --server.enableXsrfProtection false --browser.gatherUsageStats false`.
2. Serve the host page with `python -m http.server 8598 -d host`.
3. Open `http://localhost:8598/` in Chromium.

Two things unrelated to this bug get in the way first. Streamlit sends no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header on `/static/`, so the opaque-origin document can't load the module scripts. On loopback, Chromium's Local Network Access check also blocks the websocket. I got past both in Playwright with:

```js
await page.context().grantPermissions(['local-network-access']);
await page.route('http://localhost:8599/**', async r => {
  const res = await r.fetch();
  await r.fulfill({ response: res, headers: { ...res.headers(), 'access-control-allow-origin': '*' } });
});
await page.goto('http://localhost:8598/');
```

### Expected Behavior

`getCookie` returns `undefined` when the document can't read cookies. The handshake goes ahead with the host auth token or the placeholder, and the app renders. With the guard below patched into the 1.65.0 bundle, the frame shows "hello from streamlit".

### Current Behavior

```
SecurityError: Failed to read the 'cookie' property from 'Document': The document is sandboxed and lacks the 'allow-same-origin' flag.
    at wT (http://localhost:8599/static/js/index.CKCTizkM.js:26:87723)
    at aE.getSessionTokens (http://localhost:8599/static/js/index.CKCTizkM.js:29:1763)
    at async aE.connectToWebSocket (http://localhost:8599/static/js/index.CKCTizkM.js:29:2122)
```

No websocket request goes out and the frame stays blank.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0 (also 1.56.0)
- Python version: 3.12.14
- Operating system: Linux
- Browser: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (headless)

### Additional Information

Three call sites read the cookie:

title: getCookie throws SecurityError in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, so the websocket never opens
text:
### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0 (also 1.56.0)
- Python version: 3.12.14
- Operating system: Linux
- Browser: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (headless)

### Additional Information

Three call sites read the cookie:

- `WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens`, on every connect.
- `DefaultStreamlitEndpoints.csrfRequest`, for file upload and delete when XSRF protection is on.
- `MetricsManager.getAnonymousId`, when usage stats are on. It then calls `setCookie` in `frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts`, which writes `document.cookie` without a guard and throws the same way.

A sandboxed frame can't hold the `_streamlit_xsrf` cookie, so it needs `server.enableXsrfProtection=false`. #16476 gives the same advice for cross-origin pages, and this fix doesn't change that.

A possible fix is to guard both helpers:

```diff
--- a/frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts
+++ b/frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts
 export function getCookie(name: string): string | undefined {
-  const r = document.cookie.match(`\\b${name}=([^;]*)\\b`)
+  let cookies: string
+  try {
+    cookies = document.cookie
+  } catch {
+    // A frame sandboxed without allow-same-origin has no cookie access.
+    return undefined
+  }
+  const r = cookies.match(`\\b${name}=([^;]*)\\b`)
   return r ? r[1] : undefined
 }
--- a/frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts
+++ b/frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts
-  document.cookie = `${name}=${value};${expirationStr}path=/`
+  try {
+    document.cookie = `${name}=${value};${expirationStr}path=/`
+  } catch {
+    // A frame sandboxed without allow-same-origin has no cookie access.
+  }
```

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend connection bug. An iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and no `allow-same-origin` has an opaque origin, and reading `document.cookie` there throws `SecurityError`. `getCookie` in `frontend/utils/src/browser/index.ts` reads `document.cookie` with no guard, while `localStorageAvailable()` a few lines below already catches storage access failures. `WebsocketConnection.getSessionTokens` always calls `getCookie("_streamlit_xsrf")` after `claimHostAuthToken()`, so the exception rejects `connectToWebSocket` before `new WebSocket` and the frame stays blank. The same read is used by `DefaultStreamlitEndpoints.csrfRequest` (upload and delete) and `MetricsManager.getAnonymousId`; `setCookie` in `frontend/lib/src/util/utils.ts` writes `document.cookie` the same way and can throw when usage stats are on. Catching the error and treating cookies as unavailable matches the reported patch. A sandboxed frame still cannot store `_streamlit_xsrf`, so this embed needs `server.enableXsrfProtection=false`, which is the same constraint [PR #16476](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16476) documents for cross-origin handshakes.

### Related Issues

- [#16477](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16477) — Same `getSessionTokens` path: the host auth token and the XSRF cookie share one WebSocket subprotocol slot. This report fails earlier, while reading the cookie, and both are about connecting when that cookie is not a usable credential.
- [#9397](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9397) — File uploads from an iframed app fail with an Axios 403 tied to the XSRF cookie. That is the `csrfRequest` call site of `getCookie`, a later iframe failure once the socket is up. The issue is closed and was marked as not reproducible.

No open issue reports this `SecurityError` on `document.cookie` in a sandbox without `allow-same-origin`.

title: Improve app-shell landmarks and add a skip link (WCAG 2.4.1)
text:
Issue #17416: Improve app-shell landmarks and add a skip link (WCAG 2.4.1)
Labels: type:enhancement, area:accessibility

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit’s app shell should expose clear page landmarks and a way to skip repeated chrome, so keyboard and screen-reader users can move straight to the main content (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks).

Today the shell has a semantic `<header>` and a labeled sidebar region, but the primary content area (`stMain`) is a `<section>` rather than `<main>`, sidebar/page navigation is not exposed as a `navigation` landmark, and there is no skip link.

### Why?

Without a main landmark and a skip mechanism, assistive-tech users often have to tab through header, toolbar, and sidebar controls on every page load or navigation. This was called out as part of the “page structure” ask in #8399 (now closed/triaged). Our theme a11y inventory also leaves WCAG **2.4.1** unscored.

### How?

Suggested shell improvements (exact shape TBD):

1. **Main landmark** — Render the primary app content as `<main>` (or give `stMain` an equivalent landmark role), without breaking existing layout/scroll behavior or `data-testid="stMain"` consumers.
2. **Navigation landmark** — Expose sidebar page nav and/or top nav as `<nav>` (or `role="navigation"`) with an accessible name when present.
3. **Skip link** — Add a keyboard-focusable “Skip to main content” link (visually hidden until focused) that moves focus into the main landmark.

text:
Issue #17422: Allow pyarrow 26 (needed for Python 3.15 wheels)
Labels: type:enhancement, area:arrow, area:dependencies

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit 1.65.0 pins `pyarrow>=7.0,!=25.0.0,<26` (and `develop` still has `<26`). pyarrow 26.0.0 was released on 2026-10-09 and is the first release with CPython 3.15 wheels; pyarrow 25.x has no `cp315` wheels.

Since Python 3.15.0 is also out, installing Streamlit on Python 3.15 currently forces the resolver onto pyarrow 25.0.1, which has to be built from source and fails unless the Arrow C++ libraries are installed.

Could the upper bound be raised to `<27`?

### Reproducible Code Example

```bash
uv init demo && cd demo
uv python pin 3.15
uv add streamlit
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use Python 3.15.0 (macOS arm64 here).
2. Install `streamlit==1.65.0`.

### Expected Behavior

Streamlit installs using the pyarrow 26.0.0 `cp315` wheel.

### Current Behavior

The resolver picks pyarrow 25.0.1, tries to build it from source and fails:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:294 (find_package):
  By not providing "FindArrow.cmake" in CMAKE_MODULE_PATH this project has
  asked CMake to find a package configuration file provided by "Arrow", but
  CMake did not find one.

*** CMake configuration failed

hint: `pyarrow` (v25.0.1) was included because ... depends on `streamlit` (v1.65.0) which depends on `pyarrow`
```

### Is this a regression?

title: Allow pyarrow 26 (needed for Python 3.15 wheels)
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Streamlit 1.65.0 and current `develop` require `pyarrow>=10.0.1,!=25.0.0,<26` in `lib/pyproject.toml`. The `<26` cap is the usual next-major bound, last raised in #16529; the `!=25.0.0` exclusion should stay with any bump because PyArrow 25.0.0 can segfault on first import from a short-lived worker thread. PyArrow 26.0.0 (2026-10-09) is the first release with CPython 3.15 wheels, and the 25.x line has none, so a 3.15 install resolves to 25.0.1, which has no `cp315` wheel and fails in CMake while building from source without the Arrow C++ libraries. Supported versions are still 3.11–3.14 (`PYTHON_MAX_VERSION` is 3.14), while `requires-python` is `>=3.11` with no upper cap, so resolvers still attempt the install. Raising the bound to `<27` would allow the 26.0.0 wheel; adding 3.15 classifiers and CI would be a follow-up.

### Related Issues

- [#14847](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14847) (closed): PyArrow installation failed on Python 3.14 because the allowed range did not include a release with 3.14 wheels. Same install-time failure mode on the previous CPython release.
- [#12774](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12774) (closed): Request to officially support Python 3.14, including dependency and CI updates. This issue is the narrower PyArrow 26 step toward the same kind of support for 3.15.

No open duplicate was found.
