title: time range slider in 1.64 inconsistent with previous versions (can't select 23:59 with default step)
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a regression in time-range `st.slider`, filed on the enhancement template. A time slider still defaults to `step=timedelta(minutes=15)`, with bounds `time.min` (00:00) and `time.max` (23:59:59.999999, displayed as 23:59 via the `HH:mm` format). Fifteen-minute steps from midnight land on 23:45, so the thumb can no longer reach 23:59; an explicit `max_value=time(23, 59)` has the same gap (14 minutes past the last step). Before 1.59.0, the BaseWeb slider (`react-range`) returned `max` when the pointer moved past the end of the track, so end-of-day stayed selectable even when it was off the step grid. [#15439](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15439) replaced that with React Aria, whose `snapValueToStep` clamps to the last step that is still `<= max`. That is the behavior in 1.64 and on current `develop` (1.66.0). The same clamp applies to any slider whose span is not a multiple of `step`. `step=timedelta(minutes=1)` reaches 23:59 only because that bound then sits on the grid. ### Related Issues No duplicate of this report was found. - [#6328](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6328) — request to type an exact value into `st.slider`, because dragging to a precise number is impractical. That is the same reason a 1-minute step is a poor workaround for selecting 23:59. It does not restore an off-grid maximum. - [#9184](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9184) — closed step bug where some float values were unreachable because an integer-valued `step` (such as `1.0`) was measured from 0 instead of `min_value`. Same “step grid skips an expected value” symptom, different cause. --- *This is an automated triage comment using `grok-4.7-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels

### Summary

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st

def cook_breakfast():
    msg = st.toast("Gathering ingredients...")
    time.sleep(1)
    msg.toast("Cooking...")
    time.sleep(1)
    msg.toast("Ready!", icon="🥞")

if st.button("Cook breakfast"):
    cook_breakfast()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Click the button
3. Watch as the toast does not update

### Expected Behavior

Watch as the toast updates to reflect the new message.

### Current Behavior

No error message in either the python or in the browser console. 

### Is this a regression?

title: Bug: Update a toast message example fails, even on docs page
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a regression in the documented `st.toast` update pattern (`msg = st.toast(...); msg.toast(...)`), including Example 3 on the docs page. The first toast appears, later calls produce no Python or browser error, and the visible text never changes. The backend still does the right thing: `st.toast` returns a `DeltaGenerator` locked to that element (`Cursor.lock_element`), so `msg.toast()` overwrites the same delta path within the run. The break matches 1.59 / [#15523](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15523). That change replaced BaseWeb with React Aria’s `toastQueue` and dropped the old `toaster.update()` effect that pushed body and icon changes into an already-visible toast. `Toast` now calls `toastQueue.add` only on mount (`useEffect` with `[]` in `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Toast/Toast.tsx`). Within one run the node keeps the same `scriptRunId` key, so React updates props in place and the effect never runs again. On 1.66, [#16498](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16498) adds a second guard: if a toast with the same `toastId` (the delta path) is already in `toastQueue.visibleToasts`, the effect returns and keeps the original content. A fix needs to write the new body and icon into the existing queue entry, while still avoiding a duplicate when a rerun re-emits the same toast. No other open issue reports this update failure. ### Related Issues - [#7740](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7740) (closed by [#16498](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16498)): toasts disappeared when `st.rerun()` followed `st.toast()`. The fix keeps the toast alive across remounts and skips a second enqueue when that delta path is already visible, which also drops a real in-place `msg.toast()` update. - [#15523](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15523): removed the BaseWeb toaster, including the effect that applied body and icon

title: Bug: Update a toast message example fails, even on docs page

This is the 1.59 change; the docs example worked in 1.58. --- *This is an automated triage comment using `grok-4.7-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

title: Bug: Update a toast message example fails, even on docs page
text: [NONE] I've gone ahead and tried to fix the bug. I've interacted with the 1.58, 1.59, 1.66 and proposed fixes. The proposed bug version appears to replicate the 1.58 behavior though I know there was an issue that changed how toast behave during a re-run and I haven't tested that explicitly. :robot: _AI text below_ :robot: ## Root cause #15523 (released in 1.59.0) replaced the BaseWeb toaster with react-aria's `ToastQueue`. The BaseWeb version had a `toaster.update` effect, and `msg.toast(...)` relied on it to update the toast already on screen. `ToastQueue` has no update API (only `add`, `close`, `pauseAll`, `resumeAll` and `clear`), and the `Toast` component only calls `add` on mount. When `msg.toast(...)` re-sends the element at the same delta path in the same run, the new props reach the component but are never applied, so the first toast stays on screen until it expires. 1.58.0 is the last release where the docs example works. There, each update replaced the toast's content in place and restarted its 4s timer. ## Open design question: interaction with #16498 #16498 (for #7740) de-duplicates a toast that a new run re-emits at the same position while it's still visible. The existing toast and its timer are kept, whatever the new content is. That also affects the docs example. If you click "Cook breakfast" again while "Ready!" is still showing, the new run's "Gathering ingredients..." is treated as a duplicate and suppressed. In 1.58, a second click restarted the sequence. One way to keep both behaviors:

title: Bug: Update a toast message example fails, even on docs page
text: the docs example. If you click "Cook breakfast" again while "Ready!" is still showing, the new run's "Gathering ingredients..." is treated as a duplicate and suppressed. In 1.58, a second click restarted the sequence. One way to keep both behaviors: compare the new content with what is on screen. - **Identical body, icon and duration:** leave the toast and its timer alone, as #16498 does. An unconditional `st.toast("Saved")` still expires 4s after it first appeared, across reruns. - **Different content:** replace the toast and restart its timer, as 1.58 did. ## Reference implementation I tried that approach in [one commit on my fork](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/compare/develop...tabedzki:streamlit:tabedzki/fix/toast-update-in-place), in case it's useful. **How it works:** - A small store holds each visible toast's current content and is read by `StreamlitToastItem`. Each update replaces the content and restarts the timer, keeping the toast's stack position and expanded state. - Dismissed or expired toasts are not shown again, as the docstring says. **Testing:** it includes Vitest tests, plus two E2E tests that fail on `develop` and pass with the change. **Differences from 1.58:** - The restarted timer uses the update's `duration`. - Switching between a timed and an infinite duration replaces the toast, because react-aria fixes the timer when the toast is created.

title: `st.chat_input(accept_audio=True)`: recording waveform disappears once the text area has expanded to multiple lines
text:
Issue #17528: `st.chat_input(accept_audio=True)`: recording waveform disappears once the text area has expanded to multiple lines
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.chat_input

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

### Summary
With `accept_audio=True`, the live waveform shows while recording only until the chat input's text area has once expanded to more than one line. After that, every later recording shows an empty waveform area until the page is reloaded. Recording itself still works: the audio is captured and returned correctly. Only the visualization is missing, so users can't tell whether the microphone is picking anything up.

This is easy to hit when an app pre-fills the input via session state, e.g. putting a speech transcript into the field so the user can edit it before sending. But it also reproduces with nothing but typed text.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

value = st.chat_input("Say something", accept_audio=True)
if value:
    st.write(value)
```

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Run the app and open it in the browser.
2. Click the mic: the waveform animates while recording. Cancel or send.
3. Type a message with at least two lines (Shift+Enter) so the text area expands.
   Don't send it.
4. Click the mic again and speak.

title: `st.chat_input(accept_audio=True)`: recording waveform disappears once the text area has expanded to multiple lines
text:
Variant with programmatic text: set `st.session_state["<key>"] = "line 1\n\nline 2"` before rendering a keyed `st.chat_input(key="<key>", accept_audio=True)`, then record.

### Expected Behavior
The waveform animates during every recording, whatever was in the text area before.

### Current Behavior
In step 4 the recording UI appears (cancel and stop buttons, timer), but the waveform area stays empty. It stays empty for all later recordings, even after the text is cleared, until the page is reloaded.

### Possible cause (from reading the 1.66.0 frontend bundle)
- `ChatInput` renders two layouts:
  `isExtended && !isRecording ? <expanded layout> : <compact layout>`. The waveform container (`<div ref={waveformContainerRef}>` inside the `isRecording` wrapper) exists only in the compact layout.
- When the text area extends, the compact layout unmounts, so the container `<div>` is removed. When recording starts, the compact layout mounts again with a **new** container element.
- `useWaveformController` creates the WaveSurfer instance and the record plugin only once. `start()` does `if (initializedRef.current || await initialize()) ...`, and the init effect depends only on stable callbacks, not on the container element. WaveSurfer therefore stays bound to the first, now detached container and draws into a node that is no longer in the DOM.

Possible fixes:
- (a) Keep the waveform container mounted in both layouts and hide it with CSS instead of unmounting it.
- (b) Use a callback ref, or compare `containerRef.current` with the element WaveSurfer was created with, and tear down and reinitialize when it changes.

title: `st.chat_input(accept_audio=True)`: recording waveform disappears once the text area has expanded to multiple lines

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-17528)


[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend bug in `st.chat_input(accept_audio=True)`: once the text area has expanded past one line, later recordings still capture audio and show the recording controls, but the live waveform stays empty until the page reloads.

The waveform node (`StyledChatAudioWave`, `waveformContainerRef` in `ChatInput.tsx`) is rendered only in the compact row. The expanded toolbar branch (`hasExpandedHeight && !isRecording`) unmounts it, and starting a recording mounts a new empty div. `useWaveformController` builds WaveSurfer once: `initializeWaveSurfer` skips work when `isInitializedRef` is already set, and its effect depends on the stable ref object, theme, and sample rate, so it never notices the DOM node was replaced. `start()` keeps painting into the detached node.

An input that is already expanded on first paint (a multiline value, or `height` other than `"content"`) can fail earlier. The init effect sees a null container and returns, and the first `start()` throws `Record backend not initialized`. `st.audio_input` keeps its waveform node mounted, so it does not have this layout bug. Keeping one container mounted across both layouts, or recreating WaveSurfer when the element changes, would fix it.

### Related Issues

No open duplicate was found.

- [#12446](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12446) (closed): `st.audio_input` kept playback waveform colors after seeking and recording again. It shares `useWaveformController` / WaveSurfer, with a different symptom (stale colors, not a missing waveform). The reporter already separated it from this bug.

title: Button help tooltip reopens and sticks after closing the st.dialog it opened

Issue #17562: Button help tooltip reopens and sticks after closing the st.dialog it opened
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:tooltip, feature:st.button, feature:st.dialog

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a button with `help=` opens an `st.dialog`, closing the dialog brings the button's tooltip back. It then stays open until the pointer moves over the button or the user clicks somewhere else. This happens with centered dialogs and with `position="right"` drawers, and with every way of closing (✕, clicking outside, or a button inside the dialog that calls `st.rerun()`).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


[USER].dialog("Centered dialog")
def centered():
    st.write("Close me with the X, Esc, clicking outside, or the button.")
    if st.button("Close"):
        st.rerun()


[USER].dialog("Right drawer", position="right")
def drawer():
    st.write("Close me with the X, Esc, clicking outside, or the button.")
    if st.button("Close"):
        st.rerun()


st.subheader("With help (bug)")
if st.button("Open dialog", help="This tooltip reappears after the dialog closes."):
    centered()
if st.button("Open drawer", help="This tooltip reappears after the drawer closes."):
    drawer()

st.subheader("Without help (control)")
if st.button("Open dialog (no help)"):
    centered()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog** with the mouse.
2. Close the dialog with the mouse (✕, click outside, or **Close**).
3. Leave the mouse still, away from the button.

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a frontend bug: an `st.button` with `help` reopens its tooltip and leaves it on screen after the `st.dialog` it opened is closed. It happens for centered dialogs and `position="right"` drawers, and for every close path in the report (close button, outside click, Escape, or an inner button that calls `st.rerun()`). React Aria’s dialog overlay restores focus to the opener button. `TriggerArea` in `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Tooltip/Tooltip.tsx` treats any focus inside the trigger as a reason to open immediately (`useFocusWithin` → `state.open(true)`), which skips the 500ms hover delay used for button help. `onPointerLeave` then leaves the tooltip open while that focus remains, so it stays visible with the pointer still elsewhere until the button blurs. That focus-within behavior has been in place since the BaseWeb tooltip replacement (#15310). #17489 and #17502 are the later React Aria / Floating UI tooltip updates; they changed portal placement, and the open-on-any-focus path predates them. Keyboard focus (Tab, and Escape when focus is restored as keyboard focus) should still show the tooltip. jsdom does not model input modality, so a Playwright test is the right coverage. ### Related Issues - [#13263](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13263) (closed): opening a dialog with a button shortcut left a focus-visible ring on controls inside the dialog. Adjacent dialog focus-modality bug; closed as fixed after the React Aria migration. The stuck tooltip is a separate failure on the opener after close. - [#9243](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243): the first widget inside `st.popover` or `st.dialog` appears active when the overlay opens. Also dialog focus, on content inside the overlay.

text:
### Summary

a StreamlitInvalidLayoutContextError is raised when triggering process_user_prompt_chat_input, even with setting up correctly the outside container.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
"""
Standalone fragment/chat_input bug.
No external dependencies — only streamlit + stdlib.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import sys
import logging
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Iterator, List, Optional

import streamlit as st
from streamlit import session_state as ss
from streamlit import runtime
from streamlit.web import cli as stcli

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# ── Stub models ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[USER]
class FakeEvent:
    step_name: str
    content: str


[USER]
class FakePromptEvents:
    user_prompt: str
    session_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    run_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    task_id: Optional[str] = None
    events: List[FakeEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
    is_complete: bool = False

    def is_incomplete(self) -> bool:
        return not self.is_complete


# ── Stub workflow ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def fake_run(user_prompt: str) -> Iterator[FakeEvent]:
    """Simulates a streaming workflow response."""
    yield FakeEvent(step_name='think', content=f'Thinking about: {user_prompt}')
    yield FakeEvent(step_name='answer', content=f'Here is my answer to: **{user_prompt}**')


# ── Main page ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def launch(page_key: str):

    user_prompt_events: List[FakePromptEvents] = [FakePromptEvents(user_prompt='reloading from db', events=list(fake_run('reloading ...')))]

    # ── Session-state keys ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    _k_userprompt    = f'pg_{page_key}_userprompt'
    _k_mode          = f'pg_{page_key}_mode'
    _k_rerun         = f'pg_{page_key}_rerun'
    _k_rerun_prompt  = f'pg_{page_key}_rerun_prompt'
    _k_title         = f'pg_{page_key}_title'
    _fk_chat_input   = f'pg_{page_key}_chat_input'
    _fk_input_prompt = f'pg_{page_key}_input_prompt'

    st.set_page_config(layout="wide", page_title=ss.get(_k_title, 'Chat Page'))

    # ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def push_prompt_events(pe: FakePromptEvents):
        user_prompt_events.append(pe)

    def process_event_output(events: Iterator[FakeEvent], is_new):
        """Render streaming events; returns collected list."""
        collected = list(events)
        with st.container(border=True):
            for ev in collected:
                st.markdown(f'**{ev.step_name}** — {ev.content}')
        return collected


    def process_user_prompt(user_prompt=None, last: bool = False):
        is_new = not isinstance(user_prompt, FakePromptEvents)

        if is_new:
            if user_prompt is None or user_prompt == '':
                return
            prompt_event = FakePromptEvents(user_prompt=user_prompt)
            push_prompt_events(prompt_event)
        else:
            prompt_event = user_prompt
            user_prompt = prompt_event.user_prompt

        with st.container():
            with st.chat_message('user'):
                st.markdown(prompt_event.user_prompt)

            with st.chat_message('assistant'):
                with st.spinner('⏳', show_time=True):
                    try:
                        if is_new:
                            events_iter = fake_run(prompt_event.user_prompt)
                        else:
                            events_iter = iter(prompt_event.events)

                        new_events = process_event_output(events_iter, is_new)

                        if is_new:
                            prompt_event.events.extend(new_events)
                            prompt_event.is_complete = True

                    except Exception as e:
                        logger.error('process_user_prompt failed', exc_info=e)
                        st.error(f'❌ Error: {e}')

    _content_container = st.container()
    _content_container.empty()

    [USER].fragment(key=_fk_chat_input)
    def process_user_prompt_chat_input():
        logger.info(f'process_user_prompt_chat_input page={page_key}')
        with _content_container:
            process_user_prompt(user_prompt=ss.get(_k_userprompt, None))

    [USER].fragment(key=_fk_input_prompt)
    def input_prompt():
        def chat_input_submit():
            st.rerun([_fk_chat_input])

        with st.bottom:
            st.chat_input(
                'Ask anything …',
                key=_k_userprompt,
                submit_mode='stop',
                on_submit=chat_input_submit,
            )

    [USER].fragment
    def reload_prompt():
        logger.info(f'reload_prompt page={page_key} n={len(user_prompt_events)}')

        with _content_container:
            if user_prompt_events:
                for p_ev in user_prompt_events[:-1]:
                    process_user_prompt(p_ev, last=False)
                process_user_prompt(user_prompt_events[-1], last=True)

    reload_prompt()
    process_user_prompt_chat_input()
    input_prompt()

    logger.info(f'page={page_key} Ready.')


# ── Entry point ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if runtime.exists():
        st.set_page_config(layout="centered", page_title="Counter Demo", page_icon="🔢")
        launch(page_key="standalone")
    else:
        sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", sys.argv[0]]
        sys.exit(stcli.main())
```

title: StreamlitInvalidLayoutContextError with outside.empty()
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Submitting the chat input reruns only `process_user_prompt_chat_input` via `st.rerun([_fk_chat_input])`, and the first `st.container()` inside that fragment raises `StreamlitInvalidLayoutContextError` from `_get_or_create_outside_wrapper`. A fragment can fill an outside container on a standalone rerun only after that same fragment has enqueued a write during a full app run, which stores a wrapper keyed by `(fragment_id, container_id)`. In this app `_content_container.empty()` runs in the main script and its return value is discarded, so it never registers a wrapper for the chat fragment. On the initial run that fragment enters `with _content_container` and returns before drawing anything, because the chat value is still empty; a `with` block only pushes the delta generator and does not reserve a slot. `reload_prompt` does write to the same container on the full run, and its wrapper is stored under a different fragment id, so the chat fragment's lookup still misses and the guard raises. The error text's `outside.empty()` example has to run inside the fragment that will rerun. A reserved wrapper is one stable slot that fragment rewrites; appending a new turn under history drawn by `reload_prompt` means re-emitting the full list into that slot, or rerunning the history fragment as well. ### Related Issues - [#12762](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12762) (closed, intended behavior): a fragment writing into a container created outside it appended duplicate elements on each rerun. That is the same outside-container write pattern. The maintainer workaround was to pass an `st.empty()` placeholder into the fragment; the wrapper added since then turns a missing in-fragment claim into this exception. -

Looking at your code, I think the architecture can be simplified — you don't need outside containers or multiple fragments for this pattern. ### Recommended approach Streamlit's standard chat pattern handles this natively with a full-script rerun — render history from session state, handle new input, append, and let the rerun re-render: ```python import streamlit as st st.set_page_config(layout="wide", page_title="Chat Page") if "messages" not in st.session_state: st.session_state.messages = [] # Display chat history for msg in st.session_state.messages: with st.chat_message(msg["role"]): st.markdown(msg["content"]) # Handle new input if prompt := st.chat_input("Ask anything…"): st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt}) with st.chat_message("user"): st.markdown(prompt) with st.chat_message("assistant"): # Replace with your actual workflow call response = f"Here is my answer to: **{prompt}**" st.markdown(response) st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response}) ``` If you have expensive work elsewhere on the page that shouldn't rerun on every chat message, you can wrap the chat loop in `[USER].fragment` so only the chat section re-executes. title: StreamlitInvalidLayoutContextError with outside.empty()
text: The error you hit is working as designed — it's a guard against a fragment writing to an outside container without having claimed a stable position for it. The error message's suggestion to use `outside.empty()` is correct but easy to misapply: the claim must happen **inside the fragment body** during the initial full-app run, not from the main script. The wrapper is keyed per-fragment, so calling `.empty()` from the main script registers a slot for the main script, not for your fragment. If you do have a use case that requires outside-container writes, here's what to keep in mind: 1. **The fragment must write to the outside container on every run**, including the very first full-app run — even if there's nothing to display yet. A `with outside_container: pass` that exits without writing won't claim the slot. 2. **Use `st.container()`, not `st.empty()`**, if you want to render multiple elements. `st.empty()` is a single-element placeholder with replacement semantics — it replaces its content on every write, which is why your second example kept replacing the last block instead of appending. 3. **Fragment reruns replace the entire outside-container slot**, so the fragment must re-render the full content (not just the new addition) from session state on every rerun.

title: st.audio_input in the sidebar shows "An error has occurred, please try again." after a successful recording
text:
Issue #17585: st.audio_input in the sidebar shows "An error has occurred, please try again." after a successful recording
Labels: type:bug, type:regression, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P2, feature:st.sidebar, feature:st.audio_input

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `st.audio_input` is rendered inside `st.sidebar`, stopping a recording shows "An error has occurred, please try again." in place of the waveform. The upload itself succeeds: the script receives the file, and `st.audio` can play it back. The same code in the main area works correctly.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

with st.sidebar:
    audio = st.audio_input("Record", key="voice_audio")
    if audio is not None:
        st.success("Audio received successfully!")
        st.audio(audio)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. In the sidebar, click **Record**, speak for a second or two, and click **Stop recording**.

### Expected Behavior

The widget shows the recorded waveform and the play/download controls, the same as in the main area.

### Current Behavior

The widget shows "An error has occurred, please try again." Meanwhile "Audio received successfully!" and the `st.audio` player render below it, and the upload `PUT /_stcore/upload_file/...` returns 204.

No console error is printed because the exception is swallowed. Logging the `catch` in the playback-load effect of `AudioInput.tsx` shows:

```
Error: Player not initialized
    at load (useWaveformController.ts)
```

title: st.audio_input in the sidebar shows "An error has occurred, please try again." after a successful recording
text:
No console error is printed because the exception is swallowed. Logging the `catch` in the playback-load effect of `AudioInput.tsx` shows:

```
Error: Player not initialized
    at load (useWaveformController.ts)
```

**Cause.** `ThemedSidebar` calls `createSidebarTheme(activeTheme)` on every render, and that returns a new object each time:

```tsx
// frontend/app/src/components/Sidebar/ThemedSidebar.tsx
const sidebarTheme = createSidebarTheme(activeTheme)
```

1. `useWaveformController`'s `initializeWaveSurfer` callback depends on `theme`.
2. A new theme identity therefore re-runs the mount effect. Its cleanup calls `destroy()`, and the effect re-initializes WaveSurfer asynchronously.
3. Stopping a recording triggers a rerun that re-renders the sidebar several times in quick succession.
4. I instrumented the DOM and saw WaveSurfer destroyed and re-created 5+ times within about 100 ms. In the main area it is created exactly once.
5. When the playback-load effect calls `playback.load()` during one of those windows, it throws `Player not initialized`, and the widget enters its error state.

Wrapping the call in `useMemo(() => createSidebarTheme(activeTheme), [activeTheme])` removes the churn and the error.

Local results (headless Chromium with a fake microphone, sidebar app above):

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0 (also reproduced on 1.64.0, 1.65.0, 1.66.0, and `develop` @ 4365bdc4)

- Operating System: Windows 11, Linux; also reported on mobile devices

### Additional Information

The last version I tested without a visible error is 1.51.0. I did not bisect 1.52–1.62.

The churn affects any sidebar descendant that uses the Emotion theme as a hook dependency, not only `st.audio_input`. Separately, because `useWaveformController` has `theme` in `initializeWaveSurfer`'s dependencies, any legitimate theme change (light/dark switch, auto theme, host theme message) also destroys and re-creates WaveSurfer, in the main area too and for audio-enabled `st.chat_input`.

title: Allow Pillow 13 in the published dependency range
text:
Issue #17586: Allow Pillow 13 in the published dependency range
Labels: type:enhancement, area:dependencies

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues for similar requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

## Summary

Please update Streamlit's published Pillow requirement from `pillow>=9.2.0,<13` to `pillow>=9.2.0,<14` and regenerate the lockfile so Streamlit can resolve Pillow 13.0.0.

## Why?

Pillow 13.0.0 was released on 2026-10-16 and contains security fixes. Streamlit 1.66.0 currently caps Pillow below 13, which prevents downstream applications from receiving the patched release. This currently blocks the Markets/scdpy services audit because Streamlit resolves Pillow 12.3.0, which has known vulnerabilities fixed in Pillow 13.0.0.

## How?

I prepared the minimal change locally:

```diff
- pillow>=9.2.0,<13
+ pillow>=9.2.0,<14
```

The lockfile resolves successfully to Pillow 13.0.0. Existing Streamlit Pillow usage is covered by the image, hashing, and write-path tests.

## Additional Context

- Current dependency metadata: https://pypi.org/pypi/streamlit/json
- Pillow 13.0.0 release: https://pypi.org/project/Pillow/13.0.0/
- Streamlit dependency policy requires runtime dependencies to be capped below the next major version until compatibility is reviewed.
- A full upstream PR was not submitted because `CONTRIBUTING.md` states that outside pull requests are currently paused.
- The prepared local commit is `50bc26e2b6` on the `fchareyr/streamlit` fork.

Focused local validation: `uv lock --check` and Ruff passed; tests require the repository's `protoc` tool, which was unavailable in the local environment.

title: Allow Pillow 13 (raise upper bound to <14)
text:
Issue #17587: Allow Pillow 13 (raise upper bound to <14)
Labels: type:enhancement

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Raise the Pillow cap in `lib/pyproject.toml` from `<13` to `<14`.

### Why?

[Pillow 13.0.0](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/releasenotes/13.0.0.html) fixes two critical and about a dozen high-severity CVEs. Projects that depend on Streamlit can't upgrade while the cap is `<13`.

### How?

```diff
-  "pillow>=9.2.0,<13",
+  "pillow>=9.2.0,<14",
```

Then regenerate `uv.lock`. Streamlit doesn't use any of the APIs that 13.0 removed, and the one `fromarray` call doesn't pass `mode`.

One behavior change: `st.image` with an `I`-mode `PIL.Image` and `output_format="PNG"` now raises instead of silently clipping.

### Additional Context

#14881 and #15782 raised the lower bound but left the `<13` cap.

title: New API: st.set_page_config
text:
Issue #1770: New API: st.set_page_config
Labels: type:enhancement

## Proposal

```
st.set_page_config(
	layout="centered",  # Can be "centered" or "wide". In the future also "dashboard", etc.
	initial_sidebar_state="auto",  # Can be "auto", "expanded", "collapsed"
	page_title=None,  # String or None. Strings get appended with "• Streamlit". 
	page_icon=None,  # String, anything supported by st.image, or None.
)
```

## Background
We want to support the following in Streamlit:

1. Ability to set page favicon
2. Ability to set page title
3. Ability to make a page start in wide mode (today you need to toggle it in "preferences")
4. Ability to make a page start with the sidebar collapsed (today you need to collapse via the UI)

## Must be first st command
For all of these settings, we'd prefer if the user sets them near the top of their script. Because it would be weird to have an app load, then show a bunch of stuff, *and then* change into wide mode, for example.

## Immutable, for now
For title and favicon, it makes a lot of sense to support mutation. But it's not what 99% of the users will be doing, so it's OK if we don't support it at first.
For wide-mode and expand-sidebar, mutations make a lot less sense.

(Copied from our internal spec [here](https://www.notion.so/streamlit/Product-1472107ee200491b82894fe5fb5e4559?p=44a10601796749f6bf8c130c4f2892cc))

title: New API: st.set_page_config

[NONE] [USER] This sounds like a great solution, looking forward to it! One question I'm curious about is the difference between "auto" and "expanded" for the initial sidebar state. My impression is that in either case, if any `st.sidebar.*` functions have been called, the sidebar would show up expanded, and if no `st.sidebar.*` functions have been called, there will be no sidebar to expand or collapse. Is there something I'm missing?

[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] Thanks! "auto" and "expanded" will have different results depending on the width of the browser window. "auto" sidebar (aka today's behavior) starts expanded if the window is wider than a certain point, and starts collapsed otherwise. The two new options allow you to force the initial sidebar state one way or the other, ignoring browser width.

Incidentally, I'm wondering whether it makes sense to show an empty sidebar when `initial_sidebar_state="expanded"`. I can imagine that somebody might want to dynamically append things to the sidebar and thus leave an open canvas there? But it's a pretty weird/niche use case, and it's already possible with st.sidebar.empty(). Will do some more product thinking here.

(in favor of showing the expanded empty sidebar: I don't think Streamlit is currently capable of looking forward through the app to detect whether there's an st.sidebar somewhere later, so as soon as st.set_page_config is called we'd need to make a decision)

[NONE] For anybody who arrived here and is looking for the fix:

**streamlit.set_page_config(page_title=None, page_icon=None, layout='centered', initial_sidebar_state='auto')**

Configures the default settings of the page.
Note: This must be the first Streamlit command used in your app, and must only be set once.
Parameters
• page_title (str or None) – The page title, shown in the browser tab. If None,
defaults to the filename of the script (“app.py” would show “app • Streamlit”).
• page_icon (Anything supported by st.image or str or None) – The
page favicon. Besides the types supported by st.image (like URLs or numpy arrays), you
can pass in an emoji as a string (“”) or a shortcode (“:shark:”). If you’re feeling lucky,
try “random” for a random emoji! Emoji icons are courtesy of Twemoji and loaded from
MaxCDN.
• layout ("centered" or "wide") – How the page content should be laid out. Defaults to “centered”, which constrains the elements into a centered column of fixed width;
“wide” uses the entire screen.
• initial_sidebar_state ("auto" or "expanded" or "collapsed") –
How the sidebar should start out. Defaults to “auto”, which hides the sidebar on mobilesized devices, and shows it otherwise. “expanded” shows the sidebar initially; “collapsed”
hides it.

title: Look for Configuration Files in Platform-Recommended Directories
text:
Issue #2068: Look for Configuration Files in Platform-Recommended Directories
Labels: type:enhancement, papercut

# Problem

Streamlit uses the home directory for its configuration, but that adds _another_ config file to pollute a home directory. We should be good platform citizens and provide thoughtful locations for configuration files.

# Solution

We as a team agreed on the following order:

1. `$PROJECT_FOLDER/.streamlit`
2. (great if possible, but not required) `$PROJECT_FOLDER/{../}+.streamlit` (i.e. any subfolder containing .streamlit)
3. `~/.config/streamlit` if Unix/macOS (or in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, if defined), `%CSIDL_COMMON_APPDATA%/streamlit` if Windows (that's [`ProgramData`](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/deployment/usmt/usmt-recognized-environment-variables), meaning we follow Git and Conda)
4. `~/.streamlit`

### Additional context

See Closed Pull Request #1907

# Summary
When I try to show Pydeck map with view other than "MapView", nothing happens, it does not change the view of the map.

# Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-2302)

1. Use code:

```
import streamlit as st
import pydeck as pdk

view_state = pdk.ViewState(latitude=0, longitude=0, zoom=2, min_zoom=2)
view = pdk.View(type="MapView", controller=True)

deck = pdk.Deck(views=[view],initial_view_state=view_state)
st.pydeck_chart(deck)
```

2. Try to change view:
`view = pdk.View(type="OrbitView", controller=True)` or `view = pdk.View(type="OrthographicView", controller=True)`, or any other

## Expected behavior:

It should change the view of the map.

## Actual behavior:

It still shows the same "MapView" view of the map.

## Is this a regression?
no

- Python version: (3.7.7)
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? No

[NONE] 👍  Seconding the need for this. Ran into the same issue while trying to host a _streamlit_ app in k8s Google Cloud behind a corporate VPN. 

**Hot patching the package is a really ugly and maintainable fix when deploying the app to others**. 

Regardless, the commands above did not work for me with _streamlit_ `1.16.0` as they were excessively generic replacement and break the JS file. Here's what worked: 

```
sed -i -e 's/),1e3)/),1e4)/g' [PATH_TO_PYTHON_DIR]/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/main.*.js

sed -i -e 's/baseUriPartsList,500/baseUriPartsList,10000/g' [PATH_TO_PYTHON_DIR]/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/static/static/js/main.*.js
```

Adapt `[PATH_TO_PYTHON_DIR]` accordingly to the Python installation/environment you are working in.

_(Note, you don't have to fill out every section here. They're just here for guidance. That said, nicely detailed feature requests are more likely to get eng attention sooner)_

### Problem

When I call `st.dataframe(df)` on a dataframe that has too many columns to fit into the width of the page, the `st.dataframe` container allows me to scroll sideways to see the other columns.
However, when I attempt to display multiple graphs side-by-side using `st.columns`, the graphs in the columns get cut by the vertical edges of the column space. Is there a way to allow the columns to scroll horizontally to solve this problem?

title: Deck object with PointCloudLayer cannot be integrated properly with pydeck_chart
text:
Issue #2590: Deck object with PointCloudLayer cannot be integrated properly with pydeck_chart 
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.pydeck_chart

# Summary

The `pydeck_chart` cannot properly integrate a Deck object with a `PointCloudLayer` without embedding a mapbox view.
The following example shows how to create a 3D point cloud layer with pydeck: https://deckgl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/point_cloud_layer.html

# Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-2590)

```
import pandas as pd
import pydeck as pydeck
import streamlit as st

def main():
    DATA_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajduberstein/geo_datasets/master/small_waterfall.csv"
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL)

    target = [df.x.mean(), df.y.mean(), df.z.mean()]

    point_cloud_layer = pydeck.Layer(
        "PointCloudLayer",
        data=DATA_URL,
        get_position=["x", "y", "z"],
        get_color=["r", "g", "b"],
        get_normal=[0, 0, 15],
        auto_highlight=True,
        pickable=True,
        point_size=3,
    )

    view_state = pydeck.ViewState(target=target, controller=True, rotation_x=15, rotation_orbit=30, zoom=5.3)
    view = pydeck.View(type="OrbitView", controller=True)

    r = pydeck.Deck(point_cloud_layer, initial_view_state=view_state, views=[view])
    #r.to_html("point_cloud_layer.html", css_background_color="#add8e6")
    st.pydeck_chart(r)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## Expected behavior:

Using `st.pydeck_chart(r)`, I would expect a visualization of the 3D point cloud as in this example: https://deckgl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/point_cloud_layer.html 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77327738/104307831-093f3480-54d0-11eb-885f-1e543d88e80b.png)

## Actual behavior:

- The point cloud is flat
- The map cannot be disabled
- The orbit view does not work

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77327738/104308270-adc17680-54d0-11eb-8566-dc1e46550700.png)

## Is this a regression?

no

# Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.73.1
- Python version: 3.8.3
- Using Conda
- OS version: macOS 11.0.1
- Browser version: Chrome 87.0.4280.88 

# Additional information

With streamlit version 0.73.1 the following error appears when navigating the map (this error does not come up with streamlit version 0.69):

```
/usr/local/anaconda3/lib/python3.8/site-packages/pydeck/bindings/deck.py:105: UserWarning: Mapbox API key is not set. This may impact available features of pydeck.
  warnings.warn(
````

title: Add option to limit st.cache size by memory footprint rather than total number of entries
text:
Issue #2911: Add option to limit st.cache size by memory footprint rather than total number of entries
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:cache

### Problem

The ability to limit the size of the cache was added by https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/1152 which is extremely useful when deploying a streamlit app to a remote server to prevent a memory leak, however it leaves the question as to what value `max_entries` should be set to.  For example, if my remote server has 1GB of memory and I'd like to allocate 500MB of it for the purposes of caching responses, what values of `max_entries` should I set for each of the functions I am caching to ensure I don't exceed that memory limit?  As of right now the only way to determine it is through trial and error.

### Solution

**MVP:** One solution would be to add another parameter to the `st.cache` function like `max_memory_footprint` to limit the size of the cache by memory rather than number of entries.

**Possible additions:** An addition to this would be a global parameter like `maxCacheSize` in the `config.toml` file, this would be more convenient than limiting memory footprint by function as it may be difficult to determine what the optimal allocation per function would be in the case that you are caching multiple functions. 

**Preferred solution:** The preferred solution would probably be both options, a global memory limit that can be set to prevent the application from running out of memory, and a per-function memory limit for finer control when necessary.

[CONTRIBUTOR] AFAICT this is working as expected.

When you ctrl-c out of Streamlit (and at some other points, like when you click "stop" in the UI) we need to kill running thread(s), but Python doesn't actually have a way to kill threads. 

So what we do is:
1. Set a boolean when we want to kill a thread
2. Before every st.foo command, we check if the thread running that command has the boolean set to True
3. If True, raise a special exception. (Because exceptions kill threads)
    _So the thread is now stopped — yay!_
4. Handle the exception at the parent thread if needed

This works well any script where the interpreter often encounters an st.foo command. And it doesn't work at all when you have a loop that has no st.foo command. 

In this case, the loop has no st command, so it runs forever.

[CONTRIBUTOR] This issue reports that the Streamlit server fails to exit cleanly when a user script is stuck in an infinite loop without any `st.*` commands. The root cause is a fundamental Python limitation: Python doesn't support forcefully terminating threads. Streamlit's current approach uses a cooperative mechanism where stop requests are checked only at "interrupt points" - specifically, when `st.*` commands are called (see `_maybe_handle_execution_control_request` in `script_runner.py`). If a script is in a tight loop without calling any Streamlit commands, it never reaches an interrupt point, so the stop signal is never processed. Since the script thread is created as a non-daemon thread, the Python process waits indefinitely for it to complete.

A community contributor has proposed a solution using `ctypes.pythonapi.PyThreadState_SetAsyncExc` to inject a `SystemExit` exception into hung threads (referenced in the comments via a forked branch).

### Related Issues

- [#6494 - Infinite loop after breaking](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6494): Same underlying issue where while loops continue running even after the loop condition should break, because there's no `st.*` command inside the loop to trigger an interrupt point check.

- [#6611 - Graceful Shutdown of Server](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6611): Request for programmatic server shutdown (`st.stop_server()`), related to shutdown mechanism improvements.

- [#7688 - On session start/shutdown hooks](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7688): Request for shutdown hooks to properly clean up resources, which intersects with the broader shutdown handling architecture.

Caching improvements
text:
Issue #3263: Caching improvements
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:cache

### Problem

I'm using Streamlit to build a complicated report which takes about an hour to generate an output. It processes a hundred megabytes of Pandas dataframes. The performance of this report is important to keep UX better. Data processing has also it's own cost.

title: Caching improvements
text:
To show report results during a reasonable amount of time and minimize processing costs I utilize caching approach. Using Streamlit's caching mechanism I've faced multiple difficulties:
1. I would like to use persistence on the disk instead of keeping the cache inside in RAM. It helps to avoid wasting RAM when you have multiple nodes where the report is hosted. I understand that it needs time to load the cache into memory but it is excepted. When there are multiple cache values which take 100MB it is reasonable to keep this on disk instead of in RAM to avoid OOM. Unfortunately, Streamlit keeps a copy of cache value in memory when `persist=True`.
2. There are only two strategies of caching: memory and disk. In my particular case, it is reasonable to have the possibility to keep cache directly in S3/Minio.
3. Streamlit has only one strategy of data serialization: Pickle. In the case of large Pandas data frames, it is reasonable to have other formats support like Arrow (it more efficient in term of memory usage and loading time). In general, it would be great to have different strategies which depend on the data type.
4. I'm not able to configure caching folder. Currently, Streamlit keep all cache in `~/.streamlit`

I'm still exploring Streamlit features and code, so probably it is not a complete list of missing cache features.

### Solution

title: Caching improvements
text:
I'm still exploring Streamlit features and code, so probably it is not a complete list of missing cache features.

### Solution

**MVP:**
1. Add `skip_memory_cache=True`
2. As a workaround we can mount S3 into `~/.streamlit` folder using the FUSE driver ([s3 FUSE driver](https://github.com/s3fs-fuse/s3fs-fuse), [Minio FUSE driver](https://github.com/minio/minfs))
3. Pickle is good enough but it does not support unserialization streaming which leads to RAM usage spike.
4. Add cache folder into config (see #3269)
5. Do not remove `cache` directory, because it might be mounted using `s3fs`

**Preferred solution:**
1-2. Add different caching strategies and possibility to chain different strategies (like `cache_strategies=['memory', 'disk', 's3']`). Initially, we can fetch from the fast cache and if it is miss then from the slower cache.
3. Implement data serialization for Pandas. Parquet is a preferable format (see formats [comparison](https://towardsdatascience.com/the-best-format-to-save-pandas-data-414dca023e0d))
4. Cache folder should be a part of `disk` strategy configuration.
5. Decouple cache component as a separate library to avoid coupling on the whole streamlit project. I found this useful when I want to use the same caching approach in my libraries.

### Additional context

Probably integration of an already existing cache library that already supports all these features might be a faster and more robust solution.

Here is a library that can be easily replace FS Python operations with S3:
https://s3fs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

[NONE] This appears to be an issue with the entrypoints package – I've closed the Altair issue. Reproduce by doing ``pip install entrypoints`` and then ``import entrypoints``

[CONTRIBUTOR] It seems there is an issue with `configparser` that is installed by `apt-get`. This only happen for Python 2.7.
A possible workaround is to remove `configparser` via `apt-get` before `pip install streamlit`:
```
apt-get update
apt-get install python python-pip 
apt-get remove python-configparser
pip install streamlit
streamlit hello
```
This will take care of the bug.

Another solution is to use a different python image. For example for Python-2.7: `python:2.7-slim` does not have this problem, likely because python is preinstalled and the `apt-get` does not conflict with `pip`.

[USER] this will probably work for `altair` as well.

---
At this point, we're at a loss how to automatically fix this for users. But it seems very localized to the specific Docker image, and specifically on Python 2.x — and we have the work-around above. So we'll stop work on this at the moment.

If anyone has a solution, please let us know. We'll be happy to merge it in!

Issue #3508: A way to add Python functionalities/custom HTML/CSS code to streamlit
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:custom-components

### Problem

I'm finding it a bit difficult to add a few Python functions onto the existing `components.html()`. Like say I'm scraping data from a 
site using bs4 or something, and write a function to extract certain data from a given URL and then pass it on as an input to get 
some prediction from it and I want to add some specific styling to it. `components.html()` and `components.iframe()` are not really fitting the bill.

### Solution

doesn't solve the problem of especially using functions, loops and styling, for which I have to keep going back to Flask, which 
makes things more difficult, since streamlit is being used to make it easy in the first place

**Possible additions:** Possibly, some arguments can be added on to `components.html()` to be able to use jinja-like syntax to 
solve the issue or add new functionalities for it.

For example, after changing the selection of some radio button which causes the script to rerun, all the component values are restored properly again. **Expected behavior:** At step 4 above, all component values are restored properly so that the second `st.write()` shows "Bacon" and the third "Sausage". **Actual behavior:** As explained above, at step 4, the second and third `st.write()` show wrong restored component values. ### Is this a regression? [NONE] bumping this issue -- it makes st.checkbox unusable for a number of use-cases where st.rerun is required. I've not yet found a chack to make st.checkbox + button that calls st.rerun work in the meantime... but if someone else has that would be cool

The best I've got is to make a button that acts like checkbox as follows

```python
if 'toggle' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['toggle'] = False

def change_toggle():
    st.session_state.toggle = not st.session_state.toggle

st.button(label="Toggle",
          key='toggle-button',
          type='primary' if st.session_state.toggle else 'secondary',
          on_click=change_toggle)
```
Changing the `type` between primary/secondary does change the color of the button.

Or even more simply you can just replace st.checkbox with the `toggle_button` function below

```python
def toggle_button(label, key=None, help=None, on_click=None, args=None, kwargs=None, *, icon=None, disabled=False, use_container_width=False) -> bool:

    def toggle():
        st.session_state[key] = not st.session_state.get(key, False)

        if on_click is not None:
            on_click()

    return st.button(label=label,
                     key=key + '-button',
                     help=help,
                     type='primary' if st.session_state.get(key, False) else 'secondary',
                     on_click=toggle,
                     args=args,
                     kwargs=kwargs,
                     icon=icon,
                     disabled=disabled,
                     use_container_width=use_container_width)


```

title: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
text:
Issue #4162: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:cli

### Problem

Right now streamlit requires a raw Python script (e.g. `your_script.py`) that is invoked, e.g.

```
streamlit run your_script.py [-- script args]
```

This is really frustrating if you want to package your streamlit application in a wheel file and distribute it to your friends & colleagues.  Streamlit's requirement of a raw Python script makes this impossible.

Assume I have created a proper Python package/distribution `my-streamlit-dashboard` and uploaded it to PyPI or some company-internal artefact store. If my colleagues now runs `pip install my-streamlit-dashboard`, my package will be installed but how would my colleague now run my dashboard? There is no `script.py` entry point for him or her to run. 

### Solution

For use-cases like this, Python packaging allows the definition of `console_scripts` which allow you to define command-line scripts that are installed e.g. within your virtual environment, and behave like normal shell scripts (but are actual Python scripts). All details can be found [here](https://python-packaging.readthedocs.io/en/latest/command-line-scripts.html#the-console-scripts-entry-point). Quite many Python tools & frameworks use this capability like for instance [PyScaffold's `putup` command](https://github.com/pyscaffold/pyscaffold), [Django's `django-admin` command](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.2/ref/django-admin/), [poetry's `poetry` command](https://python-poetry.org/docs/) and streamlit's own `streamlit` command.

Continuing the example from above, I could define a console-script `my-cool-dashboard` within the package `my-streamlit-dashboard` that would act as the initial script to run for streamlit, i.e.

```
streamlit run my-streamlit-dashboard
```

title: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
text:
Continuing the example from above, I could define a console-script `my-cool-dashboard` within the package `my-streamlit-dashboard` that would act as the initial script to run for streamlit, i.e.

```
streamlit run my-streamlit-dashboard
```

For this to work, streamlit would need to allow console scripts defined by `console_scripts` as start points for dashboard. Technically this should be possible as they are just Python scripts. Doing this right now leads to the error:

```
Error: Streamlit requires raw Python (.py) files, but the provided file has no extension.
For more information, please see https://docs.streamlit.io
```

if the console script doesn't end with `.py`, which is common. Adding `.py` leads to:

```
Error: Invalid value: File does not exist: my-cool-dashboard.py
```

A crude and unsatisfying workaround is:

```
streamlit run `which my-cool-dashboard.py`
```

This seems to mostly work but also emits nasty errors during execution:

```
File "/[HOME]/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 354, in _run_script
    exec(code, module.__dict__)
File "/[HOME]/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/bin/my-streamlit-dashboard.py", line 33, in <module>
    sys.exit(load_entry_point('my-streamlit-dashboard', 'console_scripts', 'my-cool-dashboard.py')())
```

### Additional context

title: Allow console_scripts as streamlit run scripts
text:
```
streamlit run `which my-cool-dashboard.py`
```

This seems to mostly work but also emits nasty errors during execution:

```
File "/[HOME]/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/lib/python3.9/site-packages/streamlit/script_runner.py", line 354, in _run_script
    exec(code, module.__dict__)
File "/[HOME]/.mambaforge/envs/streamlit-demo/bin/my-streamlit-dashboard.py", line 33, in <module>
    sys.exit(load_entry_point('my-streamlit-dashboard', 'console_scripts', 'my-cool-dashboard.py')())
```

### Additional context

What are the benefits of making packaging for streamlit apps possible? I'm glad you asked! 
* Another way of distribution. For production, a streamlit app would right now be deployed as docker container most likely. Allowing proper packaging would also make it possible for users to just install and run it locally via pip. Thus more **flexibility**.
* Proper **versioning**. Since Python packages/distributions are versioned, one could apply proper versioning to these packages and enforce certain processes within an organisation, like semantic versioning etc. which is hard if everyone is just cloning a git repo. 
* Enabling [**ML-Ops** principles](https://ml-ops.org/content/mlops-principles). Most organisation provide templates for Python projects that support developers in applying techniques like testing (CI/CD), reproducibility, documentation, deployment, etc. With the suggested solution it would be much easier to incorporate streamlit in such templates as e.g. provided by [PyScaffold](https://pyscaffold.org/).

---

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

**If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

What I understood is that `my-streamlit-dashboard` would register a streamlit `entry_point` which `streamlit` would then find and just provide. [NONE] Sure [USER], what I meant was that according to your suggestion, app developers would just need to set in `setup.cfg` something like:
```init
[options.entry_points]
streamlit.dashboards =
    my-cool-dashboard = my_streamlit_dashboard.dashboad:main
```
following the example from above. `my_streamlit_dashboard` would be the package and `dashboard` the module wherein a function `main()` is defined. This function acts like the main entrance point for the dashboard in a similar way currently a pure Python script is used by streamlit.

To make this work, the developers of streamlit would then need to register those `entry_points` using the entry-point group `streamlit.dashboards` from above, i.e.
```python
from importlib.metadata import entry_points

# find all dashboards provided by customer packages and load them.
dashboards = {entry_point.name: entry_point.load() 
              for entry_point in entry_points().select(group="streamlit.dashboards")
# assume user has selected `my-cool-dashboard`, e.g. with `streamlit run my-cool-dashboard`,
# then streamlit would execute the dashboard internally with
dashboards["my-cool-dashboard"](*args, **kwargs)
```

This is what you meant with your first comment, right?

[NONE] > Python has an API for running modules, so you can create a entrypoint script that provides similar functionality. See this thread: #5471

I can confirm [USER] suggestion works. I added some more details [below the original answer](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5471#issuecomment-1341051365).

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update 

The packaging use case is now supported via `st.App.run()` (added in #15563 and available since Streamlit 1.59.0), although `streamlit run <console-script>` itself still requires a Python-file target.

A package can expose a console script whose entry point does:

```python
from pathlib import Path
import streamlit as st

def main() -> None:
    st.App(Path(__file__).with_name("dashboard.py")).run()
```

Using an absolute package path is important because the generated console-script executable lives in the virtual environment's `bin` directory.

text:
Issue #4320: Make picture size returned by camera_input consistent via parameter
Labels: type:enhancement, papercut, feature:st.camera_input

st. camera_input returns a picture. The dimensions of that picture depend on the camera widget size as displayed in the browser. 

### Problem

Getting randomly sized pictures from the camera_input widget is not exactly defined behaviour.
The documentation doesn't list any setting to request a certain dimension.

```
import streamlit as st
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

imgbuffer = st.camera_input('cam')

if imgbuffer:
    img = Image.open(imgbuffer)
    imgnp = np.array(img)
    st.write(imgnp.shape)
```

1. run snippet
2. take picture
3. resize browser window so that the widget is also resized
4. take another picture

### Solution

**MVP:** No idea

**Preferred solution:** Add a parameter to request a defined size, maybe a second one to set what to do if that size is not available from the device (upscaling, cropping, downscaling.). Add missing documentation if such a parameter already exists.

title: Rerun on each new keystroke in `st.text_input`
text:
Issue #4553: Rerun on each new keystroke in `st.text_input`
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.text_input

### Problem

I wanted to create a Streamlit application which has an input text field which immediately responds to user input, e.g. like the Google search field does. Something like this:

```py
def search_callback():
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)


search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian', on_input=search_callback)
```

### Solution

I couldn't find any way to achieve this with Streamlit. I think what would be necessary is a new type of `on_input` callback or similar.

Further, I think it would make sense to have a kwarg containing the current input. I would also have liked this for the `on_change` callback. As a workaround I have been using the session state instead:

```py
def search_callback():
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)


search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian', on_change=search_callback)
```

title: Rerun on each new keystroke in `st.text_input`
text:
[NONE] Hi [USER],

Regarding `on_change ` callback, I think using `session_state ` for the input value is indeed how it is meant to be used according to: https://blog.streamlit.io/session-state-for-streamlit/

Currently, you can use args and kwargs to pass in other data (other than the input) to your callback.

```python
def search_callback(*args, **kwargs):
  st.write("You searched for:", st.session_state.input)
  st.write(args, kwargs)

search_str = st.text_input('Search', key='input', placeholder='Life of Brian',
    on_change=search_callback, args=["Hello", "Brian"], kwargs={"Bye": "Brian"} )
```

[NONE] It appears the name `on_change` is badly chosen;` on_press_enter` would be more appropriate for the current behavior. A real `on_key_change` should indeed be responding directly to any changed input, that means while typing, not pressing enter.

edit: better explanation


[CONTRIBUTOR] If the user has to hit enter before the behavior happens, this seems to just be a callback, which already exists. Is that accurate? [USER] [USER] 

[NONE] I was hoping for immediate updates, without additional key presses. So like in Google search with every typed character the result is immediately updated.

[NONE] Hello, any update on this? I am also currently using session states to access the changed input value. However, this rules out wrapping the `on_change` callback with a `[USER].cache_resource` decorator because if I was passing the input value as a parameter to the actual callback function, it will still have the old value of user input and hence, returns an older cached value

title: Rerun on each new keystroke in `st.text_input`
text:
[NONE] +1 for the documentation being very confusing on the meaning of `on_change` - I was expecting this indeed to change every time the user changes the input (i.e. types something), and not only when the user presses enter. Especially since this usecase is already well covered by `value := st.text(…`. 

Thankfully, [USER] developed a component that solves the problem brought up by [USER]. It can be found here: https://github.com/blackary/streamlit-keyup

[COLLABORATOR] Changed the title to make it a bit more obvious what this is. I think there is an option we'll prioritize this if the issue gets more upvotes or the custom component linked above gets more usage!

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update 

Wrote up a spec [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14905).

[COLLABORATOR] ## UPdate

This will be available in 1.64+ via the `live` parameter on `st.text_input` ([#16662](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16662)). `live=True` commits the value after a 250ms pause while typing (or pass a duration like `"300ms"`). Prefer wrapping the live UI in a fragment so typing doesn't rerun the rest of the app:

```python
[USER].fragment
def search():
    query = st.text_input("Search", type="search", live=True)
    st.write("You searched for:", query)

search()
```

text:
Issue #4860: Allow sharing of Streamlit apps through JupyterHub
Labels: type:enhancement, area:deployment, status:unlikely

**Problem.**
Working in a Jupyter Hub environment the best way to share applications/dashboards across an organization is to render them with voila and share the link to whoever needs it. Moreover, in such structure its always possible to run your streamlit solution in a port of your k8s instance, but that port if of course not accessible to other users.

**Solution.**
Using https://cdsdashboards.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ ContainDS to do that is in theory possible. 
It looks to me that containDS is a separate project to streamlit.

**Additional context.**
This thread shows how some organizations already use such approach for panel, one of the big four:
https://twitter.com/JamesABednar/status/1535371689323896842?s=20&t=sbk7MWdigcZbzl1ywmU78w

**Request/Question.**
Is there any specific documentation regarding rendering streamlit with voila in a Jupyter Hub environement?

**Comment:**
Being streamlit one of the most powerful dashboards frameworks it is so far out of scope for us since the first requirement is "sharability" via urls, within the jupyterhub  since it has to be transparent to several thousands of people who do not even know what python is (I.e. forgot about asking them to open the terminal to do this or that to fire a streamlit app)

title: Streamlit not detecting changes to multipage apps in WSL2
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Hey [USER],

I had some time to do some digging on this and believe I was able to find the WSL issues that I only vaguely remembered before: https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/4581, https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/4739, https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/4064 (there are also a bunch of other related issues linked from those three).

The summary of what I've been able to find is that WSL2 doesn't support inotify except in certain situations (I believe it's possible to get things to work on ext4 filesystems, but as far as I can tell there isn't any way to fix things on ntfs or other common Windows filesystem formats), and without inotify we're unable to watch for changes to directories.

I'm going to close this as I don't believe there's much we can do on our end to fix this, but let me know if I'm missing something here.

One thing to try in the meantime would be setting the `server.fileWatcherType` config option to `"poll"` since, if one suspected reason for file watchers not always working is that inotify is having issues, then using that file watcher type should circumvent the problem entirely.

title: Streamlit not detecting changes to multipage apps in WSL2
text:
[NONE] I tested on WSL2, Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12. It is working correct. 

[CONTRIBUTOR] This is a confirmed bug related to Streamlit's file watcher not detecting changes to nested pages and imported modules when running in WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux). The root cause is a known limitation of WSL2's inotify support, particularly when files are stored on NTFS filesystems. Streamlit's default file watcher (`auto` mode) uses the watchdog library which relies on inotify events on Linux. When inotify doesn't work properly in WSL2, the event-based watcher fails to detect changes in subdirectories. The recommended workaround is to set `server.fileWatcherType = "poll"` in the config, which uses a polling-based approach that doesn't depend on inotify. A potential long-term fix would be to auto-detect WSL2 environments and default to polling mode.

### Related Issues

- **#11037** - [Watch changes in uv workspaces](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11037): Similar file watcher issue where changes in local dependencies managed by `uv` workspaces are not detected, breaking hot reload. Both issues relate to the file watcher not detecting changes in certain directory structures.

- **#8275** - [Keep symbolic links / re-resolve symlinks if target changes](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8275): Related file watcher issue where symlink target changes are not properly handled. This shares the underlying theme of file system event detection limitations.

- **#11559** - [`make frontend-dev` fails during build under WSL2](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11559): Another WSL2 compatibility issue, demonstrating that WSL2 environment has multiple friction points with the current codebase.

The following code should show it quite clearly:

[USER].experimental_memo(ttl=1)

def main():
    format = "%(asctime)s: %(message)s"
    logging.basicConfig(format=format)

    threads = []
    for index in range(25):
        x = threading.Thread(target=function1, args=(index,))
        # Hack to remove the following logging messages:
        #    `Thread 'Thread-123': missing ScriptRunContext`
        # see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1326
        add_script_run_ctx(x)
        threads.append(x)
        x.start()

    logging.info("Waiting for threads to finish")
    for thread in threads:
        thread.join()

    logging.info("done")
    st.write("done")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

**Expected behavior:**

The threaded function should be run.  No error should be shown.

**Actual behavior:**

The function runs fine.  The data is cached.   But, the frontend fails with an ugly error message:

"Bad 'setIn' index XX (should be between [0, X])"

### Is this a regression?

I don't think so

text:
Issue #5616: Bring back colored borders for `st.info`, `st.success`, `st.warning` and `st.error` to improve visibility
Labels: type:enhancement, area:layout, area:frontend, area:styling

### Problem

- Today I updated to a more recent version (1.14.0) of Streamlit and the alerts/notifications (`st.info`, `st.success`, `st.warning`, `st.error`) do not have borders anymore.
- For those of us with some difficulty to distinguish colors, the borders really helped. `st.warning` is the trickiest one to see in my case, both in the main area as well as in the sidebar, followed by `st.success`.
- I tried adding borders using the CSS markdown trick, but haven't found a way to add a different border color depending on alert type.

### Example

```
# Using streamlit 1.14.0
import streamlit as st


# CSS markdown trick to add border - cannot achieve different border colors depending on alert type
st.markdown("""
<style>
    .stAlert {border-style: solid; border-radius: 5px; border-width: 1px; border-color:darkblue;}
</style>
""",unsafe_allow_html=True)


# Streamlit Alerts in sidebar
with st.sidebar:
    st.info('Info')
    st.success('Success')
    st.warning('Warning')
    st.error('Error')


# Streamlit Alerts in main area
st.info('Info')
st.success('Success')
st.warning('Warning')
st.error('Error')

```

### Solution

**MVP:** A CSS markdown trick example on how to add different border colors depending on alert type.

**Preferred solution:** Bring back the colored borders for `st.info`, `st.success`, `st.warning` and `st.error`.
