[CONTRIBUTOR] As a minimum viable feature we could make this not even behave like an empty -- it just inserts a skeleton animation into the UI with a specified height. If you want it to be replaced by content, you just stick it in an empty by itself and then write over it. 

Users/streamlit extras could implement their own extensions on this, including all of the features mentioned in the original spec. And if it become widely used, perhaps those features could be brought into the core package.

```python
# Draw UI
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.empty()
census_data_placeholder.skeleton(height=500px)  # The skeleton holds space for the future data

# Get data from source, assume this takes a long time

# Draw the data, replacing the skeleton animation that was previously there
with census_data_placeholder.container():
   st.dataframe(census_dataframe)
   st.write(f"Data for {year} loaded successfully")
```

[COLLABORATOR] Just came across this old issue, random thought I had: maybe `st.skeleton` would actually be more intuitive if we do it similarly to `st.spinner`:

```python
with st.skeleton(width="stretch", height=300):
    data = load_data()
st.dataframe(data, height=300)
```

So the `with` here is not a container (which feels a bit weird to me in the proposal above, where we basically have a container, but it's filled with an element to begin with), but just a simple timing thing that's similar to `st.spinner` – once the content is loaded, the skeleton goes away (and in the case above is replaced by a dataframe of the same size). 

The example from the original issue above (where the skeleton/dataframe are displayed above a selectbox) could then be handled with the normal `st.empty` pattern:

```
st.write("Census Data")
census_data_placeholder = st.empty()
year = st.selectbox("Select Year", options=[2022, 2023, 2024])

with census_data_placeholder.skeleton():
    census_dataframe = get_census_data_from_database(year)
    census_statistics = compute_statistics(census_dataframe)

with census_data_placeholder.container():
    st.dataframe(census_dataframe)
    st.write(census_statistics)
```

title: st.skeleton() - Implementation Proposal for space-filling empties.
text:
[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

An `st.skeleton` element will be released in 1.59 which can be used in two usage modes:

1. **Standalone mode** (like `st.empty()`): Returns a replaceable placeholder
   ```python
   placeholder = st.skeleton(height=200)
   # ... load data ...
   placeholder.dataframe(df)  # Replaces skeleton with content
   ```

2. **Context manager mode** (like `st.spinner()`): Shown after a short delay while the block runs and auto-clears on exit
   ```python
   with st.skeleton(height=100):
       # ... loading happens here ...
   # Skeleton automatically clears when block exits
   ```

**Parameters:**
- `height`: int, `"stretch"`, or `None` (default: `None`). `None` uses the standard element height (same as most input widgets); an integer sets a fixed pixel height; `"stretch"` fills a parent container with a bounded height.
- `width`: int or `"stretch"` (default: `"stretch"`)

title: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
text:
Issue #8186: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
Labels: type:enhancement, area:layout

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit has expanded its layout options, which compound on each others to create complex application user flows beyond the single page, top to bottom interaction. 

As `st.dialog` is coming along, and `st.popover` merged, most types of surfaces are being covered by streamlit, except the drawer concept, which is a dismissable container sliding from the right of the screen on demand, which blocks the screen from the side without masking the context, can be used as an information surface, for continuous interactions (like LLM Chat), or for form input. 

### Why?

`st.sidebar`, which is the current closest equivalent has been very useful to have a permanent set of widget independent of the main window context but fall short when

- The interface has to be conditional, it requires more `session_state `trickery to redraw the sidebar
- The navigation gets rich, and the sidebar should have only a few other static elements but not a full form entry / sub interface

Thus, the sidebar and drawer concepts may overlap for simple usage, but are very different in practice and we would beneficiate from a better separation of duty

title: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
text:
Thus, the sidebar and drawer concepts may overlap for simple usage, but are very different in practice and we would beneficiate from a better separation of duty 

Gitlab makes a good example of using a rich navigation sidebar to the left hand side, and drawers for Gitlab Duo AI Chat, or to input CI Variables

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/97103608/3c830664-12c6-4b8a-8e91-8192c326a05d)

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/97103608/5bd212a0-f31a-4f73-b4f4-3fca85374585)

### How?

The [Base Web](https://baseweb.design/components/drawer/) component is a starting point.

The main behaviours between the background and drawer I can refine in a first round are : 

- _Focused_ : The background is frozen, the user must exit using a default exit button. Clicking on the background does not exit the drawer (as it leads to different input errors). A drawer is always exitable. The background gets slightly greyed out, to ensure the drawer is in focus but remains readable
- _Scrollable_ : The background can be scrolled. This ensures that the user can retain a mental image of where they are in the UX Flow of the app.
- _Form Like (Optional)_ : The developer should be able to set a condition which closes the drawer, similar to how `st.form_submit_button` allows to exit the form. Perhaps we could reuse behaviours, and a form could be nested within a drawer, upon submission it closes the drawer.

With only those basic behaviour we can address most use cases:

title: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
text:
With only those basic behaviour we can address most use cases:

1. A one-shot configuration (i.e. use a drawer to make a request, drawer closes and request shows up in main app area)
2. A continuous data entry, where the drawer remains open whilst the user makes several input (i.e. add multiple records)
3. An information/documentation panel with little interactions, but potentially rich display elements
4. A chat like interface on demand, a la copilot or gitlab duo chat.

On the python end, `st.drawer` should be similar syntaxically to st.dialog and st.popover to ease on the cognitive load, meaning

```python
with st.drawer("Open Drawer"):
   ...

```

Should call the drawer to expand, clicking away or on a well visible close/exit button should close the drawer.

### Additional Context

_No response_

[COLLABORATOR] That's a pretty interesting suggestion! Reminds me of the side-peek feature in Notion. I was very much against a "right-hand sidebar" in the past because I think it would just make the app look super cluttered if you have 3 different sections (left sidebar, main area, right sidebar). But in this fashion (where it isn't a proper sidebar but just shows up temporarily and overlaps the main page), I could actually see this be a thing!

That being said, I definitely want to focus on getting out dialog right now and then we'll have a few major non-layout-related features coming up. So I don't think we'll realistically get to this very soon. But I'll keep it in mind for when we plan out the next few quarters in April.

text:
[COLLABORATOR] Just noting for my future self, maybe we could also name this `st.side_peek` or something like that to make it a bit more similar to `st.sidebar`. 

[NONE] This would be a nice addition to Streamlit!

It could help declutter the left sidebar, which could be more focused on listing the pages in a multi-app page. The drawer would focus more on settings and other features.

Some thoughts:
I think `st.drawer` should work nicely with multi-app pages. That is, we should be able to set a generic setup. For instance, if we want a button (e.g., chatbot) to be displayed in all app pages, we shouldn't define it in all app pages but just in the entry point where `st.navigation` is called. In addition, custom setups per page should be possible.

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

This will be available in Streamlit **1.66+** via `[USER].dialog` with `position="right"` or `position="left"`. That shows the dialog as a user-resizable, full-height side drawer (it stays modal, so the rest of the app is inert while the drawer is open):

```python
import streamlit as st


[USER].dialog("Details", position="right")
def show_details(item):
    st.write(f"Details for {item}")


if st.button("Open details"):
    show_details("Order #1234")
```

The other side-drawer use case — a panel that stays open while you interact with the main content — is tracked in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1980.

title: `st.popover` not closing when opening another PopOver
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] This issue reports that when a `st.selectbox` or `st.multiselect` dropdown is open inside a `st.popover`, clicking on another popover button fails to close the first one, leaving both popovers open simultaneously. 

**Root Cause Analysis:** According to team member [USER]'s comment, this is an **upstream bug with BaseWeb** (the UI library Streamlit uses). The issue stems from how BaseWeb handles outside click events - document clicks only activate the _last_ event handler, which in this case is the multiselect's close handler rather than the popover's `onClickOutside` handler. This prevents the popover from detecting the click as an "outside click" when the dropdown is active. The team has indicated this will need to be addressed during the planned migration off of BaseWeb.

### Related Issues

- **#8265** - [Add open/close parameter to st.popover](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8265): Enhancement request to programmatically control popover open/closed state. If implemented, this could provide a workaround for this bug by allowing users to manually manage popover state.

- **#10239** - [Dynamic popover height](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10239): Related issue about popovers not adjusting their height when expandable elements like selectbox dropdowns are opened inside them. Both issues involve the interaction between dropdowns and popovers.

- **#9243** - [Popover and dialog first widget is always active](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243): Related focus/activation issue with widgets inside popovers. Both issues stem from interactions between popover containers and their child widgets.

---

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.

### Summary

This was originally requested in #3651 for the deprecated `st.cache`, and the same problem still exists with  `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data`.

### `st.cache_data`

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


[USER].cache_data
async def get_data():
    return 42


async def main():
    data = await get_data()
    st.write(data)


asyncio.run(main())
```

This results in the following error because the returned value of `get_data()`, a coroutine object, is not pickleable.

```
UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type get_data()) in get_data(). st.cache_data uses [pickle](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html) to serialize the function’s return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see [our docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/caching) for differences).
```

### `st.cache_resource`

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


[USER].cache_resource
async def get_resource():
    return 42


async def main():
    resource = await get_resource()
    st.write(resource)


asyncio.run(main())
```

It runs successfully at the first run, but the following error occurs in the second run and later because the coroutine object returned from `get_resource()` is cached and the same coroutine object is awaited again.

```
RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine
```

[CONTRIBUTOR] Hi, and thank you for opening / upvoting this issue
Sorry [USER], I forgot to answer to this issue (mostly because I didn't have an elegant answer). 

Stremalit cache primitives work with sync functions, you couldn't decorate an async function, but:
you can call an async operation inside a cached function in separate thread (to have isolated event loop):

This should work correctly, and the result should be very close to what you want:


```python
import asyncio
import streamlit as st
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor


[USER].cache_data
def get_data(x:int) -> int:
    # Use a separate thread to run the async operation
    # This lets us create an isolated event loop that won't conflict
    def run_in_thread(x:int) -> int:
        async def _async_operation(x:int) -> int:
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
            return x ** 2

        return asyncio.run(_async_operation(x))

    # Execute in a separate thread and wait for the result
    with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        return executor.submit(run_in_thread, x).result()


async def main():
    x = st.slider("Pick a number" , 0, 10)
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    data = get_data(x)  # Synchronous call
    st.write(data)


asyncio.run(main())

```

title: `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data` should support async functions (coroutines)
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] Also if your main streamlit app is not run by `asyncio.run(main())`, and it is just a python sync script, you can do a async call in your cached function in more laconic way:



```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


async def get_data(number):
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    return number ** 2

[USER].cache_data
def get_cached_data(number: int):
    return asyncio.run(get_data(number))

x = st.slider("x", 0, 100)

st.write(get_cached_data(x))
```

[CONTRIBUTOR] I wrote a twisted function transformer in my library https://github.com/jokester/streamlit-concurrency to use `st.cache_data()` with async function. [demo in st cloud](https://concurrency.streamlit.app/cached_async)

Internally it uses `st.cache_data` to cache a sync function waiting for `asyncio.run(the_real_async_fun())` result in an executor thread. Similar to the pattern mentioned in other comments.

[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] this will be included in the 1.64 release -- I just merged a PR so if you want to try this in the nightly then that is possible as well. 

Note, there were a lot of product decisions on what exactly to support here. The PR has a document exploring them linked, and I also made some issues for areas that are still unsupported (see mentions above). Please let me know if you have any feedback on these decisions, and whether further support is needed for your use cases!

title: Impossible to disable st.chat_input while writing the model's response
text:
Issue #8323: Impossible to disable st.chat_input while writing the model's response
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.chat_input, feature:st.write_stream

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When a user enters a prompt in st.chat_input, it is not possible to disable the input while an LLM is generating the response to that input. 

This leads to the possibility of the user 'interrupting' the model output and messing up the conversation structure.

I've tried binding the `disable` argument to a variable inside the `st.session_state`, but it does not work.

This happens in the official ['chat-GPT like' implementation on streamlit forums](https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/build-conversational-apps#write-the-app).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

st.title("ChatGPT-like clone")

def stream_example_response():
    response = "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua."

    # yield 5 characters every 0.1 seconds
    for i in range(0, len(response), 5):
        time.sleep(0.1)
        yield response[i:i+5]

if "messages" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.messages = []

if "disable_chat_input" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.disable_chat_input = False

for message in st.session_state.messages:
    with st.chat_message(message["role"]):
        st.markdown(message["content"])

if prompt := st.chat_input("What is up?", disabled=st.session_state.disable_chat_input):
    
    st.session_state['disable_chat_input'] = True

    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})
    with st.chat_message("user"):
        st.markdown(prompt)

    with st.chat_message("assistant"):
        response = st.write_stream(stream_example_response())
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response})

    st.session_state['disable_chat_input'] = False
```

### Steps To Reproduce

[NONE] Following is my workaround; it works well for my simple chatbot:

1. use session state to control the input state, and get the input value
2. move everything into the **on_submit** callback, DO NOT use *st.chat_message("user").write(...)* in it, or will write dup items.

```python

if "disabled" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.disabled = False

if "messages" not in st.session_state or 0 == len(st.session_state.messages):
    st.session_state.messages = [{"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi, what can I do for you?"}]
    

for msg in st.session_state.messages:
    st.chat_message(msg["role"]).write(msg["content"])

def on_submit():
    st.session_state.disabled = True

    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": st.session_state.prompt})
    # st.chat_message("user").write(st.session_state.prompt)

    response = llm.chat(st.session_state.prompt)

    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response})
    # st.chat_message("assistant").write(response)

    st.session_state.disabled = False


if prompt := st.chat_input("You question here", on_submit=on_submit, disabled=st.session_state.disabled, key="prompt"):
    pass

```

This was was a 'must be fixed'. Callback was not working for me. I ended up using following css hack:
```python
import time
import streamlit as st

# .stApp[data-teststate=running] is present when bot answer is streaming
st.markdown("""
<style>
    .stApp[data-teststate=running] .stChatInput textarea,
    .stApp[data-test-script-state=running] .stChatInput textarea {
        display: none;
    }
</style>
""", unsafe_allow_html=True)

def stream_text(text):
    for char in text:
        time.sleep(0.1)
        yield char

if prompt := st.chat_input("Say something. (This is disabled while assistant is streaming)"):
    with st.chat_message("user"):
        st.write(prompt)
    with st.chat_message("assistant"):
        st.write_stream(stream_text(f"user typed: {prompt}"))
```

[NONE] For future readers, following this worked for me - https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/disable-st-input-chat-during-conversation/50258/2?u=aflah1

[NONE] For future readers, here is my approach (it works for me on streamlit version 1.39.0):

```python
import time
import streamlit as st

# beginning of your code here

def _handle_user_interaction():
    st.session_state["waiting_for_answer"] = True

if "waiting_for_answer" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["waiting_for_answer"] = False

# some more code here

if user_prompt := st.chat_input(
    "Ask a question",
    on_submit=_handle_user_interaction,
    disabled=st.session_state["waiting_for_answer"]
):
    with st.chat_message("user"):
        st.write(user_prompt)

    with st.chat_message("assistant"):
        with st.spinner():
            time.sleep(5)
        # stream the answer here

if st.session_state["waiting_for_answer"]:
    st.session_state["waiting_for_answer"] = False
    st.rerun()
```

The callback is needed for disabling the `st.chat_input` component and any other component you'd like to disable when the user submits a prompt, through setting the `waiting_for_answer` flag. Then, after printing the response, the flag is set to False again. Unfortunately, streamlit needs another user interaction to re-render the app with the flag disabled, so a `st.rerun` is needed

title: Impossible to disable st.chat_input while writing the model's response
text:
[NONE] The problem with this last solution is that apparently , the chat text box loses focus every time...

[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

Streamlit 1.59+ will have a `submit_mode` parameter for `st.chat_input` that controls widget behavior after submission while the script is running:

- "submit" (default): The widget remains fully enabled after submission. Users can submit new messages while the script is running (existing behavior).
- "disable": The widget is automatically disabled after submission and re-enabled when the run completes. This prevents users from interrupting ongoing operations like LLM streaming.
- "stop": The submit button transforms into a stop button while the script runs, allowing users to halt execution (like the app's "Stop" button). The text area is disabled during the run.

title: Server hangs on startup when offline
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Further investigation turned up a few things:

The issue is only triggered in headless mode, because that is the only codepath that calls `net_util.get_external_ip()`. I recently enabled headless mode in my config, which is why I didn't experience it before.
The issue is in the http requests that function makes, which hang even though a connection timeout is set.
It gets stuck right after urllib3 starts a new connection, with no further information. Would have to dig into it deeper, possibly with some tracing tools, to work out what's happening.

I don't know if we actually need an external ip address lookup for running headless mode, but this is also quite an edge case, so it is probably not worth removing the lookup.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Is this possibly related to the bug on Windows where a headless server hangs on closure / startup? Possibly a different root cause but might be hanging in a similar place...

[COLLABORATOR] Closing this since I believe we have fixed this recently by adding a timeout.

### Summary

To begin with, it is a great product. In its current state, it seems advisable to generate a final web page with considerations for web accessibility. This includes aspects such as the page name, language, structure, and named links. Currently, these tags cannot be controlled and may result in errors or warnings in accessible web page verification tools.

### Why?

The product is described as excellent. However, it lacks certain features related to web accessibility. Enhancing web accessibility can improve user experience and ensure compliance with accessibility standards. This proactive approach can also prevent errors and warnings in verification tools.

### How?

To address this, efforts should be made to generate a final web page that incorporates aspects of web accessibility. This may involve adjusting tags related to page name, language, structure, and links to comply with accessibility guidelines. By implementing these changes, errors and warnings in verification tools can be minimized, thereby improving the overall accessibility and usability of the web page.

### Additional Context

I know there are some questions in forums about compatibility e.g. with 508 standards (https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/508-compliance-for-streamlit/13579) which of course would be great but my recommendation would be to start with simple compatibilities that do not incorporate too much development overhead, or diminish Stremlit's capabilities.

[COLLABORATOR] Hey! The data that is being downloaded is exactly the same data you'd get by selecting all cells and copy-pasting them into a file. So disabling that button wouldn't really improve security in any way, that's why we decided not to add an option for disabling it.  

[NONE] Hey! I understand. 
What if this new st.dataframe/st.data_editor parameter disabled the "Download as CSV" button AND copy-pasting the values from the cells?

[COLLABORATOR] Yeah sure, we could do that. But then again... your user can also just write the value of every single cell somewhere else or take a screenshot and use OCR to get the full table. [COLLABORATOR] Re-verified against current `develop` at `0aba4dab0b`.

Calling `AppTest.from_file("server/pages/register.py")` treats `register.py` as the main script, so `page_link("main.py")` is resolved relative to the `pages` directory. The supported multipage testing flow is to start from the actual main script and then switch pages:

```python
at = AppTest.from_file("server/main.py").run()
at.switch_page("pages/register.py").run()
assert not at.exception
```

That flow passes, and page switching has been supported since #8280. Closing as completed because the requested capability is implemented. The AppTest documentation can be clarified separately if the main-script requirement remains confusing.

### Summary

Streamlit needs native asyncio support.

I would like to point the following:

- asyncio interface is also important for snowflake, so usability or applicability of that should be a no brainer
- all modern databases have async interfaces and they will only expand with time
- streamlit is based on asyncio itself, so at least properly exposing the original tornado's event loop would also not require to much work for you

Known problems for now:
- when using asyncio.run() -> RuntimeError: Event loop is closed if the requests follow concurrently in the tornado eventlets
- every eventlet with own event loop -> tasks are getting to the wrong event loop
- cached event loop for all eventlets through session state -> best for now, gets event loop is closed when multile sessions are acessing the app simultaneously

So with that said, very ugly workaround that I found working best for now:

```python

    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    return loop


if not st.session_state.get("event_loop"):
    st.session_state["event_loop"] = get_event_loop()
```

title: Native asyncio support
text: [NONE] Having done a bunch of experimentation myself I have a few things to add. There is a lot of inaccurate information floating around on the web about this subject. The really important thing to remember is what's mentioned in the comment by [USER] above: > Every time a re-render is required (state change, user interaction, etc), a new thread is created and the script is run fresh. The old thread, if it hasn't already completed the script, may keep going (due to fastRerun) but any interaction with st objects will throw a Shutdown Exception. This means that whlie you can use `asyncio.run()` in your script (the [Medium post](https://sehmi-conscious.medium.com/got-that-asyncio-feeling-f1a7c37cab8b) unfortunately linked from Streamlit's own documentation falsely claims otherwise), you can't allow any interaction with your app while the event loop is running, and any tasks you launch on it can't reliably access `st.` functions for the reasons mentioned above. It will also lead to a possibly large number of threads being created since, as mentioned above, the resulting asyncio event loop may run forever. While you can manually create an event loop, set it for the current thread, and recover it on future invocations of your script **in that same thread**, this isn't particularly useful because your script code may or may not (actually won't, probably) run on that thread. You also can't, for example, call `run_until_complete` on the event loop for [well-known reasons](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/66435). Also, despite what said Medium post claims, calling `asyncio.get_running_loop` **definitely does not** return Streamlit's own event

title: Native asyncio support
text: or may not (actually won't, probably) run on that thread. You also can't, for example, call `run_until_complete` on the event loop for [well-known reasons](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/66435). Also, despite what said Medium post claims, calling `asyncio.get_running_loop` **definitely does not** return Streamlit's own event loop, as it will always be on a different thread than the one that runs your script. This is, of course, what this bug is actually about :-) If you don't care about security, reliability, stability, etc, and you don't want to call `st.` functions from your tasks, you can get it by calling `_get_async_objs()` on the session runtime. For instance: ```python import asyncio import time import streamlit as st loop = st.runtime.get_instance()._get_async_objs().eventloop async def do_nothing(seconds): await asyncio.sleep(3) print("HELLO WORLD", seconds) if st.button(label="Do something"): loop.create_task(do_nothing(time.time())) if st.button(label="Do something else"): st.toast("Hello!") ``` The best workaround for the moment, if you need to use asyncio for something, is probably to explicitly create a separate thread to run asyncio tasks, using `add_script_run_ctx` to give it access to the session state so that it can communicate with the rest of the UI.

[NONE] Hello -

Just a bit of experimentation around Streamlit, threads, and asyncio.

My understanding:
- Every time a re-render is required (state change, user interaction, etc), a new thread is created and the script is run fresh. The old thread, if it hasn't already completed the script, may keep going (due to fastRerun) but any interaction with st objects will throw a Shutdown Exception.
- Streamlit does not care about asyncio, rather only if the thread has terminated or not.

I'm not sure how scalable this is -- threads will be active for each user potentially -- but my approach has been:
- Use asyncio.run() at the end of the script. This will create a new event loop for the thread (and render).
- The asyncio loop has tasks, which may run forever, *must* frequently interact with st (e.g. st.session_state) to trigger potential Shutdown exceptions to clean up the threads.
- If the asyncio loop ends early, then the "Running" indicator stops. So you can see the thread is still busy.

I haven't done scaled testing, but this approach seems to be working sensibly in my tests.

title: Native asyncio support
text:
[NONE] I also don't really see how a solution to this problem could easily be implemented in Streamlit.  Conceptually, what is necessary, is what the original poster's "ugly workaround" is supposed to do, and what the Medium post claims Streamlit does, but which neither of them actually do, namely creating (possibly on demand) an event loop for each session context which script code can use to launch tasks.  Why this doesn't work:

- Simply creating an event loop doesn't actually start it!  So calling `create_task` on said loop will not do anything at all.
- Running an event loop is a blocking, non-reentrant operation.   Obviously a Streamlit `AppContext` (which runs in the main thread) can't do this.   But also a Streamlit `ScriptRunner` (which runs in its own thread) can't do this either, because there could be any number of threads for a given session context.

I don't claim to really understand Streamlit's architecture but it seems like a possible implementation woud be to create a separate thread for each script context, run an event loop there, and somehow give script code access to this event loop so that it can create and wait on tasks launched in it.  The evil solution would be to do magic on `await` in script code to make it do that ;-)

title: Native asyncio support
text:
[NONE] Here's a sketch of how you can do what's mentioned in the previous comment.  There are a couple of caveats:

- Accessing the ui from a coroutine doesn't work for some reason, most likely because at the moment when you might want to do so, the script is no longer actually running, or a new script runner has been started (this is not clear to me).
- There is no signal handling possible in the local event loop.  So you have to hit Control-C multiple times to stop the server, and you will get an "Event loop is closed" exception.
- Any running tasks will do ... something undefined, I think ... if you stop the event loop, and Python will complain about this.

Gist here: https://gist.github.com/dhdaines/574d58eed7da9c459e3ef2b50a3ac27b


[CONTRIBUTOR] While not officially supported, I think Streamlit mostly works with this simple pattern (my [user-space effort towards easier concurrency](https://concurrency.streamlit.app/) is based on this and other workarounds):

```py
# a_page.py
import asyncio
import streamlit as st

async def task1(): ...

async def task2(): ...

async def main():
  res1, res2 = await asyncio.gather(task1(), task2())
  # update widgets if required 

asyncio.run(main())
```

A Streamlit `scriptThread` is a 'clean' one without an event loop, just as `asyncio.run()` requires. A new event loop will get created, used, and shutdown properly. Code in coroutines have access to `ScriptRunContext` and should still work.

title: Native asyncio support
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] > reuse tornado's event loop

While not impossible this looks risky to me:

1. An eventloop for net IO should be kept away from possibly blocking code. Like a `async def fun(): a_slow_long_function()`
2. When `ScriptRunContext` and other thread-local object are involved, they may get leaked during interleaved coroutine execution.
    - This applies to other shared event loop solutions. IMO an event loop should not be shared at a scope larger than Streamlit session.

> possiblity of leaked or forever-spinning user-created event loop

Yes, a solution should take care of this. I'm still trying to.

My current thought is to expose script run / session shutdowns to user code, and allow some form of cancellation (forced or cooperative).

Then at least we could use a file update as the refresh trigger, which is a cleaner workaround than a browser hack or refresh loop.

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Thanks everyone for the rich discussion here. 🙏 Over time this issue has become a catch-all for several *distinct* needs, and most of them now have clearer, dedicated homes. To keep the conversation focused and actionable, we're closing this in favor of the more specific issues below — please 👍 and continue in whichever one matches your use case: - **Loading independent sections / data in parallel to speed up a page** → use `st.fragment(parallel=True)`. Independent sections run concurrently and render into reserved containers, so total load time is the slowest section rather than the sum. See [Run fragments in parallel](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/architecture/fragments#run-fragments-in-parallel) (and the [`st.fragment` API reference](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment)). - **Long-running or non-blocking background work** — e.g. kicking off a slow computation or database/API call, updating the app when it finishes, or cancelling in-flight work → **#6687** (background execution). - **Reacting to external events / webhooks** — receiving external HTTP calls is now supported via custom routes on **`st.App`** (the ASGI/Starlette integration, #439, available since 1.53 and the default in 1.57; feedback in #13600). Pushing such an event into a running session to update the UI is tracked in **#6687**. - **CPU-bound work / `multiprocessing` / `ProcessPoolExecutor`** → tracked separately in **#4788** and **#7851**. A note on calling `st.*` from your own or a library's threads: this remains unsupported and is not thread-safe — elements can arrive in the UI in an unpredictable order. For concurrency that renders as part of your app, use parallel fragments (which render into reserved containers). For

text: or a library's threads: this remains unsupported and is not thread-safe — elements can arrive in the UI in an unpredictable order. For concurrency that renders as part of your app, use parallel fragments (which render into reserved containers). For work whose result you want to surface when it finishes, follow **#6687** — getting a completed background task to update the UI (rather than polling for it) is part of what that issue covers. If your specific need isn't captured by any of the above, please open a new issue so we can track it! Thanks again for all the input here! 🎈

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I love experimental_fragment but I really wish there was a function like `st.fragment_rerun` or something that allowed you to check for certain conditions on which to rerun that fragment on. Right now you can only do it every n seconds, and if you put a while loop to stop reruns it doesn't stop the reruns from just piling up in the queue (or at least I think that's what's going on). 

Alternatively you can run `st.rerun` under a condition and just rerun the whole script but that's quite heavy handed when the point of fragments is to isolate reruns.

[NONE] I think that this could be solved by having an invalidation callback. If the callback returns true, the fragment is invalidated and re-rendered. This would allow for you to check for changes in session state that impact the fragment.

Here is a really simple example using a counter. In a more complex application, there might be many places that increment the count that exist outside the fragments which display it.

```python
import streamlit as st

def invalidator():
    if st.session_state['prev'] != st.session_state['current']
        st.session_state['prev'] = st.session_state['current']
        return true
    return false

def increment_value():
    st.session_state['current'] = st.session_state['current'] + 1

[USER].experimental_fragment(invalidation_callback=invalidator)
def display_value():
    st.print(st.session_state['current'])

if st.session_state.get('current') == None:
    st.session_state['current'] = 0

st.button('Increment Value', on_click=increment_value)
display_value()
```

[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] actually asked me to make a ticket for this the other week, haha. I'll just post my support for a `st.rerun(scope='fragment')` feature here. 

Having this feature would allow me to use fragments in https://github.com/Asaurus1/streamlit-process-manager which I currently can't do very nicely (no way to stop running the fragment when process terminates)

The invalidator function is interesting but difficult to understand and technically challenging to implement. When does the invalidator get run and by what script runner or in what context? Is it every time session state changes? How do you ensure that the invalidator does not mutate session state thereby causing a recursion problem?

if anyone else has feedback / use case / input feel free to add please!

[NONE] I don't think you need to ensure that the invalidator does not mutate session state. Recursion problems are possible to create in streamlit already, it's up to the developer to avoid them. It would run every time any fragment updates, so you'd have to be careful about performance when implementing it.

A more straightforward approach to resolve my use case that is also in line with what you guys are thinking would be the ability to tag fragments like `st.experimental_fragment(tags=['tag1', 'tag2'])` and be able to rerun all of the fragments that include that tag like `st.rerun(tag='tag1')`.

title: Rerun fragment only programatically with `st.fragment` instead of `run_every`
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] We agreed to solve this by adding an optional `scope=` kwarg to `st.rerun()`, so you can do e.g. `scope="app"` or `scope="fragment"`.

One question I'd love some input on, is whether the default should remain `scope="app"` (as today), or if we'd want some `scope="auto"` which by default only re-runs the fragment when called in a fragment. A few developers reported that that's the default behavior they would expect.

A main downside of `scope="auto"` is that `st.rerun()` is the main way to break out of a dialog today, so either we'd have to force everyone to always do `st.rerun(scope="app")` in a dialog to exit, or else have a different behavior for dialogs vs fragments. I don't really like either of those options.

Someone else may even have another, more clever idea in this vein - ideas and feedback welcome!

[CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] the tag thing is very interesting for triggering fragment calls from outside themselves or establishing dependency chains. We'll plan to add the `scope=` feature first ^ but I bookmarked this to come back later since it does sound very interesting and powerful. Not sure if we want to break that into a separate issue from this one (or move the scope thing to its own issue)

title: Rerun fragment only programatically with `st.fragment` instead of `run_every`
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Oh, yep sorry for using shorthand.
- Every dialog is a fragment already - so if I draw a widget inside a dialog and move the widget, the dialog code reruns but the rest of the app does not.
- Dialogs support exiting via top right `x` and ESC, but to use a "Submit" button etc you need to use `st.rerun()`.

From [the docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.dialog)
> st.experimental_dialog inherits behavior from [st.experimental_fragment](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment). When a user interacts with an input widget created inside a dialog function, Streamlit only reruns the dialog function instead of the full script.
> 
> A user can dismiss a modal dialog by clicking outside of it, clicking the "X" in its upper-right corner, or pressing``ESC`` on their keyboard. Dismissing a modal dialog does not trigger an app rerun. To close the modal dialog programmatically, call st.rerun() explicitly inside of the dialog function.

e.g. I might do something like:

```python
[USER].experimental_dialog("Login")
def login():
    user_name = st.text_input("Username:")
    if st.button("Submit", disabled=not user_name):
        st.session_state.user_name = user_name
        st.rerun()
```

So it would probably be un-intuitive if `st.rerun()` worked differently on a dialog vs a fragment (since they're otherwise basically identical). On the other hand, it might also be annoying to be forced to remember `st.rerun(scope="app")` for every form-style dialog.

[NONE] Any progress on this?  This would be very helpful for a project I am working on currently.  I personally like the st.rerun("fragment") but any of the ideas would be fine if was implemented.

text: [CONTRIBUTOR] [USER] that is a _really_ good question and I have a two part answer/opinion. 1. I think that the behavior you've gone with _is_ reasonable, and your logic is sound. 2. This unfortunately means (I think) that the `fragment` mechanism won't do what I was originally hoping it _could_ do. To explain #2, here is a simplified version of the code that I was _hoping_ would be enabled by allowing you to re-run fragments programatically. ```python [USER].experimental_fragment def a_simple_counter(): current_count = st.session_state.counter st.write("The counter is at", current_count) if current_count < 10: time.sleep(1) st.session_state.counter += 1 st.rerun(scope="fragment") else: st.button("Reset Counter", on_click=reset_counter) st.success("Finished") def reset_counter(): st.session_state.counter = 0 # Page code reset_counter() a_simple_counter() st.button("rerun-page", help="just a button to click to force a full rerun") ``` If the behavior of `st.rerun(scope="fragment")` is as you have described above, then every time the _full page_ re-runs, the counter will sleep for 1 second, increment the counter by 1, and then do nothing since the rerun is skipped. Only by clicking the "Reset Counter" button _inside of the fragment_ will it trigger a fragment-rerun that causes the fragment to count to 10 before it completes and ceases to run. In my ideal world, when the fragment is first encountered during a full page re-run, it would start running in it's own separate script thread and continue to re-run itself, updating it's little block of the page until the counter reaches 10. Almost like a thread spawn. Meanwhile, the rest of the script _continues_ to run

title: Rerun fragment only programatically with `st.fragment` instead of `run_every`
text: would start running in it's own separate script thread and continue to re-run itself, updating it's little block of the page until the counter reaches 10. Almost like a thread spawn. Meanwhile, the rest of the script _continues_ to run until it reaches the end of the main page. This is not how I think you guys originally envisioned `fragments` to work. For fairly obvious reasons this would have all the race-conditiony fun and joy of dealing with threaded concurrency. I am not saying you should make fragments do this. Now, the behavior where `st.rerun(scope="fragment")` queues up the fragment to be "rerun" _after_ the main script execution **would actually solve my problem here**. Once the page code finishes, the fragment would resume counting from wherever it left off until it reached 10, whereupon it too would exit. However I can, as you likely did, envision many other uses for `fragment` where this behavior would not be expected and potentially even cause major issues or confusion. It leaves major questions open like "what if a `rerun` is encountered multiple times in the fragment"? You could make the "scheduled execution" opt-in via a second argument; `st.rerun(scope="fragment", when="soon")` perhaps. This could have the behavior of causing the rerun of the page/fragment to be scheduled "soon" (e.g. as soon as possible after the current thing that is running finishes, similar to how scheduling things "soon" in async code works). I don't know that that would be easy to implement, though, and would definitely have

[NONE] Do you have any updates on this? 


It seems that having the possibility to check for certain conditions on which to rerun a fragment on is still a needed feature. (See here https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/fragment-as-an-inner-function-to-control-run-every-dynamically/100507/2)
The case describe in the end of this thread is also my exact need and I don't think that we are alone.

When a fragment is use to display the status of let's say a long running process we want the fragment to stop refreshing when the process is finished.

Having the possibility to stop the "run_every" of the fragment or to choose when to rerun or not the fragment is still a needed feature. It seems that the only working workaround as of now is to put a contidition at the begining of the fragment to stop it's rendering but it is not a graceful approach.


[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

This is available in Streamlit 1.63+. You can rerun a specific fragment from a widget callback:

```python
[USER].fragment(key="results")
def results():
    st.write(st.session_state.filter)

results()

st.selectbox(
    "Filter",
    OPTIONS,
    key="filter",
    on_change=lambda: st.rerun("results"),
)
```

### Summary

We're soon going to add chart selections for Altair in Streamlit, via `st.altair_chart(..., on_select="rerun")`. However, this only works for Altair v5 today, while `st.altair_chart` without selections enabled supports both Altair v4 and v5. Supporting selections for v4 wouldn't be easy due to differences in the underlying JSON representation and the need to set up new testing infrastructure to test both versions in parallel. That's why we decided to cut it from the initial release. 

If you'd like us to implement support for chart selections with Altair v4, please upvote this issue with a 👍 and let us know in the comments below why you need v4 and can't upgrade to v5!

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-8531)


[CONTRIBUTOR] Hey [USER] Thanks for the issue.

So the problem is this faceted chart in vega ignores any hints from us about the responsive width. I think the goal would be to make sure vega can address this issue in their code, so we don't have to calculate the optimal size for each chart.

There is certainly more we can do to better inform the users, but we will keep track of updates.

[COLLABORATOR] Running the snippet on current develop, `st.altair_chart(fig, use_container_width=True)` renders a single grouped bar chart — one shared y-axis, one column per site — instead of splitting into a separate chart per site value. Facet charts now deliberately opt out of container-width stretching and render at their natural size, which is what removed the splitting.

The second half of the issue — that the single chart spans the container width — is not fixed, and is tracked separately in #9091. It's an upstream limitation: Vega-Lite doesn't support responsive fit sizing for faceted, concatenated, or repeated views (vega-lite#5219 (https://github.com/vega/vega-lite/issues/5219)), so `width="stretch"` is currently a no-op for these charts. In a 736px container the chart renders at 484px. Please follow #9091 for that half.

Please note: `use_container_width=True` is deprecated in favour of `width="stretch"`. Both behave identically for this chart.

### Summary

Since some recent time, [st. date_input](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.date_input) is not working anymore when it is put in the sidebar (e.g., `st.sidebar.date_input()`) *and* the streamlit app is either run on a mobile device or with a very narrow browser window (the important point is that the app width is so small that the sidebar is automatically hidden). In these cases, opening the sidebar first, then the [st. date_input](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets/st.date_input), and then trying to change the month or the year results in the whole sidebar being collapsed again, rendering the input method unusable.

The problem occurs when streamlit is run locally (with the latest version 1.33.0) or in the cloud. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import datetime
import streamlit as st

d = st.sidebar.date_input("When's your birthday", datetime.date(2019, 7, 6))
st.write('Your birthday is:', d)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

- Open app at https://datepicker-bug.streamlit.app (or locally)
- Reduce browser window width until the sidebar is automatically hidden (not needed when opening with mobile device)
- Open sidebar by clicking on the `>` in the top left
- Click on the date picker
- Click on the month or year to change it
- The sidebar will collapse

title: Add alt text to images & charts for improved accessibility
text:
Issue #8563: Add alt text to images & charts for improved accessibility
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.dataframe, feature:charts, feature:st.image, area:accessibility

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a way for developers to add alt text to commands such as `st.image` and chart objects.

### Why?

For accessibility reasons, images, charts, and other visualizations should always have [alt text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/tips/) that describes the content. 

### How?

This should probably be a parameter that the developer can set since we can't automatically generate alt text (even though this might be a cool LLM application 😉 ). Maybe just a parameter `alt` or `alt_text` or `alternative_text` that accepts a string. 

Elements for which we could/should add this:
- st.image
- st.dataframe and st.table (see [this article on accessible tables](https://www.albany.edu/web-services/accessibility/accessibility-basics/5-creating-accessible-tables))
- all [chart elements](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/charts)

Note that some of these elements also have other parameters to describe the content (e.g. `st.image` has a `caption` parameter), so we'd have to see how these two work together. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Add alt text to images & charts for improved accessibility
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This is a feature enhancement request to add alt text support to `st.image`, `st.dataframe`/`st.table`, and all chart elements for improved accessibility. Currently, `st.image` uses a generic key as the `alt` attribute on `` tags (see `ImageList.tsx`), and chart elements have no alt text or ARIA description support in their protobuf definitions or frontend components. Implementing this would require adding an `alt_text` (or similar) parameter to the Python API for each affected element, extending the corresponding protobuf messages, and updating the frontend components to render the provided alt text. The relationship between `st.image`'s existing `caption` parameter and the new alt text would need to be defined (caption is visual, alt text is for screen readers). ### Related Issues - **[#12873 - 508 Compliance - Add Alt="" tag to decorative elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12873)**: Closely related accessibility request focused on adding empty `alt=""` to *decorative* elements (like icons in selectboxes) to prevent screen reader clutter. This issue (#8563) covers adding *descriptive* alt text to content elements like images and charts — complementary but distinct scope. - **[#8399 - Basic accessibility web features](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8399)**: Broader request for basic web accessibility features (page lang attribute, accessible link naming, structural compliance). Alt text for images/charts would fall under this umbrella of accessibility improvements. - **[#10119 - Fullscreen label for `st.image`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10119)**: Request to add descriptive labels/context to images in fullscreen mode. While focused on visual descriptions rather than screen reader accessibility, both involve adding metadata/descriptions to `st.image` and could share implementation patterns. --- *This is an automated triage comment

title: Add alt text to images & charts for improved accessibility
text:
[NONE] Any update on this? It would be great to be able to provide alt text for blind users without caption for sighted users.

[COLLABORATOR] I think we should apply this to `st.image`, `st.dataframe` and `st.data_editor` and all chart commands. It should be one parameter that can be used across all of them, probably either:

1. `alt` or `alt_text` or something similar: standard and very well understood, but technically the HTML alt attribute only exists for images
2. `accessible_description` or `accessible_text` or something similar: bit more generic and potentially more correct than `alt`; need to check with accessibility guidelines which term is correct here though

And then under the hood we should set whichever HTML attribute is the "best" one for that specific element. For images probably the HTML `alt` attribute, for dataframes/charts probably one of the `aria` attributes. Need to look into accessibility best practices what works well.

**What shipped**: keyword-only `alt=` so authors can give an accessible name to the surfaces this issue called for — `st.image`, `st.dataframe` / `st.table`, and the chart commands — plus related media and embeds covered by the approved product spec ([#16937](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16937) / specs/2026-09-14-element-alt-text/product-spec.md).

**Representative PRs**: [#16568](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16568) (audio/video), [#17040](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17040) (iframe), [#17041](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17041) (altair_chart, vega_lite_chart), [#17069](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17069) (line_chart, bar_chart, area_chart, scatter_chart), [#17080](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17080) (echarts_chart), [#17081](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17081) (plotly_chart), [#17085](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17085) (graphviz_chart), [#17086](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17086) (map, pydeck_chart), [#17095](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17095) (table), [#17096](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17096) (mermaid_chart), [#17118](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17118) (pdf), [#17125](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17125) (dataframe/data_editor), [#17136](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17136) & [#17137](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17137) (image/pyplot). Agent guidance: [#17201](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17201).

`caption` stays the visible label on `st.image`; alt is the assistive name (independent, including decorative `alt=""` on image/pyplot only).

title: `st.runtime.get_instance()._session_mgr.list_active_sessions()[0].client.request.protocol` is http on https pages.
text:
[CONTRIBUTOR] Hi [USER],

I'm not sure if there's much we can do about this in the Streamlit OS lib side. The issue is most likely because, in a Community Cloud deployment, the connection is indeed an http connection since the TLS connection isn't terminated by the Streamlit server, it's terminated at the load balancer level (and security is maintained by having the network permissions set such that the Streamlit server only accepts traffic from the load balancer in front of it).

This would be true of any deployment made where the Streamlit server itself isn't configured to terminate the TLS connection, and while we do have some basic configurability for this included in our config options (see the `server.sslCertFile` and `server.sslKeyFile`), it's unlikely we'll add full support for this in Community Cloud given the community focus of the product.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Interesting!

Well, fixing this isn't crucial for me, so feel free to deprioritize it, etc.

[COLLABORATOR] Closing this since this is referring to an internal tornado API, and we have migrated to Starlette recently

In similar way to other framework, there should be an additional parameter, named, for example, "tooltip_delay", which would delay the display of the Help string.

 If the new parameter "tooltip_delay" is 0, tooltip appears immediately. When value increase (ms), help string is not show even if the mouse pointer remains positioned on the button. With selection enables the altair binding widgets render multiple times and chart data is not visible for some reason. 

Without new selection API enabled.

```Python
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data

import streamlit as st

df = pd.read_json(data.cars.url)

input_dropdown = alt.binding_radio(

)

        y="Horsepower:Q",

    )
        
    
)

return_event = st.checkbox('Use selection')
if return_event:

        use_container_width=True)
    st.write(event_data)
else:

    )
```

Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.plotly_chart

### Checklist

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When updating a plotly_chart, with for ex. a scatter_mapbox, the resulting map is flickering.
This was not the case before the 1.35.0 upgrade.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-8782)

```Python
import random
import time

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import streamlit as st

dfData = {'longitude': [0.0], 'latitude': [0.0]}
df = pd.DataFrame(dfData)

mapData = px.scatter_mapbox(df, lat="latitude", lon="longitude", zoom=6, width=400, height=300)
mapData.update_layout(mapbox_style="open-street-map")

latitude = 57.0
longitude = -110.0

mapDisplay = st.empty()
while True:
    latitude += random.uniform(-0.005, 0.005)
    longitude += random.uniform(-0.005, 0.005)
    mapData.data[0].lat = [latitude]
    mapData.data[0].lon = [longitude]
    mapData.update_layout(mapbox_center={"lat": latitude, "lon": longitude})
    mapDisplay.plotly_chart(mapData, use_container_width=True)
    time.sleep(0.1)
```

In order to reproduce the issue update streamlit to 1.35.0 (currently latest) version and run the code above.

Sadly the chart flickers as its been updated.

This resolved various other issues with plotly, but negatively impacted this type of usecase of updating plotly charts. We should probably provide a way via the `key` parameter to keep the plotly chart identity stable.

title: Support client-side validation via regex pattern for `st.text_input`
text:
Issue #8790: Support client-side validation via regex pattern for `st.text_input` 
Labels: type:enhancement, feature:st.text_input

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add support for client-side regex validation in `st.text_input`. This is already supported for the `column_config.TextColumn` via the `validate` parameter.

### Why?

Client-side validation is a lot more efficient since it doesn't require triggering an app rerun. It also makes it easier to validate user input and can provide a more user-friendly behavior. 

### How?

Add a `validate` parameter that supports a regex pattern (same behavior as with `TextColumn`): 

```python
st.text_input("Streamlit Widget", validate="^st\.[a-z_]+$")
```

If the input does not conform with the pattern, it must somehow show information about the pattern to the user.

### Additional Context

Basic HTML input elements also support client-side validation via the `pattern` property: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input#pattern 

A related feature would be to support [input masks](https://baseweb.design/components/input/#maskedinput) in addition to the pattern validation. This feature is also somewhat related to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6704.

title: Support client-side validation via regex pattern for `st.text_input`
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] Thank you [USER] for opening this issue! I believe that incorporating validation logic for input fields is one of the most crucial enhancements needed in the current Streamlit framework. Most front-end frameworks include some form of validation logic/UI. Here are two examples: **Tailwind UI:** **Bootstrap:** While client-side validation with regex would be useful, it has its limitations. Allowing developers to pass a custom validation function would be more versatile, enabling validation logic that can include database queries and other complex checks. This approach would also generalize the validation logic to all input components, not just text inputs. For instance, I have a use case where I need to ensure that the second date input is later than the first date input. There are many ways to implement this. A possible implementation could allow any function that returns `None` if the input is valid, or a string with an error message if it is not. Here’s a simple example: ```python st.text_input( "Email address", validate=lambda x: None if "@" in x else "Please enter a valid email address", ) ``` And a more advanced example: ```python st.text_input( "Email address", validate=utils.check_if_email_address_is_in_database, ) ``` I am not an expert in fragments. But maybe we can use fragments to ensure that we can have custom validation logic without requiring a full rerun? For future reference, this issue seems tangentially related to [issue #7165](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7165).

title: Support client-side validation via regex pattern for `st.text_input`
text:
[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

`st.text_input` now supports client-side regex validation via a new `validate` parameter. This will be available in Streamlit `1.62+`.

```python
email = st.text_input(
    "Email",
    validate=(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$", "Enter a valid email address."),
)
```

Invalid non-empty values are not submitted, and the custom message is shown when validation fails.

Labels: type:bug, papercut, area:network, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.session_state, area:server

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Similar to the issues linked, if the network connection is intermittent/flaky the existing session is lost and a new one created, causing unpleasant/unexpected user experience.

See:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1386
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1628
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6442

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

if "counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.counter = 0

st.write(f"Run count = {st.session_state.counter}")

st.session_state.counter += 1

time.sleep(3)

st.rerun()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the reproducible code example provided in streamlit on one server host.
2. Observe the "Run count = X" increase steadily in a client host different from the server host.
3. Disable the client network connection and wait for some arbitrary time duration.
4. Re-enable the client network connection.
5. Observer the "Run count = X" start from zero again.

### Expected Behavior

The user session should be restored so they may continue where they left off in the face of their network/internet connection being flaky (packet drops, high latency etc) causing unclean websocket close behind the scenes.

### Current Behavior

Observe streamlit warning log "Session with id %s is already connected! Connecting to a new session." and user loses their streamlit session and starts afresh.

title: Reconnect to existing sessions instead of creating new upon unclean websocket close.
text: [CONTRIBUTOR] This issue reports that when a WebSocket connection closes uncleanly (e.g., due to network disruptions), Streamlit creates a new session instead of reconnecting to the existing one, causing users to lose their session state. **Root cause analysis:** The issue originates in `lib/streamlit/runtime/websocket_session_manager.py` in the `connect_session()` method. When a client attempts to reconnect with an existing session ID, the code checks if that session is already in `_active_session_info_by_id` (line 103). If it is, a warning is logged ("Session with id %s is already connected!") and a **new** session is created instead. The session can only be restored from storage if it's NOT currently active. The core problem is a race condition: on an unclean WebSocket close, the server may not have detected the disconnect yet, so the session remains "active" in memory. When the client quickly reconnects with the same session ID, the server sees it as "already connected" and creates a new session instead of allowing reconnection. A potential fix would need to handle this case by either closing the existing connection first, implementing a grace period, or using a different strategy for tracking active vs. disconnected sessions. ### Related Issues 1. **[#9031](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9031)** - "Current recommended way to deal with restarted Streamlit sessions" - Directly related issue where users request better session recovery mechanisms after unexpected restarts. 2. **[#11012](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11012)** - "Preserve session state (e.g. in file, database, or localstorage)" - Related enhancement request for persisting session state across browser sessions, which would help mitigate the impact of session loss.

title: "ImportError: cannot import name 'runtime_version' from 'google.protobuf'" when developing on MacOS
text:
[COLLABORATOR] The original Mac `ImportError: cannot import name 'runtime_version'` happened when Homebrew `protoc` generated code newer than the Python `protobuf` in the venv.

That is no longer an issue for normal Streamlit development. We require `protobuf>=5.26.1` (which includes `runtime_version`), and `uv.lock` currently pins `protobuf==6.33.6`, which matches Homebrew protobuf 33.x and also accepts older gencode such as CI's protoc 26.1.

Python only rejects gencode *newer* than the installed runtime. A much newer Homebrew protobuf than the lockfile can still fail that check, but that is an upgrade edge case, not the 2024 setup failure, and it does not require pinning `protoc` in the Mac install instructions. CONTRIBUTING troubleshooting now notes this.

Closing.

text:
[NONE] > As a workaround, I think you should be able to do something like `at.get("imgs")` or `at.get("download_button")`

Is it possible to click the download button and receive the file from `at.get("download_button")` ? 

[NONE] The following workaround works for me for a case where there is only one download_button.

```python
import streamlit as st

class DownloadButton(object): # Singleton (only be created once) class to hold inputs to download button
    def __new__(cls, label=None, data=None, file_name=None, mime=None):
        # Note: I only set this up to handle inputs that I'm using but it can obviously be extended
        if not hasattr(cls, 'instance'):
            cls.instance = super(DownloadButton, cls).__new__(cls) # Create singleton if it does not exist
            cls.instance.value = False

        cls.instance.label = label
        cls.instance.data = data
        cls.instance.file_name = file_name
        cls.instance.mime = mime

        return cls.instance
    
    def click(self):
        self.value = True
  

def download_button(label, data, file_name, mime):
    btn = DownloadButton(label, data, file_name, mime)

    out = btn.value
    if out and callable(btn.data):
        btn.data = data()
    btn.value = False  # Set to False to revert value after a button click
    return out

def columns(ncols, *args, **kwargs):  # Extend st.columns to include download button function
    all_cols = st._main.columns(ncols, *args, **kwargs)
    for c in all_cols:
        c.download_button = download_button

    return all_cols

# Replace streamlit functions
st.download_button = download_button
st.columns = columns

def test_download(app):    
    btn = DownloadButton()
    btn.click()
    app.run()

    assert isinstance(btn.data, bytes)
```

title: Slider with floats do not use the step parameter based on min_value when step can be casted to int (e.g. 1.0)
text:
Issue #9184: Slider with floats do not use the step parameter based on min_value when step can be casted to int (e.g. 1.0)
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.slider, upstream

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using st.slider with float values, the step parameters is relative to to 0 and not relative to min_value as expected.

Apparently it is a problem from BaseWeb:

```
import * as React from "react";
import { Slider } from "baseui/slider";
export default () => {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState([3]);
  return (
    <Slider
      value={value}
      onChange={({ value }) => value && setValue(value)}
      onFinalChange={({ value }) => console.log(value)}
      min={0.5}
      max={3.5}
      step={1.0}
      marks
    />
  );
}
```

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-9184)

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.slider("Slider", min_value=1.50, max_value=100.50, value=(2.5, 41.5), step=1.0)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

streamlit run code.py

### Expected Behavior

The selection should be at step one from 1.5

### Current Behavior

Only 2.0, 3.0 and so on can be selected.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.37.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Edge

title: st.fragment incompatible with streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest
text:
[COLLABORATOR] I checked this against current `develop`. Fragments do run under `AppTest`:

- During `AppTest.from_file("app.py").run()`, the fragment body runs and its return value reaches the script.
- A button inside the fragment works with `.click().run()`. `AppTest` reruns the whole script rather than only the fragment. That gives the same result unless a test depends on the rest of the script *not* rerunning.

The test in the report calls `dummy_result()` directly from the test module. A `[USER].fragment` function runs only during a Streamlit script run. Outside one, it returns `None` without running its body, so `result` is `None`. Instead, assert on what the app renders through `AppTest`. Or move the logic into a plain function and unit-test that function directly.

#17605 documents this in the bundled testing skill. `AppTest` doesn't support fragment-scoped reruns yet (rerunning only the fragment, as the browser does). That gap is tracked with dialog inner widgets in #9786, so I'm closing this one as working as intended.

[COLLABORATOR] [USER], thanks for reporting this issue. I reproduced it [here](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9243). This looks quite easy to fix. But not 100% sure if it's a better or worse behavior to auto-focus. Are there any other opinions against or for auto-focus (cc [USER] [USER])

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.


[CONTRIBUTOR] We moved this to an enhancement because the current intention to autofocus is working as expected. The question remains whether autofocus should _not_ be a feature of popover.

[COLLABORATOR] Noticed this does really look buggy/undesirable when the popover starts with a `st.date_input`. 

https://share.cleanshot.com/wGC18Qml

[COLLABORATOR] Also: this affects st.dialog

[COLLABORATOR] In my opinion, the example with a single text box or selectbox being automatically active is nice, but with things like st.date_input it's *very* annoying. I would love a `focus_on_first=False` argument added (and also it would be nice to see this default behavior mentioned in the docs).

[COLLABORATOR] I prepared a PR to deactivate autofocus for dialog and popover. I think not using autofocus is a slightly better default than using autofocus: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10370 And I will add a new feature request to make this behavior configurable (e.g. via `focus_on_first`). 

[COLLABORATOR] New feature request: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10371

title: Don't autofocus first element in `st.popover` and `st.dialog`
text:
[COLLABORATOR] New feature request: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10371

[COLLABORATOR] After some discussion, we decided not to deactivate auto-focus as default and instead accelerate the migration of date_input away from baseweb (to fix the annoying issue with the popover) https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9243 I think adding a parameter - e.g., `focus_on_first` - is also quite valid... but will require a small product discussion (cc [USER])

[COLLABORATOR] What was the reasoning not to remove the auto-focus? I've been actually thinking for a long time that we should remove it, I always found it a bit annoying... Sure, there are certain situations (like a single text input) where it might be useful but in most situations, it felt pretty awkward to me. I'm not totally opposed to a parameter but even then I'd probably set the default to `False`. 

[COLLABORATOR] [USER] it was related to concerns about breaking web standards and accessibility: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10370#discussion_r1949575070

[COLLABORATOR] Closing this since it was fixed by the basweb to react-aria migration in the latest Streamlit version.

title: Decorators not being printed in `st.echo()`
text:
Issue #9252: Decorators not being printed in `st.echo()`
Labels: type:bug, status:confirmed, priority:P3, feature:st.echo

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.echo()` does not print a decorator if there is no other line of code before the decorator.

To reproduce, run the below script:

```
import streamlit as st


def decorator(*args):
    pass


with st.echo():

    [USER]
    def function():
        pass
```

The output will be as shown below: 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d06cb182-7ffb-4111-90c7-b062be9ec2b7)
Note that `[USER]` is not printed.

Now, add anything above the decorator in the context of `st.echo()`:

```
import streamlit as st


def decorator(*args):
    pass


with st.echo():
```
