Though, this seems to be an issue with arrow itself, not Streamlit (see also this issue: https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/30648). According to that issue, the provided datastructure is not supportable by arrow in general. How would you expect the rendered table to look like?

title: Attempting to show a table with nested lists fails with `cannot mix list and non-list, non-null values`
text:
[NONE] > How would you expect the rendered table to look like?

Just how it does it for any raw JSON (displayed as raw text, and double-click allows to see and copy/paste the entire JSON string).

I ran into this issue using a GeoJson `FeatureCollection` which consists of a hybrid of `Polygon` and `MultiPolygon` instances. According to the GeoJson specs, a polygon and a multi-polygon differ exactly in the "nestedness" illustrated in the minimal example. I wanted to display the GeoJson in a map, and at the same time offer the row-wise GeoJson in the table, giving users the possibility to access/inspect the raw GeoJson directly.

From a user perspective the role and involvement of arrow is not clear. Basically streamlit suggests that it supports pandas DataFrames in general, so it is unexpected that it crashes on certain column contents, even if they are just plain json compatible data. The serialization could e.g. internally fall back to a JSON based serialization (or even `__str__` or `__repr__` based), if arrow doesn't support serializing something.

[COLLABORATOR] Thanks for elaborating on your use-case 🙂 

> internally fall back to a JSON based serialization (or even __str__ or __repr__ based), if arrow doesn't support serializing something.

I think this is a great idea! [USER] do you think that this is easily achievable and also makes sense?

title: Attempting to show a table with nested lists fails with `cannot mix list and non-list, non-null values`
text:
[COLLABORATOR] We have a fallback to `str` for arrow-incompatible columns. This is based on some logic that detects if the content of a column is incompatible:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/fbe27d6432435ef5b957785f4d3976f81a1dae49/lib/streamlit/dataframe_util.py#L1029

Since scalar-list values are supported, we need to check the actual list value to determine the compatibility. However, we are only doing that for the first row. This works fine in most cases but does not work correctly in the case above since the first value is supported but not the second value :(

[NONE] Perhaps this can be tackled from the "EAFP vs LBYL" perspective? I.e., instead of trying to check if a column is arrow compatible via a heuristic, just try to serialize it with arrow. If this was possible one could avoid (1) inconsistencies with the heuristic and actual arrow semantics, and (2) avoid iterating over the entire column twice, once for the check, and once inside arrow. I assume the main challenge would be that serialization would have to be done "column-based" for probing/serializing on an individual column level, instead of the whole frame/table.

title: Attempting to show a table with nested lists fails with `cannot mix list and non-list, non-null values`
text: [COLLABORATOR] Yeah, this could be a solution. But not sure if we can efficiently convert Pandas to Arrow column-by-column. Also note that we are only executing these checks if the first attempt to convert to arrow fails and the big majority of cases succeed at first try. I would love if pyarrow would provide a built-in fallback-to-string option. Or maybe provide us with structured information on what column failed the serialization. At the moment, the info is just part of the exception message. But maybe parsing this info from the exception text could still be an option?

title: st.dialog Does Not Close Immediately After User Action if Followed by Blocking Operation (e.g. time.sleep(15))
text:
Issue #9405: st.dialog Does Not Close Immediately After User Action if Followed by Blocking Operation (e.g. time.sleep(15))
Labels: type:enhancement, papercut, feature:st.dialog

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When using `st.dialog` to collect feedback from a user, if the feedback submission is followed by a blocking operation (e.g., `time.sleep(15)`), the dialog's title remains visible on the screen until the blocking operation is complete. This creates a poor user experience because the user may expect the dialog to disappear immediately after submitting their input, but the dialog remains visible until the blocking operation finishes.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st

[USER].dialog("Cast your vote")
def vote(item):
    st.write(f"Why is {item} your favorite?")
    reason = st.text_input("Because...")
    if st.button("Submit"):
        st.session_state.vote = {"item": item, "reason": reason}
        st.rerun()

if "vote" not in st.session_state:
    st.write("Vote for your favorite")

    if st.button("A"):
        vote("A")
    if st.button("B"):
        vote("B")
else:
    time.sleep(15)
    f"You voted for {st.session_state.vote['item']} because {st.session_state.vote['reason']}"
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Use the provided code below to mimic collecting user feedback using `st.dialog`.
2. After the user submits their feedback, the code simulates a blocking operation using `time.sleep(15)`.
3. Notice that the dialog's title ("Cast your vote") remains visible for the full 15 seconds while `time.sleep(15)` is running.

### Expected Behavior

title: st.dialog Does Not Close Immediately After User Action if Followed by Blocking Operation (e.g. time.sleep(15))
text:
### Expected Behavior

The dialog should close immediately after the user submits their input, regardless of any blocking operation that follows, so that the UI responds promptly to the user's action.

### Current Behavior

The dialog remains open until the blocking operation (`time.sleep(15)`) is completed. This means the title "Cast your vote" is displayed on the screen for 15 seconds.

![2024-09-04_21-39-12 (1)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f664f9f7-24cf-4b3b-8fad-d5fdcf0dcfdb)

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.37.1
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: Mac OS / Linux Ubuntu 
- Browser: Chrome 

### Additional Information

### GIF:
_Attach a GIF that shows the issue occurring._

### Additional Context:

I plan to use `st.dialog` to collect user confirmation before running a long operation. However, due to this behavior, the dialog title remains visible until the operation completes, making the user experience confusing. Ideally, the dialog should close immediately after the user interaction, regardless of subsequent operations.

[COLLABORATOR] Hey [USER], thanks for opening the issue! I agree that the flow in the example is not great.
For some background, right now we clean up stale nodes (e.g. the dialog after triggering st.rerun) after a `finished session` message. This means that the cleanup is only triggered _after_ the rerun is finished (here after the sleep), not when a new session / run starts.

I believe for handling this in a nicer way, we probably would need to expose the `close` function to the dialog so that you could manually indicate to the web app that you want to close it.
However, here is a (little bit hacky) way of doing this right now:

```python
def cb():
    st.markdown("<script>document.querySelector('[aria-label=\"Close\"]').click()</script>", unsafe_allow_html=True)

[USER].dialog("Cast your vote")
def vote(item):
    st.write(f"Why is {item} your favorite?")
    reason = st.text_input("Because...")
    if st.button("Submit", on_click=cb):
        st.session_state.vote = {"item": item, "reason": reason}
        st.session_state.dialog_closed = True
        st.rerun()
```

I have marke the issue as enhancement and not bug, because theoretically this is expected behavior in the current Streamlit execution model. cc [USER]

For the second solution I noticed this: Fade effect works great, but for some reason it creates that weird white space: [NONE] In my case, at version 1.52.2, all mentioned approaches above did not work. But this worked: ```python import streamlit as st import time def set_dialog_invisible(): """Set the dialog to invisible using JavaScript.""" css = f""" """ st.markdown(css, unsafe_allow_html=True) # Make sure this state exists if "dialog_closed " not in st.session_state: st.session_state.dialog_closed = False # This dialog is not dismissable with the "X" (Close) button [USER].dialog("My Dialog", dismissable=False) def my_dialog() st.write("Click close button") if st.button("Close"): st.session_state.dialog_closed = True st.rerun() if st.session_state.dialog_closed: # This makes sure, that the closed dialog will be invisable, while rerun() is running set_dialog_invisible() # Start a long task, after dialog was closed st.write("Long task started...") time.sleep(10) st.write("Finish!") # Reset state st.session_state.dialog_closed = False else: my_dialog() ``` Workflow explained: 1. Open this page and the dialog will open instantly (since the session state `dialog_closed=False`) 2. Close the Dialog with the button (this will trigger the `st.rerun()` and set `dialog_closed=True`) 3. [CONTRIBUTOR] Hi [USER] thanks for submitting this issue. It seems there's two problems:
1) putting your db connection is session_state isn't the best place for that kind of thing to live. I'd take a look at [`st.connection`](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/connections/st.connection) instead
2) this has uncovered an issue with how were measuring memory for session_state as part of our metrics

I'll keep this issue open to track (2), but would recommend you trying (1) to see if it can unblock you.

[CONTRIBUTOR] Fixed by #15334 (merged 2026-05-27). The cache/stats sizing path now goes through a `safe_sizeof()` guard (`lib/streamlit/runtime/stats.py`) that catches the `TypeError: cannot create weak reference` raised when sizing SQLAlchemy objects, so the `/_stcore/metrics` endpoint no longer 500s. (As an extra layer, #15472 also made the expensive memory stats off by default.)

Closing as resolved — please reopen if it recurs on a current release.

### Summary

It would be convenient to allow users to simply run `python streamlit_app.py`, without having to necessarily run `streamlit run streamlit_app.py`

This would make it easier to launch streamlit apps in a more flexible way. The dependencies above were inserted to the script automatically with:

[CONTRIBUTOR] If anyone's trying to register project entry point to use with `uv`, i.e. 
```toml
[project.scripts]
my_dashboard = "my_package.my_dashboard.main:main"
```
you'll need to put the workaround in a function and replace `locals` with `globals`:
```python
def main() -> None:
    if "__streamlitmagic__" not in globals():   # <<<<< changed here
        from streamlit.web.bootstrap import run

        run(__file__, False, [], {})

    # Rest of your init code
```
Then it's possible to do `uv run my_dashboard`. HOWEVER, I am yet to find a way to get it to automatically switch to the `my_package/my_dashboard` subfolder (I don't want to specify this in the run command), so if you have a `.streamlit` folder with configs/secrets, it **won't be picked up** unless you `cd` to the app's directory manually beforehand.

title: Allow streamlit app to be run as a normal python script with `python app.py`
text:
[COLLABORATOR] ## Update

This use case is addressed by the new `st.App(...).run()` API shipping in Streamlit 1.59.

This gives Streamlit apps an officially supported Python entry point, so launcher files can be run directly with:

```bash
python app.py
uv run app.py
```

It also works well with PEP 723 inline script dependencies, e.g. a launcher can declare `streamlit` and app-specific dependencies directly in the file and be run with `uv run app.py` without a separate environment setup step.

Example:

```python
# /// script
# dependencies = [
#   "streamlit",
#   "yfinance",
# ]
# ///

import streamlit as st

app = st.App("streamlit_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

This avoids relying on internal `streamlit.web.bootstrap` calls. The supported pattern is a small Python launcher that points at the Streamlit app script, rather than making arbitrary Streamlit scripts auto-run themselves.

title: `st.container` : Enable horizontal scrolling
text:
Issue #9544: `st.container` : Enable horizontal scrolling
Labels: type:enhancement, area:layout, feature:st.container, type:possible-component

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Containers today only enable a vertical scrolling of inner elements (widgets, or nested containers). Enabling horizontal behaviour would allow a lot of new interesting UI/UX patterns to emerge.

### Why?

There has been several occurences where I thought a horizontal container would work best, as a method to optimize the layout for complex ideas. For example, when developing a sort of workbench for a specific AI use case, where I want to build a lot of different purpose driven interfaces.

I feel that some basic but powerful layout options like horizontal scrolling is still what hinders from using streamlit has a SPA/App Platform when the use case gets richer.

### How?

Introduce the `direction` or `scrolling` parameter to `st.container` . I believe containers are the right place for layout options, since they can be nested into columns and combine to create very rich and intuitive horizontal and vertical layout options, without much cognitive load. 

### Additional Context

Today, creating something similar to this requires a lot of column nesting which in my experience is tough to make readable at all screen sizes, and is very annoying to develop for.

_No response_

### Summary

I want to use streamlit to display the image from a code execution result from jupyter_client.

However, I found that importing streamlit will change the msg_type from jupyter_client, from `display_data` to `stream`
So I can't get the image to display.

Looks like that after importing,  streamlit changed the stdout or something similar.
Is this normal?

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from jupyter_client import KernelManager
import re
import streamlit as st #if you do not import streamlit, the behavior will be normal

def extract_code(text):
    import json5

    # Match triple backtick blocks first
    triple_match = re.search(r'[^\n]*\n(.+?)```', text, re.DOTALL)
    # Match single backtick blocks second
    single_match = re.search(r'`([^`]*)`', text, re.DOTALL)
    if triple_match:
        text = triple_match.group(1)
    elif single_match:
        text = single_match.group(1)
    else:
        try:
            text = json5.loads(text)['code']
        except Exception:
            pass
    # If no code blocks found, return original text
    return text

# start the kernel and manager

km = KernelManager()
km.start_kernel()
kc = km.client()

command = "\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\neven_numbers = list(range(2, 101, 2))\nplt.bar(range(len(even_numbers)), even_numbers)\nplt.xlabel('Even Numbers')\nplt.ylabel('Value')\nplt.title('Even Numbers in the Range 1-100')\nplt.show()```"
command = extract_code(command)
kc.execute(command)
while True:
    msg = kc.get_iopub_msg(timeout=5)
    msg_type = msg['msg_type']
    print(msg_type)
    print(msg)
    if msg_type == 'status':
        if msg['content'].get('execution_state') == 'idle':
            break
```

title: Stale output from a long-running computation erroneously shows as not stale when app rerun
text:
Issue #9904: Stale output from a long-running computation erroneously shows as not stale when app rerun
Labels: type:bug, area:frontend, status:confirmed, priority:P3

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

This is a bug report on behalf of Thiago in order to keep it tracked.

When a Streamlit app with long-running computation is stopped and then re-run, old stale data from the previous run show up as if it was not stale until the old thread completes execution, at which point the data is properly cleaned up.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import platform
import time

import streamlit as st

st.caption(
    f"""
Running with Python {platform.python_version()} and Streamlit {st.__version__}.
"""
)

"""
This is an app!!
"""


def slow_computation(x):
    st.write("Starting slow computation...")
    time.sleep(10)
    st.write("Stopping slow computation...")
    return f"Done, {x + 1}"


out = slow_computation(1)

st.write(out)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

This is a Playwright test that simulates the current behavior (which is to say, this test currently passes, but should fail once the underlying issue is fixed). There are `NOTE`s inline that describe expected behavior

title: Stale output from a long-running computation erroneously shows as not stale when app rerun
text:
### Steps To Reproduce

This is a Playwright test that simulates the current behavior (which is to say, this test currently passes, but should fail once the underlying issue is fixed). There are `NOTE`s inline that describe expected behavior

```py
import time

from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_threading_behavior(page: Page):
    # This uses `localhost:8501` since I was running different versions of Streamlit
    # in an attempt to bisect this issue in case it was introduced at some point in time
    page.goto("http://localhost:8501/")

    page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...").wait_for(timeout=20000)
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()

    print(page.query_selector_all(".element-container")[0].inner_text())

    # At this point, the first run of the thread completed
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # conditional logic to make it work with older versions of Streamlit
    if page.query_selector('div[data-testid="stMainMenu"]'):
        page.get_by_test_id("stMainMenu").click()
    elif page.query_selector('[id="MainMenu"]'):
        main_menu = page.query_selector('[id="MainMenu"]')
        if main_menu:
            main_menu.click()

    # Now we are re-running the app
    page.get_by_text("Rerun").click()

    # Some time delay so that the new thread is started and some elements are marked as stable
    time.sleep(2)

    # Expect some of the elements to be marked as stale
    assert len(page.query_selector_all('div[data-stale="true"]')) == 2
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # Stop the new thread
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Stop").click()

    time.sleep(2)

    # NOTE: This should not pass. Stale elements shouldn't suddenly be marked as not stale
    # since these are old results from a thread that was supposed to have been stopped
    assert len(page.query_selector_all('div[data-stale="true"]')) == 0

    # NOTE: This should not pass. It is unexpected that the results from the old thread
    # are still showing up, despite us re-running
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # wait for the thread to complete
    time.sleep(10)

    # Expect old elements to be cleared out
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).not_to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).not_to_be_visible()
```

### Checklist

- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Pydeck supports globeview, as seen in the [pydeck documentation](https://deckgl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/globe_view.html).

Running this example with `st.pydeck_chart(deck)` renders a flat earth projection instead.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-9933)

```Python
import pydeck as pdk
import pandas as pd

COUNTRIES = "https://d2ad6b4ur7yvpq.cloudfront.net/naturalearth-3.3.0/ne_50m_admin_0_scale_rank.geojson"
view_state = pdk.ViewState(latitude=51.47, longitude=0.45, zoom=2, min_zoom=0)

# Set height and width variables
view = pdk.View(type="_GlobeView", controller=True, width=1000, height=700)
layers = [
    pdk.Layer(
        "GeoJsonLayer",
        id="base-map",
        data=COUNTRIES,
        stroked=False,
        filled=True,
        get_fill_color=[200, 200, 200],
    )
]

deck = pdk.Deck(
    views=[view],
    initial_view_state=view_state,
    tooltip={"text": "{name}, {primary_fuel} plant, {country}"},
    layers=layers,
    map_provider=None,
    # Note that this must be set for the globe to be opaque
    parameters={"cull": True},
)

deck.to_html("globe_view.html", css_background_color="black")

import streamlit as st
st.pydeck_chart(deck)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

run the streamlit app example given above to reproduce.  

### Expected Behavior

The expected behavior is a 3-d earth we can rotate and spin, e.g. to a polar view like this:  
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b747a1cf-2388-4a27-8cfe-6b544ce12ddf)

We don't get an error, we simply get a 2d web-mercator projection:

title: st.pydeck_chart does not suport pydeck globeview
text:
[COLLABORATOR] I took a look at this and wanted to share my findings.

The behavior has described in the ticket is correct, thank you [USER] for a great issue report!

In the code, we've had a [long-standing statement](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/500b739c0d3cd623849ba986e390630db793b853/frontend/src/components/elements/DeckGlJsonChart/DeckGlJsonChart.tsx#L76) that intentionally removes views from being passed to deck.gl on the frontend since we've traditionally just supported a single MapView.

Deck.gl has 4 fully supported views (MapView, FirstPersonView, OrthographicView, OrbitView), and 1 experimental view (_GlobeView) [[docs](https://deck.gl/docs/developer-guide/views)]. In order to support all of these view types, we'd need to do a bit of refactoring that adds support for all the different types of views. We may even want to consider supporting multiple types of views at once, since Deck.gl supports this too.

If we were to fix this, this is a potentially breaking change for apps that may have previously passed in a pydeck View, but rely on it falling back to MapView at runtime. 

```python
st.pydeck_chart(
    pdk.Deck(
        views=[pdk.View(type="FirstPersonView")],
        # Other args...
    )
)
```

To be clear, that certainly isn't a reason _against_ fixing this as we'd be technically fixing that issue as well during this, I'm just using this to illustrate the compounding factors that are at hand with this.

With all of that said, I am going to turn this into a feature request given the breadth of what may need to be done in order to support this!

This will be available in Streamlit **1.64+** ([#16819](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16819)). `st.pydeck_chart` now honors `_GlobeView` instead of forcing a Web Mercator map.

COUNTRIES = "https://d2ad6b4ur7yvpq.cloudfront.net/naturalearth-3.3.0/ne_50m_admin_0_scale_rank.geojson"

st.pydeck_chart(
    pdk.Deck(
        layers=[

title: `st.date_input` doesn't show placeholder text when the initial value is a list of size one
text:
Issue #9946: `st.date_input` doesn't show placeholder text when the initial value is a list of size one
Labels: type:enhancement, papercut, feature:st.date_input

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

You can pass a list to `st.date_input`'s `value` parameter. An empty list will initialize the widget with an empty interval (showing placeholder text). A pair of values will initialize the widget with the given interval (showing the dates as an initial selection). However, if you pass a list of size one, the widget has only the starting date of the interval initialized with no end date. Instead of showing placeholder text for the end date, it's blank.

```
import streamlit as st
from datetime import date, datetime

a = st.selectbox("A", ["today", "2024-10-01", date(2024,9,1), datetime(2024,8,1,12,0,0,0), None])
b = st.selectbox("B", ["today", "2024-10-01", date(2024,9,1), datetime(2024,8,1,12,0,0,0), None])

x = st.date_input("Two-list", [a,b])
x
y = st.date_input("One-list", [a])
y
z = st.date_input("Empty-list", [])
z
```

### Why?

Presumably, it would look better to show placeholder text for the end date when only the initial date of a range is selected. This is also how an intermediate state looks if someone selects a new start date and clicks out of the widget before selecting the end date.

### How?

If someone unfocuses an (interval) date widget with only the start date selected, show the placeholder text for the missing end date.

### Additional Context

_No response_
